### Streams API — `Stream.gather()` (Java 22+ Preview, Java 24 Final)

`Stream.gather(Gatherer)` extends the Streams API to support stateful, flexible intermediate operations that don't fit neatly into `map`/`filter`/`flatMap`. Built-in gatherers are in `java.util.stream.Gatherers`.

```java
import java.util.stream.Gatherers;

// Sliding window — groups consecutive elements into overlapping lists
List<List<Integer>> windows = Stream.of(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
    .gather(Gatherers.windowSliding(3))
    .toList();
// [[1,2,3], [2,3,4], [3,4,5]]

// Fixed window — groups into non-overlapping chunks
List<List<Integer>> chunks = Stream.of(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
    .gather(Gatherers.windowFixed(2))
    .toList();
// [[1,2], [3,4], [5]]

// Scan — running total / prefix-sum
List<Integer> runningSum = Stream.of(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
    .gather(Gatherers.scan(() -> 0, Integer::sum))
    .toList();
// [1, 3, 6, 10, 15]

// Custom gatherer — take while sum < threshold (stateful)
Gatherer<Integer, ?, Integer> takeWhileSum = Gatherer.ofSequential(
    () -> new int[]{0},              // initializer: mutable state
    (state, element, downstream) -> {
        state[0] += element;
        return state[0] < 10 && downstream.push(element);
    }
);
List<Integer> result = Stream.of(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6)
    .gather(takeWhileSum)
    .toList();
// [1, 2, 3] — stops when cumulative sum reaches 6 (next would exceed 10)
```

---

### Sequenced Collections (Java 21 — JEP 431)

Java 21 adds `SequencedCollection`, `SequencedSet`, and `SequencedMap` interfaces to the collections hierarchy. Every ordered collection now has a uniform API for first/last access and reversed views.

```java
import java.util.*;

// SequencedCollection — new methods on List, Deque, LinkedHashSet, etc.
List<String> list = new ArrayList<>(List.of("a", "b", "c"));
list.addFirst("z");         // prepend — was add(0, "z")
list.addLast("d");          // append  — was add("d")
String first = list.getFirst();  // "z"
String last  = list.getLast();   // "d"
list.removeFirst();         // was remove(0)
list.removeLast();          // was remove(list.size()-1)

// Reversed view — backed by the same list, mutations reflected
List<String> rev = list.reversed();
System.out.println(rev.getFirst()); // last element of original

// SequencedMap — LinkedHashMap, TreeMap now expose firstEntry/lastEntry
LinkedHashMap<String, Integer> scores = new LinkedHashMap<>();
scores.put("Alice", 90); scores.put("Bob", 85); scores.put("Carol", 92);
Map.Entry<String, Integer> top    = scores.firstEntry();  // Alice, 90
Map.Entry<String, Integer> bottom = scores.lastEntry();   // Carol, 92
scores.putFirst("Zara", 99);  // inserts at head
SequencedMap<String, Integer> reversed = scores.reversed();
```

**Anti-pattern [community]:** Using `list.get(0)` and `list.get(list.size()-1)` for first/last access on lists — these are now a code smell. `getFirst()` / `getLast()` are cleaner and throw `NoSuchElementException` on empty collections (unlike `get(0)` which throws `IndexOutOfBoundsException`).

---

### AssertJ Soft Assertions and Recursive Comparison

**Soft assertions** collect all failures before reporting — useful when asserting multiple independent properties of the same object:

```java
import org.assertj.core.api.SoftAssertions;
import org.assertj.core.api.junit.jupiter.SoftAssertionsExtension;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;

@ExtendWith(SoftAssertionsExtension.class)
class OrderTest {

    @Test
    void order_hasCorrectState(SoftAssertions softly) {
        Order order = placeOrder("ITEM-001", 3, "Alice");

        // All assertions evaluated — failure report shows ALL that fail, not just first
        softly.assertThat(order.getStatus()).isEqualTo(OrderStatus.PLACED);
        softly.assertThat(order.getQuantity()).isEqualTo(3);
        softly.assertThat(order.getCustomerName()).isEqualTo("Alice");
        softly.assertThat(order.getTotalPrice()).isGreaterThan(0);
    }
}
```

**Recursive comparison** compares object graphs without implementing `equals()` — ideal for testing DTOs and response objects:

```java
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@Test
void createUser_returnsCorrectProfile() {
    UserProfile actual   = userService.create("alice@example.com", "Alice");
    UserProfile expected = new UserProfile("Alice", "alice@example.com", UserRole.USER);

    assertThat(actual)
        .usingRecursiveComparison()
        .ignoringFields("id", "createdAt")        // generated fields
        .ignoringFieldsOfTypes(UUID.class)         // or by type
        .withEqualsForType(
            (a, b) -> a.equalsIgnoreCase(b),       // custom comparator per type
            String.class)
        .isEqualTo(expected);
}
```

**AssertJ for Java records [community]:** Records implement `equals()` correctly by default, so `assertThat(actualRecord).isEqualTo(expectedRecord)` works without `.usingRecursiveComparison()`. Reserve recursive comparison for classes without proper `equals()`, or when you need to exclude auto-generated fields.

### Mockito 5.x — `thenAnswer` Patterns and `ArgumentCaptor`

**`thenAnswer`** is more powerful than `thenReturn` when the mock response depends on the call arguments:

```java
import org.mockito.ArgumentCaptor;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.*;
import static org.mockito.ArgumentMatchers.*;

class OrderServiceTest {

    @Mock UserRepository userRepo;
    @Mock OrderRepository orderRepo;
    @InjectMocks OrderService orderService;

    @Test
    void thenAnswer_returnsArgumentDependentResponse() {
        // Return a user whose name matches the queried ID (dynamic stub)
        when(userRepo.findById(anyLong()))
            .thenAnswer(invocation -> {
                long id = invocation.getArgument(0);
                return Optional.of(new User(id, "user-" + id));
            });

        User u = orderService.getOwner(42L);
        assertThat(u.getName()).isEqualTo("user-42");
    }

    @Test
    void argumentCaptor_verifiesSavedState() {
        ArgumentCaptor<Order> captor = ArgumentCaptor.forClass(Order.class);

        orderService.placeOrder("ITEM-007", 2, 1L);

        verify(orderRepo).save(captor.capture());
        Order saved = captor.getValue();
        assertThat(saved.getItemCode()).isEqualTo("ITEM-007");
        assertThat(saved.getQuantity()).isEqualTo(2);
        assertThat(saved.getStatus()).isEqualTo(OrderStatus.PLACED);
    }

    @Test
    void doThrow_stubsVoidMethod() {
        doThrow(new DataIntegrityViolationException("duplicate"))
            .when(orderRepo).save(any(Order.class));

        assertThatThrownBy(() -> orderService.placeOrder("ITEM-007", 2, 1L))
            .isInstanceOf(OrderConflictException.class)
            .hasMessageContaining("already exists");
    }
}
```

**Mockito 5.x new capabilities [community]:**
- **Inline mocking of final classes and static methods** — available without extra configuration on JDK 11+ via `MockMaker.INLINE`. No need for PowerMock.
- **`RETURNS_DEEP_STUBS`** — enables chained stubbing (`mock.getA().getB().getC()`). Use sparingly: deep stubs couple tests to object structure and hide design smells (Law of Demeter violations).
- **`@MockitoBean`** (Spring Boot 3.4+) — replaces deprecated `@MockBean`. Works with `@SpringBootTest` and slice tests. Registered in the `ApplicationContext` and reset between tests automatically.
- **`Mockito.mockConstruction()`** — intercepts `new MyClass()` calls in production code. Useful when you can't inject via constructor but need to control object creation in legacy code.

---

### Spring Boot Testing — `@MockitoBean`, `MockMvcTester`, `RestTestClient`

Spring Boot 3.4 introduced first-class Mockito integration, replacing the older Spring-owned `@MockBean`:

```java
import org.springframework.test.context.bean.override.mockito.MockitoBean;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;

@SpringBootTest
class UserControllerIntegrationTest {

    @MockitoBean          // replaces @MockBean; backed by Mockito 5; auto-reset between tests
    UserRepository userRepo;

    @Autowired
    MockMvc mockMvc;

    @Test
    void getUser_returns200WithBody() throws Exception {
        when(userRepo.findById(1L))
            .thenReturn(Optional.of(new User(1L, "Alice", "alice@example.com")));

        mockMvc.perform(get("/users/1").accept(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON))
            .andExpect(status().isOk())
            .andExpect(jsonPath("$.name").value("Alice"));
    }
}
```

**`MockMvcTester`** (Spring Boot 3.4) provides an AssertJ-native fluent API for `MockMvc`, replacing `andExpect()` chains:

```java
import org.springframework.test.web.servlet.assertj.MockMvcTester;

@WebMvcTest(UserController.class)
class UserControllerSliceTest {

    @Autowired MockMvcTester mvc;
    @MockitoBean UserRepository repo;

    @Test
    void getUser_notFound_returns404() {
        when(repo.findById(99L)).thenReturn(Optional.empty());

        assertThat(mvc.get().uri("/users/99"))
            .hasStatus(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND)
            .hasContentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_PROBLEM_JSON);
    }

    @Test
    void createUser_valid_returns201() {
        var body = """
            {"name": "Bob", "email": "bob@example.com"}
            """;

        assertThat(mvc.post().uri("/users")
                .contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
                .content(body))
            .hasStatus(HttpStatus.CREATED)
            .bodyJson()
            .hasPath("$.id").isNotNull();
    }
}
```

**Spring Boot testing anti-patterns [community]:**
- **Loading full context for unit-level concerns:** `@SpringBootTest` starts the entire application context. Use slice annotations (`@WebMvcTest`, `@DataJpaTest`, `@JsonTest`) when you only need a slice — they start in ~10% of the time.
- **`@MockBean` in `@DataJpaTest`:** Mixing mocks into a JPA slice test couples your repository tests to service layer behaviour. Test repository queries with real data; mock the repository at the service test layer.
- **Not setting `spring.jpa.show-sql=true` in test slice:** Silent SQL is a major source of N+1 query bugs in production that pass tests. Enable SQL logging in `application-test.properties` and review it during integration tests.
- **Reusing `@SpringBootTest` context across tests with different `@MockitoBean` sets:** Each unique `@MockitoBean` combination creates a new application context. Consolidate mock declarations in a shared base class to maximise context reuse across the test suite.

### Real-World Gotchas — Cycle 19 Additions [community]

**Parallel Stream on small collections [community]** — `stream.parallel()` splits work across the common ForkJoinPool. On collections smaller than ~10,000 elements, the split-and-merge overhead exceeds the benefit. Profile before parallelising; use `parallelStream()` only on large, CPU-bound pipelines where elements are independent and the collector is thread-safe.

**Record `equals()` compares component values — not identity [community]** — Records use structural equality by default. Two `record Point(int x, int y)` instances with the same coordinates are `==` in terms of `equals()` but not in terms of `==` reference equality. This is usually desired but surprises developers who use records as `Map` keys expecting identity semantics.

**Sealed class `permits` clause and compilation boundaries [community]** — All permitted subclasses of a sealed type must be in the same module (for named modules) or the same package (for unnamed modules). Attempting cross-package sealing outside a named module is a compile error. Plan sealed hierarchies within a single package or module boundary.

**Virtual thread + JDBC connection pool sizing [community]** — With virtual threads, you can spin up 10,000 concurrent requests. If your HikariCP pool has `maximumPoolSize=10` (the default), all 10,000 virtual threads will compete for 10 connections, causing contention. Set `maximumPoolSize` to match the database's actual max connections, and use a `Semaphore` in front of the pool if you need to rate-limit further.

**`StructuredTaskScope` is still in preview in Java 21/22 [community]** — Enable with `--enable-preview` and `--source 21` flags, or wait for the final API in Java 23+. Preview APIs may have minor changes between versions. Don't ship preview features in library code that other projects consume.

**`@AutoClose` on static fields closes after the last test in the class [community]** — The annotation respects the lifecycle scope: `static` fields close after `@AfterAll`; instance fields close after each `@AfterEach`. Mixing both in the same test class with resources that have ordering dependencies can produce surprising close sequences; declare lifecycle scope explicitly.

### Spring Boot Slice Testing — `@DataJpaTest`, `@JsonTest`, `@RestClientTest`

Spring Boot's slice annotations each load a minimal subset of the application context. Using the wrong slice — or `@SpringBootTest` — for a concern adds seconds of startup overhead and coupling. This section provides complete patterns for the three most-overlooked slices.

#### `@DataJpaTest` — Repository Isolation

`@DataJpaTest` configures an in-memory H2 database (or a Testcontainers DataSource via `@AutoConfigureTestDatabase`), scans only `@Repository` beans, and wraps every test in a transaction that rolls back automatically.

```java
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.orm.jpa.DataJpaTest;
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.orm.jpa.TestEntityManager;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@DataJpaTest
class UserRepositoryTest {

    @Autowired TestEntityManager em;       // thin wrapper around EntityManager
    @Autowired UserRepository   repo;

    @Test
    void findByEmail_returnsUser_whenExists() {
        // Persist a user directly through EntityManager — bypasses service layer
        User user = new User("Alice", "alice@example.com");
        em.persistAndFlush(user);         // flush to DB; SQL is visible in logs

        // Exercise the repository query
        Optional<User> found = repo.findByEmail("alice@example.com");

        assertThat(found).isPresent()
            .hasValueSatisfying(u -> {
                assertThat(u.getName()).isEqualTo("Alice");
                assertThat(u.getEmail()).isEqualTo("alice@example.com");
            });
    }

    @Test
    void findByEmail_returnsEmpty_whenMissing() {
        assertThat(repo.findByEmail("nobody@example.com")).isEmpty();
    }
}
```

**Anti-pattern [community] — using `@SpringBootTest` for repository tests:** `@SpringBootTest` loads the full application context (all `@Service`, `@Controller`, security config, etc.). For a repository test, this is ~10× slower and couples your query test to the entire application wiring. Use `@DataJpaTest` exclusively for JPA query verification.

**Anti-pattern [community] — forgetting to flush before asserting:** `TestEntityManager.persist()` stores the entity in the first-level cache but may not immediately flush to the database. `persistAndFlush()` or `em.flush()` after `em.persist()` ensures the SQL is issued before the repository query runs, avoiding tests that pass only because JPA serves the result from the cache.

#### `@JsonTest` — Jackson Serialization Isolation

`@JsonTest` configures only Jackson (or Gson) with Spring Boot auto-configuration applied — no web layer, no database. Use it to verify `@JsonAlias`, `@JsonIgnore`, custom serializers, and property naming strategies.

```java
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.json.JsonTest;
import org.springframework.boot.test.json.JacksonTester;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@JsonTest
class OrderDtoJsonTest {

    @Autowired
    JacksonTester<OrderDto> json;    // typed tester for OrderDto

    @Test
    void serializes_snakeCaseField() throws Exception {
        OrderDto dto = new OrderDto(42L, "PLACED", "alice@example.com");

        // Assert serialized JSON contains snake_case key (if naming strategy is configured)
        assertThat(json.write(dto))
            .hasJsonPathNumberValue("$.order_id")
            .extractingJsonPathStringValue("$.status").isEqualTo("PLACED");
    }

    @Test
    void deserializes_fromJson() throws Exception {
        String raw = """
            {"order_id": 99, "status": "SHIPPED", "customer_email": "bob@example.com"}
            """;

        OrderDto dto = json.parse(raw).getObject();

        assertThat(dto.orderId()).isEqualTo(99L);
        assertThat(dto.status()).isEqualTo("SHIPPED");
    }
}
```

**When to prefer `@JsonTest` over `@WebMvcTest` JSON assertions:** If your goal is to verify the serialization contract of a DTO in isolation (not the HTTP binding), `@JsonTest` is 3–5× faster because it skips the web layer entirely. Use `@WebMvcTest` when you need to verify controller → serialization → HTTP response end-to-end.

#### `@RestClientTest` — HTTP Client Isolation

`@RestClientTest` configures `RestClient` (or `RestTemplate`) beans and a `MockRestServiceServer` for asserting outbound HTTP calls. It does NOT load the web layer — it tests client code calling downstream services.

```java
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.web.client.RestClientTest;
import org.springframework.test.web.client.MockRestServiceServer;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.http.MediaType;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.springframework.test.web.client.match.MockRestRequestMatchers.*;
import static org.springframework.test.web.client.response.MockRestResponseCreators.*;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@RestClientTest(ExchangeRateClient.class)   // only this client bean is loaded
class ExchangeRateClientTest {

    @Autowired MockRestServiceServer server;
    @Autowired ExchangeRateClient     client;

    @Test
    void getRate_parsesResponse() {
        server.expect(requestTo("/rates/EUR"))
              .andExpect(method(HttpMethod.GET))
              .andRespond(withSuccess("""
                  {"currency":"EUR","rate":1.08}
                  """, MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON));

        ExchangeRate rate = client.getRate("EUR");

        assertThat(rate.currency()).isEqualTo("EUR");
        assertThat(rate.rate()).isEqualTo(1.08);
        server.verify();   // assert all expected requests were made
    }
}
```

### Property-Based Testing with jqwik (Java)

Property-based testing generates hundreds of inputs automatically, finding edge cases that manually written examples miss. `jqwik` is the leading property-based testing library for JUnit 5, running as a JUnit Platform engine.

```xml
<!-- Maven dependency -->
<dependency>
    <groupId>net.jqwik</groupId>
    <artifactId>jqwik</artifactId>
    <version>1.9.0</version>
    <scope>test</scope>
</dependency>
```

```java
import net.jqwik.api.*;
import net.jqwik.api.constraints.*;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

class StringUtilsPropertyTest {

    // @Property replaces @Test — jqwik generates 'tries' (default 1000) random inputs
    @Property
    void reverseOfReverse_isOriginal(@ForAll String original) {
        String reversed = StringUtils.reverse(original);
        assertThat(StringUtils.reverse(reversed)).isEqualTo(original);
    }

    @Property
    void sortedList_hasSameSizeAsInput(@ForAll List<@IntRange(min = -1000, max = 1000) Integer> list) {
        List<Integer> sorted = list.stream().sorted().toList();
        assertThat(sorted).hasSameSizeAs(list);
    }

    @Property
    void emailValidator_rejectsBlankLocalPart(
            @ForAll @StringLength(min = 1, max = 100) @AlphaChars String domain) {
        String email = "@" + domain + ".com";  // blank local part
        assertThat(EmailValidator.isValid(email)).isFalse();
    }

    // Shrinking: when a test fails, jqwik automatically minimises the failing input
    // e.g., if a 50-char string fails, jqwik will find the shortest failing string
}
```

**When to reach for property-based testing [community]:**
- Any pure function with an inverse (encode/decode, compress/decompress, serialize/deserialize).
- Boundary conditions: validators, parsers, comparators, sort algorithms.
- Algebraic laws: associativity, commutativity, idempotency.
- Do NOT use for integration tests or tests involving databases — jqwik runs hundreds of times; each run must be fast and isolated.

### Mutation Testing with PIT (pitest)

Mutation testing measures test suite effectiveness by systematically introducing code changes (mutations) and checking whether tests detect them. A test suite with 90% line coverage can still have a low mutation score if assertions are weak.

```xml
<!-- Maven plugin -->
<plugin>
    <groupId>org.pitest</groupId>
    <artifactId>pitest-maven</artifactId>
    <version>1.17.0</version>
    <configuration>
        <targetClasses>
            <param>com.example.service.*</param>
        </targetClasses>
        <targetTests>
            <param>com.example.service.*Test</param>
        </targetTests>
        <mutators>
            <mutator>DEFAULTS</mutator>   <!-- conditionals, math, returns, void methods -->
        </mutators>
        <withHistory>true</withHistory>   <!-- incremental — only retest changed classes -->
    </configuration>
    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.pitest</groupId>
            <artifactId>pitest-junit5-plugin</artifactId>
            <version>1.2.1</version>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>
</plugin>
```

```bash
# Run mutation tests
mvn test-compile org.pitest:pitest-maven:mutationCoverage

# HTML report at: target/pit-reports/<timestamp>/index.html
# Surviving mutants = code changes that no test caught = weak test assertions
```

**Reading the PIT report — surviving mutants to fix:**
```java
// PIT surviving mutant example: changed conditional boundary from > to >=
// ORIGINAL:
if (quantity > 0) { placeOrder(quantity); }

// MUTATION (PIT changes > to >=):
if (quantity >= 0) { placeOrder(quantity); }
// If no test asserts that quantity=0 is rejected, this mutant SURVIVES.

// FIX — add a test for the boundary:
@Test
void placeOrder_rejectsZeroQuantity() {
    assertThatThrownBy(() -> service.placeOrder(0))
        .isInstanceOf(IllegalArgumentException.class);
}
```

**Community guidance [community]:** Target a mutation score ≥ 70% for business-critical modules (domain model, service layer). Do NOT run PIT on generated code, configuration classes, or DTOs — the cost-benefit ratio is poor. Use `--excludedClasses` or `targetClasses` to focus on the code that matters.

---

### Java 25 — `Flexible Constructor Bodies` (JEP 513 / 531)

Java 25 standardizes the ability to place statements before the `super()` or `this()` call in a constructor (previously a compile error). This eliminates the need for static factory method workarounds when validation or argument computation must happen before delegation.

```java
// BEFORE Java 25 — workaround required: static method to compute argument
public class CheckedList<E> extends ArrayList<E> {

    // Cannot validate 'initialCapacity' before super() in Java 21-24
    // Workaround: static validation method called inline
    public CheckedList(int initialCapacity) {
        super(validateCapacity(initialCapacity));
    }

    private static int validateCapacity(int cap) {
        if (cap < 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Negative capacity: " + cap);
        return cap;
    }
}

// JAVA 25 — statements before super() are now legal
public class CheckedList<E> extends ArrayList<E> {

    public CheckedList(int initialCapacity) {
        // Validation before super() — no static helper needed
        if (initialCapacity < 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Negative capacity: " + initialCapacity);
        }
        super(initialCapacity);         // super() can now be non-first statement
    }
}

// Also applies to this() delegation:
public class Connection {
    private final String url;
    private final int timeoutMs;

    public Connection(String url, int timeoutMs) {
        this.url       = url;
        this.timeoutMs = timeoutMs;
    }

    public Connection(String url) {
        // Java 25: compute default timeout before delegating
        int defaultTimeout = Integer.parseInt(
            System.getProperty("conn.timeout.ms", "5000"));
        this(url, defaultTimeout);    // this() is no longer required to be first
    }
}
```

**Restriction:** You cannot read instance fields (`this.x`) before `super()` completes — the object is not yet fully constructed. Only local variables, method arguments, and static members are accessible in the pre-super block.

---

### Java 25 — `Primitive Types in Patterns` (JEP 488, 3rd Preview)

Java 25 continues the 3rd preview of primitive types in patterns (JEP 455 in Java 23, JEP 488 in Java 24). Primitive type patterns allow `instanceof` checks and `switch` exhaustiveness over primitive types without boxing.

```java
// Primitive instanceof — no boxing, direct narrowing
Object reading = getSensorReading();  // returns Integer, Long, Double, or null

// Java 25 preview — primitive patterns in instanceof
if (reading instanceof int i) {
    System.out.println("Integer reading: " + i);
} else if (reading instanceof long l && l > Integer.MAX_VALUE) {
    System.out.println("Large long: " + l);
} else if (reading instanceof double d) {
    System.out.printf("Decimal: %.2f%n", d);
}

// Exhaustive switch over Number with primitive patterns
static String describe(Number n) {
    return switch (n) {
        case int  i when i < 0    -> "negative int: "  + i;
        case int  i               -> "non-negative int: " + i;
        case long l               -> "long: "          + l;
        case double d             -> "double: "        + d;
        case float f              -> "float: "         + f;
        default                   -> "other number: "  + n;
    };
}

// Switch over a primitive directly (Java 25 preview)
static String classifyByte(byte b) {
    return switch (b) {
        case 0       -> "zero";
        case 1, 2, 3 -> "small positive";
        default      -> b > 0 ? "positive" : "negative";
    };
}
```

**When to use [community]:** Primitive patterns are most useful in data-processing pipelines that receive mixed numeric types (sensor data, financial data, protocol parsers). They eliminate the `instanceof Integer && ((Integer)x).intValue()` idiom. **Do NOT use preview APIs in library code** consumed by other projects until the feature is finalized.

### REST Assured 6.x — BDD-Style API Testing

REST Assured 6.x (Java 17+ minimum) provides a BDD-style DSL for HTTP API testing. It integrates natively with JUnit 5 and supports both standalone and Spring Boot contexts.

```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>io.rest-assured</groupId>
    <artifactId>rest-assured</artifactId>
    <version>6.0.0</version>
    <scope>test</scope>
</dependency>
<!-- For Spring MockMvc integration -->
<dependency>
    <groupId>io.rest-assured</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-mock-mvc</artifactId>
    <version>6.0.0</version>
    <scope>test</scope>
</dependency>
```

```java
import io.restassured.RestAssured;
import io.restassured.http.ContentType;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.boot.test.web.server.LocalServerPort;

import static io.restassured.RestAssured.*;
import static org.hamcrest.Matchers.*;

@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = SpringBootTest.WebEnvironment.RANDOM_PORT)
class UserApiTest {

    @LocalServerPort int port;

    @BeforeEach
    void setUp() {
        RestAssured.port = port;
        RestAssured.basePath = "/api";
    }

    @Test
    void getUser_returns200WithCorrectBody() {
        given()
            .accept(ContentType.JSON)
        .when()
            .get("/users/1")
        .then()
            .statusCode(200)
            .body("name", equalTo("Alice"))
            .body("email", matchesRegex(".+@.+\\..+"));
    }

    @Test
    void createUser_returns201_andLocationHeader() {
        String requestBody = """
            {"name": "Bob", "email": "bob@example.com"}
            """;

        String location =
            given()
                .contentType(ContentType.JSON)
                .body(requestBody)
            .when()
                .post("/users")
            .then()
                .statusCode(201)
                .header("Location", matchesRegex(".*/users/\\d+"))
                .extract().header("Location");

        // Follow the Location header to verify the created resource
        given().accept(ContentType.JSON)
            .when().get(location)
            .then().statusCode(200).body("name", equalTo("Bob"));
    }

    @Test
    void deleteUser_returns404_afterDeletion() {
        // Create
        Integer userId =
            given().contentType(ContentType.JSON)
                   .body("{\"name\":\"Tmp\",\"email\":\"tmp@x.com\"}")
            .when().post("/users")
            .then().statusCode(201)
                   .extract().path("id");

        // Delete
        when().delete("/users/{id}", userId).then().statusCode(204);

        // Verify gone
        when().get("/users/{id}", userId).then().statusCode(404);
    }
}
```

**REST Assured 6.x breaking changes vs 5.x [community]:**
- Requires Java 17 minimum (was Java 8).
- Jackson 3.x is the default serializer; projects still on Jackson 2.x must add `rest-assured-jackson2` compatibility module.
- Spring Boot 4.x requires `spring-mock-mvc` 6.x; Spring Boot 3.x stays on `spring-mock-mvc` 5.x.
- The `io.restassured` package did **not** change — migration is mostly a version bump in pom.xml.

### Virtual Thread Naming and Observability (Java 21+)

Virtual threads created via `Thread.ofVirtual()` or `Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()` have auto-generated names by default (`VirtualThread-N`). In production logs and thread dumps, unnamed virtual threads are indistinguishable. Always name virtual threads when they represent a distinct logical operation.

```java
import java.util.concurrent.*;

// NAMING VIRTUAL THREADS — carry semantic context through logs
Thread.Builder.OfVirtual namedBuilder =
    Thread.ofVirtual().name("request-handler-", 0);   // auto-increments: request-handler-0, -1, ...

Thread handler = namedBuilder.start(() -> {
    MDC.put("thread", Thread.currentThread().getName());  // SLF4J MDC for correlation
    processRequest();
});

// With an ExecutorService — name every task thread
ExecutorService executor = Executors.newThreadPerTaskExecutor(
    Thread.ofVirtual()
          .name("order-processor-", 0)
          .factory());

// Submitting tasks that inherit the naming scheme
executor.submit(() -> {
    String name = Thread.currentThread().getName();  // "order-processor-42"
    log.info("Processing on {}", name);
    processOrder(orderId);
});

// Thread dumps: virtual threads appear in JFR and jcmd Thread.dump_to_file
// jcmd <PID> Thread.dump_to_file -format=json /tmp/threads.json
// Named threads are far easier to correlate with application logs
```

**Anti-pattern [community] — one virtual thread per CPU-bound task:** Virtual threads are designed for I/O-bound work (DB queries, HTTP calls, file I/O). For CPU-bound tasks (image processing, cryptography, data compression), they provide no benefit over platform threads and can increase scheduler overhead because they still consume CPU time on carrier threads. Use `ForkJoinPool` or a fixed-size platform thread pool for CPU-bound parallelism.

---

### `@DataJpaTest` with Real Database via Testcontainers

Replace H2 in-memory with a real PostgreSQL container for production-faithful query testing:

```java
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.orm.jpa.DataJpaTest;
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.jdbc.AutoConfigureTestDatabase;
import org.springframework.boot.testcontainers.service.connection.ServiceConnection;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Container;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Testcontainers;
import org.testcontainers.containers.PostgreSQLContainer;

@DataJpaTest
@Testcontainers
@AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = AutoConfigureTestDatabase.Replace.NONE)  // use real DB
class OrderRepositoryPostgresTest {

    // @ServiceConnection wires the Testcontainers DataSource into Spring automatically
    @Container
    @ServiceConnection
    static final PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres =
        new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine")
            .withReuse(true);   // container survives test runs — faster in local dev

    @Autowired OrderRepository repo;
    @Autowired TestEntityManager em;

    @Test
    void nativeQuery_returnsTopOrdersByRevenue() {
        // Insert test data using the entity manager (real SQL, real PostgreSQL dialect)
        em.persistAndFlush(new Order("alice@example.com", new BigDecimal("199.99")));
        em.persistAndFlush(new Order("bob@example.com",   new BigDecimal("49.99")));

        List<Order> top = repo.findTopByRevenueDesc(1);

        assertThat(top).hasSize(1)
            .first().extracting(Order::getCustomerEmail)
            .isEqualTo("alice@example.com");
    }
}
```

**Why PostgreSQL in `@DataJpaTest` instead of H2 [community]:**
- H2 silently accepts PostgreSQL syntax that is subtly wrong (JSONB operators, array syntax, `ON CONFLICT` clauses differ between H2 compatibility mode and real PostgreSQL).
- Schema migrations (Flyway/Liquibase) may contain PostgreSQL-specific DDL that fails on H2.
- Using `@AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = NONE)` with Testcontainers catches dialect mismatches before production, at the cost of slightly longer test startup (~2s for first container, then reused).

---

### Real-World Gotchas — Cycle 20 Additions [community]

**`@Transactional` on `@DataJpaTest` and Testcontainers with `replace=NONE` [community]** — By default, `@DataJpaTest` wraps each test in a transaction that rolls back after the test. When using `replace=NONE` with a real Postgres container, this rollback behaviour is preserved — but if your test calls code that spawns a new transaction (e.g., a service method with `PROPAGATION_REQUIRES_NEW`), the inner transaction commits to the real database and is NOT rolled back. This leaves dirty data in the container if test isolation is not managed with explicit cleanup or a `@Sql(scripts = "cleanup.sql", ...)` annotation.

**Virtual thread executor shutdown race [community]** — `Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()` creates an unbounded executor. Calling `executor.shutdown()` prevents new tasks but does NOT interrupt running virtual threads. If a running virtual thread blocks on a slow I/O call and you want deterministic test cleanup, call `executor.shutdownNow()` followed by `executor.awaitTermination(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)` in an `@AfterEach`. The `shutdownNow()` sends an interrupt to all running virtual threads, which most blocking I/O calls respect.

**`@MockitoBean` creates a new Spring context per unique set [community]** — Every distinct combination of `@MockitoBean` fields in a `@SpringBootTest` class forces Spring to create a new `ApplicationContext`. If you have 5 different test classes each with a different subset of `@MockitoBean` declarations, you get 5 context loads. Fix: extract all mock declarations to a shared abstract base test class so all subclasses share one context load. This is the single most impactful Spring Boot test performance optimisation for large suites.

**`TestEntityManager.persistAndFlush()` does not assign database-generated IDs to the Java object pre-flush in some JPA providers [community]** — Hibernate assigns the generated `@Id` after the flush. If you call `em.persist(entity)` (without flush) and then query `entity.getId()`, you may get `null` or a Hibernate sequence-generated value that hasn't been confirmed yet. Always use `persistAndFlush()` (or call `em.flush()` + `em.clear()`) before asserting on returned entities' IDs.

**Primitive type pattern `instanceof int i` does not match `null` [community]** — This is consistent with reference-type `instanceof`: `null instanceof SomeClass c` is always `false`, and similarly `null instanceof int i` is `false`. For sensor/protocol parsing code that receives untyped `Object` values that may be `null`, always add a `case null` guard at the top of the `switch` expression before primitive type patterns. Missing the null case results in a `NullPointerException` at the default branch.

**`@JsonTest` does not apply `@JsonComponent` beans from outside the tested package [community]** — `@JsonTest` scans for `@JsonComponent` beans, but only those in the application's default component scan path. If you define a custom serializer in a utility module or a path outside `@SpringBootApplication`'s scan, it will not be picked up automatically. Register it explicitly with `@Import(MyCustomSerializer.class)` in the test class.

**jqwik `@Property` tests count as a single test in JUnit reporting [community]** — A `@Property(tries = 1000)` method appears as one test in the JUnit report regardless of how many samples ran. If jqwik finds a failing sample, it shrinks it and reports the minimal failure with the full shrinking chain. CI dashboards will show "1 test, 1 failure" not "1000 tests, 1 failure" — which is correct but can confuse developers expecting individual sample results. Use `jqwik.reporting.usejunitplatform=true` in `junit-platform.properties` to see each sample as a separate report entry.

## Cycle 22 — 2026-05-13

### JUnit 6 — Major Version Overview and Migration Path

JUnit 6.0.0 (released September 30, 2025) is the first major version of JUnit Jupiter since 5.0. It raises the Java baseline to **Java 17** and Kotlin to **2.2**, unifies version numbering across all subprojects (Platform, Jupiter, Vintage all share one version), and removes ~30 deprecated APIs that accumulated through the JUnit 5.x lifecycle.

**Key migration checklist from JUnit 5 → 6:**

```xml
<!-- JUnit 6 unified BOM — one version for all artifacts -->
<dependencyManagement>
  <dependencies>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.junit</groupId>
      <artifactId>junit-bom</artifactId>
      <version>6.0.3</version>
      <type>pom</type>
      <scope>import</scope>
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>
</dependencyManagement>

<dependencies>
  <!-- Platform Launcher — same artifact name, new unified version -->
  <dependency>
    <groupId>org.junit.platform</groupId>
    <artifactId>junit-platform-launcher</artifactId>
    <scope>test</scope>
  </dependency>
  <!-- Jupiter engine — same group/artifact, unified version -->
  <dependency>
    <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
    <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
    <scope>test</scope>
  </dependency>
</dependencies>
```

**Removed APIs to update:**
- `ReflectionSupport.loadClass(String)` → use `Class.forName()` directly
- `BlacklistedExceptions` → use `ExclusiveResource` / custom `ExecutionCondition`
- `ClasspathScanningSupport` → use `ClassPathScanner` from `junit-platform-commons`
- `junit-platform-runner` module entirely removed → migrate to Surefire/Gradle JUnit Platform support

**[community] — The single most disruptive JUnit 6 change for large suites:** `univocity-parsers` (used for `@CsvSource` / `@CsvFileSource`) has been replaced with **FastCSV**. Projects that relied on univocity-specific quoting behavior or Windows line endings being auto-stripped may see subtle test failures after migration. Run `./mvnw test -Dtest=*CsvSource*` to surface failures before a full upgrade.

---

### JUnit 6 — Kotlin `suspend` Test Functions

JUnit 6.0 natively supports Kotlin `suspend` functions as test, `@BeforeEach`, and `@AfterEach` methods without needing a third-party bridge like `kotlinx-coroutines-test`. The coroutine is run by the JUnit Jupiter engine using a `CoroutineScope`.

```kotlin
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach
import kotlinx.coroutines.delay
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.flow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.toList
import org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat

class OrderServiceKotlinTest {

    private lateinit var service: OrderService

    @BeforeEach
    suspend fun setUp() {
        service = OrderService()
        service.initialize()   // suspend call — no runBlocking wrapper needed in JUnit 6
    }

    @Test
    suspend fun placeOrder_emitsConfirmationEvent() {
        val events: Flow<OrderEvent> = service.placeOrder(OrderRequest("SKU-42", 3))

        val collected: List<OrderEvent> = events.toList()

        assertThat(collected).hasSize(1)
            .first()
            .isInstanceOf(OrderConfirmedEvent::class.java)
    }

    @Test
    suspend fun cancelOrder_afterDelay_succeeds() {
        val orderId = service.placeOrder(OrderRequest("SKU-1", 1)).toList().first().orderId
        delay(100)   // suspend delay — works directly in JUnit 6 test body

        val cancelled = service.cancelOrder(orderId)

        assertThat(cancelled).isTrue()
    }
}
```

**[community] — JUnit 5 + `runBlocking` vs JUnit 6 native suspend:** In JUnit 5, the idiomatic pattern was to wrap coroutine tests in `runBlocking { ... }` or use `@ExtendWith(CoroutinesTestExtension::class)`. In JUnit 6, the engine manages the coroutine scope automatically. **Do not mix** `runBlocking` and native `suspend` test functions in JUnit 6 — the double-scope wrapping can cause subtle timing issues and deadlocks with `TestCoroutineDispatcher`.

---

### JUnit 6 — `ExtensionContext.Store.computeIfAbsent()`

JUnit 6 deprecates `Store.getOrComputeIfAbsent()` and replaces it with `computeIfAbsent()`, which has a cleaner non-nullable contract and better type inference.

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.*;

// JUnit 5 / early 6-migration pattern — deprecated
public class DatabaseExtension implements BeforeEachCallback, AfterEachCallback {

    private static final Namespace NAMESPACE =
        Namespace.create(DatabaseExtension.class);

    @Override
    public void beforeEach(ExtensionContext ctx) {
        // DEPRECATED in JUnit 6 — getOrComputeIfAbsent returns Object
        ctx.getStore(NAMESPACE)
            .getOrComputeIfAbsent("connection", k -> createConnection(), Connection.class);
    }

    // JUnit 6 — preferred: computeIfAbsent with typed key class
    @Override
    public void afterEach(ExtensionContext ctx) {
        Connection conn = ctx.getStore(NAMESPACE)
            .computeIfAbsent(Connection.class, k -> createConnection());
        conn.close();
    }

    private Connection createConnection() {
        return DriverManager.getConnection("jdbc:h2:mem:test");
    }
}
```

**Key difference:** `computeIfAbsent(Class<V> type, Function<Class<V>, V> factory)` uses the class object as both key and type token, eliminating the unchecked cast that `getOrComputeIfAbsent` required. For compound keys (e.g., per-test state keyed by a string), use `computeIfAbsent(Object key, Class<V> type, Function<Object, V> factory)`.

---

### JUnit 6.1 — `@DefaultLocale` and `@DefaultTimeZone`

JUnit 6.1.0-RC1 (April 2026) introduces `@DefaultLocale` and `@DefaultTimeZone` as first-class annotations for controlling the JVM-wide locale and time zone during a test or test class. Previously this required a custom `@ExtendWith` or manual `Locale.setDefault()` calls.

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.condition.EnabledOnJre;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.condition.JRE;
import org.junit.jupiter.params.ParameterizedTest;
import org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.CsvSource;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.DefaultLocale;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.DefaultTimeZone;
import java.util.Locale;
import java.time.ZonedDateTime;
import java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

// Class-level: all tests in this class run with German locale, UTC+1
@DefaultLocale("de-DE")
@DefaultTimeZone("Europe/Berlin")
class DateFormattingTest {

    @Test
    void formats_germanDate() {
        // System locale is de-DE; no manual Locale.setDefault needed
        String formatted = DateTimeFormatter
            .ofPattern("d. MMMM yyyy")
            .withLocale(Locale.getDefault())   // picks up de-DE
            .format(ZonedDateTime.now());

        assertThat(formatted).matches("\\d+\\. \\p{L}+ \\d{4}");
    }

    @ParameterizedTest
    @CsvSource(value = {
        "2026-01-15, 15. Januar 2026",
        "2026-07-04, 4. Juli 2026",
        // Lines starting with '#' are treated as comments (new in JUnit 6.0)
        "# This line is a comment and will not be parsed as a test case"
    }, commentCharacter = '#')
    void formats_knownDates(String isoDate, String expected) {
        // ...
    }
}

// Method-level override: this specific test uses en-US locale
@Test
@DefaultLocale("en-US")
void formats_englishDate() {
    // locale is en-US only within this test method
}
```

**[community] — Why `@DefaultLocale` matters for CI:** Tests that rely on `String.format()`, `NumberFormat`, `DateTimeFormatter.ofLocalizedDate()`, or any locale-sensitive operation can silently pass on a developer's MacBook (en-US) and fail in CI running on a German or Japanese server. Annotate every test that touches locale-sensitive output with `@DefaultLocale("en-US")` (or your expected locale) to make it deterministic across environments.

---

### JUnit 6.1 — `@EmptySource` Extended and WorkerThreadPool

**`@EmptySource` now supports `Iterable`, `Iterator`, and `ListIterator`** in addition to strings, arrays, and collections. This is particularly useful for testing code that accepts `Iterable<T>` parameters.

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.params.ParameterizedTest;
import org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.EmptySource;
import org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.NullSource;
import java.util.List;

class OrderProcessorTest {

    // @EmptySource now generates empty List, Set, Iterable, Iterator, ListIterator etc.
    @ParameterizedTest
    @NullSource           // null input
    @EmptySource          // empty collection/iterable/iterator
    void processItems_handlesEmptyAndNull(Iterable<String> items) {
        // Must not throw, must return empty result
        List<String> result = OrderProcessor.process(items);
        assertThat(result).isEmpty();
    }
}
```

**`WorkerThreadPoolHierarchicalTestExecutorService`** is a new alternative to the default `ForkJoinPool`-based parallel executor for JUnit 6.1. It uses a fixed-size `ThreadPoolExecutor` instead of a work-stealing pool, which gives more predictable thread counts in containers with CPU limits.

```properties
# junit-platform.properties — switch to worker thread pool for bounded parallelism
junit.jupiter.execution.parallel.enabled=true
junit.jupiter.execution.parallel.mode.default=concurrent
junit.jupiter.execution.parallel.config.strategy=custom
junit.jupiter.execution.parallel.config.custom.class=\
  org.junit.platform.engine.reporting.WorkerThreadPoolHierarchicalTestExecutorService
junit.jupiter.execution.parallel.config.fixed.parallelism=4
```

**[community]:** In Kubernetes pods with CPU limits (e.g., `requests: 100m, limits: 500m`), `ForkJoinPool.commonPool()` reads the available CPU count from `/proc/cpuinfo` (which shows the node's full CPU count, not the pod limit). This can over-provision threads. `WorkerThreadPool` with an explicit `parallelism` setting is more container-aware.

---

### Mockito 5.20 — Mocking Construction of Generic Types

Mockito 5.20 (September 2025) added the ability to mock the constructor of a **generic type** via `mockConstruction`. Previously, `Mockito.mockConstruction(MyGenericClass.class)` worked but could not verify or stub calls that depended on the type parameter — the mock had an erased type at runtime. Version 5.20 introduces automatic class detection and better generic type handling.

```java
import org.mockito.MockedConstruction;
import org.mockito.Mockito;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.*;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

class GenericRepositoryTest {

    @Test
    void service_usesRepositoryToFindItems() {
        // Mock construction of a generic repository — Mockito 5.20+
        try (MockedConstruction<ItemRepository> mocked =
                Mockito.mockConstruction(ItemRepository.class,
                    (mock, context) -> {
                        // Stub via the mock instance at construction time
                        // context.arguments() contains constructor args
                        when(mock.findAll()).thenReturn(List.of(new Item("SKU-1")));
                    })) {

            // Any new ItemRepository() inside this block returns the mock
            ItemService service = new ItemService();  // internally calls new ItemRepository<>()
            List<Item> items = service.getAllItems();

            assertThat(items).hasSize(1)
                .first().extracting(Item::getSku).isEqualTo("SKU-1");

            // Verify all constructed mocks
            assertThat(mocked.constructed()).hasSize(1);
            verify(mocked.constructed().get(0)).findAll();
        }
    }

    @Test
    void mockStatic_withAutoDetection() {
        // Mockito 5.21+: no need to pass class explicitly in some scenarios
        // Automatic detection picks up the class from the lambda's return type
        try (var mocked = Mockito.mockStatic(UuidGenerator.class)) {
            mocked.when(UuidGenerator::generate)
                  .thenReturn("fixed-uuid-for-test");

            String id = OrderService.createOrderId();

            assertThat(id).isEqualTo("fixed-uuid-for-test");
        }
    }
}
```

**[community] — `mockStatic` UUID corruption on JDK 25 (Mockito 5.22 fix):** JDK 25 internalized parts of `java.util.UUID` into a value-class-like structure as part of Valhalla groundwork. Mockito's inline mock maker intercepted `UUID.randomUUID()` static calls and left the internal state corrupted after test teardown, causing subsequent `UUID.randomUUID()` calls in the same JVM to return all-zero UUIDs. Mockito 5.22 adds a specific workaround for this. **Always upgrade to Mockito 5.22+ before testing with JDK 25.**

---

### Mockito 5.22 — Kotlin Singleton Object Mocking

Mockito 5.22 added first-class API for mocking Kotlin `object` singletons (companion objects and top-level objects) from Java and Kotlin tests.

```kotlin
import org.mockito.kotlin.mock
import org.mockito.kotlin.whenever
import org.mockito.kotlin.verify
import org.mockito.Mockito
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test
import org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat

// Kotlin singleton object under test
object PaymentGateway {
    fun charge(amount: Double, currency: String): ChargeResult = TODO()
}

class CheckoutServiceTest {

    @Test
    fun checkout_chargesCorrectAmount() {
        // Mockito 5.22 — mockSingleton mocks a Kotlin object singleton
        Mockito.mockSingleton(PaymentGateway::class.java).use { mocked ->
            whenever(PaymentGateway.charge(99.99, "USD"))
                .thenReturn(ChargeResult.SUCCESS)

            val service = CheckoutService()
            val result = service.checkout(Cart(total = 99.99, currency = "USD"))

            assertThat(result.status).isEqualTo(CheckoutStatus.COMPLETED)
            verify(mocked) { PaymentGateway.charge(99.99, "USD") }
        }
    }
}
```

**[community] — `mockSingleton` does NOT work for `companion object` methods declared as `@JvmStatic`:** `@JvmStatic` methods are compiled to actual static bytecode methods on the outer class, not on the companion object class. For these, use `Mockito.mockStatic(OuterClass::class.java)` targeting the outer class. For pure Kotlin `object` singletons without `@JvmStatic`, `mockSingleton` is the correct tool.

---

### Mockito 5.23 — `@Nullable` on `when()` Parameter

Mockito 5.23 annotates the `Mockito.when(T methodCall)` parameter as `@Nullable`. This is a type-safety improvement for Kotlin callers: previously, the `T` parameter was non-nullable by default in Kotlin's view, causing a false-positive compiler warning when stubbing methods that return nullable types.

```kotlin
// BEFORE Mockito 5.23 — Kotlin may warn about passing nullable T to non-nullable when()
val userService: UserService = mock()
whenever(userService.findById(1L))           // findById returns User? (nullable)
    .thenReturn(null)                        // Kotlin compiler may warn here

// AFTER Mockito 5.23 — @Nullable annotation silences the warning cleanly
// when() parameter is now @Nullable T, matching the nullable return type
whenever(userService.findById(1L)).thenReturn(null)   // No warning
```

**Practical impact:** This is a compile-time improvement only — no behavior change. Upgrade to 5.23 if your Kotlin codebase uses `mockito-kotlin` and you see `Non-null type used where nullable type expected` warnings on stub calls.

---

### AssertJ 3.27.7 — XXE Security Fix and `XmlStringPrettyFormatter` Deprecation

AssertJ 3.27.7 (January 2026) fixes **CVE-2026-24400**, an XML External Entity (XXE) injection vulnerability in the `isXmlEqualTo(String)` assertion. Any code passing externally-supplied XML to `assertThat(xml).isXmlEqualTo(...)` in production test infrastructure (e.g., contract tests reading fixtures from untrusted sources) was potentially vulnerable.

The `XmlStringPrettyFormatter` class (used internally to pretty-print XML in assertion failure messages) is deprecated with no public replacement — it was always an internal utility.

```java
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

// AssertJ 3.27.7 — isXmlEqualTo is XXE-safe after the CVE fix
// External entity references in the actual or expected XML are now rejected
@Test
void orderConfirmation_isValidXml() {
    String actual = orderService.generateConfirmationXml(orderId);

    // Safe: the XXE fix is transparent — usage is unchanged, injection is blocked
    assertThat(actual).isXmlEqualTo("""
        <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
        <orderConfirmation>
            <orderId>42</orderId>
            <status>CONFIRMED</status>
        </orderConfirmation>
        """);
}

// New in AssertJ 3.27.0 — CompletableFuture time-bounded assertions
@Test
void asyncOperation_completesWithinTimeout() {
    CompletableFuture<String> future = asyncService.processAsync("input");

    // Blocks for at most 2 seconds; passes if future completes with matching value
    assertThat(future)
        .isCompletedWithValueMatchingWithin(
            value -> value.startsWith("processed:"),
            Duration.ofSeconds(2));
}

@Test
void asyncOperation_failsWithCorrectException() {
    CompletableFuture<String> future = asyncService.processWithError("bad-input");

    // Blocks for at most 1 second; passes if future completes exceptionally
    assertThat(future)
        .completesExceptionallyWithin(Duration.ofSeconds(1))
        .isInstanceOf(ValidationException.class)
        .hasMessageContaining("bad-input");
}
```

**[community] — Upgrade to AssertJ 3.27.7 if you test XML:** The XXE vulnerability was present in all previous AssertJ versions. In most CI environments this is unexploitable (test fixtures are controlled), but security scanners will flag older versions. The fix is a one-line `pom.xml` version bump with no API changes.

---

### Testcontainers 2.0.5 — Spring Boot 4.1 gRPC Test Support

Spring Boot 4.1.0-RC1 (April 2026) adds `spring-boot-starter-grpc-client-test` and `spring-boot-starter-grpc-server-test` for testing gRPC services without launching a full embedded server.

```xml
<!-- Spring Boot 4.1 gRPC test starters -->
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-grpc-server-test</artifactId>
    <scope>test</scope>
</dependency>
```

```java
import org.springframework.grpc.test.annotation.GrpcTest;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import net.devh.boot.grpc.client.inject.GrpcClient;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

// @GrpcTest loads only gRPC services, interceptors, and the in-process channel
@GrpcTest
class OrderGrpcServiceTest {

    @GrpcClient("in-process")   // auto-configured in-process channel
    private OrderServiceGrpc.OrderServiceBlockingStub stub;

    @Test
    void placeOrder_returnsOrderId() {
        PlaceOrderRequest request = PlaceOrderRequest.newBuilder()
            .setSku("SKU-42")
            .setQuantity(2)
            .build();

        PlaceOrderResponse response = stub.placeOrder(request);

        assertThat(response.getOrderId()).isNotBlank();
        assertThat(response.getStatus()).isEqualTo(OrderStatus.CONFIRMED);
    }
}

// @GrpcAdvice for centralized exception handling in gRPC services (Spring Boot 4.1)
import org.springframework.grpc.server.annotation.GrpcAdvice;
import io.grpc.StatusRuntimeException;
import io.grpc.Status;

@GrpcAdvice
public class GrpcExceptionHandler {

    // Catches ValidationException thrown by any gRPC service and maps to INVALID_ARGUMENT
    @GrpcExceptionHandler(ValidationException.class)
    public StatusRuntimeException handleValidation(ValidationException ex) {
        return Status.INVALID_ARGUMENT
            .withDescription(ex.getMessage())
            .asRuntimeException();
    }
}
```

**[community] — `@GrpcTest` vs `@SpringBootTest` for gRPC:** `@GrpcTest` is analogous to `@WebMvcTest` — it loads only the service layer and gRPC infrastructure, not the full application context. This makes gRPC service tests ~5× faster than `@SpringBootTest`. Use `@GrpcTest` for unit-level gRPC service testing, `@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT)` only for full end-to-end gRPC integration tests.

---

### Spring Boot 4.0 — `RestTestClient` for MockMvc Testing

Spring Boot 4.0 introduces `RestTestClient`, a fluent HTTP test client that wraps `MockMvc` (similar to how `WebTestClient` wraps `WebClient`). It bridges the gap between `MockMvc`'s server-side test approach and `WebTestClient`'s reactive fluent API.

```java
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.web.servlet.AutoConfigureMockMvc;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.boot.test.web.client.RestTestClient;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@SpringBootTest
@AutoConfigureMockMvc
class UserControllerTest {

    @Autowired
    RestTestClient restTestClient;   // Auto-configured by @AutoConfigureMockMvc in SB 4.0+

    @Test
    void getUser_returns200() {
        restTestClient.get()
            .uri("/api/users/{id}", 1L)
            .exchange()
            .expectStatus().isOk()
            .expectBody()
                .jsonPath("$.name").isEqualTo("Alice")
                .jsonPath("$.email").isEqualTo("alice@example.com");
    }

    @Test
    void createUser_returns201_withLocation() {
        restTestClient.post()
            .uri("/api/users")
            .contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
            .bodyValue("""
                {"name": "Bob", "email": "bob@example.com"}
                """)
            .exchange()
            .expectStatus().isCreated()
            .expectHeader().value("Location", loc -> assertThat(loc).contains("/api/users/"));
    }

    @Test
    void deleteUser_returns404_afterDeletion() {
        // Create user
        String location = restTestClient.post()
            .uri("/api/users")
            .contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
            .bodyValue("{\"name\":\"Tmp\",\"email\":\"tmp@x.com\"}")
            .exchange()
            .expectStatus().isCreated()
            .returnResult(Void.class)
            .getResponseHeaders().getFirst("Location");

        // Delete
        restTestClient.delete().uri(location).exchange().expectStatus().isNoContent();

        // Verify gone
        restTestClient.get().uri(location).exchange().expectStatus().isNotFound();
    }
}
```

**`RestTestClient` vs `MockMvc` vs `WebTestClient` [community]:**
- `MockMvc` (classic): verbose, but gives direct access to `ResultActions` for complex assertions. Use when you need `andDo(print())` debugging or Spring Security's `SecurityMockMvcResultMatchers`.
- `RestTestClient` (Spring Boot 4.0+): fluent, concise, runs against `MockMvc` (no real HTTP). Best default choice for new Spring Boot 4+ projects.
- `WebTestClient`: reactive, for `@WebFlux` applications. Runs against MockWebServer or a real server.

**[community] — HtmlUnit integration change in Spring Boot 4.0:** `LocalHostWebClient` and `LocalHostWebConnectionHtmlUnitDriver` are replaced by `UriBuilderFactoryWebClient` and `UriBuilderFactoryWebConnectionHtmlUnitDriver`. If you use HtmlUnit for form-based UI testing, update your test setup class — the old classes will not compile against Spring Boot 4.0.

### Real-World Gotchas — Cycle 22 Additions [community]

**JUnit 6 `@CsvSource` comment lines break existing tests after FastCSV migration [community]** — JUnit 6 replaced univocity-parsers with FastCSV for `@CsvSource` and `@CsvFileSource`. FastCSV parses CSV slightly differently for edge cases: rows containing only whitespace are no longer silently skipped (they produce a test invocation with blank arguments), and the `emptyValue` attribute now defaults to `""` instead of `null`. If your `@CsvSource` data had blank lines between data rows as visual separators, these become test cases after migration. Use the new `commentCharacter = '#'` attribute or remove blank rows.

**Mockito `mockConstruction` scope leakage when exceptions are thrown [community]** — `Mockito.mockConstruction()` returns an `AutoCloseable` that must be closed to restore real construction behavior. If the code under test throws an exception before the `try-with-resources` block closes, the mock scope is still properly cleaned up by Java's try-with-resources guarantee. However, if you use the older non-try-with-resources pattern (`MockedConstruction mocked = mockConstruction(...); ... mocked.close()`), an exception before `mocked.close()` leaves ALL subsequent `new MyClass()` calls in the test JVM returning mocks for the rest of the test run, causing bizarre failures in unrelated tests. **Always use try-with-resources for `mockConstruction` and `mockStatic`.**

**Spring Boot `@GraphQlTest` now includes `@ControllerAdvice` beans [community]** — Spring Boot 4.0.6 changed `@GraphQlTest` to scan `@ControllerAdvice` beans by default. If you have a global exception handler annotated with `@ControllerAdvice` that handles `DataFetchingException`, it will now apply to `@GraphQlTest` tests. Tests that previously expected a raw exception to propagate may now receive a transformed error response. Review your `@GraphQlTest` assertions if you have global exception handlers.

**`AssertJ isXmlEqualTo()` fails on XML with DOCTYPE declarations after XXE fix [community]** — The CVE-2026-24400 fix disables external entity resolution AND disables DOCTYPE declarations in the XML parser used by `isXmlEqualTo()`. If your XML test fixtures contain `<!DOCTYPE ...>` declarations (even harmless ones), assertions will now throw `XMLStreamException: DOCTYPE is disallowed`. Remove DOCTYPE declarations from test XML fixtures or switch to `containsIgnoringCase` / manual string assertions.

**Kotlin `suspend` test methods in JUnit 6 do not inherit `@Timeout` from enclosing class [community]** — `@Timeout` applied at class level is NOT automatically inherited by `suspend` test methods in JUnit 6.0.0. This is a known limitation of the coroutine integration — the timeout is applied by the JUnit engine as a thread interrupt, but `suspend` functions may be executing on a coroutine dispatcher that does not respect thread interrupts in the same way. Apply `@Timeout` explicitly on each `suspend` test method that needs a time boundary, or use `withTimeout { ... }` from `kotlinx-coroutines-test` inside the test body.

**Testcontainers 2.0 module renaming breaks `@ServiceConnection` auto-detection [community]** — Testcontainers 2.0 moved container classes to module-specific packages. For example, `org.testcontainers.containers.PostgreSQLContainer` moved to `org.testcontainers.postgresql.PostgreSQLContainer`. Spring Boot's `@ServiceConnection` auto-detection relies on the fully-qualified class name to determine which `ConnectionDetails` to create. If you are on Testcontainers 2.0 but Spring Boot < 3.4, `@ServiceConnection` may fail to recognize the renamed class. Upgrade Spring Boot to 3.4+ (which includes updated `@ServiceConnection` mappings for Testcontainers 2.0 package names) before upgrading Testcontainers.

### JUnit 6 — `CancellationToken` and `LauncherExecutionRequest`

JUnit 6.0.0 introduced a proper cancellation mechanism for long-running test suites. A `CancellationToken` can be passed to the `Launcher` via `LauncherExecutionRequest`, allowing programmatic or user-triggered cancellation mid-run. The `--fail-fast` flag on `ConsoleLauncher` now uses this mechanism internally.

```java
import org.junit.platform.launcher.Launcher;
import org.junit.platform.launcher.LauncherDiscoveryRequest;
import org.junit.platform.launcher.LauncherExecutionRequest;
import org.junit.platform.launcher.core.LauncherDiscoveryRequestBuilder;
import org.junit.platform.launcher.core.LauncherFactory;
import org.junit.platform.engine.CancellationToken;
import org.junit.platform.engine.discovery.DiscoverySelectors;

public class ProgrammaticTestRunner {

    public static void runWithCancellation(String packageName) {
        // Build a discovery + execution request in one step
        LauncherDiscoveryRequest discoveryRequest =
            LauncherDiscoveryRequestBuilder.request()
                .selectors(DiscoverySelectors.selectPackage(packageName))
                .build();

        // Create a CancellationToken — call cancel() from another thread to abort
        CancellationToken token = CancellationToken.create();

        // Schedule cancellation after 30 seconds (e.g., for CI timeout enforcement)
        new Thread(() -> {
            try { Thread.sleep(30_000); } catch (InterruptedException ignored) {}
            token.cancel();
        }).start();

        LauncherExecutionRequest executionRequest =
            LauncherExecutionRequest.builder()
                .launcherDiscoveryRequest(discoveryRequest)
                .cancellationToken(token)
                .build();

        try (Launcher launcher = LauncherFactory.create()) {
            launcher.execute(executionRequest);
        }
    }
}
```

**[community] — `--fail-fast` now uses `CancellationToken` under the hood:** Prior to JUnit 6, `--fail-fast` was implemented as an `ExecutionCondition` that checked a shared flag, meaning already-started test methods could still complete before the suite stopped. In JUnit 6, the `CancellationToken`-based implementation signals cancellation at the engine level, which allows `HierarchicalTestEngine` to stop starting new test nodes more aggressively. Tests that are mid-execution still run to completion, but no new test containers are opened. This means `--fail-fast` is noticeably faster at halting large parallel suites.

---

### JUnit 6 — `@TestMethodOrder` Inherited by `@Nested` Classes

Before JUnit 6, `@TestMethodOrder` on a parent class did not propagate to `@Nested` inner classes — each nested class needed its own annotation. JUnit 6.0.0 changes this: `@TestMethodOrder` (and `@TestClassOrder`) annotations are now inherited recursively by all `@Nested` inner classes.

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.MethodOrderer;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Nested;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Order;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.TestMethodOrder;

@TestMethodOrder(MethodOrderer.OrderAnnotation.class)   // Applied to ALL nested classes now
class PaymentFlowTest {

    @Test @Order(1) void initializePaymentGateway() { /* runs first */ }
    @Test @Order(2) void authorizePayment() { /* runs second */ }

    @Nested
    // In JUnit 5, this nested class would use default ordering (ignored the parent's @TestMethodOrder)
    // In JUnit 6, it INHERITS MethodOrderer.OrderAnnotation — no need to re-annotate
    class RefundFlow {
        @Test @Order(1) void initiateRefund() { /* runs first in this nested class */ }
        @Test @Order(2) void confirmRefund() { /* runs second */ }
    }

    @Nested
    @TestMethodOrder(MethodOrderer.Random.class)   // Override: this specific nested class uses random
    class EdgeCaseFlow {
        @Test void missingPaymentMethod() {}
        @Test void expiredCard() {}
    }
}
```

**Use `MethodOrderer.Default` to opt out of inherited ordering in a specific nested class.** The new `MethodOrderer.Default` sentinel explicitly reverts to JUnit's default (deterministic but non-alphabetic) ordering, which is useful when a parent forces an ordering that does not apply to one nested group.

**[community] — Hidden risk: nested class ordering changed in JUnit 6.0.0:** The order of `@Nested` inner classes within an enclosing class changed from alphabetic (JUnit 5 default) to a "deterministic but intentionally nonobvious" order. If you had tests that relied on nested classes running in alphabetical order (e.g., "AccountCreation" before "AccountDeletion"), those assumptions break silently after migration. Explicitly annotate the enclosing class with `@TestClassOrder(ClassOrderer.OrderAnnotation.class)` and add `@Order` to each nested class to guarantee a specific sequence.

---

### JUnit 6 — `ExtensionContext.Store.computeIfAbsent()` vs `getOrComputeIfAbsent()`

JUnit 6 deprecates all `getOrComputeIfAbsent(…)` variants in `ExtensionContext.Store` and `NamespacedHierarchicalStore` in favor of the new `computeIfAbsent(…)` methods, which eliminate the unchecked cast required by the old API.

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.BeforeEachCallback;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtensionContext;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtensionContext.Namespace;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtensionContext.Store;

public class DatabaseConnectionExtension implements BeforeEachCallback {

    private static final Namespace NS =
        Namespace.create(DatabaseConnectionExtension.class);

    @Override
    public void beforeEach(ExtensionContext context) {
        Store store = context.getStore(NS);

        // OLD (JUnit 5 / deprecated in JUnit 6) — requires unchecked cast
        // DatabaseConnection conn = (DatabaseConnection)
        //     store.getOrComputeIfAbsent("conn", key -> new DatabaseConnection());

        // NEW (JUnit 6) — type-safe, no cast needed
        DatabaseConnection conn = store.computeIfAbsent(
            "conn",
            key -> new DatabaseConnection(),
            DatabaseConnection.class   // explicit type token — eliminates raw cast
        );

        conn.open();
    }
}

// DatabaseConnection must implement AutoCloseable to be auto-closed by JUnit
record DatabaseConnection(String url) implements AutoCloseable {
    DatabaseConnection() { this("jdbc:h2:mem:test"); }
    void open() { /* open connection */ }
    @Override public void close() { /* close connection */ }
}
```

**Why the change matters:** The old `getOrComputeIfAbsent(key, creator)` returned `Object`, requiring a cast that suppressed compiler warnings. The new overload `computeIfAbsent(key, creator, type)` uses the `Class<V>` token to return a properly typed `V`. This eliminates `@SuppressWarnings("unchecked")` from extension code and catches type mismatches at compile time.

### Mockito 5.21 — Auto-Detection in `mockStatic` and `mockConstruction`

Mockito 5.21 (December 2025) added automatic class detection for `mockStatic` and `mockConstruction` when called from a lambda or method reference that already implies the type. Previously, you had to pass the class explicitly every time.

```java
import org.mockito.MockedConstruction;
import org.mockito.MockedStatic;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.mockConstruction;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.mockStatic;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.when;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

class UuidServiceTest {

    @Test
    void generateOrderId_usesUuidRandomUUID() {
        // Mockito 5.21+: class can be auto-detected from mock setup lambda
        // when the compiler can infer the type from context
        try (MockedStatic<UUID> uuidMock = mockStatic(UUID.class)) {
            UUID fixed = UUID.fromString("00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001");
            uuidMock.when(UUID::randomUUID).thenReturn(fixed);

            String orderId = new OrderService().generateOrderId();

            assertThat(orderId).isEqualTo("ORDER-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001");
        }
    }

    @Test
    void createRepository_mocksConstructionWithGenericType() {
        // Mockito 5.20+: can mock construction of generic types
        // Previously, Mockito could not reliably mock new Repository<String>() — now it can
        try (MockedConstruction<Repository> mock =
                 mockConstruction(Repository.class, (repo, ctx) -> {
                     when(repo.findById(1L)).thenReturn(Optional.of("cached-value"));
                 })) {

            String result = new UserService().loadUser(1L);

            assertThat(result).isEqualTo("cached-value");
            assertThat(mock.constructed()).hasSize(1);
        }
    }
}
```

**[community] — Mockito 5.21 completed Future / CompletionStage default stubbing:** `ReturnsEmptyValues` (the default answer for unstubbed calls) now returns a **completed** `CompletableFuture<Void>` for methods returning `Future`, `CompletableFuture`, or `CompletionStage`, rather than `null`. Tests that previously asserted `null` on unstubbed async methods will now receive a completed future. Update assertions from `assertThat(result).isNull()` to `assertThat(result).isCompletedWithValue(null)` if you relied on the old behavior.

---

### Mockito 5.22 — Kotlin `object` Singleton Mocking

Mockito 5.22 (February 2026) introduced first-class support for mocking Kotlin `object` singletons. Previously, mocking a Kotlin `object` required `mockk` or a custom `MockMaker` configuration.

```kotlin
import org.mockito.kotlin.any
import org.mockito.MockedStatic
import static org.mockito.Mockito.mockStatic
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat

// Kotlin object singleton — compiled to a Java class with a private constructor
object PaymentGateway {
    fun charge(amount: java.math.BigDecimal): PaymentResult =
        PaymentResult.success(amount)
}

class CheckoutServiceTest {

    @Test
    fun checkout_usesGatewayCharge() {
        // Mockito 5.22+: mock the Kotlin object directly via mockStatic on its class
        mockStatic(PaymentGateway::class.java).use { mocked ->
            mocked.`when`<PaymentResult> { PaymentGateway.charge(any()) }
                  .thenReturn(PaymentResult.success(java.math.BigDecimal("50.00")))

            val result = CheckoutService().checkout(Order(total = java.math.BigDecimal("50.00")))

            assertThat(result.status).isEqualTo("PAID")
        }
    }
}
```

**[community] — Why Kotlin `object` mocking was hard before 5.22:** Kotlin `object` declarations compile to a Java class with a `INSTANCE` field and a private constructor. The byte-buddy mock maker could not intercept calls to `INSTANCE.method()` because the JVM inlines calls to `INSTANCE` fields when optimization is enabled. Mockito 5.22 added a JVM agent-level patch specifically for the Kotlin `INSTANCE` field access pattern, so `mockStatic` now works reliably without `mockk`. However, this requires the inline mock maker (byte-buddy agent on the JVM command line) — the subclass mock maker cannot mock Kotlin `object` types.

---

### Mockito 5.23 — `@Nullable` on `Mockito.when()` Parameters

Mockito 5.23 (March 2026) annotated the parameter of `Mockito.when(T methodCall)` with `@Nullable`. This is a **source-level change only** — it allows null-safe static analysis tools (NullAway, IntelliJ's null inference, Kotlin's strict null checks) to accept `when(methodCallThatMightReturnNull)` without a false-positive warning.

```java
import static org.mockito.Mockito.when;
import static org.mockito.ArgumentMatchers.anyString;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import java.util.Optional;

class UserServiceTest {

    // BEFORE 5.23: NullAway flagged this with "passing @Nullable to @NonNull parameter"
    // because userRepository.findByEmail() is annotated @Nullable in some codebases.
    // AFTER 5.23: @Nullable on Mockito.when()'s parameter silences the false positive.

    @Test
    void findUser_returnsEmpty_whenNotFound() {
        when(userRepository.findByEmail(anyString())).thenReturn(null);

        Optional<User> result = userService.findByEmail("nobody@example.com");

        assertThat(result).isEmpty();
    }

    @Test
    void findUser_returnsUser_whenFound() {
        User alice = new User(1L, "alice@example.com");
        when(userRepository.findByEmail("alice@example.com")).thenReturn(alice);

        Optional<User> result = userService.findByEmail("alice@example.com");

        assertThat(result).hasValue(alice);
    }
}
```
