## Cycle 29 — 2026-05-14

### 1. JUnit 5 `@ParameterizedTest` with `@MethodSource` — Table-Driven Tests for Domain Logic [official]

`@MethodSource` feeds a stream of `Arguments` to a parameterized test, enabling table-driven test cases where each row carries input, expected output, and an optional display name. Unlike `@CsvSource` (strings only), `@MethodSource` can supply fully constructed domain objects, avoiding error-prone string parsing.

**When to use:** Domain validation logic (price tiers, discount rules, state machine transitions) where you have ≥4 input/output combinations and want failure messages to identify the failing case by row.
**When NOT to use:** When there are fewer than 3 cases — a standard `@Test` is clearer. Avoid when the argument factory is expensive to compute or has side effects (factories run once at test plan creation).

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.params.ParameterizedTest;
import org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.Arguments;
import org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.MethodSource;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.util.stream.Stream;

class DiscountEngineTest {

    @ParameterizedTest(name = "{0} units at ${1} → discount {2}%")
    @MethodSource("discountScenarios")
    void appliesCorrectDiscountTier(int quantity, BigDecimal unitPrice, int expectedDiscountPct) {
        BigDecimal discounted = DiscountEngine.apply(quantity, unitPrice);
        BigDecimal expected = unitPrice.multiply(
            BigDecimal.ONE.subtract(new BigDecimal(expectedDiscountPct).movePointLeft(2))
        );
        assertThat(discounted).isEqualByComparingTo(expected);
    }

    static Stream<Arguments> discountScenarios() {
        return Stream.of(
            Arguments.of(1,   new BigDecimal("10.00"), 0),   // no discount
            Arguments.of(10,  new BigDecimal("10.00"), 5),   // 5% at 10+ units
            Arguments.of(50,  new BigDecimal("10.00"), 10),  // 10% at 50+ units
            Arguments.of(100, new BigDecimal("10.00"), 15),  // 15% at 100+ units
            Arguments.of(0,   new BigDecimal("10.00"), 0)    // edge: zero quantity
        );
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `@MethodSource` arguments are evaluated once at plan time, so they cannot depend on state initialized in `@BeforeEach`. Alternative: `@CsvSource` for primitive-only tables; `@EnumSource` for enum constants; `@FieldSource` (JUnit 5.11+) to reference a `static` field directly without a factory method.

[official]

---

### 2. JUnit 5 `@ParameterizedClass` — Shared Test Template for Multiple Configurations [official]

`@ParameterizedClass` (JUnit 5.13+) applies a full test class to multiple configurations. Unlike `@ParameterizedTest` (one method), the entire class — including `@BeforeEach`, `@Nested` classes, and multiple `@Test` methods — runs once per set of parameters.

**When to use:** Integration tests for a domain component that must behave identically across multiple backends (e.g., `InMemoryOrderRepository` vs `JpaOrderRepository`); or the same service tested with production config vs relaxed config.
**When NOT to use:** When the parameter set requires a different Spring context per variant — `@ParameterizedClass` does not integrate with Spring's context infrastructure. Use separate `@SpringBootTest` subclasses instead.

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.params.ParameterizedClass;
import org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.MethodSource;

import java.util.stream.Stream;

@ParameterizedClass
@MethodSource("repositoryVariants")
class OrderRepositoryContractTest {

    final OrderRepository repository;

    OrderRepositoryContractTest(OrderRepository repository) {
        this.repository = repository;
    }

    static Stream<OrderRepository> repositoryVariants() {
        return Stream.of(
            new InMemoryOrderRepository(),
            new SqliteOrderRepository(":memory:")
        );
    }

    @Test
    void saveAndFindById_roundTrips() {
        Order order = new Order("ORD-001", "CUST-1", List.of(new LineItem("SKU-A", 2)));
        repository.save(order);

        Optional<Order> found = repository.findById("ORD-001");
        assertThat(found).isPresent();
        assertThat(found.get().customerId()).isEqualTo("CUST-1");
    }

    @Test
    void findById_returnsEmpty_whenMissing() {
        assertThat(repository.findById("MISSING")).isEmpty();
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** Produces N × (number of test methods) test cases in reports — can be noisy for large classes. Named display via `@ParameterizedClass(name = "{0}")` helps readability. Alternative: abstract base test class with concrete subclasses that supply the repository variant (classic "contract test" pattern; less automation but more compatible with all test runners).

[official]

---

### 3. Mockito Strict Stubbing with `@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)` [official]

Mockito's strict stubbing mode (default when using `MockitoExtension`) fails tests that configure `when(...)` stubs that are never invoked during the test. This catches test rot: stubs set up for behavior that no longer exists, silently "passing" while testing nothing.

**When to use:** All new tests using `@Mock`. Strict stubbing surfaces dead stubs (refactored methods) and unnecessary stubs (wrong assumptions about call flow) as immediate failures rather than silent green tests.
**When NOT to use:** When you use `@MockitoSession` with `Strictness.LENIENT` for integration-style tests where some stubs may be conditional. Lenient stubbing is appropriate in shared `@BeforeEach` setup methods that configure stubs for the common case when not every test exercises every stub.

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;
import org.mockito.InjectMocks;
import org.mockito.Mock;
import org.mockito.junit.jupiter.MockitoExtension;

@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)  // strict stubbing enabled by default
class OrderFulfillmentServiceTest {

    @Mock
    InventoryService inventoryService;

    @Mock
    PaymentGateway paymentGateway;

    @InjectMocks
    OrderFulfillmentService service;

    @Test
    void fulfilsOrderWhenInventoryAvailable() {
        when(inventoryService.isAvailable("SKU-1", 2)).thenReturn(true);
        // paymentGateway NOT stubbed — if code calls it without a stub, Mockito throws
        // if paymentGateway were stubbed but never called, strict mode fails the test

        FulfilmentResult result = service.fulfil(new Order("ORD-1", "SKU-1", 2));

        assertThat(result.status()).isEqualTo(FulfilmentStatus.DISPATCHED);
        verify(inventoryService).isAvailable("SKU-1", 2);
    }

    @Test
    void sharedBaselineSetupUsingLenient() {
        // Use lenient() when a stub is shared across tests but not all tests invoke it
        lenient().when(inventoryService.isAvailable(anyString(), anyInt())).thenReturn(true);
        // lenient() suppresses UnnecessaryStubbingException for this stub
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** Strict mode requires per-test stub granularity — move common stubs to `lenient()` wrappers or declare them in `@BeforeEach` with `lenient()` to avoid `UnnecessaryStubbingException` for stubs that only some tests use. Alternative: `Mockito.mock(X.class, withSettings().strictness(Strictness.LENIENT))` for individual lenient mocks.

[official]

---

### 4. `@DataJpaTest` with `@AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = NONE)` for Real Database Tests [official]

`@DataJpaTest` by default replaces the datasource with an in-memory H2 database. For repositories using database-specific features (Postgres JSON operators, window functions, custom enums), you must opt out of replacement and supply a Testcontainers datasource via `@ServiceConnection`.

**When to use:** Repositories that use native queries, vendor-specific column types (`JSONB`, `UUID`, `ENUM`), or window functions that H2 does not support. Also required when validating Flyway/Liquibase schema migrations against the real database engine.
**When NOT to use:** Pure JPQL/Spring Data derived-query repositories with no vendor-specific SQL — H2 is faster and requires no Docker. Adding `replace = NONE` makes the test slower and Docker-dependent.

```java
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.jdbc.AutoConfigureTestDatabase;
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.orm.jpa.DataJpaTest;
import org.springframework.boot.testcontainers.service.connection.ServiceConnection;
import org.testcontainers.containers.PostgreSQLContainer;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Container;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Testcontainers;

@DataJpaTest
@AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = AutoConfigureTestDatabase.Replace.NONE)
@Testcontainers
class ProductSearchRepositoryTest {

    @Container
    @ServiceConnection
    static final PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres =
        new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine");

    @Autowired
    ProductSearchRepository repository;

    @Test
    void findByJsonbTagContains_usesPostgresJsonbOperator() {
        repository.save(new Product("P1", "{\"tags\":[\"spring\",\"java\"]}"));
        repository.save(new Product("P2", "{\"tags\":[\"kotlin\"]}"));

        List<Product> results = repository.findByTagContaining("spring");

        assertThat(results).hasSize(1);
        assertThat(results.get(0).productId()).isEqualTo("P1");
    }

    @Test
    void countByStatus_returnsCorrectAggregate() {
        repository.saveAll(List.of(
            new Product("P3", Status.ACTIVE),
            new Product("P4", Status.INACTIVE),
            new Product("P5", Status.ACTIVE)
        ));
        assertThat(repository.countByStatus(Status.ACTIVE)).isEqualTo(2);
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `replace = NONE` requires Docker and makes the test ~5–10s slower due to container startup. Share the container as a `@Container static` field and enable Testcontainers reuse (`withReuse(true)`) to amortize startup across the test suite. Alternative: abstract the vendor-specific query behind a `Specification` and test it with H2; test the native query separately in an integration test module.

[official]

---

### 5. Spring Boot `MockMvcTester` — AssertJ-Fluent MVC Integration Tests [official]

`MockMvcTester` (Spring Boot 3.4+) is an AssertJ-native wrapper for `MockMvc`. Instead of chaining `andExpect(...)` matchers, you get a `MvcTestResult` that integrates directly with AssertJ's `.assertThat()`, enabling soft assertions, `extracting`, and `satisfies` patterns on HTTP responses.

**When to use:** `@WebMvcTest` integration tests where you want AssertJ's expressive failure messages instead of `MockMvc`'s Hamcrest matchers. Particularly powerful for asserting JSON body shape alongside status and headers in a single fluent chain.
**When NOT to use:** When you have a large existing `MockMvc` test suite — migration is optional, not urgent. Also avoid in `@SpringBootTest` with `webEnvironment=RANDOM_PORT` where `RestTestClient` (Boot 4.0+) or `WebTestClient` is the correct tool.

```java
import org.springframework.test.web.servlet.assertj.MockMvcTester;
import org.springframework.test.web.servlet.assertj.MvcTestResult;

@WebMvcTest(OrderController.class)
class OrderControllerTest {

    @Autowired
    MockMvcTester mvc;

    @MockitoBean
    OrderService orderService;

    @Test
    void getOrder_returns200WithBody() {
        when(orderService.findById("ORD-1"))
            .thenReturn(new OrderDto("ORD-1", "alice@example.com", new BigDecimal("49.99")));

        MvcTestResult result = mvc.get().uri("/orders/{id}", "ORD-1").exchange();

        assertThat(result)
            .hasStatusOk()
            .hasContentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
            .bodyJson()
            .extractingPath("$.order_id").isEqualTo("ORD-1");
    }

    @Test
    void getOrder_returns404WhenNotFound() {
        when(orderService.findById("MISSING")).thenThrow(new OrderNotFoundException("MISSING"));

        assertThat(mvc.get().uri("/orders/{id}", "MISSING").exchange())
            .hasStatus(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND)
            .bodyJson()
            .extractingPath("$.error").asString().contains("MISSING");
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `MockMvcTester` requires Spring Boot 3.4+. The `bodyJson()` fluent API does not support every JSONPath operation that `JsonPathResultMatchers` does. Alternative: classic `MockMvc` with `andExpect(status().isOk())` and `andExpect(jsonPath("$.order_id").value("ORD-1"))` — mature, widely documented, and compatible with older Spring Boot versions.

[official]

---

### 6. Testcontainers `@ServiceConnection` — Zero-Config Container Wiring [official]

`@ServiceConnection` (Spring Boot 3.1+) auto-configures `spring.datasource.url`, `spring.redis.host`, `spring.kafka.bootstrap-servers`, and similar properties directly from the container's exposed ports. No `@DynamicPropertySource` boilerplate required.

**When to use:** Any `@SpringBootTest` or slice test needing a real database, cache, or message broker. Works with Testcontainers' auto-discovery of container types via the `ConnectionDetails` SPI.
**When NOT to use:** When the container type is not in the supported `@ServiceConnection` registry (custom images, non-standard ports). Fall back to `@DynamicPropertySource` with `registry.add("spring.datasource.url", container::getJdbcUrl)` for those cases.

```java
import org.springframework.boot.testcontainers.service.connection.ServiceConnection;
import org.testcontainers.containers.PostgreSQLContainer;
import org.testcontainers.containers.KafkaContainer;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Container;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Testcontainers;
import org.testcontainers.utility.DockerImageName;

@SpringBootTest
@Testcontainers
class OrderEventIntegrationTest {

    @Container
    @ServiceConnection  // auto-configures spring.datasource.* from container ports
    static final PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres =
        new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine");

    @Container
    @ServiceConnection  // auto-configures spring.kafka.bootstrap-servers
    static final KafkaContainer kafka =
        new KafkaContainer(DockerImageName.parse("confluentinc/cp-kafka:7.6.1"));

    @Autowired
    OrderService orderService;

    @Autowired
    KafkaConsumerTestHelper consumerHelper;

    @Test
    void placingOrderPersistsAndPublishesEvent() throws Exception {
        String orderId = orderService.place(new PlaceOrderCommand("CUST-1", "SKU-A", 3));

        assertThat(orderService.findById(orderId)).isPresent();

        await().atMost(Duration.ofSeconds(10))
               .untilAsserted(() ->
                   assertThat(consumerHelper.received("orders.placed"))
                       .extracting("orderId").contains(orderId));
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `@ServiceConnection` requires Spring Boot 3.1+ and `spring-boot-testcontainers` on the classpath. Declare containers as `static` fields to share them across all test methods in the class. For context caching across multiple test classes, move containers to a shared abstract base class. Alternative: `@DynamicPropertySource` for explicit control over property names and fallback to non-Testcontainers sources.

[official]

---

### 7. AssertJ `usingRecursiveComparison()` with Custom Comparators [official]

`usingRecursiveComparison()` compares two objects field-by-field without requiring `equals()` to be overridden. It traverses the entire object graph, supports `ignoringFields()` for volatile timestamps, and allows per-type comparators for tricky types like `BigDecimal` (which has scale-sensitive `equals()`).

**When to use:** Asserting domain objects returned from services or repositories where implementing `equals()` adds boilerplate. Especially useful for JPA entities where `equals()` is based on identity (ID) and does not capture field-level correctness.
**When NOT to use:** Do NOT use on objects containing `Optional<T>` fields without unwrapping them first — recursive comparison calls `Optional.equals()` which uses identity on the wrapped type. Also avoid on objects with circular references. For simple records with auto-generated `equals()`, plain `isEqualTo()` is cleaner.

```java
import org.assertj.core.api.recursive.comparison.RecursiveComparisonConfiguration;

@Test
void savedOrderMatchesOriginalIgnoringAuditFields() {
    Order original = new Order("ORD-1", "CUST-1",
        List.of(new LineItem("SKU-A", 2, new BigDecimal("9.99"))));

    Order saved = orderRepository.save(original);
    Order retrieved = orderRepository.findById(saved.id()).orElseThrow();

    assertThat(retrieved)
        .usingRecursiveComparison()
        .ignoringFields("createdAt", "updatedAt", "version")
        .ignoringFieldsMatchingRegexes(".*\\.id")
        .isEqualTo(original);
}

@Test
void pricingMatchesIgnoringBigDecimalScale() {
    assertThat(actualPricing)
        .usingRecursiveComparison(
            RecursiveComparisonConfiguration.builder()
                .withComparatorForType(BigDecimal::compareTo, BigDecimal.class)
                .build()
        )
        .isEqualTo(expectedPricing);
}
```

**Tradeoff:** Recursive comparison traverses private fields via reflection — this can surface Hibernate proxy state or internal framework fields you didn't intend to compare. Use `ignoringFields()` or `ignoringFieldsOfTypes()` aggressively to limit scope. Alternative: `isEqualToComparingOnlyGivenFields()` for comparing only a named subset of fields when the object has many noise fields.

[official]

---

### 8. `@MockitoBean` — Replacing Spring Beans With Mockito Mocks [official]

`@MockitoBean` (Spring Boot 3.4+, successor to `@MockBean`) registers a Mockito mock as a Spring bean and resets it between tests via the new Bean Override mechanism. It is the forward-compatible replacement in the migration path to Spring Boot 4.0 (where `@MockBean` is removed).

**When to use:** `@WebMvcTest` and `@SpringBootTest` tests that need to stub out a service dependency without loading the real implementation. Auto-resets between tests to prevent stub state from leaking.
**When NOT to use:** Avoid declaring `@MockitoBean` on fields with types that differ from the registered bean definition type — this prevents context cache reuse. Also do not share `@MockitoBean` declarations across unrelated test classes in a base class unless ALL those classes mock the same set of beans.

```java
import org.springframework.test.context.bean.override.mockito.MockitoBean;

@WebMvcTest(ProductController.class)
class ProductControllerTest {

    @Autowired
    MockMvcTester mvc;

    @MockitoBean  // Spring Boot 3.4+; replaces @MockBean
    ProductService productService;

    @Test
    void listProducts_delegatesToService() {
        when(productService.findAll()).thenReturn(List.of(
            new ProductDto("P1", "Widget", new BigDecimal("9.99")),
            new ProductDto("P2", "Gadget", new BigDecimal("24.99"))
        ));

        assertThat(mvc.get().uri("/products").exchange())
            .hasStatusOk()
            .bodyJson()
            .extractingPath("$").asArray().hasSize(2);

        verify(productService).findAll();
    }

    @Test
    void createProduct_returns201WithLocation() {
        when(productService.create(any()))
            .thenReturn(new ProductDto("P3", "Donut", new BigDecimal("1.99")));

        assertThat(mvc.post().uri("/products")
            .contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
            .content("{\"name\":\"Donut\",\"price\":1.99}")
            .exchange())
            .hasStatus(HttpStatus.CREATED)
            .bodyJson()
            .extractingPath("$.id").isEqualTo("P3");
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** Each unique `@MockitoBean` type is part of the Spring context cache key. A base class with `@MockitoBean` fields that subclasses extend with additional `@MockitoBean` fields creates a combinatorial explosion of context cache entries. Alternative: `@MockitoSpyBean` when you need the real implementation with selected method overrides; `@TestBean` for hand-crafted test doubles that don't use Mockito.

[official]

---

### 9. JUnit 5 `@AutoClose` — Automatic Resource Cleanup Without `@AfterEach` [official]

`@AutoClose` (JUnit 5.11+) annotates an `AutoCloseable` field in a test class. JUnit calls `close()` on it after each test (or after the test class for `static` fields with `@TestInstance(PER_CLASS)`), eliminating `@AfterEach` boilerplate for resources like WireMock servers or custom stubs.

**When to use:** Test classes that manage their own `AutoCloseable` resources (custom WireMock instances, database connections, temporary file managers) and need deterministic cleanup. Pairs well with `@RegisterExtension` for programmatic setup.
**When NOT to use:** For Testcontainers — use `@Container` lifecycle management which provides better reuse semantics. Avoid for resources shared across all tests where `@AfterAll` with a `static` field is the correct pattern.

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.AutoClose;
import com.github.tomakehurst.wiremock.WireMockServer;
import com.github.tomakehurst.wiremock.core.WireMockConfiguration;

class ExternalApiClientTest {

    @AutoClose  // JUnit 5.11+: calls server.stop() after each test method
    WireMockServer server =
        new WireMockServer(WireMockConfiguration.wireMockConfig().dynamicPort());

    @AutoClose
    TempFileManager tempFiles = new TempFileManager();

    @Test
    void fetchesPriceFromExternalApi() {
        server.start();
        server.stubFor(WireMock.get("/prices/SKU-1")
            .willReturn(WireMock.okJson("{\"price\": 9.99}")));

        ExternalApiClient client =
            new ExternalApiClient("http://localhost:" + server.port());
        BigDecimal price = client.getPrice("SKU-1");

        assertThat(price).isEqualByComparingTo("9.99");
        // server.stop() called automatically — no @AfterEach needed
    }

    @Test
    void writesResponseToCacheFile() throws IOException {
        Path cacheFile = tempFiles.createTemp("response-", ".json");
        // test body ...
        assertThat(cacheFile).exists();
        // tempFiles.close() called automatically — temp files cleaned up
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `@AutoClose` uses instance lifecycle by default (`@TestInstance(PER_METHOD)`) — the resource is freshly created per test. For `@TestInstance(PER_CLASS)`, `@AutoClose` closes after all tests run, so tests in the class share one instance. Alternative: `@RegisterExtension` with a custom `AfterEachCallback`; `@AfterEach` for explicit, visible teardown.

[official]

---

### 10. Testcontainers `withReuse(true)` — Container Reuse Across Test Suite Runs [community]

`withReuse(true)` keeps a container alive between Maven Surefire forks and even across separate JVM invocations (within a Docker session), dramatically reducing CI startup time for large suites with expensive containers.

**When to use:** Slow containers (Postgres, Kafka, Elasticsearch) in large suites where each CI run incurs 30–60 seconds of container startup. `withReuse(true)` can reduce integration test suites from 3 minutes to 30 seconds.
**When NOT to use:** When tests rely on pristine database state between runs — reused containers retain data. Requires `testcontainers.reuse.enable=true` in `~/.testcontainers.properties` on each machine; if the flag is absent, the option is silently ignored and a fresh container starts anyway.

```java
public final class SharedContainers {

    public static final PostgreSQLContainer<?> POSTGRES =
        new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine")
            .withReuse(true)
            .withLabel("reuse.UUID", "myproject-postgres");  // prevents cross-project reuse

    static {
        POSTGRES.start();  // first call starts container; subsequent calls no-op
    }
}

// In any @DataJpaTest that needs it:
@DataJpaTest
@AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = AutoConfigureTestDatabase.Replace.NONE)
class OrderRepositoryTest {

    @DynamicPropertySource
    static void configurePostgres(DynamicPropertyRegistry registry) {
        registry.add("spring.datasource.url",      SharedContainers.POSTGRES::getJdbcUrl);
        registry.add("spring.datasource.username", SharedContainers.POSTGRES::getUsername);
        registry.add("spring.datasource.password", SharedContainers.POSTGRES::getPassword);
    }

    @BeforeEach
    void cleanDatabase(@Autowired JdbcTemplate jdbc) {
        // MANDATORY cleanup when reusing containers — tests must not depend on prior state
        jdbc.execute("TRUNCATE TABLE orders, line_items CASCADE");
    }

    @Test
    void savesAndRetrievesOrder() {
        // ... test body — Postgres is already running from static initializer
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** Reuse requires explicit cleanup in every `@BeforeEach` (TRUNCATE or `@Sql`). Without cleanup, tests become order-dependent and flake intermittently based on execution order. Alternative: `@DynamicPropertySource` with a fresh container per class — simpler, no cleanup needed, but slower in large suites.

[community]

---

### 11. Mockito `ArgumentCaptor` — Verifying Complex Arguments Passed to Mocks [official]

`ArgumentCaptor<T>` captures the actual argument passed to a mock, enabling assertions on computed fields (generated IDs, timestamps, mapped DTOs) that cannot be expressed with `eq(...)` matchers because the value is only known at test execution time.

**When to use:** When you need to assert on domain object arguments (e.g., the `OrderPlacedEvent` passed to `eventPublisher.publish(event)`) whose `equals()` is identity-based. Also useful for verifying that transformations produce correct embedded values.
**When NOT to use:** For simple scalar arguments (`String`, `int`) — `eq("expected-value")` is more readable. Avoid `captor.capture()` inside `when(...)` stubbing — it records null instead of the invocation argument (see gotcha below).

```java
import org.mockito.ArgumentCaptor;
import org.mockito.Captor;

@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class OrderEventPublishTest {

    @Mock
    EventPublisher publisher;

    @Captor
    ArgumentCaptor<OrderPlacedEvent> eventCaptor;

    @InjectMocks
    OrderService orderService;

    @Test
    void placeOrder_publishesEventWithCorrectFields() {
        orderService.place(new PlaceOrderCommand("CUST-1", "SKU-A", 3));

        verify(publisher).publish(eventCaptor.capture());  // MUST be in verify(), not when()
        OrderPlacedEvent event = eventCaptor.getValue();

        assertThat(event.customerId()).isEqualTo("CUST-1");
        assertThat(event.lineItems()).hasSize(1);
        assertThat(event.lineItems().get(0).sku()).isEqualTo("SKU-A");
        assertThat(event.occurredAt()).isCloseToUtcNow(byLessThan(1, ChronoUnit.SECONDS));
    }

    @Test
    void placeMultipleOrders_capturesAllPublishedEvents() {
        orderService.place(new PlaceOrderCommand("CUST-1", "SKU-A", 1));
        orderService.place(new PlaceOrderCommand("CUST-2", "SKU-B", 2));

        verify(publisher, times(2)).publish(eventCaptor.capture());
        List<OrderPlacedEvent> events = eventCaptor.getAllValues();  // use getAllValues() for N>1

        assertThat(events)
            .extracting(OrderPlacedEvent::customerId)
            .containsExactly("CUST-1", "CUST-2");
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** When using `times(N)`, call `getAllValues()` not `getValue()` — `getValue()` returns only the last captured argument. Captors used with `@InjectMocks` can behave unexpectedly when multiple arguments of the same type exist in a method — use specific `ArgumentMatchers` (e.g., `argThat(e -> e.customerId().equals("CUST-1"))`) to distinguish them. Alternative: `ArgumentMatchers.argThat(predicate)` for complex matching inline in `verify()`.

[official]

---

### 12. AssertJ `CompletableFuture` Assertions [official]

AssertJ 3.27+ provides native `CompletableFuture` assertions: `succeedsWithin(Duration)`, `failsWithin(Duration)`, and `isCompletedWithValueMatching(predicate)`. These eliminate try/catch boilerplate for `future.get()` and assert completion state declaratively.

**When to use:** Services that return `CompletableFuture<T>` where you want to assert both the outcome and that completion happens within a time budget. Also for asserting that a future fails with a specific exception type and message.
**When NOT to use:** When the future represents a long-running background operation — use Awaitility's `untilAsserted` for polling. `failsWithin` and `succeedsWithin` block the test thread; keep timeout values realistic to avoid flaky CI failures on loaded agents.

```java
import java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture;
import java.time.Duration;

class AsyncPricingServiceTest {

    AsyncPricingService service = new AsyncPricingService(ForkJoinPool.commonPool());

    @Test
    void priceComputedSuccessfully() {
        CompletableFuture<BigDecimal> future = service.computePrice("SKU-A", 10);

        assertThat(future)
            .succeedsWithin(Duration.ofSeconds(2))
            .asInstanceOf(InstanceOfAssertFactories.BIG_DECIMAL)
            .isGreaterThan(BigDecimal.ZERO);
    }

    @Test
    void unknownSkuCompletesExceptionally() {
        CompletableFuture<BigDecimal> future = service.computePrice("UNKNOWN", 1);

        assertThat(future)
            .failsWithin(Duration.ofSeconds(2))
            .withThrowableOfType(ExecutionException.class)
            .havingCause()
            .isInstanceOf(SkuNotFoundException.class)
            .withMessage("SKU not found: UNKNOWN");
    }

    @Test
    void allPricesArePositive() {
        CompletableFuture<List<BigDecimal>> future =
            service.computePricesForAll(List.of("SKU-A", "SKU-B", "SKU-C"));

        assertThat(future)
            .isCompletedWithValueMatching(
                prices -> prices.stream().allMatch(p -> p.compareTo(BigDecimal.ZERO) > 0),
                "all prices must be positive"
            );
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `succeedsWithin` blocks the test thread for up to the full timeout on slow agents. For production-grade async tests with variable latency, prefer Awaitility with `atMost` + `pollInterval` which retries the assertion rather than blocking. Alternative: `future.get(2, TimeUnit.SECONDS)` in a try/catch — familiar but produces less readable failure messages.

[official]

---

### 13. JUnit 5 `@TempDir` with `CleanupMode` — Temporary Directory Lifecycle Control [official]

`@TempDir` injects a fresh `Path` per test and deletes it automatically. `CleanupMode.ON_SUCCESS` (JUnit 5.9+) preserves the directory on test failure, enabling forensic inspection of generated files without manual cleanup code.

**When to use:** Tests that write files, generate artifacts, or verify file-based persistence. `ON_SUCCESS` mode is especially valuable during local development: failed test output remains on disk for debugging, while passing tests stay clean.
**When NOT to use:** Avoid for tests where the directory must outlive the test (use `static` `@TempDir` for class scope). Do not use for very high-frequency test methods where creating a temp directory per test is a measurable bottleneck.

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.CleanupMode;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

class ReportGeneratorTest {

    @TempDir(cleanup = CleanupMode.ON_SUCCESS)  // keep on failure for debugging
    Path outputDir;

    @Test
    void generatesCsvReport() throws IOException {
        ReportGenerator generator = new ReportGenerator();
        List<SalesRecord> records = List.of(
            new SalesRecord("2026-01-01", "SKU-A", 100, new BigDecimal("9.99")),
            new SalesRecord("2026-01-02", "SKU-B", 50, new BigDecimal("19.99"))
        );

        Path output = outputDir.resolve("sales-report.csv");
        generator.writeCsv(records, output);

        List<String> lines = Files.readAllLines(output);
        assertThat(lines).hasSize(3);  // header + 2 data rows
        assertThat(lines.get(0)).isEqualTo("date,sku,quantity,price");
        assertThat(lines.get(1)).startsWith("2026-01-01");
        // If this assertion fails, outputDir is NOT deleted — inspect sales-report.csv directly
    }

    @TempDir  // default: CleanupMode.ALWAYS — deleted whether test passes or fails
    static Path sharedDir;  // static: one directory shared across the entire test class

    @Test
    void secondTestCanWriteToSharedDir() throws IOException {
        Files.writeString(sharedDir.resolve("config.json"), "{\"enabled\": true}");
        assertThat(sharedDir.resolve("config.json")).exists();
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `CleanupMode.NEVER` leaves directories indefinitely — useful in local development but will fill up CI agent disk over time. Prefer `ON_SUCCESS` in CI. The default `CleanupMode.ALWAYS` is safe for CI. Alternative: `Files.createTempDirectory("prefix")` with manual `@AfterEach` cleanup — more control but more boilerplate.

[official]

---

### 14. `@SpringBootTest` `@ActiveProfiles` + `@TestPropertySource` — Per-Test Environment Configuration [official]

`@ActiveProfiles("test")` activates a profile-specific `application-test.properties`, while `@TestPropertySource` inlines specific overrides on the test class. Together they give each test class precise control over the environment without polluting main application configuration.

**When to use:** Tests that need to disable scheduled jobs, reduce connection pool sizes, point to a different service endpoint, or override feature flags. Profile + property source combination is more explicit than relying on autoconfiguration defaults.
**When NOT to use:** When `@ServiceConnection` or `@DynamicPropertySource` is sufficient — mixing all three mechanisms reduces clarity. Avoid creating more than 2–3 test profiles; a proliferation of profiles signals an over-complicated configuration strategy.

```java
import org.springframework.test.context.ActiveProfiles;
import org.springframework.test.context.TestPropertySource;

@SpringBootTest
@ActiveProfiles("test")                          // activates application-test.properties
@TestPropertySource(properties = {
    "spring.task.scheduling.pool.size=1",        // minimize threads
    "app.feature.email-notifications=false",     // disable side effects
    "spring.jpa.show-sql=true"                   // surface SQL during debugging
})
class OrderServiceIntegrationTest {

    @Autowired
    OrderService orderService;

    @Test
    void placeOrder_persists() {
        // application-test.properties: spring.datasource.url=jdbc:h2:mem:testdb
        // @TestPropertySource: show-sql=true only for this test class
        Order placed = orderService.place(new PlaceOrderCommand("CUST-1", "SKU-A", 2));
        assertThat(placed.id()).isNotNull();
    }
}

// src/test/resources/application-test.properties
// spring.datasource.url=jdbc:h2:mem:testdb;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1
// spring.datasource.driver-class-name=org.h2.Driver
// spring.datasource.username=sa
// spring.datasource.password=
// spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=create-drop
// spring.mail.host=localhost
// spring.mail.port=3025
```

**Tradeoff:** `@TestPropertySource` properties take the highest precedence, silently overriding profile-specific files — intentional but can confuse when debugging property resolution order. For large override sets, prefer `@TestPropertySource(locations = "classpath:test-override.properties")`. Alternative: `@SpringBootTest(properties = {"key=value"})` for one or two inline overrides; less discoverable for large property sets.

[official]

---

### 15. `@WebFluxTest` with `WebTestClient` — Reactive Controller Testing [official]

`@WebFluxTest` loads only the reactive web layer (controllers, filters, `WebExceptionHandler`) without starting a full server. `WebTestClient` provides a fluent DSL to assert on the reactive stream of responses, including `StepVerifier`-style element-by-element assertions for streaming endpoints.

**When to use:** Spring WebFlux controllers returning `Mono<T>` or `Flux<T>`. Faster and lighter than `@SpringBootTest` for testing reactive controller logic, serialization, and error handling in isolation.
**When NOT to use:** For Spring MVC (servlet-based) controllers — use `@WebMvcTest` with `MockMvcTester`. Also not suitable when the controller has complex `@RequestScope` or `@SessionScope` bean dependencies that `@WebFluxTest` does not load.

```java
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.web.reactive.WebFluxTest;
import org.springframework.test.web.reactive.server.WebTestClient;

@WebFluxTest(ProductController.class)
class ProductControllerWebFluxTest {

    @Autowired
    WebTestClient webClient;

    @MockitoBean
    ProductService productService;

    @Test
    void listProducts_returnsAllProducts() {
        when(productService.findAll()).thenReturn(Flux.just(
            new ProductDto("P1", "Widget", new BigDecimal("9.99")),
            new ProductDto("P2", "Gadget", new BigDecimal("24.99"))
        ));

        webClient.get().uri("/products")
            .accept(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
            .exchange()
            .expectStatus().isOk()
            .expectBodyList(ProductDto.class)
            .hasSize(2)
            .contains(new ProductDto("P1", "Widget", new BigDecimal("9.99")));
    }

    @Test
    void streamProducts_returnsServerSentEvents() {
        when(productService.stream()).thenReturn(
            Flux.interval(Duration.ofMillis(100))
                .take(3)
                .map(i -> new ProductDto("P" + i, "Product " + i, BigDecimal.TEN))
        );

        webClient.get().uri("/products/stream")
            .accept(MediaType.TEXT_EVENT_STREAM)
            .exchange()
            .expectStatus().isOk()
            .returnResult(ProductDto.class)
            .getResponseBody()
            .as(StepVerifier::create)
            .expectNextCount(3)
            .verifyComplete();
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `@WebFluxTest` only loads the reactive web layer — services must be mocked with `@MockitoBean`. If your controller uses `@Transactional` or JPA (which require a full Spring context), use `@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT)` with a real `WebTestClient`. Alternative: `MockMvcTester` for Spring MVC; `@SpringBootTest` + `WebTestClient` for full-stack reactive tests.

[official]

---

### Community Gotchas — Cycle 29 [community]

**`@MockitoBean` declared with a type that differs from the actual registered bean definition type forces a Spring context reload, silently degrading CI speed [community]** — Spring's context cache key includes every `@MockitoBean` type. If `OrderService` is registered as `OrderServiceImpl` in the application context but you declare `@MockitoBean OrderService orderService` (the interface), the mock type does not match the bean definition type, invalidating the cached context. The test still passes but every test run recreates the context. WHY: The Bean Override mechanism replaces beans by resolved type; a type mismatch means the override cannot be applied to the existing cache entry. Fix: declare `@MockitoBean OrderServiceImpl orderService` (the concrete type) to match the registered bean, or ensure your `@Service` class is declared against the interface type.

**`@ParameterizedTest @MethodSource` argument providers execute at plan-discovery time before `@BeforeAll` and Spring context initialization — any factory that reads `@Value`-injected fields or queries a database will see null [community]** — JUnit 5 builds the complete test plan (including collecting all `@MethodSource` arguments) during the discovery phase, before any lifecycle callbacks run. A `@MethodSource` factory that calls a Spring-managed service or reads an `@Autowired` field will receive `null` because the Spring context has not yet started. WHY: Test plan discovery is intentionally separated from test execution in the JUnit Platform architecture. Fix: `@MethodSource` factories must use only static domain data; if runtime data is needed, use `@ParameterizedTest` with a custom `ArgumentsProvider` that delays data loading to execution time.

**`@TempDir` cleanup runs inside JUnit's `AfterEach` callback — if the JVM is killed with `SIGKILL` (OOM, CI hard timeout), temp directories accumulate on the agent's disk indefinitely [community]** — JUnit's temp directory cleanup is an `AfterEachCallback` that walks the file tree and deletes entries. Unlike OS-managed resources, this callback does not run if the JVM is terminated abruptly. On busy CI agents with many test forks, temp directories from killed JVMs can consume gigabytes over weeks. WHY: Java's `ShutdownHook` mechanism only runs on graceful JVM exit (`SIGTERM`, `System.exit()`); `SIGKILL` (OOM killer, Docker kill) bypasses all shutdown hooks and extension callbacks. Fix: add a CI-level cron job that prunes `java.io.tmpdir` directories older than 2 hours; or configure the OS temp directory to a CI workspace path that is cleaned on workspace teardown.

**`MockMvcTester.bodyJson()` throws `IllegalStateException` (not an `AssertionError`) if the response Content-Type is not `application/json` — error message mentions "body" not "content type", making the failure misleading [community]** — When a controller returns `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457 error format) or `text/plain`, calling `.bodyJson()` on the `MvcTestResult` throws an `IllegalStateException` with a message like "No response body available" or "Content-Type is not JSON", but the exception is not an AssertJ assertion failure — it propagates as a test error, not a test failure. The failure report shows an exception trace rather than an assertion diff. WHY: `MockMvcTester` checks Content-Type eagerly inside `bodyJson()` and throws immediately rather than recording a soft failure. Fix: assert `.hasContentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)` as a hard assertion first, then call `.bodyJson()`; or use `.body().asString()` for non-JSON response bodies.

**`ArgumentCaptor.capture()` called inside `when(...)` stubbing records `null` instead of the invocation argument — the captor is not triggered until the real call happens in `verify()` [community]** — A developer writes `when(service.process(captor.capture())).thenReturn(result)` expecting to capture the argument during stubbing. But `capture()` inside `when(...)` registers the matcher at stub-setup time when no real invocation exists — it captures the default `null`. The `verify(service).process(captor.capture())` form is the only correct placement because `verify()` replays recorded invocations. WHY: `captor.capture()` is an `ArgumentMatcher` that executes during mock invocation matching. Inside `when(...)`, no real method has been called yet, so the captured value is always the type's default (`null` for objects, `0` for primitives). This is a Mockito API design quirk that has no compile-time warning.

**`withReuse(true)` on a Testcontainers container is silently ignored if `testcontainers.reuse.enable=true` is not present in `~/.testcontainers.properties` — a new container starts instead, and no warning is emitted [community]** — Teams that adopt container reuse often forget to update CI agent configuration. Without the flag in `~/.testcontainers.properties`, the `.withReuse(true)` call does nothing — Testcontainers starts a fresh container as if `withReuse(false)`. The behavior is identical to a non-reuse run except the team assumes reuse is active. The CI speedup is never realized. WHY: Testcontainers requires explicit opt-in per machine to prevent accidental reuse across projects sharing the same Docker daemon. Fix: document the required `~/.testcontainers.properties` entry in your project's README and onboarding guide; add a `@BeforeAll` assertion: `Assumptions.assumeTrue(Boolean.parseBoolean(System.getProperty("testcontainers.reuse.enable", "false")), "Container reuse not enabled")` to skip the reuse test in CI if the flag is absent.
