## Cycle 30 — 2026-05-14

### 1. Spring Boot `@MockitoSpyBean` — Partial Mocking of Real Spring Beans [official]

`@MockitoSpyBean` (Spring Framework 6.2+, replacing `@SpyBean`) wraps the real Spring bean in a Mockito spy, allowing you to stub specific methods while all other invocations call the real implementation. It is the lightweight alternative to a full mock when you need to test one edge case in a complex bean without reimplementing the entire rest of its behaviour.

**When to use:** Verifying that a real service calls an internal helper method correctly, or stubbing only the external-network portion of an otherwise real service. Use when most methods should run real code and only one or two need to return controlled values.
**When NOT to use:** Avoid for beans that have expensive `@PostConstruct` or stateful side effects — the spy wraps a fully-initialised real bean, so those side effects still execute. Do not use `@MockitoSpyBean` when a full `@MockitoBean` makes the test simpler and more explicit. Alternative: constructor injection + manual `Mockito.spy(real)` in a pure unit test.

```java
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.test.context.bean.override.mockito.MockitoSpyBean;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.mockito.BDDMockito.willReturn;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.verify;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@SpringBootTest
class AuditServiceIntegrationTest {

    @Autowired
    OrderService orderService;           // real bean under test

    @MockitoSpyBean
    AuditLogger auditLogger;             // real bean, but we can verify calls

    @MockitoSpyBean
    PricingService pricingService;       // stub only the remote-call method

    @Test
    void placeOrder_auditsThePlacedOrder() {
        // Stub just the remote pricing lookup; everything else runs for real
        willReturn(new BigDecimal("49.99"))
            .given(pricingService).fetchCurrentPrice("SKU-X");

        Order placed = orderService.place(new PlaceOrderCommand("CUST-1", "SKU-X", 2));

        assertThat(placed.totalAmount()).isEqualByComparingTo("99.98");
        // Verify the real auditLogger.log() was called with the placed order id
        verify(auditLogger).log("ORDER_PLACED", placed.id());
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** Spring still creates, initialises, and injects the full real bean — startup cost is unchanged. If `AuditLogger` has a slow `@PostConstruct` or opens a connection, the test pays that cost. Unlike `@MockitoBean`, the spy shares the application context's singleton — resetting it between tests requires `@DirtiesContext` or `Mockito.reset(spy)` in `@AfterEach`.

[official]

---

### 2. Spring Boot `MockMvcTester` with AssertJ — Fluent Web Layer Tests [official]

`MockMvcTester` (Spring Boot 4.0 / Spring Framework 6.2) replaces `MockMvc` with an AssertJ-native API. Test results are AssertJ assertion objects, so you get diff-aware failure messages, chained assertions, and no checked-exception boilerplate from `andExpect`.

**When to use:** All new `@WebMvcTest` tests in Spring Boot 4.x projects. Particularly valuable when asserting multiple response fields — chaining replaces verbose `andExpect` calls.
**When NOT to use:** Legacy projects on Spring Boot 3.x that do not yet have `MockMvcTester`; stick to `MockMvc` + `ResultActions` to avoid a partial migration. Also avoid mixing `MockMvcTester` and `MockMvc` in the same test class — the APIs overlap but produce different assertion styles.

```java
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.web.servlet.WebMvcTest;
import org.springframework.test.web.servlet.assertj.MockMvcTester;
import org.springframework.test.context.bean.override.mockito.MockitoBean;
import org.springframework.http.MediaType;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.mockito.BDDMockito.given;

@WebMvcTest(ProductController.class)
class ProductControllerTest {

    @Autowired
    MockMvcTester mvc;

    @MockitoBean
    ProductService productService;

    @Test
    void getProduct_returnsJsonBody() {
        given(productService.findById("P-1"))
            .willReturn(new ProductDto("P-1", "Widget", new BigDecimal("9.99")));

        assertThat(mvc.get().uri("/products/P-1")
                       .accept(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON))
            .hasStatusOk()
            .hasContentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
            .bodyJson()
                .extractingPath("$.id").isEqualTo("P-1");
    }

    @Test
    void getProduct_returns404_whenMissing() {
        given(productService.findById("MISSING"))
            .willThrow(new ProductNotFoundException("MISSING"));

        assertThat(mvc.get().uri("/products/MISSING"))
            .hasStatus(404)
            .bodyJson()
                .extractingPath("$.title").asString()
                .contains("not found");
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `bodyJson()` requires `Content-Type: application/json`; for `application/problem+json` responses, assert `hasContentTypeCompatibleWith(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)` or use `.body().asString()`. The AssertJ method chaining works as soft assertions only inside `satisfies()` — top-level chained assertions still fail-fast at the first failure. Alternative: `MockMvc` + `andExpect(jsonPath(...))` for Spring Boot 3.x; `WebTestClient` for reactive stacks.

[official]

---

### 3. Spring Boot `RestTestClient` — Fluent HTTP Testing Against a Running Server [official]

`RestTestClient` (Spring Boot 4.0+, module `spring-boot-resttestclient`) is a dedicated HTTP client for integration tests that start a real server (`RANDOM_PORT` or `DEFINED_PORT`). It provides a DSL similar to `WebTestClient` but does not require a reactive stack — it works with both servlet and reactive applications.

**When to use:** Full-stack integration tests where you need to exercise the complete HTTP stack including embedded Tomcat, security filters, and the real bean wiring. Prefer over `TestRestTemplate` when you want a fluent assertion API.
**When NOT to use:** Web-layer-only tests where `MockMvcTester` or `WebTestClient` (mock mode) is sufficient and faster. Avoid when the test must assert on raw response bytes or requires streaming — `WebTestClient` has stronger reactive stream support.

```java
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest.WebEnvironment;
import org.springframework.boot.test.web.client.RestTestClient;
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.web.servlet.AutoConfigureMockMvc;
import org.springframework.test.context.bean.override.mockito.MockitoBean;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.mockito.BDDMockito.given;

@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = WebEnvironment.RANDOM_PORT)
@AutoConfigureRestTestClient
class OrderApiIntegrationTest {

    @Autowired
    RestTestClient restClient;

    @MockitoBean
    InventoryService inventoryService;

    @Test
    void placeOrder_returns201_withLocationHeader() {
        given(inventoryService.reserve("SKU-A", 2)).willReturn(true);

        restClient.post()
            .uri("/orders")
            .contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
            .bodyValue("""
                { "customerId": "CUST-1", "sku": "SKU-A", "quantity": 2 }
                """)
            .exchange()
            .expectStatus().isCreated()
            .expectHeader().valueMatches("Location", "/orders/[\\w-]+");
    }

    @Test
    void placeOrder_returns409_whenOutOfStock() {
        given(inventoryService.reserve("SKU-B", 99)).willReturn(false);

        restClient.post()
            .uri("/orders")
            .bodyValue("""
                { "customerId": "CUST-2", "sku": "SKU-B", "quantity": 99 }
                """)
            .exchange()
            .expectStatus().isEqualTo(409);
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** Starting a full server per test class is slower than `@WebMvcTest`. Use `@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT)` at the class level and share the context across test methods to minimise startup overhead. `RestTestClient` is auto-configured and injected — do not manually construct it. Alternative: `TestRestTemplate` (Spring Boot 3.x); `WebTestClient` with `bindToServer()` for reactive servers.

[official]

---

### 4. Spring Boot `@JsonTest` with `JacksonTester` — Isolated JSON Serialisation Slice [official]

`@JsonTest` loads only the Jackson (or Gson/JSONB) auto-configuration, giving a lightweight context for testing serialisation and deserialisation logic. `JacksonTester<T>` wraps `ObjectMapper` with assertion helpers — no need to bootstrap a full `@SpringBootTest` context.

**When to use:** Verifying custom Jackson serialisers, deserialiser edge cases, `@JsonProperty` mappings, `@JsonTypeInfo` discriminators, and `null`/`Optional` handling. Fast to run — the slice context starts in milliseconds.
**When NOT to use:** When the DTO's JSON shape is only meaningful in the context of a controller (validation, content-type negotiation) — use `@WebMvcTest` to test the full round-trip. Also avoid for simple DTOs with no custom mapping — trust Jackson defaults and only add `@JsonTest` when serialisation failures have occurred.

```java
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.json.JsonTest;
import org.springframework.boot.test.json.JacksonTester;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import java.time.Instant;
import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.util.List;

@JsonTest
class OrderEventJsonTest {

    @Autowired
    JacksonTester<OrderEvent> json;

    @Test
    void serialize_producesExpectedShape() throws Exception {
        OrderEvent event = new OrderEvent(
            "ORD-001",
            OrderStatus.CONFIRMED,
            Instant.parse("2026-05-14T10:00:00Z"),
            List.of(new LineItem("SKU-A", 2, new BigDecimal("9.99")))
        );

        assertThat(json.write(event))
            .hasJsonPathStringValue("$.orderId", "ORD-001")
            .hasJsonPathStringValue("$.status", "CONFIRMED")
            .hasJsonPathStringValue("$.confirmedAt", "2026-05-14T10:00:00Z")
            .hasJsonPathArrayValue("$.items")
            .hasSize(1);
    }

    @Test
    void deserialize_handlesIso8601Timestamp() throws Exception {
        String payload = """
            {
              "orderId": "ORD-002",
              "status": "PENDING",
              "confirmedAt": "2026-05-14T09:30:00Z",
              "items": []
            }
            """;

        OrderEvent event = json.parseObject(payload);
        assertThat(event.orderId()).isEqualTo("ORD-002");
        assertThat(event.confirmedAt()).isEqualTo(Instant.parse("2026-05-14T09:30:00Z"));
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `@JsonTest` does NOT load Spring MVC or `@Valid` bean validation — deserialisaton constraints are not triggered. Use `@WebMvcTest` when you need to test that a controller rejects malformed JSON with a `400`. Alternative: direct `ObjectMapper` instantiation with `new ObjectMapper()` — faster but skips Spring Boot's auto-configured `ObjectMapper` customisers, which can silently differ from production behaviour.

[official]

---

### 5. Spring Boot `@RestClientTest` — HTTP Client Slice for Outbound Calls [official]

`@RestClientTest` loads only the auto-configuration needed for testing `RestClient`, `RestTemplate`, and `WebClient` beans declared in a specific component class. It provides a `MockRestServiceServer` to stub outbound HTTP calls without starting a real server.

**When to use:** Testing service classes that call external APIs — price feeds, payment gateways, notification services. Isolates the outbound HTTP client layer without a full Spring context.
**When NOT to use:** When the component under test also depends on JPA repositories or other non-HTTP beans — those are not loaded by `@RestClientTest` and will fail with a `NoSuchBeanDefinitionException`. Add a `@TestConfiguration` with `@Bean` stubs or switch to `@SpringBootTest`.

```java
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.web.client.RestClientTest;
import org.springframework.test.web.client.MockRestServiceServer;
import org.springframework.http.MediaType;
import org.springframework.http.HttpMethod;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.springframework.test.web.client.match.MockRestRequestMatchers.*;
import static org.springframework.test.web.client.response.MockRestResponseCreators.*;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThatThrownBy;

@RestClientTest(ExchangeRateClient.class)
class ExchangeRateClientTest {

    @Autowired
    ExchangeRateClient client;

    @Autowired
    MockRestServiceServer server;

    @Test
    void fetchRate_parsesResponseCorrectly() {
        server.expect(requestTo("https://api.exchange.example/rates/USD/EUR"))
              .andExpect(method(HttpMethod.GET))
              .andRespond(withSuccess("""
                  { "base": "USD", "target": "EUR", "rate": 0.9234 }
                  """, MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON));

        ExchangeRate rate = client.fetchRate("USD", "EUR");

        assertThat(rate.base()).isEqualTo("USD");
        assertThat(rate.rate()).isEqualByComparingTo("0.9234");
        server.verify();
    }

    @Test
    void fetchRate_throwsOnServerError() {
        server.expect(requestTo("https://api.exchange.example/rates/USD/GBP"))
              .andRespond(withServerError());

        assertThatThrownBy(() -> client.fetchRate("USD", "GBP"))
            .isInstanceOf(ExchangeRateException.class);
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `MockRestServiceServer` verifies call count and order automatically — calling `server.verify()` at the end of each test confirms all expected requests were made. If your `RestClient` uses request interceptors or observability wiring, confirm they are loaded by the slice or add them via `@AutoConfigureWith`. Alternative: WireMock for more complex request matching, scenario simulation, or multi-request chains; `MockRestServiceServer` is simpler but less expressive.

[official]

---

### 6. Testcontainers `@ImportTestcontainers` Interface — Shared Container Declarations [official]

`@ImportTestcontainers` lets you declare container fields in a plain Java interface and import that interface into multiple test configuration classes, achieving container sharing without inheritance. Combined with `@ServiceConnection`, connection details are auto-wired with no `@DynamicPropertySource` boilerplate.

**When to use:** Large projects where dozens of test classes share the same PostgreSQL or Redis container. Centralise container declarations in one interface; all test classes import it and share the container instance (since interface fields are implicitly `static`).
**When NOT to use:** When containers must have different configurations per test class (different database names, different seeds). Also avoid when the team is not yet on Spring Boot 3.1+ — `@ServiceConnection` does not exist in earlier versions.

```java
// TestContainers.java — shared container declarations in an interface
import org.testcontainers.containers.PostgreSQLContainer;
import org.testcontainers.containers.GenericContainer;
import org.springframework.boot.testcontainers.service.connection.ServiceConnection;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Container;

interface TestContainerFixtures {

    @Container
    @ServiceConnection
    PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres = new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine");

    @Container
    @ServiceConnection(name = "redis")
    GenericContainer<?> redis = new GenericContainer<>("redis:7-alpine")
        .withExposedPorts(6379);
}

// SharedContainerConfiguration.java
import org.springframework.boot.testcontainers.context.ImportTestcontainers;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.TestConfiguration;

@TestConfiguration(proxyBeanMethods = false)
@ImportTestcontainers(TestContainerFixtures.class)
class SharedContainerConfiguration {}

// OrderServiceIntegrationTest.java
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Import;

@SpringBootTest
@Import(SharedContainerConfiguration.class)
class OrderServiceIntegrationTest {

    @Autowired
    OrderService orderService;

    @Test
    void persistsOrderToPostgresAndCachesInRedis() {
        Order order = orderService.place(new PlaceOrderCommand("CUST-1", "SKU-A", 1));
        assertThat(order.id()).isNotNull();
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** Container fields in interfaces are implicitly `public static final`. If `PostgreSQLContainer` is declared without `static`, Testcontainers starts a new container per test class. Always verify that the declaration is `static` (the interface field default) when using `@ImportTestcontainers`. Alternative: abstract base class with `@Testcontainers` and `@Container static` fields — identical effect but forces inheritance; the interface approach is more composable.

[official]

---

### 7. Spring Boot `@AutoConfigureObservability` — Metrics and Tracing Assertions in Integration Tests [official]

`@AutoConfigureObservability` (Spring Boot 3.x+) adds an in-memory `SimpleMeterRegistry` and a no-op `Tracer` to the test context, allowing assertions on metric counters, timers, and gauges generated by the code under test — without a full Micrometer backend.

**When to use:** Verifying that a service correctly increments `orders.placed` counter, records `payment.latency` timer, or exposes a `queue.depth` gauge. Catches regressions where business events stop emitting metrics before they reach production dashboards.
**When NOT to use:** For performance benchmarks or distribution summaries that require many samples — `SimpleMeterRegistry` accumulates all samples in memory. Do not use in `@WebMvcTest` slices unless you explicitly add `@AutoConfigureObservability`; it is not enabled by default in slices.

```java
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.actuate.observability.AutoConfigureObservability;
import io.micrometer.core.instrument.MeterRegistry;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@SpringBootTest
@AutoConfigureObservability
class OrderMetricsTest {

    @Autowired
    OrderService orderService;

    @Autowired
    MeterRegistry meterRegistry;

    @Test
    void placeOrder_incrementsOrdersPlacedCounter() {
        double before = meterRegistry
            .counter("orders.placed", "status", "success")
            .count();

        orderService.place(new PlaceOrderCommand("CUST-1", "SKU-A", 1));

        double after = meterRegistry
            .counter("orders.placed", "status", "success")
            .count();

        assertThat(after).isEqualTo(before + 1.0);
    }

    @Test
    void placeOrder_recordsProcessingTimeTimer() {
        orderService.place(new PlaceOrderCommand("CUST-2", "SKU-B", 2));

        assertThat(meterRegistry.find("orders.processing.time").timer())
            .isNotNull()
            .satisfies(timer -> assertThat(timer.count()).isGreaterThanOrEqualTo(1L));
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `SimpleMeterRegistry` does not emit metrics to any backend — it is purely in-memory. Assertions on tag values (`"status", "success"`) are exact string matches; typos in tag names produce counter-not-found `null` silently. Add a `assertThat(meterRegistry.find("orders.placed").counter()).isNotNull()` guard before reading `.count()`. Alternative: `TestMeterRegistry` if using Micrometer 1.13+ test module; WireMock-style metric stub if testing the metrics infrastructure rather than the counter values.

[official]

---

### 8. AssertJ `usingRecursiveComparison()` — Deep Object Equality Without `equals()` [official]

`usingRecursiveComparison()` compares two object graphs field-by-field, ignoring `equals()` / `hashCode()` implementations. It produces a detailed failure message listing the exact fields that differ — far more useful than `assertEquals(expected, actual)` when the mismatch is deep inside a nested object.

**When to use:** Asserting on returned domain objects, JPA entities, or DTOs where implementing `equals()` is undesirable (e.g., entity identity vs value equality). Especially powerful for partially populated objects using `.ignoringFields("id", "createdAt")`.
**When NOT to use:** When `equals()` is the contract being tested (e.g., value object correctness). Also avoid on cyclic object graphs — recursive comparison will stack-overflow unless cycles are detected (AssertJ handles simple cycles but deep circular references can cause issues).

```java
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.time.Instant;
import java.util.List;

class OrderMapperTest {

    OrderMapper mapper = new OrderMapper();

    @Test
    void toDto_mapsAllFields() {
        Order order = Order.builder()
            .id("ORD-001")
            .customerId("CUST-1")
            .status(OrderStatus.CONFIRMED)
            .items(List.of(new LineItem("SKU-A", 2, new BigDecimal("9.99"))))
            .placedAt(Instant.parse("2026-05-14T10:00:00Z"))
            .build();

        OrderDto dto = mapper.toDto(order);

        assertThat(dto)
            .usingRecursiveComparison()
            .ignoringFields("_links")
            .isEqualTo(new OrderDto(
                "ORD-001", "CUST-1", "CONFIRMED",
                List.of(new LineItemDto("SKU-A", 2, new BigDecimal("9.99"))),
                "2026-05-14T10:00:00Z"
            ));
    }

    @Test
    void toDto_ignoresAuditFields_whenAssertingBusinessData() {
        Order order = somePersistedOrder();

        assertThat(mapper.toDto(order))
            .usingRecursiveComparison()
            .ignoringFieldsMatchingRegexes(".*At", ".*By", "version")
            .isEqualTo(expectedBusinessDataDto());
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** Recursive comparison traverses ALL fields including private ones via reflection — this can expose fields you do not intend to compare. Use `.ignoringFields(...)` or `.ignoringFieldsMatchingRegexes(...)` liberally. For collections of objects, chain `.usingRecursiveFieldByFieldElementComparator()` on list assertions to apply the same deep comparison element-by-element. Alternative: `@EqualsAndHashCode` (Lombok) for POJOs; custom `equals()` for value objects — both enable direct `isEqualTo()` with no special config.

[official]

---

### 9. AssertJ `SoftAssertionsExtension` — Collect All Failures Before Reporting [official]

`SoftAssertionsExtension` (AssertJ + JUnit 5) collects assertion failures and reports all of them at the end of the test, instead of stopping at the first failure. This is essential for diagnostic-heavy tests (serialisation, form validation, complex mapping) where you want to see all mismatches at once.

**When to use:** Tests that validate multiple fields of a response object, a parsed document, or a migrated database row. Each assertion failure gives a separate message — one test run reveals all problems rather than requiring repeated runs.
**When NOT to use:** Avoid for tests where later assertions depend on earlier ones being true (e.g., `assertThat(result).isNotNull()` must pass before `assertThat(result.id()).isEqualTo("X")`). Soft assertions do not stop execution — a `NullPointerException` on `result.id()` will obscure the actual issue.

```java
import org.assertj.core.api.SoftAssertions;
import org.assertj.core.api.junit.jupiter.SoftAssertionsExtension;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.time.LocalDate;

@ExtendWith(SoftAssertionsExtension.class)
class InvoiceValidationTest {

    InvoiceParser parser = new InvoiceParser();

    @Test
    void parsedInvoice_hasAllRequiredFields(SoftAssertions softly) {
        Invoice invoice = parser.parse(SAMPLE_INVOICE_XML);

        softly.assertThat(invoice.invoiceNumber()).isEqualTo("INV-2026-001");
        softly.assertThat(invoice.issueDate()).isEqualTo(LocalDate.of(2026, 5, 14));
        softly.assertThat(invoice.dueDate()).isAfter(invoice.issueDate());
        softly.assertThat(invoice.totalAmount()).isEqualByComparingTo("1234.56");
        softly.assertThat(invoice.currency()).isEqualTo("EUR");
        softly.assertThat(invoice.lineItems()).hasSize(3);
        softly.assertThat(invoice.seller().vatId()).matches("DE[0-9]{9}");
        softly.assertThat(invoice.buyer().email()).contains("@");
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `SoftAssertionsExtension` requires the `SoftAssertions` parameter to be declared on the test method — forgetting it means the test uses hard assertions silently. Alternatively, `SoftAssertions.assertSoftly(softly -> { ... })` is a lambda-based form that does not require the extension. Performance: soft assertions buffer all collected failures in memory until the end of the test — negligible for typical test sizes but avoidable by grouping unrelated assertions into separate test methods.

[official]

---

### 10. JUnit 5 `@FieldSource` — Parameterised Tests Backed by a Static Field [official]

`@FieldSource` (JUnit 5.11+) references a `static` field by name to supply arguments to `@ParameterizedTest`. It eliminates the zero-argument factory method required by `@MethodSource` for simple list-backed argument sets.

**When to use:** When argument data is a constant set declared as a `static final` field — e.g., a list of valid currency codes, a set of illegal characters, or a set of test locales. `@FieldSource` is more concise than `@MethodSource` when no computation is needed.
**When NOT to use:** When argument construction requires logic — use `@MethodSource`. Also avoid `@FieldSource` when the field is mutable — mutation between test runs can cause ordering-dependent failures.

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.params.ParameterizedTest;
import org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.FieldSource;
import java.util.List;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

class CurrencyValidatorTest {

    static final List<String> VALID_CURRENCY_CODES = List.of(
        "USD", "EUR", "GBP", "JPY", "CHF", "CAD", "AUD", "CNY", "INR", "BRL"
    );

    static final List<String> INVALID_CURRENCY_CODES = List.of(
        "XX", "123", "", "usd", "EURX", null
    );

    CurrencyValidator validator = new CurrencyValidator();

    @ParameterizedTest(name = "valid: {0}")
    @FieldSource("VALID_CURRENCY_CODES")
    void accepts_validIsoCurrencyCode(String code) {
        assertThat(validator.isValid(code)).isTrue();
    }

    @ParameterizedTest(name = "invalid: {0}")
    @FieldSource("INVALID_CURRENCY_CODES")
    void rejects_invalidCurrencyCode(String code) {
        assertThat(validator.isValid(code)).isFalse();
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `@FieldSource` resolves the field by name — if you rename the field without updating the annotation, you get a runtime `PreconditionViolationException` (not a compile error). Consider using `@MethodSource("validCurrencies")` with a factory method that returns the field — this is refactor-safe because the method name is a compile-time string. Alternative: `@EnumSource` for enum-backed test data; `@ValueSource` for simple primitive/string sets without a named field.

[official]

---

### 11. Mockito `InOrder` Verification — Strict Call Sequence Assertions [official]

`InOrder` (Mockito) verifies that mocked interactions occurred in a specific order. It is essential for workflow-style code where the sequence of operations (reserve inventory → charge payment → send confirmation) is a correctness invariant.

**When to use:** Business workflows where operation order matters for correctness (payment before fulfilment), or event-driven services where messages must be emitted in a defined sequence. `InOrder` makes the intended ordering explicit in the test.
**When NOT to use:** Avoid `InOrder` when operations are intentionally parallel or when the order is an implementation detail that may change. Over-specifying call order makes tests brittle — a refactoring that reverses two independent operations will break a test even if observable behaviour is unchanged.

```java
import org.mockito.InOrder;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.*;
import static org.mockito.BDDMockito.given;
import java.math.BigDecimal;

class OrderFulfilmentServiceTest {

    InventoryService inventoryService = mock(InventoryService.class);
    PaymentService   paymentService   = mock(PaymentService.class);
    NotificationService notifications  = mock(NotificationService.class);

    OrderFulfilmentService service = new OrderFulfilmentService(
        inventoryService, paymentService, notifications
    );

    @Test
    void fulfil_executesStepsInCorrectOrder() {
        Order order = new Order("ORD-1", "CUST-1", "SKU-A", 1, new BigDecimal("9.99"));
        given(inventoryService.reserve("SKU-A", 1)).willReturn(true);
        given(paymentService.charge("CUST-1", new BigDecimal("9.99"))).willReturn("PAY-123");

        service.fulfil(order);

        InOrder inOrder = inOrder(inventoryService, paymentService, notifications);
        inOrder.verify(inventoryService).reserve("SKU-A", 1);
        inOrder.verify(paymentService).charge("CUST-1", new BigDecimal("9.99"));
        inOrder.verify(notifications).sendConfirmation("CUST-1", "ORD-1", "PAY-123");
        inOrder.verifyNoMoreInteractions();
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `InOrder.verifyNoMoreInteractions()` checks that no additional verified interactions occurred on the in-order mocks — but it does NOT check mocks that are NOT in the `inOrder(...)` call. If `notifications` calls a second method after `sendConfirmation`, only `verifyNoMoreInteractions()` on the `InOrder` object catches it for the listed mocks. Use `Mockito.verifyNoMoreInteractions(mock1, mock2, ...)` at the end for a complete check. Alternative: Mockito's `verify()` without `InOrder` for unordered verification; `ArgumentCaptor` for asserting on values passed rather than on order.

[official]

---

### 12. Mockito `thenAnswer` with `Answer<T>` — Dynamic Stub Responses [official]

`thenAnswer(Answer<T>)` computes a stub return value at invocation time using the actual call arguments. This is the right tool for stubs that need to echo inputs, simulate retry logic, or return values that vary based on the argument's content.

**When to use:** Stubs that must return a transformed version of the input (e.g., a repository `save()` that populates an `id` field), or stubs that simulate stateful retry scenarios.
**When NOT to use:** Avoid `thenAnswer` for stubs that simply return a constant — `thenReturn` is clearer. Avoid deeply complex `Answer` lambdas — they make tests hard to read; if the logic is non-trivial, extract it as a named `Answer` class or use a real fake implementation.

```java
import org.mockito.stubbing.Answer;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.*;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;
import java.math.BigDecimal;

class RetryingPricingClientTest {

    PricingService pricing = mock(PricingService.class);
    RetryingPricingClient client = new RetryingPricingClient(pricing);

    @Test
    void save_assignsIdToReturnedEntity() {
        OrderRepository repository = mock(OrderRepository.class);
        when(repository.save(any(Order.class))).thenAnswer(invocation -> {
            Order original = invocation.getArgument(0, Order.class);
            return original.withId("ORD-" + System.nanoTime());
        });

        Order unsaved = new Order(null, "CUST-1", "SKU-A", 1);
        Order saved   = repository.save(unsaved);

        assertThat(saved.id()).startsWith("ORD-");
        assertThat(saved.customerId()).isEqualTo("CUST-1");
    }

    @Test
    void fetchPrice_succeedsAfterTwoTransientFailures() {
        AtomicInteger callCount = new AtomicInteger(0);
        when(pricing.fetchPrice("SKU-A")).thenAnswer((Answer<BigDecimal>) inv -> {
            if (callCount.incrementAndGet() < 3) {
                throw new TransientServiceException("upstream timeout");
            }
            return new BigDecimal("9.99");
        });

        BigDecimal price = client.fetchWithRetry("SKU-A");

        assertThat(price).isEqualByComparingTo("9.99");
        verify(pricing, times(3)).fetchPrice("SKU-A");
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `thenAnswer` lambdas capturing mutable state (like `AtomicInteger`) must be declared inside the test method — if declared as a field, state accumulates across test methods and causes order-dependent failures. Alternative: `thenReturn(v1, v2, v3)` for simple sequence stubs (first call returns `v1`, second returns `v2`); Mockito's `doThrow().doReturn()` chain for exception-then-success without lambdas.

[official]

---

### 13. Testcontainers `Network` with `withNetworkAliases` — Multi-Container DNS Communication [official]

`Network.newNetwork()` creates an isolated Docker network for a test, and `withNetworkAliases("alias")` makes one container reachable from another by DNS name. This pattern is essential for testing services that communicate with each other rather than using host-port mappings.

**When to use:** Integration tests where the application itself runs in a container (e.g., `GenericContainer` for the app under test) and must reach a database or broker container by hostname. Also useful for testing microservice interactions where two or more services must discover each other by DNS.
**When NOT to use:** When you only need the container from the test JVM (not from another container) — host-port mapping is simpler. Avoid creating a new `Network` per test method — create it `static` at class level and share it, as network creation and teardown are slow.

```java
import org.testcontainers.containers.GenericContainer;
import org.testcontainers.containers.Network;
import org.testcontainers.containers.PostgreSQLContainer;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Container;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Testcontainers;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@Testcontainers
class MultiContainerNetworkTest {

    static final Network network = Network.newNetwork();

    @Container
    static final PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres = new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine")
        .withNetwork(network)
        .withNetworkAliases("postgres-db");

    @Container
    static final GenericContainer<?> appContainer = new GenericContainer<>("my-app:latest")
        .withNetwork(network)
        .withEnv("DB_URL", "jdbc:postgresql://postgres-db:5432/test")
        .withEnv("DB_USER", postgres.getUsername())
        .withEnv("DB_PASSWORD", postgres.getPassword())
        .withExposedPorts(8080)
        .dependsOn(postgres);

    @Test
    void appContainerConnectsToPostgresViaNetworkAlias() {
        assertThat(appContainer.isRunning()).isTrue();
        String baseUrl = "http://localhost:" + appContainer.getMappedPort(8080);
        // RestAssured.given().baseUri(baseUrl).get("/health").then().statusCode(200);
        assertThat(appContainer.getLogs()).doesNotContain("Connection refused");
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `static Network` and `static @Container` declarations share the network and containers for the entire test class lifecycle. Containers declared as instance fields create a new container per test method — correct isolation but far slower. Remember to call `network.close()` in `@AfterAll` when not using `@Testcontainers` (which handles lifecycle automatically). Alternative: Docker Compose module (`DockerComposeContainer`) for complex multi-service stacks defined in `docker-compose.yml`; simpler to maintain for more than three services.

[official]

---

### 14. Spring Boot `@DataJpaTest` with `replace = Replace.NONE` — Real Database Slice Testing [official]

By default, `@DataJpaTest` replaces the configured datasource with an embedded H2 database. Setting `replace = AutoConfigureTestDatabase.Replace.NONE` disables this substitution, allowing tests to run against a real database (typically a Testcontainers-managed instance) while still loading only the JPA slice.

**When to use:** When your JPA queries use database-specific SQL dialects, JSON operators, window functions, or `@Query` with native SQL that H2 does not support. PostgreSQL-specific queries must be validated against PostgreSQL, not H2.
**When NOT to use:** For simple CRUD repositories where H2 compatibility is sufficient — `replace = NONE` adds container startup time. Also avoid if your team does not have Docker available in CI (Testcontainers requires Docker).

```java
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.jdbc.AutoConfigureTestDatabase;
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.orm.jpa.DataJpaTest;
import org.springframework.boot.testcontainers.service.connection.ServiceConnection;
import org.testcontainers.containers.PostgreSQLContainer;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Container;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Testcontainers;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import java.util.List;

@DataJpaTest
@AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = AutoConfigureTestDatabase.Replace.NONE)
@Testcontainers
class OrderRepositoryPostgresTest {

    @Container
    @ServiceConnection
    static final PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres =
        new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine");

    @Autowired
    OrderRepository orderRepository;

    @Test
    void findByStatusIn_usesNativePostgresQuery() {
        orderRepository.save(new OrderEntity("CUST-1", OrderStatus.CONFIRMED));
        orderRepository.save(new OrderEntity("CUST-2", OrderStatus.PENDING));

        List<OrderEntity> confirmed = orderRepository
            .findByStatusIn(List.of(OrderStatus.CONFIRMED));

        assertThat(confirmed).hasSize(1);
        assertThat(confirmed.get(0).customerId()).isEqualTo("CUST-1");
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `@DataJpaTest` with `Replace.NONE` still loads only the JPA layer (no web, no services). If your repository tests need `@Service` beans or `@EventListener` beans, switch to `@SpringBootTest`. The Testcontainers `@ServiceConnection` annotation eliminates `@DynamicPropertySource` boilerplate but requires Spring Boot 3.1+. Alternative: `@SpringBootTest` with `@Transactional` for full-context repository tests; Flyway/Liquibase migrations run automatically in both approaches.

[official]

---

### 15. JUnit 5 Custom `ParameterResolver` Extension — Injectable Test Dependencies [official]

`ParameterResolver` is the JUnit 5 extension SPI that supplies custom objects to test method parameters. It lets you inject typed test fixtures, clocks, random seeds, or factory helpers without Spring IoC — keeping unit tests free of framework overhead.

**When to use:** Shared test infrastructure that needs to be initialised per-test — e.g., a `FakeClock`, a `TestDatabaseClient`, or a pre-seeded `Random`. Much lighter than Spring context injection for pure unit tests that do not need IoC.
**When NOT to use:** For Spring-managed beans — use `@Autowired` parameter injection which `SpringExtension` provides automatically. Do not use `ParameterResolver` when `@BeforeEach` assignment is simpler — extension wiring adds indirection.

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.*;
import java.time.Clock;
import java.time.Instant;
import java.time.ZoneOffset;

// Extension: supplies a fixed Clock to any test method that declares a Clock parameter
class FrozenClockExtension implements ParameterResolver {

    static final Instant FROZEN_TIME = Instant.parse("2026-05-14T12:00:00Z");

    @Override
    public boolean supportsParameter(ParameterContext paramCtx,
                                     ExtensionContext extCtx) {
        return paramCtx.getParameter().getType().equals(Clock.class);
    }

    @Override
    public Object resolveParameter(ParameterContext paramCtx,
                                   ExtensionContext extCtx) {
        return Clock.fixed(FROZEN_TIME, ZoneOffset.UTC);
    }
}

// Test class using the extension
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@ExtendWith(FrozenClockExtension.class)
class SubscriptionExpiryServiceTest {

    @Test
    void isExpired_returnsFalse_forFutureExpiry(Clock clock) {
        SubscriptionExpiryService svc = new SubscriptionExpiryService(clock);
        Instant futureExpiry = FrozenClockExtension.FROZEN_TIME.plusSeconds(3600);
        assertThat(svc.isExpired(futureExpiry)).isFalse();
    }

    @Test
    void isExpired_returnsTrue_forPastExpiry(Clock clock) {
        SubscriptionExpiryService svc = new SubscriptionExpiryService(clock);
        Instant pastExpiry = FrozenClockExtension.FROZEN_TIME.minusSeconds(1);
        assertThat(svc.isExpired(pastExpiry)).isTrue();
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `ParameterResolver` extensions are global (registered with `@ExtendWith`) and apply to every test method that declares the matching parameter type — there is no per-test opt-out short of removing the parameter. If different tests need different clock values, store the desired instant in the `ExtensionContext.Store` keyed by a test-specific annotation, or switch to `@RegisterExtension` (instance-level) with a configurable initial time. Alternative: constructor injection in the service under test combined with `Clock.fixed(...)` set in `@BeforeEach` — simpler but requires a `clock` field per test class.

[official]

---

### Community Gotchas — Cycle 30 [community]

**`@DataJpaTest` with H2 silently accepts invalid native SQL that fails on PostgreSQL in production — the mismatch is only discovered at deployment time, not during CI [community]** — H2's compatibility modes (`MODE=PostgreSQL`) only replicate a subset of PostgreSQL syntax. Queries using `JSONB` operators (`->>`), `unnest()`, `LATERAL`, `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`, or window functions like `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ...)` parse and execute on H2 but may not test PostgreSQL-specific behaviour at all. The test passes green on H2 and fails with a `PSQLException` in production. WHY: H2 is a general-purpose embedded database — its PostgreSQL compatibility mode is best-effort and lags behind actual PostgreSQL versions. Fix: use `@DataJpaTest` with `replace = Replace.NONE` and a Testcontainers `PostgreSQLContainer` for all repositories that contain any PostgreSQL-specific SQL; reserve H2 for simple CRUD repositories only.

**`@MockitoBean` does NOT reset mock state between test methods in the same class — stubs recorded in one `@Test` method can bleed into subsequent methods, causing order-dependent failures [community]** — Unlike `Mockito.reset()` which explicitly clears stubbing and interaction records, `@MockitoBean` resets its mock only at context reload boundaries. Within a single test class, each `@Test` method sees the accumulated stub state from all previous methods unless `MockitoTestExecutionListener` resets before each method. WHY: Spring's `MockitoTestExecutionListener` calls `Mockito.reset()` before each test method in Spring Boot 3.x, but this can be suppressed by `@DirtiesContext` or skipped in older versions. Fix: always use `@BeforeEach` to re-declare stubs explicitly; treat each test method as if it owns the mock from scratch and never rely on stubbing set up in a previous test.

**`WebTestClient` built with `bindToServer()` in `@BeforeAll` connects at construction time — if the server is not yet fully started, all requests fail with `ConnectException` rather than a readable assertion failure [community]** — In `@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT)`, the `@LocalServerPort` field is populated before test methods run but the field injection timing relative to `@BeforeAll` is not guaranteed. A `WebTestClient` constructed in `@BeforeAll` using the `localServerPort` field may connect to port `0`. WHY: `@LocalServerPort` injection happens during the Spring context lifecycle — the value is populated before any test method but not necessarily before a `@BeforeAll` that references the field at class-load time. Fix: inject `WebTestClient` directly with `@Autowired` when using `@AutoConfigureWebTestClient` (Spring Boot wires it correctly), or defer `WebTestClient` construction to a `@BeforeEach` method.

**`MockRestServiceServer.verify()` does not fail if the client makes unexpected additional requests beyond those declared with `expect(...)` — undeclared calls succeed silently with an empty `200 OK` [community]** — A developer assumes that `server.verify()` validates the exact set of HTTP calls made. In reality, `MockRestServiceServer` silently serves a default empty `200 OK` for any requests not covered by an `expect(...)` declaration — an outbound call to the wrong URL goes completely undetected. WHY: `MockRestServiceServer` is designed as a permissive stub server — it fails only on declared expectations, not on undeclared ones. Fix: ensure all outbound URLs your component may call are declared with `expect(...)`; use strict-mode WireMock when undeclared requests should cause test failure.

**`thenAnswer` lambdas that accidentally call the stubbed method on the mock cause infinite recursion — the stack trace mentions Mockito internals and obscures the true cause [community]** — A developer writes `when(service.process(any())).thenAnswer(inv -> service.process(inv.getArgument(0)))` intending to delegate to a different overload. Since `service` is a mock and `process` is stubbed with this `Answer`, each invocation triggers the `Answer` which calls `process` again — producing a `StackOverflowError` with a Mockito stack trace that obscures the root cause. WHY: Mockito stubs intercept ALL invocations of the method including recursive ones inside an `Answer`. Fix: use `Mockito.CALLS_REAL_METHODS` or a `Spy` instead of constructing the delegation manually inside `thenAnswer`; if you need to call a different method, inject the real collaborator and call it explicitly rather than going through the mock.

**`InOrder.verifyNoMoreInteractions()` covers only mocks explicitly listed in `inOrder(...)` — interactions on unlisted mocks are invisible and can hide unexpected calls [community]** — After verifying an ordered sequence, calling `inOrder.verifyNoMoreInteractions()` validates that the listed mocks had no further calls in the ordered sequence. A mock that was NOT passed to `inOrder(mockA, mockB)` can have any number of additional interactions without triggering a failure. WHY: `InOrder` is a narrowly scoped verification tool — it tracks only the mocks explicitly listed in its constructor. This is by design but the asymmetry with `Mockito.verifyNoMoreInteractions()` is a common source of missed interactions. Fix: always follow `inOrder.verifyNoMoreInteractions()` with a standalone `Mockito.verifyNoMoreInteractions(mockA, mockB, mockC)` to catch any unexpected calls on all mocks in the test.
