## Cycle 31 — 2026-05-14

### 1. JUnit 5 `@RegisterExtension` with `@Order` — Deterministic Extension Execution [official]

`@RegisterExtension` allows field-level extension registration without the class-level `@ExtendWith`. Combining it with `@Order` controls the sequence in which multiple extensions wrap the test — outer extensions must start before inner ones for correct resource ownership (e.g., a network extension must start before a container extension that uses that network).

**When to use:** When two or more programmatic extensions have a startup dependency — e.g., a `WireMockExtension` that must bind its port before a `RestTemplateExtension` reads it, or a `PostgresExtension` that must create its schema before a `FlywayExtension` migrates it.
**When NOT to use:** For single extensions with no ordering requirements — `@ExtendWith` on the class is simpler and does not require a field. Avoid `@RegisterExtension` in base classes if subclasses also register extensions; ordering across inheritance hierarchies is defined but confusing.

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Order;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.RegisterExtension;
import com.github.tomakehurst.wiremock.junit5.WireMockExtension;
import static com.github.tomakehurst.wiremock.client.WireMock.*;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

class PaymentGatewayClientTest {

    @Order(1)
    @RegisterExtension
    static final WireMockExtension wireMock = WireMockExtension.newInstance()
        .options(wireMockConfig().dynamicPort())
        .build();

    @Order(2)
    @RegisterExtension
    static final PaymentClientExtension clientExt =
        new PaymentClientExtension(() -> wireMock.baseUrl());

    @Test
    void charge_returnsApproved_on200() {
        wireMock.stubFor(post("/charge")
            .willReturn(okJson("{\"status\":\"APPROVED\"}")));

        ChargeResult result = clientExt.client().charge("tok_123", 5000);

        assertThat(result.status()).isEqualTo("APPROVED");
        wireMock.verify(postRequestedFor(urlEqualTo("/charge")));
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `@Order` on `@RegisterExtension` fields controls the wrapping sequence — lower order numbers are outermost (started first, torn down last). Without `@Order` the sequence is undefined and can vary between JVM runs. Alternative: nest extensions by composing them inside a single `BeforeAllCallback` in a custom extension — reduces the number of registered extensions but loses the modular reuse benefit.

[official]

---

### 2. JUnit 6 `CancellationToken` — Graceful Test Execution Cancellation [official]

JUnit 6 introduced a `CancellationToken` API that flows through `LauncherExecutionRequest`. Extensions and test engines can check `token.isCancellationRequested()` to abort long-running operations gracefully without hard-killing the JVM. This is critical for CI pipelines that impose wall-clock time limits on test suites.

**When to use:** Integration test suites with long-running setup (database migration, container warm-up) that must abort cleanly within a CI time budget. Also useful for custom test engines that spawn threads — the token lets workers stop naturally rather than leaking thread resources.
**When NOT to use:** For individual test-method timeouts — use `@Timeout` on the method or `Assertions.assertTimeoutPreemptively(...)` instead. `CancellationToken` operates at the launcher/orchestration level, not the per-test level.

```java
import org.junit.platform.launcher.Launcher;
import org.junit.platform.launcher.LauncherDiscoveryRequest;
import org.junit.platform.launcher.LauncherExecutionRequest;
import org.junit.platform.launcher.core.LauncherDiscoveryRequestBuilder;
import org.junit.platform.launcher.core.LauncherFactory;
import org.junit.platform.engine.discovery.DiscoverySelectors;

class BoundedSuiteRunner {

    static void runWithTimeout(long budgetMs) throws InterruptedException {
        Launcher launcher = LauncherFactory.create();
        LauncherDiscoveryRequest discovery = LauncherDiscoveryRequestBuilder
            .request()
            .selectors(DiscoverySelectors.selectPackage("com.example.integration"))
            .build();

        var token = launcher.getCancellationToken();
        var timerThread = new Thread(() -> {
            try {
                Thread.sleep(budgetMs);
            } catch (InterruptedException ignored) {}
            token.cancel();
        });
        timerThread.setDaemon(true);
        timerThread.start();

        launcher.execute(LauncherExecutionRequest.builder()
            .launcherDiscoveryRequest(discovery)
            .cancellationToken(token)
            .build());

        timerThread.interrupt();
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `CancellationToken` is a JUnit 6 API — unavailable in JUnit 5. Teams on JUnit 5.x must simulate cancellation via `--fail-fast` CLI flag or a custom `EngineExecutionListener`. Alternative: `@Timeout` at the `@ExtendWith` class level with `ThreadMode.SEPARATE_THREAD` for preemptive per-test timeouts; `maven-surefire-plugin` `forkedProcessTimeoutInSeconds` for whole-suite wall-clock limits.

[official]

---

### 3. AssertJ `assertThat(obj).isEqualByComparingOnlyFields` — Targeted Field Equality [official]

`assertThat(obj).isEqualByComparingOnlyFields(expected, "field1", "field2")` compares only the named fields of an object, ignoring all others. This is more surgical than `usingRecursiveComparison().ignoringFields(...)` when you want to assert that two objects agree on a small, explicit subset of properties — especially useful when the object has auto-generated identifiers or audit timestamps that legitimately differ.

**When to use:** Asserting that a persisted entity returned from a repository matches the request DTO on business fields (e.g., `name`, `email`, `status`) while ignoring `id`, `createdAt`, and `updatedAt`. Also good for asserting event payload equality ignoring `correlationId`.
**When NOT to use:** When you need to assert on the full object graph — use `usingRecursiveComparison()` instead. Avoid naming fields as strings when the object is a record with accessor methods — typos in field names produce `NoSuchFieldException` at runtime, not compile time. Alternative: AssertJ `extracting("field1", "field2").containsExactly(v1, v2)` for a compile-safe but more verbose equivalent.

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

class UserRegistrationServiceTest {

    UserRegistrationService service = new UserRegistrationService(new InMemoryUserRepo());

    @Test
    void register_persistsBusinessFieldsIgnoringAuditMetadata() {
        RegistrationRequest request = new RegistrationRequest(
            "alice@example.com", "Alice", "ROLE_USER");

        User saved = service.register(request);

        assertThat(saved)
            .isNotNull()
            .isEqualByComparingOnlyFields(
                new User(null, "alice@example.com", "Alice", "ROLE_USER", null, null),
                "email", "displayName", "role");
    }

    @Test
    void register_assignsNonNullId() {
        User saved = service.register(
            new RegistrationRequest("bob@example.com", "Bob", "ROLE_ADMIN"));
        assertThat(saved.id()).isNotNull().startsWith("USR-");
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `isEqualByComparingOnlyFields` uses reflection to locate fields by name — it works on classes and records but not on objects where the field names differ from property names (e.g., Lombok-generated classes where the field is `_name` but the accessor is `getName()`). Alternative: `usingRecursiveComparison().comparingOnlyFields("email", "displayName", "role")` is equivalent but more descriptive in failure messages.

[official]

---

### 4. Mockito `mockStatic` with `try`-with-resources — Static Method Mocking Without Leak [official]

`Mockito.mockStatic(TargetClass.class)` intercepts static method calls within a lexical `try`-with-resources block. The `MockedStatic` handle is `AutoCloseable` — closing it restores the original static behavior. Failing to close the handle leaks the static mock across test classes, causing unpredictable failures in unrelated tests.

**When to use:** Legacy code with un-injectable static utilities (e.g., `UUID.randomUUID()`, `LocalDate.now()`, framework factory methods) that must return controlled values for deterministic tests. Prefer this over PowerMock — `mockStatic` is available in Mockito 3.4+ without byte-code manipulation agents.
**When NOT to use:** When the static method can be wrapped in an injectable interface (e.g., a `ClockProvider` that wraps `Instant.now()`) — inject the interface instead. Do not leave `mockStatic` open across test methods; always use `try`-with-resources or `@BeforeEach`/`@AfterEach` pairing. Alternative: introduce a `Supplier<UUID>` parameter to the class under test and inject `UUID::randomUUID` in production, a fixed lambda in tests — no static mocking needed.

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.mockito.MockedStatic;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.*;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import java.util.UUID;

class OrderIdGeneratorTest {

    OrderIdGenerator generator = new OrderIdGenerator();

    @Test
    void generate_prefixesUuidWithOrderDomain() {
        UUID fixed = UUID.fromString("00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001");

        try (MockedStatic<UUID> uuidStatic = mockStatic(UUID.class)) {
            uuidStatic.when(UUID::randomUUID).thenReturn(fixed);

            String orderId = generator.generate();

            assertThat(orderId).isEqualTo("ORD-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001");
        }
        // UUID.randomUUID() is back to real implementation here
    }

    @Test
    void generate_producesUniqueIdsOnSubsequentCalls() {
        // No static mock — uses real UUID.randomUUID()
        String id1 = generator.generate();
        String id2 = generator.generate();
        assertThat(id1).isNotEqualTo(id2);
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `mockStatic` acquires a thread-local interception hook — it is not thread-safe when multiple test threads exercise the same class concurrently. Parallel test execution with `@Execution(CONCURRENT)` and `mockStatic` will produce flaky results. Enforce sequential execution on tests that use `mockStatic` with `@Execution(SAME_THREAD)` at the class level. Alternative: `Mockito.mockConstruction(TargetClass.class)` for mocking constructors; `@MockitoSettings(strictness = LENIENT)` to suppress unnecessary stubbing warnings in the `try` block.

[official]

---

### 5. Spring Boot `@WebMvcTest` with `@WithMockUser` — Testing Secured Endpoints [official]

`@WebMvcTest` loads only the MVC layer. When Spring Security is on the classpath it auto-configures security filters, which means requests without credentials return `401 Unauthorized`, blocking assertions on the actual controller logic. `@WithMockUser` from `spring-security-test` enables making authenticated requests without a real OAuth flow.

**When to use:** Controller unit tests where the assertion target is the response body or view, and authentication is an incidental concern — mock the user with `@WithMockUser(roles="ADMIN")` and focus on the controller logic.
**When NOT to use:** When you are specifically testing the security configuration itself (filter chain, custom `AccessDeniedHandler`, CSRF rules) — use `@SpringBootTest` with `WebEnvironment.MOCK` and explicit security setup so the full filter chain runs. Alternative: `@WebMvcTest` with `@Import(SecurityConfig.class)` and manual `SecurityMockMvcRequestPostProcessors.jwt()` for JWT-based APIs.

```java
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.web.servlet.WebMvcTest;
import org.springframework.security.test.context.support.WithMockUser;
import org.springframework.test.web.servlet.MockMvc;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.test.context.bean.override.mockito.MockitoBean;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.request.MockMvcRequestBuilders.get;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.*;
import static org.mockito.BDDMockito.given;

@WebMvcTest(OrderController.class)
class OrderControllerSecurityTest {

    @Autowired
    MockMvc mockMvc;

    @MockitoBean
    OrderService orderService;

    @Test
    @WithMockUser(username = "testuser", roles = "CUSTOMER")
    void getOrder_returnsOrder_forAuthenticatedUser() throws Exception {
        given(orderService.findById("ORD-1"))
            .willReturn(new OrderDto("ORD-1", "CONFIRMED", 99_00));

        mockMvc.perform(get("/orders/ORD-1"))
            .andExpect(status().isOk())
            .andExpect(jsonPath("$.status").value("CONFIRMED"))
            .andExpect(jsonPath("$.totalCents").value(9900));
    }

    @Test
    void getOrder_returns401_forUnauthenticatedRequest() throws Exception {
        mockMvc.perform(get("/orders/ORD-1"))
            .andExpect(status().isUnauthorized());
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `@WithMockUser` creates a `UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken` in the `SecurityContext` — it does not go through your `UserDetailsService` or custom `AuthenticationProvider`. Tests pass even if your provider would reject the credentials. For OAuth2/JWT tests, use `SecurityMockMvcRequestPostProcessors.jwt()` (Spring Security 5.5+) to supply a real `JwtAuthenticationToken`. Alternative: `@SpringBootTest` + `TestRestTemplate` with HTTP Basic credentials for end-to-end auth validation.

[official]

---

### 6. Testcontainers `withClasspathResourceMapping` — Seeding Files at Container Startup [official]

`GenericContainer.withClasspathResourceMapping("seed.sql", "/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/seed.sql", BindMode.READ_ONLY)` mounts a classpath resource as a read-only bind mount before the container starts. This is the preferred seeding approach over `copyFileToContainer` (which runs after start) because the file is available during container initialization — critical for PostgreSQL's `initdb` init scripts.

**When to use:** One-off test data seeding that does not warrant a custom Docker image — SQL seed scripts, JSON config files, SSL certificates that must be present at container startup. Faster than Docker `cp` because the bind mount is established before the container process starts.
**When NOT to use:** For large binary files (>10 MB) — the bind mount path must exist on the host or in the classpath, and classpath extraction to a temp path is synchronous. For structured, repeatable seeding prefer Flyway/Liquibase migrations or a custom image with the seed baked in. Alternative: `copyFileToContainer(MountableFile, containerPath)` for seeding after startup; `withInitScript("seed.sql")` on JDBC containers for SQL-only init.

```java
import org.testcontainers.containers.PostgreSQLContainer;
import org.testcontainers.containers.BindMode;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Container;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Testcontainers;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeAll;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import java.sql.*;

@Testcontainers
class SeededPostgresTest {

    @Container
    static final PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres =
        new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine")
            .withClasspathResourceMapping(
                "test-data/seed.sql",
                "/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/01-seed.sql",
                BindMode.READ_ONLY);

    @BeforeAll
    static void verifyContainerReady() {
        assertThat(postgres.isRunning()).isTrue();
    }

    @Test
    void seedScript_insertsThreeProducts() throws Exception {
        try (Connection conn = DriverManager.getConnection(
                postgres.getJdbcUrl(),
                postgres.getUsername(),
                postgres.getPassword());
             Statement stmt = conn.createStatement();
             ResultSet rs = stmt.executeQuery("SELECT count(*) FROM products")) {
            rs.next();
            assertThat(rs.getInt(1)).isEqualTo(3);
        }
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** Files placed in `/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/` are only executed on first container start when the data directory is empty. Container reuse (`withReuse(true)`) means the init scripts run only once — subsequent test runs against the reused container see the previously seeded data and no re-seeding occurs. If each test class needs a clean state, use `@Transactional` rollback or truncate-and-reseed in `@BeforeEach`. Alternative: `JdbcTemplate` inserts in `@BeforeEach` inside a `@Transactional` test — no Docker bind mount involved, fully portable.

[official]

---

### 7. AssertJ `satisfies` with Multiple Lambdas — Grouped Multi-Condition Assertions [official]

`assertThat(obj).satisfies(o -> { ... }, o -> { ... })` runs each lambda assertion against the same object. Unlike chained assertions where the first failure stops the chain, multi-lambda `satisfies` (AssertJ 3.22+) makes the intent clear: "all of these conditions must hold for this object."

**When to use:** When a single object must satisfy several independent conditions that together constitute its validity — e.g., a DTO has a valid ID, non-empty name, and an acceptable status. Grouping with `satisfies` makes the intent clear.
**When NOT to use:** For sequential assertions where the second depends on the first succeeding (e.g., assert non-null before asserting its fields) — use `isNotNull().satisfies(...)` ordering carefully. Prefer `SoftAssertions` for full-report assertions across multiple objects. Alternative: `AbstractObjectAssert.matches(Predicate)` for a single boolean predicate when no failure message customization is needed.

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import java.time.Instant;

class InvoiceServiceTest {

    InvoiceService service = new InvoiceService();

    @Test
    void createInvoice_producesValidInvoiceStructure() {
        Invoice invoice = service.create(
            new InvoiceRequest("CUST-42", "PROD-7", 3, 19_99));

        assertThat(invoice).satisfies(
            inv -> assertThat(inv.id()).matches("INV-[A-Z0-9]{8}"),
            inv -> assertThat(inv.customerId()).isEqualTo("CUST-42"),
            inv -> assertThat(inv.lineItems()).hasSize(1),
            inv -> assertThat(inv.totalCents()).isEqualTo(59_97),
            inv -> assertThat(inv.issuedAt())
                       .isAfter(Instant.now().minusSeconds(5))
                       .isBefore(Instant.now().plusSeconds(5)),
            inv -> assertThat(inv.status()).isEqualTo(InvoiceStatus.DRAFT)
        );
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `satisfies` with multiple lambdas does NOT collect all failures by default in AssertJ 3.x — the first lambda that throws stops subsequent lambdas unless AssertJ is configured for soft assertion mode. The multi-lambda overload of `satisfies` was introduced in AssertJ 3.22.0 — earlier versions only accept a single `Consumer`. Alternative: wrap in `SoftAssertions.assertSoftly(...)` for guaranteed all-failures reporting; `satisfiesAnyOf(...)` for OR semantics.

[official]

---

### 8. JUnit 5 `@AutoClose` — Field-Level Resource Cleanup Without `@AfterEach` [official]

`@AutoClose` (JUnit 5.12+) annotates any field that implements `Closeable` or `AutoCloseable`. JUnit invokes `close()` on it after each test method (or after the test class for `static` fields) without requiring explicit `@AfterEach`. This eliminates the boilerplate of lifecycle methods for resources that only need closing.

**When to use:** Test-local resources such as `MockedStatic`, custom `WireMockServer`, file handles, or in-process gRPC channels that must be torn down after each test. `static` + `@AutoClose` mirrors `@AfterAll` cleanup for class-scoped resources.
**When NOT to use:** For resources that require conditional cleanup (e.g., "only close if the test failed") — `@AfterEach` with explicit logic is clearer. Do not use on Spring-managed beans — Spring's context lifecycle, not JUnit, controls their `close()`.

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.AutoClose;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.mockito.MockedStatic;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.*;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import java.time.Instant;

class TokenExpiryCheckerTest {

    @AutoClose
    MockedStatic<Instant> instantMock = mockStatic(Instant.class);

    TokenExpiryChecker checker = new TokenExpiryChecker();

    @Test
    void isExpired_returnsFalse_forFutureExpiryAtFixedNow() {
        Instant now = Instant.parse("2026-05-14T10:00:00Z");
        instantMock.when(Instant::now).thenReturn(now);

        boolean expired = checker.isExpired(now.plusSeconds(3600));

        assertThat(expired).isFalse();
    }

    @Test
    void isExpired_returnsTrue_forPastExpiryAtFixedNow() {
        Instant now = Instant.parse("2026-05-14T10:00:00Z");
        instantMock.when(Instant::now).thenReturn(now);

        boolean expired = checker.isExpired(now.minusSeconds(1));

        assertThat(expired).isTrue();
    }
    // No @AfterEach needed — instantMock.close() called automatically
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `@AutoClose` requires JUnit 5.12.0 or later. In older versions, `MockedStatic` must be closed in `@AfterEach` or via `try`-with-resources per test method. Fields annotated with `@AutoClose` must be accessible (package-private, protected, or public — private fields work but emit a warning in strict mode). Alternative: `try`-with-resources per test method (more verbose but works in all JUnit 5.x versions); `@RegisterExtension` with a custom extension that owns the lifecycle.

[official]

---

### 9. Spring Boot `@DynamicPropertySource` with `Supplier` — Deferred Container Property Injection [official]

`@DynamicPropertySource` registers `Supplier`-backed properties that are resolved lazily when the Spring context starts, after containers are fully initialized. Using a `Supplier` lambda (not a direct value) ensures the container's mapped port or URL is read after `start()` completes, avoiding `IllegalStateException` for unmapped ports.

**When to use:** Any Testcontainers integration test on Spring Boot 3.x where the container's URL, port, or credentials must populate `application.properties` values (`spring.datasource.url`, `spring.kafka.bootstrap-servers`). More explicit than `@ServiceConnection` when you need to compose the URL or apply a prefix.
**When NOT to use:** When `@ServiceConnection` covers your container type (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Redis, Kafka, MongoDB) — `@ServiceConnection` is simpler and achieves the same result without a `@DynamicPropertySource` method. Alternative: `@TestPropertySource` with a fixed URL for tests that use a pre-running service rather than Testcontainers.

```java
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.test.context.DynamicPropertyRegistry;
import org.springframework.test.context.DynamicPropertySource;
import org.testcontainers.containers.KafkaContainer;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Container;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Testcontainers;
import org.testcontainers.utility.DockerImageName;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@SpringBootTest
@Testcontainers
class OrderEventPublisherIntegrationTest {

    @Container
    static final KafkaContainer kafka =
        new KafkaContainer(DockerImageName.parse("confluentinc/cp-kafka:7.6.1"));

    @DynamicPropertySource
    static void kafkaProperties(DynamicPropertyRegistry registry) {
        registry.add("spring.kafka.bootstrap-servers", kafka::getBootstrapServers);
        registry.add("spring.kafka.consumer.auto-offset-reset", () -> "earliest");
    }

    @Autowired
    OrderEventPublisher publisher;

    @Test
    void publish_sendsEventToOrdersTopic() {
        publisher.publish(new OrderEvent("ORD-99", "CONFIRMED"));
        assertThat(publisher.lastPublishedTopic()).isEqualTo("orders");
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `@DynamicPropertySource` must be `static` — it participates in context caching. If two test classes define `@DynamicPropertySource` methods that register the same property key with different values, they produce different context cache keys and trigger two separate context loads. For shared containers, extract the `@DynamicPropertySource` into a base class that both test classes extend. Alternative: `ApplicationContextInitializer` for more complex dynamic configuration that cannot be expressed as simple key-value pairs.

[official]

---

### 10. Mockito `ArgumentMatchers.assertArg` — Inline Argument Assertion in `verify` [official]

`assertArg(Consumer<T>)` (Mockito 5.3+) is an `ArgumentMatcher` that runs an AssertJ (or any) assertion block against the captured argument during `verify()`. It combines `ArgumentCaptor` capture and assertion into a single call, eliminating the two-step `verify + captor.getValue()` dance.

**When to use:** Verifying that a collaborator was called with a complex argument that requires multiple field-level assertions — e.g., an event object with several properties, a command DTO, or a method call argument built internally by the system under test.
**When NOT to use:** When the argument can be expressed as a simple equality check — `eq(expected)` is more readable. Avoid `assertArg` in `when(...)` stubs — it is only meaningful in `verify()` because it records assertions against actual invocations. Alternative: `ArgumentCaptor` + `verify(mock).method(captor.capture())` then `assertThat(captor.getValue()).satisfies(...)` — functionally equivalent and available in Mockito 4.x without `assertArg`.

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;
import org.mockito.InjectMocks;
import org.mockito.Mock;
import org.mockito.junit.jupiter.MockitoExtension;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.*;
import static org.mockito.ArgumentMatchers.assertArg;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class ShipmentServiceTest {

    @Mock
    ShipmentEventPublisher publisher;

    @InjectMocks
    ShipmentService service;

    @Test
    void confirmShipment_publishesEventWithCorrectFields() {
        service.confirmShipment("SHP-001", "CARRIER-DHL", "TRACK-XYZ");

        verify(publisher).publish(assertArg(event -> {
            assertThat(event.shipmentId()).isEqualTo("SHP-001");
            assertThat(event.carrier()).isEqualTo("CARRIER-DHL");
            assertThat(event.trackingNumber()).isEqualTo("TRACK-XYZ");
            assertThat(event.confirmedAt()).isNotNull();
            assertThat(event.type()).isEqualTo("SHIPMENT_CONFIRMED");
        }));
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `assertArg` is a Mockito 5.3+ API — earlier versions raise `NoSuchMethodError`. In mixed teams with varying Mockito versions, `ArgumentCaptor` is the safe cross-version alternative. `assertArg` failures appear as `AssertionError` inside a `WantedButNotInvoked` message when the argument assertion throws — the nested cause is visible but the failure message is less clear than a direct captor assertion. Alternative: `refEq(expected, "id", "timestamp")` for simple equality ignoring a few fields; `argThat(Predicate)` for boolean-predicate-based matching without AssertJ.

[official]

---

### 11. Spring Boot `TestRestTemplate` vs `WebTestClient` — Choosing the Right HTTP Test Client [official]

`TestRestTemplate` (blocking) and `WebTestClient` (reactive-friendly, AssertJ-fluent) both test a real running server started by `@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT)`. `WebTestClient` provides a fluent assertion API and supports both reactive (`WebFlux`) and servlet stacks since Spring Boot 2.7, making it the preferred choice for new test code.

**When to use `WebTestClient`:** New tests on any stack — servlet or reactive. Its fluent API (`expectStatus().isOk().expectBody(Dto.class).returnResult()`) composes cleanly with AssertJ chains.
**When to use `TestRestTemplate`:** Legacy test code that already uses `RestTemplate`-style method calls, or when you need to follow redirects automatically (TestRestTemplate follows 3xx by default; WebTestClient does not).

```java
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest.WebEnvironment;
import org.springframework.boot.test.web.client.TestRestTemplate;
import org.springframework.boot.test.web.server.LocalServerPort;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.http.*;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = WebEnvironment.RANDOM_PORT)
class ProductApiIntegrationTest {

    @LocalServerPort
    int port;

    @Autowired
    TestRestTemplate restTemplate;

    @Test
    void getProduct_returns200_withJsonBody() {
        ResponseEntity<ProductDto> response = restTemplate
            .getForEntity("/products/PROD-1", ProductDto.class);

        assertThat(response.getStatusCode()).isEqualTo(HttpStatus.OK);
        assertThat(response.getBody()).isNotNull();
        assertThat(response.getBody().sku()).isEqualTo("PROD-1");
        assertThat(response.getHeaders().getContentType())
            .isEqualTo(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON);
    }

    @Test
    void createProduct_returns201_withLocationHeader() {
        var request = new ProductRequest("SKU-NEW", "Widget", 999);
        ResponseEntity<Void> response = restTemplate
            .postForEntity("/products", request, Void.class);

        assertThat(response.getStatusCode()).isEqualTo(HttpStatus.CREATED);
        assertThat(response.getHeaders().getLocation()).isNotNull();
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `TestRestTemplate` raises `HttpClientErrorException` for 4xx responses when using `getForObject` — use `exchange(...)` to get the `ResponseEntity` and inspect status without catching exceptions. `WebTestClient` never throws on error status; it returns the response for assertion. Neither client shares the server's `SecurityContext` — use `withBasicAuth(user, password)` on `TestRestTemplate` or `SecurityMockMvcRequestPostProcessors.jwt()` on `WebTestClient` for authenticated requests. Alternative: `MockMvc` (in-process, no real port) is faster for controller-layer tests that do not need a real HTTP stack.

[official]

---

### 12. AssertJ `filteredOn` + `extracting` — Chained Collection Filtering and Assertion [official]

`assertThat(list).filteredOn(Predicate).extracting("field").containsExactlyInAnyOrder(...)` chains a filter and a projection in a single readable assertion. It avoids the Java stream idiom (`list.stream().filter(...).map(...).collect(...)`) inline in tests and keeps the assertion DSL cohesive.

**When to use:** Asserting on a subset of a collection — e.g., "all CONFIRMED orders have a non-null shipmentId", or "the FAILED events all carry an error code". Also useful after `filteredOn` to assert that the filtered result is non-empty before asserting its contents.
**When NOT to use:** For single-element collections — `assertThat(list).singleElement().extracting(...)` is cleaner. Avoid deep reflection-based `extracting("a.b.c")` chains on mutable domain objects — use `extracting(Obj::getA)` method-reference form to get compile-time safety. Alternative: `allMatch(Predicate)` for homogeneous conditions; `satisfiesExactlyInAnyOrder` for per-element assertions.

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import java.util.List;

class OrderSummaryServiceTest {

    OrderSummaryService service = new OrderSummaryService(new InMemoryOrderRepository());

    @Test
    void getSummaries_confirmedOrdersAllHaveShipmentIds() {
        service.seedOrders(List.of(
            new Order("ORD-1", OrderStatus.CONFIRMED, "SHP-A"),
            new Order("ORD-2", OrderStatus.CONFIRMED, "SHP-B"),
            new Order("ORD-3", OrderStatus.PENDING,   null),
            new Order("ORD-4", OrderStatus.CANCELLED, null)
        ));

        List<OrderSummary> summaries = service.getSummaries();

        assertThat(summaries)
            .filteredOn(s -> s.status() == OrderStatus.CONFIRMED)
            .hasSize(2)
            .extracting(OrderSummary::shipmentId)
            .doesNotContainNull()
            .containsExactlyInAnyOrder("SHP-A", "SHP-B");
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `filteredOn` + `extracting` chain produces a new `ListAssert` whose context description drops the filter predicate text from failure messages — the message reads "expected to contain..." without mentioning the filter. Wrap in `as("confirmed orders")` to label the assertion context. Alternative: AssertJ `allSatisfy(Consumer)` for asserting every element meets a condition without extracting; Java streams for complex multi-step transformations where readability benefits from intermediate named variables.

[official]

---

### 13. JUnit 5 `@ParameterizedTest` with `@FieldSource` — Reusing Static Field Data [official]

`@FieldSource("fieldName")` (JUnit 5.12+) reads arguments from a `static` field in the test class, eliminating the need for a factory method when the data is a simple constant. It accepts `Iterable`, arrays, and `Stream` fields. Unlike `@MethodSource`, there is no method body — the data lives as a declarative field.

**When to use:** When the argument set is a fixed constant that does not require computation — enum sets, boundary values, known error codes. `@FieldSource` is more readable than a zero-argument `@MethodSource` method that only returns a literal collection.
**When NOT to use:** When the data requires any computation, lazy initialization, or access to injected beans — use `@MethodSource` or a custom `ArgumentsProvider`. Do not use `@FieldSource` across test classes (it only reads fields from the current class); for cross-class sharing, use `@MethodSource("com.example.TestData#statusCodes")`. Alternative: `@ValueSource(strings = {...})` for a single-argument, single-type flat list; `@EnumSource` for exhaustive enum parameter sets.

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.params.ParameterizedTest;
import org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.FieldSource;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import java.util.List;

class HttpStatusNormalizerTest {

    static final List<Integer> CLIENT_ERROR_CODES =
        List.of(400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 410, 422, 429);

    static final List<Integer> SERVER_ERROR_CODES =
        List.of(500, 502, 503, 504);

    HttpStatusNormalizer normalizer = new HttpStatusNormalizer();

    @ParameterizedTest
    @FieldSource("CLIENT_ERROR_CODES")
    void normalizeClientError_returnsClientErrorCategory(int code) {
        assertThat(normalizer.normalize(code))
            .isEqualTo(ErrorCategory.CLIENT_ERROR);
    }

    @ParameterizedTest
    @FieldSource("SERVER_ERROR_CODES")
    void normalizeServerError_returnsServerErrorCategory(int code) {
        assertThat(normalizer.normalize(code))
            .isEqualTo(ErrorCategory.SERVER_ERROR);
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `@FieldSource` fields must be `static` — instance fields trigger a `PreconditionViolationException` at test plan discovery time. The field type must be a `Stream`, `Iterable`, or array; raw collections of `Arguments` objects work for multi-parameter tests. JUnit 5.11 and earlier do not have `@FieldSource` — check your JUnit version before adopting. Alternative: `@MethodSource` with a no-arg method body; `@CsvSource` / `@CsvFileSource` for tabular multi-argument parameterization.

[official]

---

### 14. Testcontainers `@ImportTestcontainers` — Cross-Class Container Sharing via Interface [official]

`@ImportTestcontainers(ContainerConfig.class)` (Spring Boot 3.1+ / Testcontainers Spring Support) imports container definitions from a separate interface annotated with `@Testcontainers`. All test classes that import the same container config share the same container instance subject to the Spring context cache, eliminating redundant container startups across the test suite.

**When to use:** Multiple integration test classes that all require the same database or message broker container. Centralizing container declarations in a single interface makes the startup cost visible, prevents duplication, and ensures all tests use a consistent container version.
**When NOT to use:** When containers must be customized per test class (different environment variables, different versions). Also avoid if the `@ServiceConnection` approach is available — `@ServiceConnection` auto-wires without needing a separate import class.

```java
// Shared container configuration interface
import org.testcontainers.containers.PostgreSQLContainer;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Container;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Testcontainers;

@Testcontainers
interface SharedPostgresContainers {

    @Container
    PostgreSQLContainer<?> POSTGRES =
        new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine")
            .withDatabaseName("testdb")
            .withUsername("test")
            .withPassword("test");
}

// Test class — imports and uses the shared container
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.orm.jpa.DataJpaTest;
import org.springframework.boot.testcontainers.context.ImportTestcontainers;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@DataJpaTest
@ImportTestcontainers(SharedPostgresContainers.class)
class CustomerRepositoryTest {

    @Autowired
    CustomerRepository customerRepo;

    @Test
    void findByEmail_returnsCustomer() {
        customerRepo.save(new CustomerEntity("alice@example.com"));
        assertThat(customerRepo.findByEmail("alice@example.com")).isPresent();
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** The shared container is `static` in the interface — it starts once when the JVM first loads the interface. If one test class dirtily modifies data without rollback, subsequent classes see polluted state. Use `@Transactional` on test classes or explicit `@BeforeEach` cleanup to guard against cross-test pollution. Alternative: `@ServiceConnection` when the container type is directly supported; abstract base class with `@Container` + `static` fields for pre-Spring-Boot-3.1 compatibility.

[official]

---

### 15. Mockito `BDDMockito` — BDD-Style Stubbing for Readable Test Structure [official]

`BDDMockito.given(mock.method(args)).willReturn(value)` mirrors the Given-When-Then BDD vocabulary in test code. It is a static import alias over the standard `when/thenReturn` API — functionally identical but makes the stub read as "given that method returns value", aligning with the test narrative.

**When to use:** Test classes that follow BDD naming (`given_`, `when_`, `then_`) or Gherkin-style comments (`// Given`, `// When`, `// Then`). Consistent use of `given/willReturn` throughout a class improves readability when all collaborator behavior is stubbed in the Given section.
**When NOT to use:** Do not mix `when/thenReturn` and `given/willReturn` within the same test class — the inconsistency is confusing. Do not use `BDDMockito.willThrow(...).given(mock).method()` when `doThrow(...).when(mock).method()` is more idiomatic for `void` methods. Alternative: Standard `Mockito.when(...).thenReturn(...)` if the team does not follow BDD structure; `BDDMockito.then(mock).should()` for BDD-style verification replacing `verify(mock)`.

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;
import org.mockito.InjectMocks;
import org.mockito.Mock;
import org.mockito.junit.jupiter.MockitoExtension;
import static org.mockito.BDDMockito.*;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class InventoryReservationServiceTest {

    @Mock
    InventoryRepository inventoryRepo;

    @Mock
    ReservationEventPublisher eventPublisher;

    @InjectMocks
    InventoryReservationService service;

    @Test
    void reserve_publishesReservationEvent_whenStockIsSufficient() {
        // Given
        given(inventoryRepo.availableStock("SKU-100")).willReturn(50);
        willDoNothing().given(eventPublisher).publish(any());

        // When
        ReservationResult result = service.reserve("SKU-100", 10);

        // Then
        assertThat(result.isSuccess()).isTrue();
        assertThat(result.reservedQty()).isEqualTo(10);
        then(eventPublisher).should().publish(assertArg(event ->
            assertThat(event.sku()).isEqualTo("SKU-100")));
        then(inventoryRepo).should().availableStock("SKU-100");
        then(inventoryRepo).shouldHaveNoMoreInteractions();
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff:** `BDDMockito.then(mock).should()` verification does not support `times(N)` inline — use `then(mock).should(times(N)).method()` for counted verifications. `BDDMockito` is in `org.mockito.BDDMockito` and requires an explicit static import. Alternative: `Mockito.verify` + `when/thenReturn` for teams that prefer the original Mockito style; AssertJ `satisfies` for assertions instead of `then().should()`.

[official]

---

### Community Gotchas — Cycle 31 [community]

**`@FieldSource` is silently skipped if the referenced field name has a typo — JUnit reports zero test invocations rather than a hard error, and the suite stays green with no coverage [community]** — If `@FieldSource("CLIENT_ERRRO_CODES")` has a typo, JUnit 5 does not always throw `NoSuchFieldException` at plan-discovery time; depending on the JUnit release, the parameterized test may be reported as having zero cases. The CI build stays green while providing zero coverage for that test. WHY: `@FieldSource` resolution happens at test plan generation time in a catch-friendly block — a reflective lookup failure may degrade to a skipped test rather than a fatal error, giving false confidence. Fix: always run the test locally and confirm the test count in IDE output matches the expected number of parameter rows; add a standalone `@Test` that asserts `assertThat(CLIENT_ERROR_CODES).hasSizeGreaterThan(0)` to guard the data source.

**`mockStatic` on `java.time.LocalDate` intercepts `LocalDate.now()` but does NOT intercept `LocalDate.now(ZoneId)` — overloaded static methods require separate `when` declarations [community]** — A developer stubs `mockStatic(LocalDate.class).when(LocalDate::now).thenReturn(fixedDate)` but production code calls `LocalDate.now(ZoneId.of("Europe/Paris"))`. The overloaded `now(ZoneId)` is a different method reference; the single `when(LocalDate::now)` stub covers only the no-arg form. The production call goes unstubbed and returns the real system date. WHY: `mockStatic` treats each overload as an independent method — `LocalDate.now()` and `LocalDate.now(ZoneId)` have different signatures and must be stubbed separately. Fix: also add `localDateMock.when(() -> LocalDate.now(any(ZoneId.class))).thenReturn(fixedDate)` and add a test that explicitly exercises the zoned overload.

**`@WithMockUser` in a `@WebMvcTest` does not propagate the security context to `@Async` methods triggered by the controller — the async thread sees an empty `SecurityContextHolder` [community]** — When a controller dispatches work to an `@Async` service, Spring's `DelegatingSecurityContextTaskExecutor` must be configured to copy the `SecurityContext` to the async thread. Without it, the async method throws `AccessDeniedException` or reads `null` from `SecurityContextHolder.getContext().getAuthentication()`. WHY: Spring's default `SimpleAsyncTaskExecutor` creates a bare thread with no context propagation; `SecurityContext` is thread-local by default and is not inherited. Fix: configure a `DelegatingSecurityContextTaskExecutor` wrapping your async executor, or set `SecurityContextHolder.setStrategyName(SecurityContextHolder.MODE_INHERITABLETHREADLOCAL)` — and add an integration test with `@SpringBootTest` that validates the async path's security behavior.

**`@DynamicPropertySource` methods in test base classes are inherited but their container declarations are NOT — if the container is declared as a non-static field in a subclass, the static method runs before instance initialization and produces `NullPointerException` [community]** — A base class declares `@DynamicPropertySource` reading `postgres.getJdbcUrl()`, but a subclass declares `PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres` as a non-static field. Static methods run before instance initialization, so `postgres` is `null`. WHY: `@DynamicPropertySource` is called during context refresh — a static phase — instance state from the subclass is not yet populated. Fix: always declare `@Container` fields as `static` in the same class (or a common parent) that owns the `@DynamicPropertySource` method; never mix static property sources with instance-level container fields.

**`WebTestClient` exchange calls hang indefinitely when the server sends a chunked streaming response and the test does not scope the read — the test thread blocks past the configured test timeout [community]** — When a Spring WebFlux endpoint returns a `Flux<T>` with infinite or long-duration streams, `WebTestClient.get().uri("/events").exchange()` starts consuming the stream. Without `.returnResult().getResponseBody().take(N).collectList().block(Duration)`, the assertion waits for the stream to complete — which never happens for SSE endpoints. WHY: `WebTestClient` faithfully models the reactive contract — it does not add a read timeout unless you configure one via `.responseTimeout(Duration)`. Fix: always scope `WebTestClient` calls to streaming endpoints with `.take(N)` on the response body flux, or configure a response timeout: `WebTestClient.bindToServer().baseUrl(url).responseTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(5)).build()`.
