## Cycle 53 — 2026-05-14

### Pattern 211 — `@WebFluxTest` with `WebTestClient` for Reactive Controllers

`@WebFluxTest` is the reactive counterpart of `@WebMvcTest`: it loads only `@Controller`, `@ControllerAdvice`, `@JsonComponent`, and WebFlux-specific infrastructure. It wires a `WebTestClient` automatically, giving you a fluent API for sending requests and asserting on responses without starting a real server.

```java
@WebFluxTest(ProductController.class)
class ProductControllerTest {

    @Autowired
    WebTestClient webClient;

    @MockitoBean
    ProductService productService;

    @Test
    void getProduct_returnsProductJson() {
        given(productService.findById("p1"))
            .willReturn(Mono.just(new Product("p1", "Widget", 9.99)));

        webClient.get().uri("/products/p1")
            .accept(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
            .exchange()
            .expectStatus().isOk()
            .expectBody()
            .jsonPath("$.name").isEqualTo("Widget")
            .jsonPath("$.price").isEqualTo(9.99);
    }

    @Test
    void getProduct_notFound_returns404() {
        given(productService.findById("missing"))
            .willReturn(Mono.empty());

        webClient.get().uri("/products/missing")
            .exchange()
            .expectStatus().isNotFound();
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `@WebFluxTest` does not load `@Service` or `@Repository` beans — every collaborator must be provided via `@MockitoBean` or `@Import`. This keeps the test fast and isolated but means you must remember to import any WebFlux `WebFilter` or `HandlerFilterFunction` beans that are applied globally; omitting them produces tests that pass locally but fail in integration because the filter (e.g., a rate-limiter or auth filter) is never exercised. [official]

---

### Pattern 212 — Singleton Container Pattern with `@Testcontainers` Static Field

Starting a new database container per test class multiplies CI time linearly with the number of test classes. The singleton pattern declares the container as a `static` field — either on a shared base class or on a `@TestConfiguration` class — so Testcontainers' JVM shutdown hook stops it once at the end of the entire test run rather than between classes.

```java
// Shared base class used by all @DataJpaTest classes
@Testcontainers
@DataJpaTest
@AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = AutoConfigureTestDatabase.Replace.NONE)
public abstract class PostgresIntegrationBase {

    @Container
    static final PostgreSQLContainer<?> POSTGRES =
        new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine")
            .withReuse(true);   // requires ~/.testcontainers.properties: testcontainers.reuse.enable=true

    @DynamicPropertySource
    static void registerPgProps(DynamicPropertyRegistry registry) {
        registry.add("spring.datasource.url",      POSTGRES::getJdbcUrl);
        registry.add("spring.datasource.username", POSTGRES::getUsername);
        registry.add("spring.datasource.password", POSTGRES::getPassword);
    }
}

// Test class just extends
class OrderRepositoryTest extends PostgresIntegrationBase {

    @Autowired OrderRepository repo;

    @Test
    void saveAndFind_roundTrip() {
        Order saved = repo.save(new Order("ORD-1", BigDecimal.TEN));
        assertThat(repo.findById(saved.getId())).isPresent()
            .hasValueSatisfying(o -> assertThat(o.getReference()).isEqualTo("ORD-1"));
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `withReuse(true)` requires the developer to opt in by setting `testcontainers.reuse.enable=true` in `~/.testcontainers.properties`; it is off by default to avoid polluting developer machines with orphaned containers. In CI, where machines are ephemeral, reuse is often unnecessary — the static field already achieves single-startup-per-JVM without `withReuse`. Use `withReuse` only when you want the container to survive across separate test-suite invocations (e.g., rapid `./mvnw test` re-runs during local development). [official]

---

### Pattern 213 — `Awaitility.await()` with `conditionEvaluationListener` for Async Diagnostics

When an async assertion times out, the default `ConditionTimeoutException` message only says the condition was not met — it does not tell you what the intermediate values were. Attaching a `ConditionEvaluationListener` emits a log line on every poll cycle, turning opaque timeouts into a readable progression of observed values.

```java
@Test
void orderEventually_transitions_to_SHIPPED() {
    orderService.submit(orderId);

    await()
        .atMost(Duration.ofSeconds(10))
        .pollInterval(Duration.ofMillis(200))
        .conditionEvaluationListener(condition -> log.info(
            "poll #{}: status={}, elapsed={}ms, remaining={}ms",
            condition.getEvaluationCount(),
            orderRepository.findById(orderId).map(Order::getStatus).orElse(null),
            condition.getElapsedTimeInMS(),
            condition.getRemainingTimeInMS()))
        .failFast("Order was CANCELLED — stop polling",
            () -> orderRepository.findById(orderId)
                      .map(o -> o.getStatus() == OrderStatus.CANCELLED)
                      .orElse(false))
        .untilAsserted(() ->
            assertThat(orderRepository.findById(orderId))
                .isPresent()
                .hasValueSatisfying(o ->
                    assertThat(o.getStatus()).isEqualTo(OrderStatus.SHIPPED)));
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `conditionEvaluationListener` calls your lambda on every poll, which can produce noisy logs in a passing test suite. Wrap the listener in a guard that only logs when the test is about to fail (e.g., when `remainingTimeInMS < 1000`) or register the listener only in a `@BeforeEach` block that runs exclusively when the `VERBOSE_AWAIT` system property is set. The `failFast` predicate is valuable when a terminal failure state (like `CANCELLED`) is detected early, cutting wasted poll time. [community]

---

### Pattern 214 — `@DataMongoTest` with Flapdoodle Embedded MongoDB for Repository Slice Tests

`@DataMongoTest` loads only the MongoDB layer (repositories, `MongoTemplate`, converters) without starting the full application context. By default it uses the Flapdoodle embedded MongoDB — add the `de.flapdoodle.embed:de.flapdoodle.embed.mongo` dependency with `test` scope and Spring Boot auto-configures it automatically.

```java
@DataMongoTest
class ProductCatalogRepositoryTest {

    @Autowired ProductCatalogRepository repo;
    @Autowired MongoTemplate mongoTemplate;

    @BeforeEach
    void seedData() {
        mongoTemplate.dropCollection(ProductCatalog.class);
        mongoTemplate.insertAll(List.of(
            new ProductCatalog("cat-1", "Electronics", List.of("TV", "Phone")),
            new ProductCatalog("cat-2", "Books",       List.of("Novel", "Guide"))
        ));
    }

    @Test
    void findByName_returnsMatchingCategory() {
        Optional<ProductCatalog> found = repo.findByName("Electronics");
        assertThat(found).isPresent()
            .hasValueSatisfying(c -> {
                assertThat(c.getId()).isEqualTo("cat-1");
                assertThat(c.getItems()).containsExactlyInAnyOrder("TV", "Phone");
            });
    }

    @Test
    void findByItemsContaining_returnsParentCategory() {
        List<ProductCatalog> results = repo.findByItemsContaining("Novel");
        assertThat(results).hasSize(1)
            .first().extracting(ProductCatalog::getName).isEqualTo("Books");
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** Flapdoodle embedded MongoDB ships only the MongoDB 4.x wire protocol by default; if your production cluster runs MongoDB 7.x with features like time-series collections or `$setWindowFields` aggregation operators, those tests will silently pass against the older in-process implementation but fail in production. For production-version fidelity, replace Flapdoodle with a `MongoDBContainer` from Testcontainers and set `@AutoConfigureDataMongo(replace = Replace.NONE)`. [official]

---

### Pattern 215 — `@AutoConfigureObservability` + `TestObservationRegistry` for Micrometer Assertions

Spring Boot's `@AutoConfigureObservability` wires a `TestObservationRegistry` into the test context. The registry captures every `Observation` started during the test — spans, metrics, and high-cardinality key-values — and exposes them for assertion via `TestObservationRegistryAssert` from `micrometer-test`.

```java
@SpringBootTest
@AutoConfigureObservability
class PaymentServiceObservabilityTest {

    @Autowired PaymentService paymentService;
    @Autowired TestObservationRegistry observationRegistry;

    @BeforeEach
    void resetRegistry() {
        observationRegistry.clear();   // isolate from other tests
    }

    @Test
    void processPayment_recordsObservationWithOutcomeTag() {
        paymentService.process(new PaymentRequest("TXN-001", Money.of(50, "USD")));

        TestObservationRegistryAssert.assertThat(observationRegistry)
            .hasObservationWithNameEqualTo("payment.process")
            .that()
            .hasLowCardinalityKeyValue("outcome", "success")
            .hasHighCardinalityKeyValue("transaction.id", "TXN-001")
            .hasBeenStarted()
            .hasBeenStopped();
    }

    @Test
    void processPayment_insufficientFunds_recordsFailureTag() {
        assertThatThrownBy(() ->
            paymentService.process(new PaymentRequest("TXN-002", Money.of(999_999, "USD"))))
            .isInstanceOf(InsufficientFundsException.class);

        TestObservationRegistryAssert.assertThat(observationRegistry)
            .hasObservationWithNameEqualTo("payment.process")
            .that()
            .hasLowCardinalityKeyValue("outcome", "error");
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `observationRegistry.clear()` in `@BeforeEach` is mandatory when multiple tests run in the same context; without it, observations from earlier tests accumulate and cause false positives or spurious counts. If your service delegates to another instrumented service, the registry captures nested observations too — use `hasNumberOfObservationsWithNameEqualTo` to guard count assertions. `@AutoConfigureObservability` auto-imports both `micrometer-core` and `micrometer-test`; verify both are on the test classpath or the annotation silently does nothing. [official]

---

### Pattern 216 — PIT Mutation Testing with `withHistory` for Incremental CI Builds

Running PIT on every build in a large codebase is prohibitive — full mutation analysis of 100k LOC can take 20+ minutes. PIT's incremental mode (`historyInputFile` + `historyOutputFile`) skips re-mutating source files whose bytecode hash has not changed since the last run, reducing incremental build time by 70-90% on typical codebases.

```xml
<!-- pom.xml: PIT with incremental history and threshold enforcement -->
<plugin>
    <groupId>org.pitest</groupId>
    <artifactId>pitest-maven</artifactId>
    <version>1.17.0</version>
    <configuration>
        <targetClasses>
            <param>com.example.domain.*</param>
            <param>com.example.service.*</param>
        </targetClasses>
        <targetTests>
            <param>com.example.*Test</param>
        </targetTests>
        <mutationThreshold>80</mutationThreshold>
        <coverageThreshold>85</coverageThreshold>
        <threads>4</threads>
        <historyInputFile>${project.build.directory}/pit-history.bin</historyInputFile>
        <historyOutputFile>${project.build.directory}/pit-history.bin</historyOutputFile>
        <avoidCallsTo>
            <avoidCallsTo>org.slf4j</avoidCallsTo>
            <avoidCallsTo>org.apache.log4j</avoidCallsTo>
        </avoidCallsTo>
    </configuration>
</plugin>
```

```java
// Unit test that kills the "boundary off-by-one" mutant PIT would otherwise survive
@Test
void discount_exactlyAtThreshold_appliesDiscount() {
    // PIT generates a mutant that changes >= to >
    // Both a test for == threshold AND a test for threshold+1 kill the mutant
    assertThat(pricer.calculateDiscount(100)).isEqualTo(0.10);  // exactly at threshold
    assertThat(pricer.calculateDiscount(99)).isEqualTo(0.00);   // just below
    assertThat(pricer.calculateDiscount(101)).isEqualTo(0.10);  // just above
}
```

**Tradeoff.** The `historyInputFile` path must be persisted between CI runs (e.g., stored as a build artifact or in a cache volume). If the history file is missing (first run, cache eviction), PIT falls back to a full analysis — so the first run after a cache miss is expensive. Set `mutationThreshold` conservatively (start at 70%) and raise it gradually; setting 90% immediately will break the build on equivalent mutants that no test can reasonably kill (e.g., `return null` vs `return Collections.emptyList()` when callers never inspect the return value). [official]

---

### Pattern 217 — `@TestBean` with Static Factory Method for Partial Production Config Override

`@TestBean` (Spring Framework 6.2+) is a lighter-weight bean override than `@MockitoBean`: instead of replacing a bean with a Mockito mock, it calls a static factory method in the test class to produce a real (or custom-stub) implementation. This is ideal when you want to override a single property of a production bean — e.g., a `Clock` with a fixed time — without writing a full Mockito stub.

```java
@SpringBootTest
class InvoiceDateTest {

    // Static factory: name must match the bean name or use @TestBean(methodName = "...")
    static Clock clock() {
        return Clock.fixed(
            Instant.parse("2026-01-15T09:00:00Z"),
            ZoneOffset.UTC
        );
    }

    @TestBean   // replaces the Clock @Bean in production config with the static factory above
    Clock clock;

    @Autowired InvoiceService invoiceService;

    @Test
    void invoice_usesInjectedClock_forDueDate() {
        Invoice inv = invoiceService.createInvoice(
            new InvoiceRequest("CUST-1", Money.of(200, "EUR"), 30));

        // Due date = 2026-01-15 + 30 days = 2026-02-14
        assertThat(inv.getDueDate())
            .isEqualTo(LocalDate.of(2026, 2, 14));
    }

    @Test
    void invoice_timestamp_matchesFixedClock() {
        Invoice inv = invoiceService.createInvoice(
            new InvoiceRequest("CUST-2", Money.of(100, "EUR"), 0));
        assertThat(inv.getCreatedAt())
            .isEqualTo(LocalDateTime.of(2026, 1, 15, 9, 0));
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `@TestBean` does NOT reset the bean between test methods — the same `Clock` instance (and its fixed instant) is shared for the entire test class. If your service caches the `Instant` during construction (e.g., `this.now = clock.instant()` in a `@PostConstruct`), the cached value never changes between tests, causing misleading results. Use `@DirtiesContext` per method if you need a fresh context, or redesign the service to call `clock.instant()` lazily at invocation time. [official]

---

### Pattern 218 — `@ParameterizedClass` (JUnit 6) for Shared Test Logic Across Implementations

JUnit 6 introduces `@ParameterizedClass`, which applies the parameterization machinery to an entire test class rather than a single method. This is the idiomatic replacement for the copy-paste-test-class pattern used when testing multiple implementations of the same interface.

```java
// JUnit 6 — run the entire test class once per CacheProvider implementation
@ParameterizedClass
@MethodSource("cacheProviders")
class CacheProviderContractTest {

    static Stream<CacheProvider> cacheProviders() {
        return Stream.of(
            new InMemoryCacheProvider(),
            new RedisCacheProvider(REDIS_CONTAINER.getConnectionDetails()),
            new CaffeineCacheProvider()
        );
    }

    // Constructor receives the argument(s) declared by the source
    CacheProviderContractTest(CacheProvider provider) {
        this.cache = provider;
    }

    private final CacheProvider cache;

    @BeforeEach
    void clearCache() { cache.clear(); }

    @Test
    void put_thenGet_returnsValue() {
        cache.put("key", "value", Duration.ofMinutes(5));
        assertThat(cache.get("key")).isPresent().hasValue("value");
    }

    @Test
    void get_afterTtlExpiry_returnsEmpty() throws InterruptedException {
        cache.put("expiring", "val", Duration.ofMillis(50));
        Thread.sleep(100);
        assertThat(cache.get("expiring")).isEmpty();
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `@ParameterizedClass` requires JUnit 6 (or 5.11+ with `@Experimental` preview). In JUnit 5, the same intent is approximated with `@ExtendWith` + abstract base class or with dynamic test factories — both approaches require more boilerplate. With `@ParameterizedClass`, all test methods share the same source arguments; if individual tests need different parameterization, nest `@ParameterizedTest` methods inside the class. Large test classes parameterized over slow containers (e.g., a full `RedisContainer` per argument) should use a class-scoped `static` container initialized in `@BeforeAll`, not a new container per test instance. [official]

---

### Pattern 219 — `STRICT_STUBS` Mode with `lenient()` Escapes for Shared Test Fixtures

Mockito's `MockitoSettings(strictness = Strictness.STRICT_STUBS)` (the default in JUnit extension mode) catches two classes of mistakes: unnecessary stubbing (stubs defined but never invoked during the test) and stubbing argument mismatches. However, shared `@BeforeEach` fixtures often define "defensive" stubs that are needed by only some tests — use `lenient()` on those stubs to suppress the UnnecessaryStubbingException without disabling strictness globally.

```java
@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
// STRICT_STUBS is the default with MockitoExtension
class OrderProcessorTest {

    @Mock OrderRepository orderRepository;
    @Mock NotificationService notificationService;
    @InjectMocks OrderProcessor processor;

    @BeforeEach
    void stubDefaults() {
        // lenient(): this stub is shared; not every test invokes notificationService
        lenient().when(notificationService.isEnabled()).thenReturn(true);

        // Non-lenient: every test in this class MUST exercise findById
        when(orderRepository.findById("ORD-1"))
            .thenReturn(Optional.of(new Order("ORD-1", OrderStatus.PENDING)));
    }

    @Test
    void process_pendingOrder_sendsNotification() {
        processor.process("ORD-1");
        verify(notificationService).send(any(OrderNotification.class));
    }

    @Test
    void process_pendingOrder_savesUpdatedStatus() {
        processor.process("ORD-1");
        ArgumentCaptor<Order> captor = ArgumentCaptor.forClass(Order.class);
        verify(orderRepository).save(captor.capture());
        assertThat(captor.getValue().getStatus()).isEqualTo(OrderStatus.PROCESSED);
        // notificationService.isEnabled() may or may not be called — lenient() suppresses warning
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** Overusing `lenient()` defeats strict stubbing's purpose: it is a suppression, not a fix. Before reaching for `lenient()`, ask whether the defensive stub belongs in `@BeforeEach` at all — if only one test uses it, move the stub into that test. Use `lenient()` only for genuinely shared stubs that are invoked conditionally (e.g., "only when notifications are enabled"). Keep the count of `lenient()` calls small; if you have more than two or three, the test fixture is probably doing too much. [community]

---

### Pattern 220 — `@DefaultLocale` and `@DefaultTimeZone` (JUnit 6.1) for Locale-Sensitive Tests

JUnit 6.1 introduces `@DefaultLocale` and `@DefaultTimeZone` as class- or method-level annotations that temporarily set `Locale.setDefault()` and `TimeZone.setDefault()` for the duration of the annotated scope and restore the originals afterward. This replaces the fragile `@BeforeEach`/`@AfterEach` try-finally pattern that developers used to write by hand.

```java
@ExtendWith(JupiterExtension.class)  // JUnit 6.1+
class CurrencyFormatterTest {

    @Test
    @DefaultLocale("de-DE")
    @DefaultTimeZone("Europe/Berlin")
    void format_germanLocale_usesCommaDecimalSeparator() {
        CurrencyFormatter formatter = new CurrencyFormatter();
        String result = formatter.format(1_234.56, Currency.getInstance("EUR"));
        // German locale: 1.234,56 EUR
        assertThat(result).isEqualTo("1.234,56 EUR");
    }

    @Test
    @DefaultLocale("en-US")
    @DefaultTimeZone("America/New_York")
    void format_usLocale_usesPeriodDecimalSeparator() {
        CurrencyFormatter formatter = new CurrencyFormatter();
        String result = formatter.format(1_234.56, Currency.getInstance("USD"));
        assertThat(result).isEqualTo("$1,234.56");
    }

    @Test
    @DefaultLocale("ja-JP")
    void parseDate_japaneseLocale_recognizesEraFormat() {
        DateParser parser = new DateParser();
        LocalDate date = parser.parse("令和7年1月15日");
        assertThat(date).isEqualTo(LocalDate.of(2025, 1, 15));
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `@DefaultLocale` and `@DefaultTimeZone` mutate JVM-global state (`Locale.setDefault()`, `TimeZone.setDefault()`), which makes them unsafe when tests run in parallel within the same JVM. JUnit 6.1 mitigates this by serializing tests annotated with these annotations (via an internal resource lock), but if you use `@Execution(CONCURRENT)` at the class level and mix locale-sensitive and locale-insensitive tests in the same class, the lock still allows concurrent execution of the non-annotated tests, which may inherit a mid-mutation locale state. Run locale-sensitive tests in their own dedicated class to avoid cross-contamination. [official]

---

### Pattern 221 — `@RestClientTest` for HTTP Client Slice Testing with `MockRestServiceServer`

`@RestClientTest` loads only the beans needed to test a component that uses `RestClient`, `RestTemplate`, or `WebClient` as an HTTP client — the slice auto-configures a `MockRestServiceServer` (or `MockWebServer` equivalent) without booting the web layer or database layer.

```java
@RestClientTest(WeatherApiClient.class)
class WeatherApiClientTest {

    @Autowired WeatherApiClient client;
    @Autowired MockRestServiceServer server;

    @Test
    void getCurrentWeather_success_returnsParsedResponse() {
        server.expect(requestTo("/weather/current?city=London"))
            .andExpect(method(HttpMethod.GET))
            .andExpect(header("Accept", "application/json"))
            .andRespond(withSuccess("""
                {
                  "city": "London",
                  "tempC": 12.5,
                  "condition": "Cloudy"
                }
                """, MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON));

        WeatherReport report = client.getCurrentWeather("London");

        assertThat(report.city()).isEqualTo("London");
        assertThat(report.tempC()).isEqualTo(12.5);
        server.verify();
    }

    @Test
    void getCurrentWeather_serverError_throwsWeatherApiException() {
        server.expect(requestTo("/weather/current?city=InvalidCity"))
            .andRespond(withServerError());

        assertThatThrownBy(() -> client.getCurrentWeather("InvalidCity"))
            .isInstanceOf(WeatherApiException.class)
            .hasMessageContaining("500");
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `MockRestServiceServer` validates that all registered expectations were fulfilled via `server.verify()` — calling `verify()` in an `@AfterEach` guarantees no unexpected interactions sneak through. However, `MockRestServiceServer` binds to a single `RestTemplate` or `RestClient` bean in the context; if your `WeatherApiClient` uses a `@Qualifier`-ed template, you must wire the `MockRestServiceServer` to the same qualified bean using `MockRestServiceServer.createServer(qualifiedRestTemplate)` rather than relying on auto-configuration. [official]

---

### Pattern 222 — `@Sql` + `@SqlMergeMode(MERGE)` for Per-Test Database State Composition

`@Sql` executes SQL scripts before (or after) a test method or class. When both a class-level and a method-level `@Sql` annotation are present, the default `SqlMergeMode.OVERRIDE` discards the class-level scripts. Switching to `@SqlMergeMode(MERGE)` runs class-level scripts first, then method-level scripts, enabling a "base state + delta" pattern for data-driven integration tests.

```java
@DataJpaTest
@AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = AutoConfigureTestDatabase.Replace.NONE)
@Sql(scripts = "/sql/base-catalog.sql")               // class-level: seed reference data
@SqlMergeMode(SqlMergeMode.MergeMode.MERGE)           // method-level @Sql adds to class-level
class ProductSearchTest {

    @Autowired ProductRepository repo;

    @Test
    @Sql("/sql/search-test-products.sql")              // runs AFTER base-catalog.sql
    void search_byCategory_returnsMatchingProducts() {
        List<Product> found = repo.findByCategoryId("cat-electronics");
        assertThat(found).hasSize(3)
            .extracting(Product::getSku)
            .containsExactlyInAnyOrder("TV-001", "PHONE-001", "LAPTOP-001");
    }

    @Test
    @Sql(scripts = "/sql/discontinued-products.sql",
         executionPhase = Sql.ExecutionPhase.AFTER_TEST_METHOD)  // cleanup
    void getActive_excludesDiscontinued() {
        List<Product> active = repo.findAllActive();
        assertThat(active).noneMatch(p -> p.getStatus() == ProductStatus.DISCONTINUED);
    }

    @Test   // no method-level @Sql — only base-catalog.sql runs
    void count_baselineData_exactlyMatchesScript() {
        assertThat(repo.count()).isEqualTo(5L);  // exactly what base-catalog.sql inserts
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `@SqlMergeMode(MERGE)` at the class level applies to every method; if one test genuinely needs to start from a clean slate (no class-level data), you must override with `@Sql(scripts = "/sql/reset.sql")` at the method level and keep `OVERRIDE` semantics — which requires explicitly re-annotating with `@SqlMergeMode(OVERRIDE)` on that method. Scripts execute within the test transaction by default, so they are rolled back automatically; but scripts with `executionPhase = AFTER_TEST_METHOD` run after transaction commit, so cleanup scripts should be idempotent (using `DELETE FROM … WHERE …` rather than `TRUNCATE`). [official]

---

### Pattern 223 — `WireMock` Stateful Scenarios for Multi-Step HTTP Protocol Testing

WireMock's Scenario API lets you model HTTP interactions that change state — retry-after-transient-error, OAuth token refresh, pagination — by assigning stubs to named states and declaring transitions via `willSetStateTo`.

```java
@ExtendWith(WireMockExtension.class)
class RetryingApiClientTest {

    @RegisterExtension
    static WireMockExtension wm = WireMockExtension.newInstance()
        .options(wireMockConfig().dynamicPort())
        .build();

    @Test
    void client_retriesOnce_thenSucceeds() {
        // First call: transient 503
        wm.stubFor(get(urlEqualTo("/api/data"))
            .inScenario("RetryScenario")
            .whenScenarioStateIs(STARTED)
            .willReturn(aResponse().withStatus(503))
            .willSetStateTo("AfterFirstFailure"));

        // Second call (retry): 200 OK
        wm.stubFor(get(urlEqualTo("/api/data"))
            .inScenario("RetryScenario")
            .whenScenarioStateIs("AfterFirstFailure")
            .willReturn(aResponse()
                .withStatus(200)
                .withHeader("Content-Type", "application/json")
                .withBody("""{"value": 42}""")));

        ApiClient client = new ApiClient(
            "http://localhost:" + wm.getPort(), maxRetries(1));

        ApiResponse response = client.fetchData();

        assertThat(response.value()).isEqualTo(42);
        wm.verify(2, getRequestedFor(urlEqualTo("/api/data")));
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** Scenario state is global to the WireMock server instance — if multiple tests run in parallel and share the same `WireMockExtension`, they will corrupt each other's scenario state. Declare the `@RegisterExtension` as an instance field (not `static`) when running tests in parallel, so each test method gets its own WireMock server. The cost is port acquisition overhead; mitigate with `dynamicPort()` and avoid `static` when parallelism is enabled. [community]

---

### Pattern 224 — `AssertJ` `satisfiesExactlyInAnyOrder` for Order-Agnostic Collection Contracts

When asserting that a collection contains exactly the right elements but order is unspecified (e.g., a query result sorted by DB implementation), `containsExactlyInAnyOrder` with scalar values works — but when each element needs multi-field assertions, `satisfiesExactlyInAnyOrder` lets you provide one lambda per expected element, applied in any matching order.

```java
@Test
void findTopContributors_returnsThreeContributorsWithCorrectFields() {
    List<Contributor> top = contributorService.findTop(3);

    assertThat(top).satisfiesExactlyInAnyOrder(
        c -> {
            assertThat(c.getUsername()).isEqualTo("alice");
            assertThat(c.getCommitCount()).isGreaterThanOrEqualTo(100);
            assertThat(c.getBadges()).contains("top-10");
        },
        c -> {
            assertThat(c.getUsername()).isEqualTo("bob");
            assertThat(c.getCommitCount()).isGreaterThanOrEqualTo(50);
        },
        c -> {
            assertThat(c.getUsername()).isEqualTo("carol");
            assertThat(c.getRole()).isEqualTo(ContributorRole.MAINTAINER);
        }
    );
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `satisfiesExactlyInAnyOrder` uses a brute-force matching algorithm: each consumer is tried against each element, so the complexity is O(n!) in the worst case. For collections larger than ~10 elements this becomes slow; prefer `usingRecursiveFieldByFieldElementComparator` with `containsExactlyInAnyOrderElementsOf` for large collections. Also note that `satisfiesExactlyInAnyOrder` requires the collection size to match the number of lambdas exactly — use `satisfies` (varargs) when you want subset assertions or have a variable-size collection. [official]

---

### Pattern 225 — `@AutoConfigureMetrics` + Micrometer `SimpleMeterRegistry` for Metric Assertions in Slice Tests

Slice tests do not boot the full Spring actuator stack, so `MeterRegistry` is not available by default. Adding `@AutoConfigureMetrics` to a slice test wires a `SimpleMeterRegistry` that accumulates counter increments, timer recordings, and gauge snapshots in memory — assertable in the test body.

```java
@DataJpaTest
@AutoConfigureMetrics
class OrderRepositoryMetricsTest {

    @Autowired OrderRepository repo;
    @Autowired MeterRegistry meterRegistry;

    @Test
    void saveOrder_incrementsSavedCounter() {
        long before = meterRegistry.counter("order.saved").count();
        repo.save(new Order("ORD-METRICS-1", OrderStatus.PENDING));

        assertThat(meterRegistry.counter("order.saved").count())
            .isEqualTo(before + 1);
    }

    @Test
    void findByStatus_recordsQueryTimer() {
        repo.findByStatus(OrderStatus.PENDING);

        Timer timer = meterRegistry.find("order.query")
            .tag("status", "PENDING")
            .timer();

        assertThat(timer).isNotNull();
        assertThat(timer.count()).isGreaterThanOrEqualTo(1);
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `SimpleMeterRegistry` does not enforce uniqueness of meter names across tag dimensions the same way a production `PrometheusMeterRegistry` does — a counter registered with `{"status": "PENDING"}` and one with `{"status": "SHIPPED"}` are distinct meters in `SimpleMeterRegistry` but share the same metric name. When asserting on `.count()` be careful to use `.find("name").tag("k", "v").counter()` rather than `.get("name")` which throws if there are multiple meters with that name. [community]

---

### Community Gotchas — Cycle 53

**`@Transactional` on a `@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT)` test method does NOT roll back — the test method runs in a different thread than the HTTP request handler, so the test's transaction is never propagated to the servlet container's thread pool — WHY: Spring's `TransactionSynchronizationManager` uses `ThreadLocal` storage. The test method's thread opens a transaction and registers it in its own `ThreadLocal`, but the HTTP server dispatches the request handler on a separate thread from the embedded Tomcat/Jetty thread pool. The handler opens its own transaction, commits it, and the test's `ThreadLocal` transaction never wraps the handler's work. Fix: use `MOCK` web environment for transactional rollback, or clean up test data explicitly in `@AfterEach` when using `RANDOM_PORT`. Never rely on `@Transactional` for cleanup in full-server integration tests.**

**Mockito's `STRICT_STUBS` mode throws `UnnecessaryStubbingException` when a stub is defined in `@BeforeEach` but only some tests in the class exercise it — the error message points at the stub definition line, not the test that doesn't use it, leading developers to incorrectly delete the stub rather than wrapping it in `lenient()` — WHY: Mockito validates stubbing usage at test teardown by checking whether each registered `OngoingStubbing` was ever matched. Stubs defined in `@BeforeEach` are evaluated per-test but the strictness check runs per-test-method teardown; a stub that is only needed in 3 of 5 tests will fail the 2 tests that don't invoke it. Fix: wrap shared defensive stubs with `lenient().when(...)` instead of plain `when(...)` — this preserves the strict check for all non-lenient stubs while suppressing the false positive for intentionally shared setup.**

**Testcontainers container fields declared as `static` in a `@Nested` test class are NOT treated as static by the `@Testcontainers` extension — the extension processes `@Container` fields on the declaring class, and nested classes are treated as instance-level, so the container is started and stopped once per test method rather than once per class, causing extreme slowness — WHY: `@Testcontainers` extension reflects over the test instance to find `@Container` fields. For a `@Nested` class, the outer class's static lifecycle applies to the outer class's `@Container` fields, but the nested class is a separate class hierarchy. `static` fields in `@Nested` classes are not reachable via `@BeforeAll`/`@AfterAll` class-lifecycle hooks. Fix: move shared containers to the outer class as `static` fields with `@Container`, or use `@BeforeAll`/`@AfterAll` in the nested class with `@TestInstance(Lifecycle.PER_CLASS)` and start/stop the container manually.**

**`AssertJ` `satisfiesExactlyInAnyOrder` with a collection that contains duplicate elements matching the same consumer lambda causes an `AssertionError` even when the collection is logically correct — if two elements match the same lambda, the remaining element has no consumer left and the assertion fails — WHY: `satisfiesExactlyInAnyOrder` performs a one-to-one mapping between consumers and elements. It uses a bipartite matching algorithm that assigns each element to exactly one consumer. If two elements both satisfy consumer #1 and neither satisfies consumer #2, the algorithm fails even though both elements are "valid". Fix: write discriminating lambdas that uniquely identify each expected element (add an ID assertion), or use `allSatisfy` when you want every element to meet the same condition.**

**`@DataJpaTest` with a custom `@EntityListener` that injects a Spring bean via `@Autowired` will fail with `NullPointerException` on the injected field because `@DataJpaTest` does not load `ApplicationContext`-aware JPA infrastructure by default — the `EntityListener` is instantiated by JPA, not by Spring, so Spring's `@Autowired` injection never runs — WHY: The JPA `EntityListenerFactory` (Hibernate's `BeanContainer`) delegates to the Spring `BeanFactory` only if `hibernate.resource.beans.container` is configured pointing to `SpringBeanContainer`. `@DataJpaTest` auto-configures this bridge, but only for listeners declared as Spring-managed beans. If the listener is not a `@Component` or is not registered in a `@EntityListeners` annotation visible to the slice's component scan, the bridge is not invoked. Fix: annotate the listener class with `@Component` and add its package to the `@DataJpaTest` component scan, or declare it as a `@TestConfiguration` `@Bean`. Verify with `SpringBeanContainer` in the Hibernate `SessionFactory` configuration.**

## Cycle 54 — 2026-05-14

### New Patterns

**Pattern 226: `MockMvcTester` — AssertJ-fluent MockMvc API in Spring Boot 3.4+** [official]
Spring Boot 3.4 introduced `MockMvcTester` as a fluent AssertJ-native alternative to `MockMvc`. Instead of `andExpect(status().isOk())` chains, `MockMvcTester` returns an `MvcTestResult` that integrates directly with AssertJ's `assertThat`. This eliminates the awkward mixing of Hamcrest and AssertJ and surfaces compilation errors for response body assertions.

```java
@WebMvcTest(OrderController.class)
class OrderControllerTest {

    @Autowired
    private MockMvcTester mvc;

    @MockitoBean
    private OrderService orderService;

    @Test
    void getOrder_returnsOrderJson() {
        given(orderService.findById(42L))
            .willReturn(new Order(42L, "ORD-42", OrderStatus.SHIPPED));

        assertThat(mvc.get().uri("/orders/42"))
            .hasStatusOk()
            .hasContentTypeCompatibleWith(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
            .bodyJson()
            .extractingPath("$.status")
            .isEqualTo("SHIPPED");
    }

    @Test
    void createOrder_returns201WithLocation() {
        given(orderService.create(any()))
            .willReturn(new Order(99L, "ORD-NEW", OrderStatus.PENDING));

        assertThat(mvc.post().uri("/orders")
            .contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
            .content("{\"ref\":\"ORD-NEW\"}"))
            .hasStatus(HttpStatus.CREATED)
            .headers().containsKey("Location");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `MockMvcTester` requires Spring Boot 3.4+ and the `spring-boot-webmvc-test` module. Existing test classes using raw `MockMvc` can coexist — you do not need to migrate all tests at once. However, `MvcTestResult` does not implement `AutoCloseable`, so resource-leak warnings from static analysis tools may appear; suppress with `@SuppressWarnings("resource")` or wrap in try-with-resources. The fluent body assertions over JSON use `JsonPathResultMatchers` internally and require Jackson on the test classpath. [official]

---

**Pattern 227: `RestTestClient` — unified fluent HTTP test client for both mock and live environments** [official]
Spring Boot 3.4 introduced `RestTestClient`, which wraps either `MockMvc` (for `MOCK` environment) or a real HTTP client (for `RANDOM_PORT` / `DEFINED_PORT`). A single test class can switch environments by changing `@SpringBootTest`'s `webEnvironment` without modifying assertion code, enabling promotion from unit to integration test without rewriting assertions.

```java
@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = SpringBootTest.WebEnvironment.RANDOM_PORT)
@AutoConfigureRestTestClient
class OrderIntegrationTest {

    @Autowired
    private RestTestClient restClient;

    @Test
    void listOrders_returnsPagedResult() {
        restClient.get().uri("/orders?page=0&size=10")
            .exchange()
            .expectStatus().isOk()
            .expectBody()
            .jsonPath("$.content").isArray()
            .jsonPath("$.totalElements").value(greaterThanOrEqualTo(0));
    }

    @Test
    void createOrder_thenRetrieve() {
        String location = restClient.post().uri("/orders")
            .contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
            .bodyValue("{\"ref\":\"ORD-INTEGRATION-1\"}")
            .exchange()
            .expectStatus().isCreated()
            .returnResult(Void.class)
            .getResponseHeaders().getFirst("Location");

        assertThat(location).isNotNull();

        restClient.get().uri(location)
            .exchange()
            .expectStatus().isOk()
            .expectBody(Order.class)
            .value(o -> assertThat(o.ref()).isEqualTo("ORD-INTEGRATION-1"));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `RestTestClient` unifies the API surface but requires importing `spring-boot-resttestclient`. In `MOCK` mode it delegates to `MockMvcTester` under the hood — so mocked beans work. In `RANDOM_PORT` mode it makes real network calls and `@MockitoBean` replacements only affect the server-side context, not transport-level concerns. Customise with `RestTestClientBuilderCustomizer` beans (e.g., to add auth headers) rather than per-test configuration to keep tests DRY. [official]

---

**Pattern 228: `@AutoConfigureTracing` + `TestObservationRegistry` for distributed-trace assertions** [official]
`@AutoConfigureTracing` (from `spring-boot-micrometer-tracing-test`) wires a no-op `Tracer` and a `TestObservationRegistry` into slice and integration tests. The registry accumulates all started observations, enabling assertions on span names, key-value tags, and the presence of parent-child span relationships without hitting a real Zipkin/Jaeger endpoint.

```java
@WebMvcTest(OrderController.class)
@AutoConfigureTracing
class OrderControllerTracingTest {

    @Autowired MockMvcTester mvc;
    @Autowired TestObservationRegistry observationRegistry;
    @MockitoBean OrderService orderService;

    @BeforeEach
    void resetRegistry() {
        observationRegistry.clear();
    }

    @Test
    void getOrder_createsSpanWithOrderIdTag() throws Exception {
        given(orderService.findById(42L))
            .willReturn(new Order(42L, "ORD-42", OrderStatus.PENDING));

        assertThat(mvc.get().uri("/orders/42")).hasStatusOk();

        TestObservationRegistryAssert.assertThat(observationRegistry)
            .hasObservationWithNameEqualTo("http.server.requests")
            .that()
            .hasHighCardinalityKeyValue("http.url", "/orders/42")
            .hasLowCardinalityKeyValue("http.status_code", "200");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `TestObservationRegistry` only accumulates observations from beans wired through the `ObservationRegistry` bean in the test context. Custom `@EventListener` or AOP advice that bypasses `ObservationRegistry` will not appear in assertions. Also, `clear()` in `@BeforeEach` is essential — failing to clear leaves stale observations from previous tests and causes false positives when using `hasObservationWithNameEqualTo`. The registry is not thread-safe across parallel test execution; set `junit.jupiter.execution.parallel.enabled=false` for tracing tests. [official]

---

**Pattern 229: `@SpringBootTest(useMainMethod = ALWAYS)` for testing custom `SpringApplication` configuration** [official]
By default `@SpringBootTest` constructs the `ApplicationContext` via reflection, bypassing any customisation applied in the `main` method (custom `SpringApplication` builder flags, additional listeners, deferred closers). `UseMainMethod.ALWAYS` invokes the actual `main(String[])` method to build the context, ensuring test startup mirrors production startup exactly.

```java
@SpringBootTest(
    useMainMethod = SpringBootTest.UseMainMethod.ALWAYS,
    args = "--app.feature.flag=true"
)
class ApplicationMainMethodTest {

    @Autowired
    Environment env;

    @Autowired
    ApplicationContext ctx;

    @Test
    void featureFlag_isLoadedFromArgs() {
        assertThat(env.getProperty("app.feature.flag")).isEqualTo("true");
    }

    @Test
    void customBannerListenerIsRegistered() {
        // Verify a listener registered in main() is present
        assertThat(ctx.containsBean("customBannerListener")).isTrue();
    }

    @Test
    void applicationContextLoads() {
        assertThat(ctx).isNotNull();
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `UseMainMethod.ALWAYS` requires the `main` class to be discoverable (the test must be in the same package tree as `@SpringBootApplication`). It also means any `SpringApplication.exit()` calls in `main` will terminate the context during test teardown — guard with `SpringApplication.setRegisterShutdownHook(false)` or restructure the `main` to avoid early exits. `WHEN_AVAILABLE` is a safer default that falls back gracefully when the main method is absent. [official]

---

**Pattern 230: JUnit 6 `@ParameterizedClass` for contract-style interface testing** [official]
JUnit 6 introduces `@ParameterizedClass`, which parameterizes the entire test class rather than individual test methods. This is ideal for testing multiple implementations of the same interface with a shared contract test suite — each implementation is injected into the class constructor via the parameterization source.

```java
@ParameterizedClass
@MethodSource("implementations")
class CacheContractTest {

    static Stream<Cache> implementations() {
        return Stream.of(
            new InMemoryCache(100),
            new RedisCache(redisTemplate),
            new CaffeineCache(Caffeine.newBuilder().maximumSize(100).build())
        );
    }

    private final Cache cache;

    CacheContractTest(Cache cache) {
        this.cache = cache;
    }

    @Test
    void put_thenGet_returnsValue() {
        cache.put("key1", "value1");
        assertThat(cache.get("key1")).isEqualTo("value1");
    }

    @Test
    void get_absentKey_returnsNull() {
        assertThat(cache.get("absent-" + UUID.randomUUID())).isNull();
    }

    @Test
    void evict_removesKey() {
        cache.put("evict-me", "v");
        cache.evict("evict-me");
        assertThat(cache.get("evict-me")).isNull();
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@ParameterizedClass` requires JUnit 6.0+ and is not backward-compatible with JUnit 5. Each parameterized instance creates a separate class lifecycle — `@BeforeAll` / `@AfterAll` methods run once per parameterized instance, not once per the entire suite. For shared expensive resources (databases, containers), declare them as `static` fields in an outer class and reference via field access, or use a shared `@ExtendWith` extension. `@DisplayName` on the class is ignored; the display name comes from the parameterization source. [official]

---

**Pattern 231: JUnit 6 Dynamic Parallel Execution with `@ResourceLock` for shared state** [official]
JUnit 6's parallel execution engine can deadlock or corrupt shared state when tests manipulate singletons, static fields, or external services. `@ResourceLock` declares named resource dependencies; the engine serialises tests that lock the same resource while allowing fully independent tests to run in parallel, giving fine-grained control without disabling parallelism globally.

```java
@Execution(ExecutionMode.CONCURRENT)
class OrderServiceParallelTest {

    @Autowired
    private OrderService service;

    @Test
    @ResourceLock("order-database")
    void createOrder_persistsToDatabase() {
        Order saved = service.create(new CreateOrderRequest("ORD-LOCK-1"));
        assertThat(saved.id()).isPositive();
    }

    @Test
    @ResourceLock(value = "order-database", mode = ResourceAccessMode.READ)
    void listOrders_doesNotModifyDatabase() {
        List<Order> orders = service.findAll();
        assertThat(orders).isNotNull();
    }

    @Test
    // No @ResourceLock — runs fully concurrently with other unlocked tests
    void priceCalculation_isPureFunction() {
        assertThat(service.calculateTotal(List.of(
            new LineItem("SKU-1", 2, new BigDecimal("9.99"))
        ))).isEqualByComparingTo("19.98");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@ResourceLock` uses string-based resource names — typos create silent failures where two tests that should be serialised run concurrently. Prefer constants (`Resources.SYSTEM_PROPERTIES` is built-in) or a `ResourceLocks` class with `static final String` fields. READ locks allow concurrent readers; WRITE locks are exclusive. Misclassifying a mutating test as READ causes data races. Combine with `junit.jupiter.execution.parallel.config.strategy=fixed` and `parallelism=4` for predictable CI throughput. [official]

---

**Pattern 232: `@JsonTest` with `JacksonTester` for serialisation contract tests** [official]
`@JsonTest` creates a minimal Spring context containing only Jackson (or Gson/Jsonb) configuration beans. `JacksonTester<T>` provides `write()` and `parse()` helpers with AssertJ-friendly assertions, making it the right tool for verifying JSON shape, field inclusion/exclusion, and date format correctness without loading the full web layer.

```java
@JsonTest
class OrderJsonTest {

    @Autowired
    private JacksonTester<Order> json;

    @Test
    void serialise_includesAllPublicFields() throws Exception {
        Order order = new Order(1L, "ORD-JSON-1", OrderStatus.PENDING,
            Instant.parse("2026-05-14T10:00:00Z"));

        assertThat(json.write(order))
            .hasJsonPath("$.id")
            .hasJsonPath("$.ref")
            .hasJsonPath("$.status")
            .hasJsonPath("$.createdAt");
    }

    @Test
    void serialise_createdAt_isIso8601() throws Exception {
        Order order = new Order(1L, "ORD-JSON-2", OrderStatus.SHIPPED,
            Instant.parse("2026-05-14T10:00:00Z"));

        assertThat(json.write(order))
            .extractingJsonPathStringValue("$.createdAt")
            .isEqualTo("2026-05-14T10:00:00Z");
    }

    @Test
    void deserialise_fromJsonFile_populatesFields() throws Exception {
        Order order = json.readObject("/order-sample.json");

        assertThat(order.ref()).isEqualTo("ORD-SAMPLE");
        assertThat(order.status()).isEqualTo(OrderStatus.PENDING);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@JsonTest` loads Jackson `ObjectMapper` customisations defined as `@JsonComponent`, `Jackson2ObjectMapperBuilderCustomizer`, and `@EnableJackson2Modules` beans from the `@SpringBootApplication` context. Custom `Module` beans that are not auto-configured (e.g., registered programmatically in a `@Configuration` class not visible to `@JsonTest`) will not be loaded — the serialisation contract test will pass but the production behaviour will differ. Explicitly import missing configuration with `@Import(MyJacksonConfig.class)` on the test class. [official]

---

**Pattern 233: `@DataR2dbcTest` for reactive repository slice tests with R2DBC** [official]
`@DataR2dbcTest` is the reactive counterpart of `@DataJpaTest`. It auto-configures R2DBC infrastructure (connection factory, `R2dbcEntityTemplate`, `DatabaseClient`) and limits the component scan to `@Repository` and related beans, without starting the full Spring context. Pair with an R2DBC-compatible embedded database (H2 in R2DBC mode) or a `@ServiceConnection` Testcontainer.

```java
@DataR2dbcTest
class ProductRepositoryTest {

    @Autowired
    private ProductRepository repository;

    @Autowired
    private R2dbcEntityTemplate template;

    @Test
    void findByCategory_returnsMatchingProducts() {
        template.insert(new Product(null, "Widget", "HARDWARE", new BigDecimal("9.99")))
            .block();

        StepVerifier.create(repository.findByCategory("HARDWARE"))
            .assertNext(p -> {
                assertThat(p.name()).isEqualTo("Widget");
                assertThat(p.category()).isEqualTo("HARDWARE");
            })
            .verifyComplete();
    }

    @Test
    void save_assignsGeneratedId() {
        Product saved = repository.save(
            new Product(null, "Gadget", "ELECTRONICS", new BigDecimal("49.99"))
        ).block();

        assertThat(saved).isNotNull();
        assertThat(saved.id()).isPositive();
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@DataR2dbcTest` does NOT roll back transactions automatically — unlike `@DataJpaTest` with `@Transactional`. R2DBC's reactive model means transaction propagation via `ThreadLocal` doesn't apply; use `StepVerifier` + explicit delete cleanup in `@AfterEach`, or use a fresh schema per test class with Liquibase/Flyway `@Sql` scripts. Also, H2 R2DBC dialect support lags H2 JDBC: some DDL features (e.g., `GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY`) require H2 2.2+ and the `r2dbc-h2` 1.0.0+ driver. [official]

---

**Pattern 234: `ArgumentCaptor` with generic types using `forClass` + `@Captor`** [community]
When capturing arguments of generic types (e.g., `List<Order>`, `Page<Item>`), raw `ArgumentCaptor.forClass(List.class)` causes unchecked cast warnings. The idiomatic fix is `@Captor` field injection via `MockitoExtension`, which infers the generic type from the field declaration and suppresses the warning without `@SuppressWarnings`.

```java
@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class OrderNotificationServiceTest {

    @Mock
    private NotificationGateway gateway;

    @InjectMocks
    private OrderNotificationService service;

    @Captor
    private ArgumentCaptor<List<Order>> ordersCaptor;

    @Captor
    private ArgumentCaptor<NotificationRequest<Order>> requestCaptor;

    @Test
    void dispatchBatch_sendsAllOrdersInSingleCall() {
        List<Order> orders = List.of(
            new Order(1L, "ORD-A", OrderStatus.SHIPPED),
            new Order(2L, "ORD-B", OrderStatus.SHIPPED)
        );

        service.dispatchShippedBatch(orders);

        verify(gateway).sendBatch(ordersCaptor.capture());
        assertThat(ordersCaptor.getValue())
            .hasSize(2)
            .extracting(Order::ref)
            .containsExactlyInAnyOrder("ORD-A", "ORD-B");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@Captor` fields are initialised by `MockitoExtension` before `@BeforeEach` runs, so they are safe to use in setup methods. However, `ArgumentCaptor` is not thread-safe — never share a single captor across tests in a parallel suite. Each test gets a fresh captor because `MockitoExtension` re-initialises the test instance per method. Also, calling `captor.capture()` more than once in a single `verify()` call sets up multiple capture slots; use `captor.getAllValues()` (returns `List`) when the method is called multiple times across a test. [community]

---

**Pattern 235: `@MockitoSpyBean` for partial mocking of Spring-managed beans** [official]
`@MockitoSpyBean` (Spring Framework 6.2+, replacing the deprecated `@SpyBean`) wraps an existing Spring bean with a Mockito spy, leaving real method implementations active unless overridden with `doReturn`. This is the correct tool when you need to assert that a specific method on a real bean was called, or to stub only one method of a complex service while keeping the rest functional.

```java
@SpringBootTest
class AuditServiceIntegrationTest {

    @MockitoSpyBean
    private AuditLogger auditLogger;

    @Autowired
    private OrderService orderService;

    @Test
    void createOrder_invokesAuditLogger_withCorrectEvent() {
        Order order = orderService.create(new CreateOrderRequest("ORD-SPY-1"));

        verify(auditLogger, times(1))
            .log(argThat(event ->
                event.type().equals("ORDER_CREATED") &&
                event.resourceId().equals(order.id().toString())
            ));
    }

    @Test
    void auditLogger_realMethodStillWorks() {
        // Spy does NOT stub the method — real implementation fires
        assertThatNoException().isThrownBy(() ->
            auditLogger.log(new AuditEvent("TEST_EVENT", "resource-id-1"))
        );
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@MockitoSpyBean` wraps the existing singleton bean in the `ApplicationContext`. If another bean has already cached a direct reference to the unwrapped bean (e.g., via constructor injection before the spy was applied), calls through that cached reference will NOT be intercepted by the spy. Use `@MockitoSpyBean` only when the bean under observation is injected via setter or field injection in the component that calls it, or when the calling component is also re-created as part of the test context. Spies cause `@DirtiesContext` semantics if the bean state is mutated between tests. [official]

---

**Pattern 236: WireMock `@WireMockTest` with `stubFor` for isolated HTTP client tests** [community]
`@WireMockTest` (from `wiremock-spring-boot` or `wiremock-junit5`) starts an embedded WireMock server on a random port and injects a `WireMockRuntimeInfo` parameter, making it the cleanest way to test `RestClient`, `WebClient`, or `RestTemplate` HTTP client code without Mockito. The server is reset between tests automatically.

```java
@WireMockTest
class ExchangeRateClientTest {

    private ExchangeRateClient client;

    @BeforeEach
    void setUp(WireMockRuntimeInfo wm) {
        client = new ExchangeRateClient(
            RestClient.builder()
                .baseUrl(wm.getHttpBaseUrl())
                .build()
        );
    }

    @Test
    void getRate_returnsDeserializedResponse(WireMockRuntimeInfo wm) {
        stubFor(get(urlEqualTo("/rates/USD/EUR"))
            .willReturn(aResponse()
                .withStatus(200)
                .withHeader("Content-Type", "application/json")
                .withBody("{\"from\":\"USD\",\"to\":\"EUR\",\"rate\":0.91}")));

        ExchangeRate rate = client.getRate("USD", "EUR");

        assertThat(rate.from()).isEqualTo("USD");
        assertThat(rate.rate()).isCloseTo(0.91, within(0.001));
    }

    @Test
    void getRate_500Response_throwsClientException(WireMockRuntimeInfo wm) {
        stubFor(get(urlEqualTo("/rates/USD/EUR"))
            .willReturn(serverError()));

        assertThatThrownBy(() -> client.getRate("USD", "EUR"))
            .isInstanceOf(ExchangeRateClientException.class)
            .hasMessageContaining("500");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@WireMockTest` resets all stubs and request journal between tests, so there is no state leakage. However, `verify(getRequestedFor(...))` assertions on the WireMock server are distinct from Mockito `verify()` — mixing both in one test class increases cognitive overhead. The embedded server runs in-process on a random port, which means you must wire the `baseUrl` dynamically (as shown above). Hardcoding localhost port values breaks parallelism. For Spring Boot integration, prefer `@SpringBootTest` + `@AutoConfigureWireMock` which registers the base URL as `wiremock.server.baseUrl` property automatically. [community]

---

**Pattern 237: `StepVerifier.withVirtualTime` for testing time-dependent reactive pipelines** [community]
`StepVerifier.withVirtualTime` manipulates virtual time in Project Reactor's `VirtualTimeScheduler`, allowing tests to advance the clock by seconds, minutes, or hours without actually waiting. This is the correct pattern for testing `Flux.interval`, `Mono.delay`, `retryWhen` with exponential backoff, and `timeout` operators.

```java
class RetryingOrderClientTest {

    private final RetryingOrderClient client = new RetryingOrderClient(
        httpClient, Duration.ofSeconds(1), 3 /* maxRetries */
    );

    @Test
    void fetchOrder_retriesOnServerError_thenSucceeds() {
        StepVerifier.withVirtualTime(() ->
            client.fetchOrder("ORD-RETRY-1")
        )
        .expectSubscription()
        // First attempt fails immediately; retry after 1s
        .thenAwait(Duration.ofSeconds(1))
        // Second attempt fails; retry after 2s (exponential backoff)
        .thenAwait(Duration.ofSeconds(2))
        // Third attempt succeeds
        .expectNext(new Order(1L, "ORD-RETRY-1", OrderStatus.PENDING))
        .verifyComplete();
    }

    @Test
    void fetchOrder_exhaustsRetries_emitsError() {
        StepVerifier.withVirtualTime(() ->
            client.fetchOrder("ORD-ALWAYS-FAILS")
        )
        .expectSubscription()
        .thenAwait(Duration.ofSeconds(7)) // 1 + 2 + 4 seconds of backoff
        .expectError(OrderServiceUnavailableException.class)
        .verify();
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `withVirtualTime` requires the publisher under test to be created inside the lambda passed to `withVirtualTime`, not outside it — if the publisher is created before the `VirtualTimeScheduler` is installed, time-based operators will use the real scheduler and the test will hang. Also, `VirtualTimeScheduler` is global per-thread; parallel test execution with virtual time causes flakiness unless each test creates its own `StepVerifier` with `withVirtualTime` freshly. Use `StepVerifier.create(publisher).expectTimeout(Duration.ofMillis(100)).verify()` as a quick sanity check that the operator does not block the calling thread. [community]

---

**Pattern 238: `@Sql(executionPhase = AFTER_TEST_METHOD)` for explicit database teardown** [official]
Rather than relying on `@Transactional` rollback (which does not work with `RANDOM_PORT` tests or multi-datasource setups), use `@Sql` with `executionPhase = AFTER_TEST_METHOD` to run a DELETE script after each test. Combined with `@Sql` for setup, this gives explicit, readable data lifecycle management that works in any test environment.

```java
@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = SpringBootTest.WebEnvironment.RANDOM_PORT)
@Sql(scripts = "/sql/insert-order-fixtures.sql",
     executionPhase = Sql.ExecutionPhase.BEFORE_TEST_METHOD)
@Sql(scripts = "/sql/cleanup-orders.sql",
     executionPhase = Sql.ExecutionPhase.AFTER_TEST_METHOD)
class OrderApiIntegrationTest {

    @Autowired
    private RestTestClient restClient;

    @Test
    void listOrders_returnsFixtureData() {
        restClient.get().uri("/orders")
            .exchange()
            .expectStatus().isOk()
            .expectBody()
            .jsonPath("$.content.length()").isEqualTo(3);
    }

    @Test
    @Sql(scripts = "/sql/insert-extra-orders.sql")  // Merged with class-level via @SqlMergeMode
    void listOrders_withExtraData_returnsMoreResults() {
        restClient.get().uri("/orders")
            .exchange()
            .expectStatus().isOk()
            .expectBody()
            .jsonPath("$.content.length()").isEqualTo(6);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@Sql` scripts run within the test's `SqlConfig` data source connection. If your integration test uses a different connection pool thread than the server (which it always does in `RANDOM_PORT` mode), the data inserted by `BEFORE_TEST_METHOD` is committed immediately and visible to the server. This is the desired behaviour for full-stack integration tests but means data persists between test methods if `AFTER_TEST_METHOD` cleanup fails (e.g., due to foreign key constraints). Always write `DELETE` in dependency order (child records before parent records) in cleanup scripts. Use `@SqlMergeMode(MERGE)` at class level so method-level `@Sql` adds to rather than replaces class-level scripts. [official]

---

**Pattern 239: `@ConditionalOnProperty` test configuration isolation with `@TestPropertySource`** [community]
Feature-flagged beans controlled by `@ConditionalOnProperty` can be toggled in tests via `@TestPropertySource(properties = "feature.x=true")`. This pattern tests both the enabled and disabled code paths in dedicated test classes without modifying `application.properties` or using profiles, keeping feature-flag tests self-documenting.

```java
// Test with feature ENABLED
@SpringBootTest
@TestPropertySource(properties = "feature.enhanced-search=true")
class EnhancedSearchEnabledTest {

    @Autowired
    private SearchService searchService;

    @Test
    void searchService_isEnhancedVariant() {
        assertThat(searchService).isInstanceOf(EnhancedSearchService.class);
    }

    @Test
    void search_usesVectorIndex() {
        SearchResult result = searchService.search("java testing");
        assertThat(result.indexUsed()).isEqualTo("vector");
    }
}

// Test with feature DISABLED (default)
@SpringBootTest
@TestPropertySource(properties = "feature.enhanced-search=false")
class EnhancedSearchDisabledTest {

    @Autowired
    private SearchService searchService;

    @Test
    void searchService_isFallbackVariant() {
        assertThat(searchService).isInstanceOf(BasicSearchService.class);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: Each `@TestPropertySource` override creates a distinct `ApplicationContext` key — Spring's context cache treats them as separate contexts, so the JVM may hold two full Spring contexts simultaneously. For a suite with many feature-flag permutations this multiplies memory usage and startup time. Group all tests for a given property value into a single test class, or use `@DirtiesContext(classMode = AFTER_CLASS)` to evict the context after the class finishes (at the cost of losing context reuse entirely). Prefer `@ActiveProfiles` over `@TestPropertySource` when the feature-flag maps cleanly to a profile, since profiles are a first-class context cache key. [community]

---

**Pattern 240: `@TestInstance(PER_CLASS)` + `@BeforeAll` for non-static expensive setup** [official]
By default JUnit creates a new test instance per method, requiring `@BeforeAll` methods to be `static`. `@TestInstance(Lifecycle.PER_CLASS)` creates one instance per class, allowing `@BeforeAll` to be non-static and enabling instance fields initialised in `@BeforeAll` to be used in test methods without `static` — critical when the setup object is inherently non-static (e.g., a Testcontainers container, a WireMock instance, or a loaded large dataset).

```java
@TestInstance(TestInstance.Lifecycle.PER_CLASS)
@SpringBootTest
class OrderBulkImportTest {

    @Autowired
    private OrderImportService importService;

    private List<Order> importedOrders;

    @BeforeAll
    void importTestData() throws IOException {
        // Expensive: parse a 10 000-row CSV and import
        Path csvPath = Path.of("src/test/resources/orders-bulk.csv");
        importedOrders = importService.importFromCsv(csvPath);
    }

    @Test
    void importedOrders_countMatchesFile() {
        assertThat(importedOrders).hasSize(10_000);
    }

    @Test
    void importedOrders_allHavePendingStatus() {
        assertThat(importedOrders)
            .extracting(Order::status)
            .containsOnly(OrderStatus.PENDING);
    }

    @Test
    void importedOrders_refsAreUnique() {
        assertThat(importedOrders)
            .extracting(Order::ref)
            .doesNotHaveDuplicates();
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `PER_CLASS` lifecycle means mutable instance state from one test method can leak into subsequent methods. This violates test isolation. Always treat `@TestInstance(PER_CLASS)` as a performance optimisation for READ-ONLY shared setup; never mutate `importedOrders` or any shared instance field in test methods. If tests need to modify shared state, use `@BeforeEach` to create a fresh copy. Also, `@AfterAll` with `PER_CLASS` can reference instance fields for teardown (e.g., `container.stop()`) — a significant ergonomic advantage over `static` teardown. [official]

---

### Community Gotchas — Cycle 54

**`@WebMvcTest` does NOT load `@ControllerAdvice` beans that are defined outside the controller's package and not included in the `@WebMvcTest(controllers = ...)` argument — global exception handlers silently missing from the test context cause tests to see raw exceptions rather than the mapped HTTP error responses — WHY: `@WebMvcTest` limits its component scan to the specified controller(s) and beans that implement MVC infrastructure interfaces. A `@ControllerAdvice` class that handles `MethodArgumentNotValidException` will only be loaded if it is either in the same package as the tested controller, or if `@WebMvcTest` is invoked without a `controllers` argument (full scan). When a `controllers` argument is provided, the scan is narrowed to that class and its package peers. Fix: explicitly import the advice class with `@Import(GlobalExceptionHandler.class)` on the test class, or write a dedicated `@WebMvcTest` (no `controllers` argument) test for the exception handler itself.**

**`@DynamicPropertySource` methods must be `static` — when defined as instance methods in a `@Nested` test class they are silently ignored, causing the dynamic properties to not be registered and the `ApplicationContext` to start with default property values — WHY: `@DynamicPropertySource` is processed by `DynamicPropertySourceExtension` which reflects over the test class looking for `static` methods annotated with `@DynamicPropertySource`. Instance methods are skipped without error or warning because the extension follows the same convention as `@BeforeAll`. In a `@Nested` class, the outer class's `static @DynamicPropertySource` is NOT inherited by the nested class's context. Fix: declare `@DynamicPropertySource` as a `static` method on the enclosing class and share the container reference via a `static` field, or use `@ServiceConnection` on a `static @Container` field to avoid `@DynamicPropertySource` entirely.**

**Mockito `doReturn(...).when(spy).method()` and `when(spy.method()).thenReturn(...)` have different behaviour on real method invocation — `when(spy.method()).thenReturn(...)` calls the real method BEFORE the stub is registered, which can cause `NullPointerException` or side effects even though the stub value is ultimately returned — WHY: the expression `spy.method()` in `when(spy.method())` executes as a real method call during the argument capture phase. Mockito intercepts the call and registers the stub, but the method body has already run. This is a known Mockito design constraint. Fix: ALWAYS use `doReturn(...).when(spy).method()` syntax when stubbing spy methods to avoid real method invocation. This is distinct from mock stubbing where both forms are equivalent since mocks do not have real implementations.**

**`@DataJpaTest` with `replace = AutoConfigureTestDatabase.Replace.NONE` and a PostgreSQL Testcontainer does NOT automatically apply Flyway or Liquibase migrations — the test slice excludes migration auto-configuration by default, so the schema is empty when the test's `EntityManager` initialises — WHY: `@DataJpaTest` includes `@AutoConfigureTestDatabase` which, even when set to `NONE`, still strips the `FlywayAutoConfiguration` and `LiquibaseAutoConfiguration` from the test's auto-configuration list. Only JPA-specific auto-configurations are retained. Fix: add `@AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = NONE)` AND explicitly re-add Flyway with `@ImportAutoConfiguration(FlywayAutoConfiguration.class)` on the test class, or use `@SpringBootTest` (full context) for tests that require schema migrations.**

**JUnit 6's `@Execution(CONCURRENT)` at class level does NOT make test methods within a single class run concurrently — `CONCURRENT` at class level only controls how that class is executed relative to OTHER classes in the suite — WHY: in JUnit 6's parallel execution model, the class-level `@Execution(CONCURRENT)` annotation tells the execution engine that this class may run concurrently with other top-level test classes. Within a class, the default method-level execution mode governs method parallelism, which is `SAME_THREAD` by default. To run methods within a class concurrently, annotate the class with `@Execution(CONCURRENT)` AND set `junit.jupiter.execution.parallel.mode.default=concurrent` in `junit-platform.properties`, OR add a second `@Execution(CONCURRENT)` at method level (which is redundant but explicit). Fix: set `junit.jupiter.execution.parallel.mode.classes.default=concurrent` for inter-class parallelism and `junit.jupiter.execution.parallel.mode.default=concurrent` for intra-class parallelism, and use `@ResourceLock` to guard shared state.**
