## Cycle 55 — 2026-05-14

### New Patterns

**Pattern 241: `@ParameterizedTest` with `@MethodSource` returning `Stream<Arguments>`** [official]
When test cases require multiple parameters that are complex objects, `@MethodSource` pointing to a factory method returning `Stream<Arguments>` is cleaner than `@CsvSource` (which handles strings only) and provides full type safety. The source method can be in the same class or referenced via fully qualified class name.
```java
@ParameterizedTest(name = "[{index}] {0} → {2}")
@MethodSource("discountScenarios")
void applyDiscount_computesExpectedPrice(
        String label,
        BigDecimal original,
        BigDecimal expected,
        DiscountPolicy policy) {

    BigDecimal actual = policy.apply(original);

    assertThat(actual)
        .as("discount scenario: %s", label)
        .isEqualByComparingTo(expected);
}

static Stream<Arguments> discountScenarios() {
    return Stream.of(
        Arguments.of("10% off",  new BigDecimal("100.00"), new BigDecimal("90.00"),  new PercentageDiscount(10)),
        Arguments.of("fixed £5", new BigDecimal("20.00"),  new BigDecimal("15.00"),  new FixedDiscount(5)),
        Arguments.of("no discount", new BigDecimal("50.00"), new BigDecimal("50.00"), DiscountPolicy.NONE)
    );
}
```
Tradeoff: The factory method must be `static` (unless `@TestInstance(PER_CLASS)` is used), which can be awkward when the objects depend on instance fields set up in `@BeforeEach`. For stateful test data, prefer `@BeforeEach` + a regular `@Test` per scenario, or use `@TestInstance(PER_CLASS)` so the factory method can reference instance fields. [official]

---

**Pattern 242: `assertThatThrownBy` for exception assertions with message content checks** [official]
JUnit 5's `assertThrows` returns the exception but requires chained calls to inspect message and cause. AssertJ's `assertThatThrownBy` provides a fluent chain that avoids intermediate variables and makes the assertion intent immediately readable.
```java
@Test
void processOrder_throwsWhenInventoryInsufficient() {
    var order = new Order("SKU-99", 1000);

    assertThatThrownBy(() -> inventoryService.reserve(order))
        .isInstanceOf(InsufficientInventoryException.class)
        .hasMessageContaining("SKU-99")
        .hasMessageContaining("requested=1000")
        .satisfies(ex -> {
            var typed = (InsufficientInventoryException) ex;
            assertThat(typed.getAvailable()).isZero();
        });
}
```
Tradeoff: `assertThatThrownBy` swallows the stack trace context in failure messages unless `.withFailMessage()` is added. When the lambda does NOT throw, AssertJ reports "Expected code to raise a throwable" with no indication of what succeeded — add a `@DisplayName` or `.as("...")` prefix to provide context in CI logs. [official]

---

**Pattern 243: `@RegisterExtension` for programmatic JUnit 5 extension registration with constructor injection** [official]
`@ExtendWith` registers extensions declaratively but cannot pass parameters to them. `@RegisterExtension` on a `static` or instance field allows constructing the extension with specific configuration, enabling parameterised extensions like a WireMock server on a specific port or a custom database extension with a given schema name.
```java
class PaymentGatewayClientTest {

    @RegisterExtension
    static WireMockExtension wireMock = WireMockExtension.newInstance()
        .options(wireMockConfig().port(8089).usingFilesUnderClasspath("wiremock/payment"))
        .configureStaticDsl(false)
        .build();

    @RegisterExtension
    @Order(2)
    final DatabaseExtension db = new DatabaseExtension("payment_schema");

    @Test
    void chargeCard_sendsCorrectPayload() {
        wireMock.stubFor(post(urlEqualTo("/v1/charges"))
            .willReturn(aResponse().withStatus(200)
                .withBodyFile("charge-success.json")));

        var result = client.charge(new ChargeRequest("tok_test", 5000, "GBP"));

        assertThat(result.status()).isEqualTo(ChargeStatus.SUCCEEDED);
        wireMock.verify(1, postRequestedFor(urlEqualTo("/v1/charges")));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@RegisterExtension static` fields are lifecycle-shared across ALL test methods (like `@BeforeAll`), while instance fields reset per method. Mixing `@Order` between static and instance extensions requires understanding JUnit's two-phase registration: static extensions are registered first regardless of `@Order`, so an instance extension with `@Order(1)` will still execute after ALL static extensions. [official]

---

**Pattern 244: `MockedStatic` try-with-resources for scoped static mocking** [official]
Mockito's `mockStatic()` installs a thread-local interceptor for an entire class's static methods. Crucially it must be closed after the test; using try-with-resources guarantees cleanup even if the test throws, preventing the interceptor from leaking into subsequent tests via the `MockitoStaticInterceptor` thread-local.
```java
@Test
void generateOrderId_usesCurrentTimestamp() {
    var fixedInstant = Instant.parse("2026-01-15T10:00:00Z");

    try (MockedStatic<Instant> mockedInstant = mockStatic(Instant.class)) {
        mockedInstant.when(Instant::now).thenReturn(fixedInstant);

        String orderId = OrderIdGenerator.generate();

        assertThat(orderId).startsWith("ORD-20260115-");
        mockedInstant.verify(Instant::now, times(1));
    }
    // After close: Instant.now() restored to real implementation
    assertThat(Instant.now()).isAfter(fixedInstant);
}
```
Tradeoff: `mockStatic` is thread-local, so if the code under test spawns virtual threads or platform threads that also call the static method, those calls go to the REAL implementation — the interception only applies to the thread that called `mockStatic`. For multi-threaded static mocking, inject a `Clock` or `Supplier<Instant>` instead and avoid static mocking entirely. [official]

---

**Pattern 245: `ArgumentCaptor` with generic types using `@Captor` annotation to avoid unchecked-cast warnings** [official]
Inline `ArgumentCaptor.forClass(List.class)` loses generic type information and requires unchecked casts. `@Captor` on a typed captor field preserves the generic type signature so AssertJ extractors work without `@SuppressWarnings("unchecked")`.
```java
@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class NotificationDispatcherTest {

    @Mock
    private NotificationRepository repo;

    @Captor
    private ArgumentCaptor<List<Notification>> notificationsCaptor;

    @InjectMocks
    private NotificationDispatcher dispatcher;

    @Test
    void dispatch_savesAllNotificationsInSingleBatch() {
        var users = List.of(new User("alice"), new User("bob"));

        dispatcher.notifyAll(users, "Welcome to the platform");

        verify(repo).saveAll(notificationsCaptor.capture());
        List<Notification> saved = notificationsCaptor.getValue();
        assertThat(saved)
            .hasSize(2)
            .extracting(Notification::recipient)
            .containsExactlyInAnyOrder("alice", "bob");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@Captor` fields are reset between tests by `MockitoExtension`, so they are safe to share across methods in the same class. However, if `verify(...).someMethod(captor.capture())` is called multiple times in the same test, `getValue()` returns only the argument from the LAST invocation; use `getAllValues()` to get all captured values in invocation order. [official]

---

**Pattern 246: `@Nested` class grouping with shared `@BeforeEach` for BDD Given/When/Then structure** [official]
Grouping related tests in `@Nested` classes with inner-class `@BeforeEach` methods allows a BDD-style "Given" setup to be shared across multiple "When/Then" test methods without code duplication or test method names encoding the setup.
```java
@DisplayName("ShoppingCart")
class ShoppingCartTest {

    private ShoppingCart cart;

    @BeforeEach
    void createEmptyCart() {
        cart = new ShoppingCart(Currency.EUR);
    }

    @Nested
    @DisplayName("when empty")
    class WhenEmpty {

        @Test
        @DisplayName("total is zero")
        void totalIsZero() {
            assertThat(cart.total()).isEqualByComparingTo(BigDecimal.ZERO);
        }

        @Test
        @DisplayName("checkout throws EmptyCartException")
        void checkoutThrows() {
            assertThatThrownBy(() -> cart.checkout())
                .isInstanceOf(EmptyCartException.class);
        }
    }

    @Nested
    @DisplayName("when items added")
    class WhenItemsAdded {

        @BeforeEach
        void addTwoItems() {
            cart.add(new Item("Book", new BigDecimal("12.99")));
            cart.add(new Item("Pen",  new BigDecimal("1.50")));
        }

        @Test
        @DisplayName("total reflects sum of items")
        void totalIsCorrect() {
            assertThat(cart.total()).isEqualByComparingTo("14.49");
        }

        @Test
        @DisplayName("remove item reduces total")
        void removeReducesTotal() {
            cart.remove("Book");
            assertThat(cart.total()).isEqualByComparingTo("1.50");
        }
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: Deep nesting (3+ levels) of `@Nested` classes produces test trees that are hard to navigate in IDE test explorers. Each `@Nested` class's `@BeforeEach` executes AFTER the enclosing class's `@BeforeEach` — this ordering is correct but can surprise developers who expect inner `@BeforeEach` to run independently. Maximum recommended nesting depth is 2 (outer + one inner level). [official]

---

**Pattern 247: `Awaitility` with `conditionEvaluationListener` for diagnosing flaky async assertions** [community]
When async conditions fail intermittently, the default Awaitility timeout error shows only the final state. Registering a `ConditionEvaluationListener` logs every evaluation attempt, enabling diagnosis of whether the condition was "almost met" (transiently true then false) or never met at all.
```java
@Test
void orderProcessor_updatesStatusAsynchronously() {
    var order = orderRepository.save(new Order("SKU-42", 3));
    eventBus.publish(new ProcessOrderEvent(order.id()));

    await()
        .atMost(10, SECONDS)
        .pollInterval(Duration.ofMillis(250))
        .conditionEvaluationListener(condition ->
            log.debug("poll attempt: order status={}, elapsed={}ms",
                orderRepository.findById(order.id()).map(Order::status).orElse(null),
                condition.getElapsedTimeInMS()))
        .failFast("order was cancelled — no point waiting",
            () -> orderRepository.findById(order.id())
                .map(o -> o.status() == OrderStatus.CANCELLED)
                .orElse(false))
        .untilAsserted(() -> {
            var updated = orderRepository.findById(order.id()).orElseThrow();
            assertThat(updated.status()).isEqualTo(OrderStatus.PROCESSED);
        });
}
```
Tradeoff: `conditionEvaluationListener` fires on every poll, potentially producing hundreds of log lines for long-running awaits. Use `Logger.isDebugEnabled()` guards or only enable in CI failure contexts via a system property. The `failFast` overload takes a `Callable<Boolean>` — if it throws, the exception is wrapped and `untilAsserted` never runs, which can obscure the real failure mode. [community]

---

**Pattern 248: `@SpringBootTest` with `webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT` + `@LocalServerPort` for full HTTP integration tests** [official]
Tests against a real HTTP stack (including servlet filters, interceptors, and exception handlers) require `webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT` to avoid port conflicts in parallel builds. `@LocalServerPort` injects the allocated port so the test client can target the correct address without hardcoding.
```java
@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = SpringBootTest.WebEnvironment.RANDOM_PORT)
@AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = AutoConfigureTestDatabase.Replace.NONE)
@Testcontainers
class ProductApiIntegrationTest {

    @Container
    static PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres = new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine");

    @DynamicPropertySource
    static void overrideDataSource(DynamicPropertyRegistry r) {
        r.add("spring.datasource.url",      postgres::getJdbcUrl);
        r.add("spring.datasource.username", postgres::getUsername);
        r.add("spring.datasource.password", postgres::getPassword);
    }

    @LocalServerPort
    int port;

    @Autowired
    TestRestTemplate restTemplate;

    @Test
    void createProduct_returns201WithLocation() {
        var request = new ProductRequest("Widget", new BigDecimal("9.99"));
        ResponseEntity<Void> response = restTemplate
            .postForEntity("/api/products", request, Void.class);

        assertThat(response.getStatusCode()).isEqualTo(HttpStatus.CREATED);
        assertThat(response.getHeaders().getLocation()).isNotNull();
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: Full `RANDOM_PORT` tests start the entire Spring context including all beans — startup time is 5–15 seconds per unique context. Reuse the context across test classes using `@SpringBootTest` with identical configurations (same annotations, same properties) so Spring's context cache can serve multiple test classes from a single boot. Avoid `@DirtiesContext` unless absolutely necessary. [official]

---

**Pattern 249: `@DataJpaTest` with `@Sql` for data-driven repository tests using SQL fixtures** [official]
Loading test data via `@Sql` keeps repository tests focused on query logic rather than object-graph construction. `@Sql(executionPhase = BEFORE_TEST_METHOD)` seeds data; `@Sql(executionPhase = AFTER_TEST_METHOD)` cleans up, which is safer than relying on `@Transactional` rollback when the test itself commits (e.g., when verifying auditing fields written in a commit hook).
```java
@DataJpaTest
@AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = AutoConfigureTestDatabase.Replace.NONE)
@Testcontainers
class OrderRepositoryQueryTest {

    @Container
    static PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres = new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine");

    @DynamicPropertySource
    static void configureDataSource(DynamicPropertyRegistry r) {
        r.add("spring.datasource.url",      postgres::getJdbcUrl);
        r.add("spring.datasource.username", postgres::getUsername);
        r.add("spring.datasource.password", postgres::getPassword);
    }

    @Autowired
    OrderRepository orderRepository;

    @Test
    @Sql("/fixtures/orders/pending-orders.sql")
    @Sql(scripts = "/fixtures/orders/cleanup.sql",
         executionPhase = Sql.ExecutionPhase.AFTER_TEST_METHOD)
    void findByStatus_returnsPendingOrdersSortedByCreatedAt() {
        List<Order> pending = orderRepository.findByStatusOrderByCreatedAtAsc(OrderStatus.PENDING);

        assertThat(pending).hasSize(3);
        assertThat(pending)
            .extracting(Order::ref)
            .containsExactly("ORD-001", "ORD-002", "ORD-003");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: SQL fixtures are brittle — schema changes require updating every affected fixture file, and there is no compile-time check that the SQL is valid until the test runs. Prefer `@Sql` for complex query testing where building the object graph in Java would require many `save()` calls. For simple cases, construct entities in Java with `@BeforeEach` to maintain type safety and refactoring support. [official]

---

**Pattern 250: `SoftAssertions` with `assertSoftly` lambda to collect all failures before reporting** [official]
A hard assertion stops test execution on first failure, hiding subsequent failures that might point to related bugs. `SoftAssertions.assertSoftly(softly -> { ... })` collects all assertion failures and reports them together, making each test run maximally informative.
```java
@Test
void createUserResponse_hasAllExpectedFields() {
    var request  = new CreateUserRequest("alice@example.com", "Alice Smith", "ADMIN");
    var response = userService.createUser(request);

    SoftAssertions.assertSoftly(softly -> {
        softly.assertThat(response.id())
              .as("id should be a positive long")
              .isPositive();
        softly.assertThat(response.email())
              .as("email should be preserved verbatim")
              .isEqualTo("alice@example.com");
        softly.assertThat(response.displayName())
              .as("displayName should be trimmed")
              .isEqualTo("Alice Smith");
        softly.assertThat(response.role())
              .as("role should default to USER when ADMIN is disallowed")
              .isEqualTo(Role.USER);
        softly.assertThat(response.createdAt())
              .as("createdAt should be within last 5 seconds")
              .isAfter(Instant.now().minusSeconds(5));
    });
}
```
Tradeoff: `assertSoftly` captures ALL assertion errors but the multi-error report shows the assertion description and mismatch without a precise line number in some versions — adding descriptive `.as("...")` labels is MANDATORY to make CI failure reports actionable. [official]

---

**Pattern 251: `Testcontainers` `@Container` on `static` field with `@ServiceConnection` for zero-config Spring Boot integration** [official]
Spring Boot 3.1+ `@ServiceConnection` reads the container's connection details (JDBC URL, host, port, credentials) and registers them as `ConnectionDetails` beans, eliminating the `@DynamicPropertySource` boilerplate. Marking the container `static` ensures one container instance is shared across all test methods in the class.
```java
@SpringBootTest
@Testcontainers
class InventoryServiceIntegrationTest {

    @Container
    @ServiceConnection
    static PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres =
        new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine")
            .withInitScript("db/schema.sql");

    @Container
    @ServiceConnection
    static RedisContainer redis = new RedisContainer("redis:7-alpine");

    @Autowired
    InventoryService inventoryService;

    @Test
    void reserveStock_decreasesAvailableQuantity() {
        inventoryService.seed("SKU-XYZ", 100);
        inventoryService.reserve("SKU-XYZ", 30);

        assertThat(inventoryService.available("SKU-XYZ")).isEqualTo(70);
    }

    @Test
    void reserveStock_isIdempotentWithSameReservationId() {
        inventoryService.seed("SKU-ABC", 50);
        var reservationId = UUID.randomUUID().toString();

        inventoryService.reserve("SKU-ABC", 10, reservationId);
        inventoryService.reserve("SKU-ABC", 10, reservationId); // duplicate

        assertThat(inventoryService.available("SKU-ABC")).isEqualTo(40);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@ServiceConnection` works only for containers with a registered `ContainerConnectionDetailsFactory` in Spring Boot's auto-configuration. Custom or less common containers (e.g., Cassandra, ClickHouse) may not have a factory, requiring `@DynamicPropertySource` as a fallback. Check the Spring Boot container support matrix before assuming `@ServiceConnection` is available. [official]

**Pattern 252: `InvocationInterceptor` JUnit 5 extension for test-level retry on flaky infrastructure tests** [official]
Rather than wrapping individual flaky tests in retry loops, a JUnit 5 `InvocationInterceptor` extension retries entire test method invocations transparently. The extension is applied via `@ExtendWith` or `@RegisterExtension` and makes the retry policy visible in the test class declaration rather than buried in utility methods.
```java
public class RetryOnFlakyInfraExtension implements InvocationInterceptor {

    private final int maxAttempts;

    public RetryOnFlakyInfraExtension(int maxAttempts) {
        this.maxAttempts = maxAttempts;
    }

    @Override
    public void interceptTestMethod(
            Invocation<Void> invocation,
            ReflectiveInvocationContext<Method> ctx,
            ExtensionContext extCtx) throws Throwable {

        Throwable lastThrowable = null;
        for (int attempt = 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++) {
            try {
                invocation.proceed();
                return; // success — stop retrying
            } catch (AssumptionViolatedException e) {
                throw e; // never retry assumption failures
            } catch (Throwable t) {
                lastThrowable = t;
                System.err.printf("Attempt %d/%d failed for [%s]: %s%n",
                    attempt, maxAttempts, ctx.getExecutable().getName(), t.getMessage());
            }
        }
        throw Objects.requireNonNull(lastThrowable);
    }
}

// Usage:
@RegisterExtension
static RetryOnFlakyInfraExtension retry = new RetryOnFlakyInfraExtension(3);

@Test
void connectToExternalService_succeeds() { /* ... */ }
```
Tradeoff: Retrying tests hides the root cause of flakiness; it should be a short-term mitigation while the underlying issue is fixed, not a permanent crutch. Each retry adds to wall-clock CI time — three retries can triple the test suite duration for affected tests. Log every retry attempt and monitor that retry counts trend toward zero over time. [official]

**Pattern 253: `@MockitoBean` replacing legacy `@MockBean` for Spring context mock replacement in Spring Boot 4** [official]
Spring Boot 4.0 removed `@MockBean` and `@SpyBean` in favour of Spring Framework 6.2's native `@MockitoBean` and `@MockitoSpyBean`. The new annotations are part of Spring's test bean override mechanism and work identically for most use cases, but the registration mechanism is framework-level rather than Boot-level.
```java
@SpringBootTest
class EmailNotificationServiceTest {

    @MockitoBean
    private EmailClient emailClient;

    @MockitoBean
    private TemplateEngine templateEngine;

    @Autowired
    private EmailNotificationService notificationService;

    @Test
    void sendWelcomeEmail_populatesTemplateAndSendsViaClient() {
        given(templateEngine.render("welcome", Map.of("name", "Alice")))
            .willReturn("<h1>Welcome, Alice!</h1>");

        notificationService.sendWelcome(new User("alice@example.com", "Alice"));

        then(emailClient).should(times(1))
            .send(argThat(email ->
                email.to().equals("alice@example.com") &&
                email.body().contains("Welcome, Alice!")));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: Adding a `@MockitoBean` to one test class but not another that otherwise shares the same `@SpringBootTest` configuration breaks Spring's context cache — each unique set of bean overrides produces a distinct context key. Keep `@MockitoBean` declarations consistent across all test classes that should share a context, or extract a shared base class with common mock declarations. [official]

**Pattern 254: `jqwik` property-based testing with `@ForAll` and `@Provide` for domain invariant verification** [community]
Property-based testing with jqwik generates hundreds of random inputs and checks that domain invariants hold for all of them. This is especially powerful for validating serialisation round-trips, commutativity, and mathematical properties that example-based tests would require hundreds of hand-crafted cases to cover.
```java
class MoneyArithmeticProperties {

    @Property(tries = 500)
    @Label("addition is commutative")
    boolean additionIsCommutative(
            @ForAll @Positive BigDecimal amount1,
            @ForAll @Positive BigDecimal amount2) {

        var m1 = Money.of(amount1, "GBP");
        var m2 = Money.of(amount2, "GBP");

        return m1.add(m2).equals(m2.add(m1));
    }

    @Property
    @Label("round-trip: serialise then deserialise preserves value")
    void serialisationRoundTrip(@ForAll("validMoneyAmounts") Money original)
            throws Exception {
        String json   = objectMapper.writeValueAsString(original);
        Money  parsed = objectMapper.readValue(json, Money.class);

        assertThat(parsed).isEqualTo(original);
    }

    @Provide
    Arbitrary<Money> validMoneyAmounts() {
        return Arbitraries.bigDecimals()
            .between(BigDecimal.ZERO, new BigDecimal("999999.99"))
            .ofScale(2)
            .map(amount -> Money.of(amount, "GBP"));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: jqwik shrinks failing inputs to a minimal counterexample automatically, which is invaluable for debugging. However, shrinking can add seconds to the first failure — configure `@Property(shrinking = ShrinkingMode.OFF)` during initial development to get fast failures, then re-enable shrinking once the property logic is correct. Generated test names in JUnit 5 launchers show as a single "property" node rather than individual samples, reducing visibility in CI dashboards. [community]

---

**Pattern 255: `ArchUnit` `layeredArchitecture()` with `ignoreDependency` for enforcing Clean Architecture boundaries** [community]
ArchUnit's `layeredArchitecture()` DSL defines layer dependencies and reports violations at test time. Adding targeted `ignoreDependency` rules for intentional cross-layer references (e.g., domain events published upward) makes the ruleset maintainable without disabling enforcement entirely.
```java
@AnalyzeClasses(packages = "com.example.orders",
                importOptions = ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests.class)
class ArchitectureEnforcementTest {

    @ArchTest
    static final ArchRule layers = layeredArchitecture()
        .consideringOnlyDependenciesInLayers()
        .layer("Domain")        .definedBy("com.example.orders.domain..")
        .layer("Application")   .definedBy("com.example.orders.application..")
        .layer("Infrastructure").definedBy("com.example.orders.infrastructure..")
        .layer("API")           .definedBy("com.example.orders.api..")
        .whereLayer("API")           .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers()
        .whereLayer("Infrastructure").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Application", "API")
        .whereLayer("Application")   .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("API")
        .whereLayer("Domain")        .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Application", "Infrastructure")
        .ignoreDependency(
            OrderPlacedEvent.class, ApplicationEventPublisher.class);

    @ArchTest
    static final ArchRule noCyclicDependencies =
        slices().matching("com.example.orders.(*)..").should().beFreeOfCycles();

    @ArchTest
    static final ArchRule repositoriesAreInterfaces =
        classes().that().haveNameEndingWith("Repository")
            .and().resideInAPackage("com.example.orders.domain..")
            .should().beInterfaces()
            .because("domain repositories must be interfaces to keep the domain free of infrastructure details");
}
```
Tradeoff: `@AnalyzeClasses` scans the entire classpath at test startup — for large monorepos with thousands of classes this can add 3–10 seconds to the test run. Scope the package narrowly and use `importOptions = DoNotIncludeTests.class` to exclude test classes from the analysis. ArchUnit rules are pure static analysis and cannot detect runtime violations or dynamic proxies; combine with integration tests for full coverage. [community]

### Community Gotchas — Cycle 55

**Gotcha G1: `@MockitoBean` causes a new `ApplicationContext` to be created for every test class that declares it unless the full configuration is identical — WHY: Spring's context cache key includes the set of bean overrides (mocks/spies) registered on the test class. Two test classes that both declare `@MockitoBean EmailClient` but have different `@SpringBootTest` configurations (e.g., different `properties` arrays, different `@Import` annotations) produce different cache keys and each get their own context. Even with identical `@SpringBootTest` configurations, adding `@MockitoBean` on a field with a different name produces a different override descriptor, breaking cache sharing. Fix: extract a common base class with all `@MockitoBean` declarations so all subclasses share the same override descriptor and Spring reuses the same context. Keep mock declarations consistent across all test classes that should share a single `ApplicationContext`.**

**Gotcha G2: `assertThat(optionalValue).isPresent()` does NOT extract the wrapped value — calling `.isEqualTo(expected)` afterward compares the `Optional` wrapper to the plain expected object and always fails with a confusing "expected: Optional[…] but was: Optional[…]" or "expected: … but was: Optional[…]" message — WHY: `AbstractOptionalAssert.isPresent()` returns `this` (the same `OptionalAssert`) to support chaining, so subsequent assertion methods operate on the `Optional` wrapper, not the value inside it. `.isEqualTo()` on an `OptionalAssert` delegates to `Optional.equals()` which wraps the plain argument in `Optional.of(expected)` for comparison, producing a misleading error. Fix: use `.hasValue(expected)` for present-and-equal checks in one step, or use `.get()` to extract the value and continue with a plain assert chain: `assertThat(result).isPresent().get().satisfies(v -> assertThat(v.name()).isEqualTo("Alice"))`.**

**Gotcha G3: `Testcontainers` `withReuse(true)` containers are NOT stopped between test classes and retain all state (rows, keys, queued messages) across the JVM lifetime — when different test classes receive the same container instance, data written by one class persists into the next class's execution, causing spurious test failures — WHY: `withReuse(true)` registers the container in Docker with a hash label computed from the container configuration. On the next `start()` call, Testcontainers finds the existing container by label and returns it rather than creating a new one, which means the container is never cleaned. Fix: use `withReuse(true)` ONLY for purely read-only or schema-only containers; for stateful integration tests, omit `withReuse` and rely on static `@Container` fields with JUnit's `@Testcontainers` lifecycle management, which stops containers after the test class completes.**

**Gotcha G4: `@Transactional` on a `@SpringBootTest` test method does NOT roll back changes made by code running in a separate thread — background executors, `@Async` methods, and virtual-thread tasks all bypass the test's transaction context and commit independently — WHY: Spring's transaction synchronisation is stored in `ThreadLocal` variables via `TransactionSynchronizationManager`. A `@Transactional` test method enrolls the current thread in a transaction; code dispatched to another thread has no transaction context and either starts its own (and commits it) or runs without a transaction entirely. The test's rollback only affects work done on the original thread. Fix: for tests that exercise async code paths, either avoid `@Transactional` on the test and clean up via `@Sql(executionPhase = AFTER_TEST_METHOD)`, or use `Awaitility` to wait for the async operation to complete before asserting, accepting that cleanup requires explicit DELETE statements in a teardown script.**

**Gotcha G5: JUnit 5 `@BeforeEach` methods in a superclass run BEFORE `@BeforeEach` methods in a subclass — if both configure stubs on a `@MockitoBean`, the subclass `@BeforeEach` stub runs AFTER the superclass one, potentially overriding or clearing it before the test method executes — WHY: JUnit 5 guarantees `@BeforeEach` execution outer-to-inner (superclass first, then subclass) per the specification. When stub setup is split across a hierarchy, later `@BeforeEach` calls can call `reset(mock)` (or re-stub with a conflicting `given(...).willReturn(...)`) and silently discard the superclass configuration. `MockitoExtension` resets mocks BETWEEN tests (before `@BeforeEach` runs), not after, so there is no automatic recovery within a single test setup chain. Fix: avoid calling `Mockito.reset()` inside `@BeforeEach`; put all stub configuration in the lowest-level `@BeforeEach` or directly in each test method, and never split stub setup across a superclass/subclass hierarchy.**

## Cycle 56 — 2026-05-14

### New Patterns

**Pattern 256: JUnit 6 `@ParameterizedClass` — parameterize an entire test class** [official]
JUnit 6 introduces `@ParameterizedClass` so a full test class, including all its `@Test` methods, is executed once per argument set. Use `@FieldSource`, `@MethodSource`, or `@CsvSource` on the class to supply arguments and inject them via constructor or `@Parameter`-annotated fields.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.params.ParameterizedClass;
import org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.MethodSource;
import org.junit.jupiter.params.Parameter;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@ParameterizedClass
@MethodSource("locales")
class LocaleFormattingTest {

    @Parameter
    Locale locale;

    static java.util.stream.Stream<Locale> locales() {
        return java.util.stream.Stream.of(Locale.US, Locale.UK, Locale.GERMANY);
    }

    @Test
    void currencySymbolIsNonEmpty() {
        String symbol = java.util.Currency.getInstance(locale).getSymbol(locale);
        assertThat(symbol).isNotEmpty();
    }

    @Test
    void dateFormatProducesOutput() {
        String formatted = java.time.LocalDate.of(2026, 1, 15)
            .format(java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter.ofLocalizedDate(
                java.time.format.FormatStyle.SHORT).withLocale(locale));
        assertThat(formatted).isNotEmpty();
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@ParameterizedClass` eliminates the need to repeat `@ParameterizedTest` on every method in a multi-scenario class, but it increases visible test count in CI dashboards linearly (methods × argument sets). Reserve it for cases where every method in the class genuinely varies with the parameter; for a single varying method, `@ParameterizedTest` is less noisy. [official]

---

**Pattern 257: JUnit 6 `@DefaultLocale` / `@DefaultTimeZone` for deterministic locale-sensitive tests** [official]
JUnit 6.1 provides `@DefaultLocale` and `@DefaultTimeZone` meta-annotations that override `Locale.getDefault()` and `TimeZone.getDefault()` for the duration of a test method or class and restore them afterward, making locale-sensitive formatting tests deterministic without global `Locale.setDefault()` side-effects.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.DefaultLocale;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.DefaultTimeZone;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import java.text.NumberFormat;
import java.time.ZonedDateTime;
import java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter;
import java.time.format.FormatStyle;

class LocaleSensitiveFormatterTest {

    @Test
    @DefaultLocale("de-DE")
    @DefaultTimeZone("Europe/Berlin")
    void priceIsFormattedWithGermanLocale() {
        String formatted = NumberFormat.getCurrencyInstance().format(1_234.56);
        // German locale formats as "1.234,56 €"
        assertThat(formatted).contains("1.234");
    }

    @Test
    @DefaultLocale("en-US")
    @DefaultTimeZone("America/New_York")
    void dateTimeIsFormattedWithUsLocale() {
        ZonedDateTime dt = ZonedDateTime.parse("2026-01-15T09:30:00-05:00[America/New_York]");
        String formatted = dt.format(DateTimeFormatter.ofLocalizedDateTime(FormatStyle.SHORT));
        assertThat(formatted).contains("1/15/26");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@DefaultLocale` mutates a JVM-global `ThreadLocal` rather than the process default, so tests using it are safe under JUnit's parallel execution model. However, if production code caches `Locale.getDefault()` at class-load time (e.g., a `static final` field), the annotation will not affect the cached value and the test remains non-deterministic. Check for eager caching before relying on this mechanism. [official]

---

**Pattern 258: JUnit 6 `CancellationToken` for cooperative test cancellation** [official]
JUnit 6 passes a `CancellationToken` to `LauncherExecutionRequest`-aware tests, enabling long-running parameterized loops or generators to exit cleanly when a timeout or external signal fires, rather than being forcibly interrupted mid-assertion.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;
import org.junit.platform.launcher.core.CancellationToken;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.TestInfo;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;

class CancellationAwareBatchTest {

    @Test
    void processBatchUntilCancelled(CancellationToken token) throws InterruptedException {
        AtomicInteger processed = new AtomicInteger(0);
        int batchSize = 10_000;

        for (int i = 0; i < batchSize; i++) {
            if (token.isCancellationRequested()) {
                // Exit cleanly — let JUnit report a partial result
                break;
            }
            // Simulate per-item work
            int result = i * 2;
            assertThat(result).isEqualTo(i * 2);
            processed.incrementAndGet();
        }

        assertThat(processed.get()).isGreaterThan(0);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: Cooperative cancellation keeps the JVM in a clean state and allows teardown lifecycle methods to run, but it requires the test body to poll `token.isCancellationRequested()` at sensible intervals. Tests that perform blocking I/O must also handle `InterruptedException` explicitly; JUnit 6 will not bypass `Thread.interrupt()` for tests that use `CancellationToken`. [official]

---

**Pattern 259: Mockito 5.x `mockConstruction` with `MockInitializer` for constructor argument capture** [official]
`Mockito.mockConstruction(Class, MockInitializer)` intercepts `new T(args)` calls and exposes the constructor arguments via `ctx.arguments()` inside the initializer. This is the standard way to verify that collaborators are constructed with the correct parameters without restructuring production code.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.mockito.MockedConstruction;
import org.mockito.Mockito;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.verify;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.when;

class OrderServiceTest {

    @Test
    void orderServiceConstructsAuditLoggerWithOrderId() {
        String expectedOrderId = "ORD-42";

        try (MockedConstruction<AuditLogger> mocked = Mockito.mockConstruction(
                AuditLogger.class,
                (mock, ctx) -> {
                    // Verify constructor arguments at construction time
                    assertThat(ctx.arguments()).containsExactly(expectedOrderId);
                    when(mock.isEnabled()).thenReturn(true);
                })) {

            OrderService service = new OrderService();
            service.placeOrder(expectedOrderId, "ITEM-7", 3);

            assertThat(mocked.constructed()).hasSize(1);
            verify(mocked.constructed().get(0)).log("ORDER_PLACED");
        }
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `mockConstruction` is thread-local — only `new` calls on the same thread as the `try` block are intercepted, so it does not capture objects created in `@Async` or virtual-thread dispatch. For multi-threaded construction scenarios, prefer injecting a factory interface and mocking the factory instead. [official]

---

**Pattern 260: AssertJ `satisfiesExactlyInAnyOrder` for unordered collection element verification** [official]
`satisfiesExactlyInAnyOrder(Consumer...)` asserts that each element in a collection satisfies exactly one of the provided consumer predicates, with no predicate left unsatisfied and no element matching more than one predicate — an unordered version of `satisfiesExactly` that tolerates list ordering variability.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import java.util.List;

class OrderSummaryTest {

    record LineItem(String sku, int qty, double price) {}

    @Test
    void cartContainsExpectedLineItemsInAnyOrder() {
        List<LineItem> cart = cartService.getCartItems("user-99");

        assertThat(cart)
            .satisfiesExactlyInAnyOrder(
                item -> {
                    assertThat(item.sku()).isEqualTo("BOOK-101");
                    assertThat(item.qty()).isEqualTo(2);
                    assertThat(item.price()).isEqualTo(12.99);
                },
                item -> {
                    assertThat(item.sku()).isEqualTo("PEN-55");
                    assertThat(item.qty()).isGreaterThanOrEqualTo(1);
                    assertThat(item.price()).isBetween(1.0, 5.0);
                },
                item -> assertThat(item.sku()).startsWith("NOTEBOOK-")
            );
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `satisfiesExactlyInAnyOrder` uses a bipartite matching algorithm internally, so its failure messages list all unmatched elements and unmatched consumers in bulk — they are detailed but lengthy. For collections larger than ~20 elements, the failure output can be hard to scan; consider adding `.as("cart items")` and `.filteredOn(...)` to narrow the assertion before calling it. [official]

---

**Pattern 261: Spring Boot `RestTestClient` for reactive and non-reactive controller testing** [official]
Spring Boot 4.0 introduces `RestTestClient` (via `@AutoConfigureRestTestClient`) as a unified fluent HTTP test client that works against both reactive (`WebFlux`) and servlet (`MVC`) stacks, replacing the need to choose between `WebTestClient` and `MockMvc` depending on the stack in use.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.web.reactive.AutoConfigureRestTestClient;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.test.web.reactive.server.RestTestClient;

@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = SpringBootTest.WebEnvironment.RANDOM_PORT)
@AutoConfigureRestTestClient
class ProductControllerTest {

    @Autowired
    RestTestClient restTestClient;

    @Test
    void getProductReturns200WithBody() {
        restTestClient.get()
            .uri("/api/products/{id}", "PROD-1")
            .exchange()
            .expectStatus().isOk()
            .expectBody()
                .jsonPath("$.id").isEqualTo("PROD-1")
                .jsonPath("$.name").isNotEmpty()
                .jsonPath("$.price").isNumber();
    }

    @Test
    void createProductReturns201() {
        restTestClient.post()
            .uri("/api/products")
            .bodyValue(new CreateProductRequest("Widget", 9.99))
            .exchange()
            .expectStatus().isCreated()
            .expectHeader().exists("Location");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `RestTestClient` uses a real HTTP stack (random port), so it exercises serialization, filters, and error handling more thoroughly than `MockMvc`. The tradeoff is longer test startup time and the need for the full application context. For pure controller unit tests without the full application context, `MockMvcTester` remains the lighter choice. [official]

---

**Pattern 262: `@DataJpaTest` with `replace=NONE` and Testcontainers PostgreSQL for production-parity persistence tests** [official]
By default, `@DataJpaTest` replaces the data source with an embedded H2 database. Setting `replace = AutoConfigureTestDatabase.Replace.NONE` and supplying a `@ServiceConnection`-annotated Testcontainers container forces the test to use the real database dialect, catching dialect-specific query issues that H2 would silently accept.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.jdbc.AutoConfigureTestDatabase;
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.orm.jpa.DataJpaTest;
import org.springframework.boot.testcontainers.service.connection.ServiceConnection;
import org.testcontainers.containers.PostgreSQLContainer;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Container;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Testcontainers;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@DataJpaTest
@AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = AutoConfigureTestDatabase.Replace.NONE)
@Testcontainers
class ProductRepositoryTest {

    @Container
    @ServiceConnection
    static PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres =
        new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine");

    @Autowired
    ProductRepository repo;

    @Test
    void fullTextSearchFindsProductByKeyword() {
        repo.save(new Product("PROD-1", "Ergonomic Keyboard", "Mechanical switches"));
        repo.flush();

        // PostgreSQL-specific tsvector full-text search — fails on H2
        var results = repo.findByFullTextSearch("ergonomic");
        assertThat(results).extracting(Product::getSku).containsExactly("PROD-1");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: Testcontainers starts a real PostgreSQL Docker container per test class, adding 5–15 seconds of cold-start overhead. Use `@Container` as a `static` field so the container is reused across all test methods in the class. If Docker is unavailable in CI, gate the test with `@EnabledIfSystemProperty(named = "testcontainers.enabled", matches = "true")` to avoid breaking the build. [official]

---

**Pattern 263: WireMock stateful scenario testing for multi-step API workflows** [community]
WireMock's Scenario API allows a stub's response to change based on a named state machine. This is the canonical approach for testing retry logic, pagination, and polling workflows where each successive HTTP call should return a different response.
```java
import com.github.tomakehurst.wiremock.junit5.WireMockExtension;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.RegisterExtension;
import static com.github.tomakehurst.wiremock.client.WireMock.*;
import static com.github.tomakehurst.wiremock.core.WireMockConfiguration.wireMockConfig;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

class PaymentPollingTest {

    @RegisterExtension
    static WireMockExtension wm = WireMockExtension.newInstance()
        .options(wireMockConfig().dynamicPort())
        .build();

    @Test
    void pollerEventuallyReceivesPaidStatus() {
        // State 1: first poll returns PENDING
        wm.stubFor(get(urlEqualTo("/payments/PAY-99/status"))
            .inScenario("payment-polling")
            .whenScenarioStateIs("Started")
            .willReturn(okJson("{\"status\":\"PENDING\"}"))
            .willSetStateTo("attempt-1"));

        // State 2: second poll returns PROCESSING
        wm.stubFor(get(urlEqualTo("/payments/PAY-99/status"))
            .inScenario("payment-polling")
            .whenScenarioStateIs("attempt-1")
            .willReturn(okJson("{\"status\":\"PROCESSING\"}"))
            .willSetStateTo("attempt-2"));

        // State 3: third poll returns PAID
        wm.stubFor(get(urlEqualTo("/payments/PAY-99/status"))
            .inScenario("payment-polling")
            .whenScenarioStateIs("attempt-2")
            .willReturn(okJson("{\"status\":\"PAID\"}")));

        PaymentPoller poller = new PaymentPoller(wm.baseUrl());
        String finalStatus = poller.pollUntilTerminal("PAY-99", 5);

        assertThat(finalStatus).isEqualTo("PAID");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: Scenarios are per-WireMock-instance and shared across all threads hitting the same mock server — parallel tests that share a `WireMockExtension` instance will corrupt each other's scenario state. Always use `@RegisterExtension` (not `@WireMockTest`) for stateful scenarios that need isolation, or call `wm.resetScenarios()` in `@BeforeEach`. [community]

---

**Pattern 264: Awaitility `failFast` condition to short-circuit polling on unrecoverable errors** [community]
`Awaitility.await().failFast(Callable<Boolean>)` lets you register a secondary "bail out immediately" predicate. If the failFast condition becomes true during polling, Awaitility throws a `ConditionTimeoutException` instantly rather than waiting for the full timeout, making tests fail loudly and quickly when infrastructure is broken.
```java
import org.awaitility.Awaitility;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicBoolean;

class MessageConsumerTest {

    @Test
    void consumerAcknowledgesMessageWithinTimeout() {
        AtomicBoolean brokerDown = new AtomicBoolean(false);
        MessageBroker broker = startTestBroker();
        MessageConsumer consumer = new MessageConsumer(broker);

        broker.publish("QUEUE-A", "order.placed", "{\"orderId\":\"ORD-1\"}");

        Awaitility.await("message acknowledged")
            .atMost(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
            .pollInterval(200, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)
            .failFast("broker crashed", () -> !broker.isRunning())
            .untilAsserted(() ->
                assertThat(consumer.acknowledgedIds()).contains("ORD-1"));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `failFast` evaluates its predicate on every poll interval, so the predicate must be cheap (a simple field check or `isRunning()` call). An expensive `failFast` predicate (e.g., a database query) can add significant overhead for the common case where the condition is met quickly. Keep failFast checks to in-memory state or lightweight health pings. [community]

**Pattern 265: `@JsonTest` with `JacksonTester` round-trip assertions** [official]
`@JsonTest` wires only the Jackson `ObjectMapper` slice of the Spring Boot context. Injecting a `JacksonTester<T>` field provides `.write(T)` and `.parseObject(String)` without the full HTTP stack, enabling fast serialization and deserialization round-trip verification.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.json.JsonTest;
import org.springframework.boot.test.json.JacksonTester;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@JsonTest
class OrderDtoJsonTest {

    @Autowired
    JacksonTester<OrderDto> json;

    @Test
    void serialisesOrderDtoToExpectedJson() throws Exception {
        var order = new OrderDto("ORD-1", "Alice", List.of("ITEM-A", "ITEM-B"), 45.00);

        assertThat(json.write(order))
            .hasJsonPathStringValue("$.orderId", "ORD-1")
            .hasJsonPathStringValue("$.customerName", "Alice")
            .hasJsonPathArrayValue("$.items").hasSize(2)
            .hasJsonPathNumberValue("$.totalAmount", 45.00);
    }

    @Test
    void deserialisesJsonToOrderDto() throws Exception {
        String content = """
            {"orderId":"ORD-2","customerName":"Bob",
             "items":["WIDGET"],"totalAmount":9.99}
            """;

        OrderDto dto = json.parseObject(content);
        assertThat(dto.orderId()).isEqualTo("ORD-2");
        assertThat(dto.totalAmount()).isEqualTo(9.99);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@JsonTest` loads only the JSON infrastructure beans — it does not load `@Service`, `@Repository`, or HTTP layer beans. If your DTO uses a custom `@JsonDeserializer` or `@JsonComponent` that depends on Spring beans, you must explicitly `@Import` those components in the test class because `@JsonTest` does not scan them automatically. [official]

**Pattern 266: PIT mutation testing with `withHistory` incremental analysis** [community]
PIT's `withHistory` mode stores the last mutation test result in a `.pit-history` file and only re-runs mutations for classes whose source or tests have changed since the last run. This makes mutation testing fast enough to run on every PR rather than only nightly.
```java
// build.gradle (Kotlin DSL)
// pitest {
//     targetClasses.set(listOf("com.example.orders.*"))
//     mutators.set(listOf("STRONGER"))
//     threads.set(4)
//     historyInputLocation.set(file(".pit-history"))
//     historyOutputLocation.set(file(".pit-history"))
//     mutationThreshold.set(80)
//     coverageThreshold.set(85)
//     outputFormats.set(listOf("HTML", "XML"))
// }

// Example test that exercises a mutation-prone boundary condition
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.*;

class DiscountCalculatorTest {

    private final DiscountCalculator calc = new DiscountCalculator();

    @Test
    void noDiscountForOrdersBelowThreshold() {
        assertThat(calc.calculateDiscount(49.99)).isZero();
    }

    @Test
    void tenPercentDiscountAtExactThreshold() {
        // Tests the boundary >= 50.00 — kills ">" vs ">=" mutation
        assertThat(calc.calculateDiscount(50.00)).isEqualTo(5.00);
    }

    @Test
    void tenPercentDiscountAboveThreshold() {
        assertThat(calc.calculateDiscount(100.00)).isEqualTo(10.00);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: Incremental PIT with `withHistory` dramatically reduces CI time for large codebases (from 20+ minutes to under 2 minutes for unchanged modules), but the history file is binary and should be stored in source control or a CI cache. If the history file is lost or corrupted, PIT falls back to a full run silently — treat the history file as a build artifact and cache it between pipeline runs. [community]

**Pattern 267: `@RestClientTest` with `MockRestServiceServer` for HTTP client slice testing** [official]
`@RestClientTest(MyClient.class)` loads only the `RestClient` (or `RestTemplate`) slice plus the named client bean, wiring a `MockRestServiceServer` that intercepts outbound HTTP calls without starting a server. This tests the client's request construction and response parsing in isolation.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.web.client.RestClientTest;
import org.springframework.http.MediaType;
import org.springframework.test.web.client.MockRestServiceServer;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.springframework.test.web.client.match.MockRestRequestMatchers.*;
import static org.springframework.test.web.client.response.MockRestResponseCreators.*;

@RestClientTest(ExchangeRateClient.class)
class ExchangeRateClientTest {

    @Autowired
    ExchangeRateClient client;

    @Autowired
    MockRestServiceServer server;

    @Test
    void fetchesEurUsdRateAndParsesBody() {
        server.expect(requestTo("/rates/EUR/USD"))
            .andExpect(method(org.springframework.http.HttpMethod.GET))
            .andExpect(header("Accept", MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON_VALUE))
            .andRespond(withSuccess("""
                {"base":"EUR","target":"USD","rate":1.0823}
                """, MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON));

        ExchangeRate rate = client.getRate("EUR", "USD");

        assertThat(rate.base()).isEqualTo("EUR");
        assertThat(rate.rate()).isEqualTo(1.0823);
        server.verify();
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `MockRestServiceServer` verifies calls in declaration order by default — if the production code issues the same URL twice, the server expects two `expect(...)` stubs in that order. Setting `MockRestServiceServer.bindTo(restTemplate).build()` with `ignoreExpectOrder(true)` relaxes this, but then `server.verify()` only checks that all stubs were hit, not their sequence. Choose the strictness level based on whether call ordering is part of the contract under test. [official]

**Pattern 268: JUnit 5 `ExtensionContext.Store` with `CloseableResource` for automatic resource cleanup** [official]
Storing a resource in `ExtensionContext.Store` as a `CloseableResource` (or `AutoCloseable` in JUnit 6) ensures the resource is released when the associated store's scope ends — no explicit `@AfterEach` teardown required even in complex extension chains.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.*;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

class TempFileExtension implements BeforeEachCallback {

    private static final ExtensionContext.Namespace NS =
        ExtensionContext.Namespace.create(TempFileExtension.class);

    @Override
    public void beforeEach(ExtensionContext context) throws Exception {
        java.nio.file.Path tmp = java.nio.file.Files.createTempFile("junit-", ".txt");
        // Store as AutoCloseable — JUnit removes the file when the test scope closes
        context.getStore(NS).put("tmpFile", (ExtensionContext.Store.CloseableResource) () ->
            java.nio.file.Files.deleteIfExists(tmp));
        context.getStore(NS).put("tmpPath", tmp);
    }

    public static java.nio.file.Path get(ExtensionContext ctx) {
        return ctx.getStore(NS).get("tmpPath", java.nio.file.Path.class);
    }
}

@ExtendWith(TempFileExtension.class)
class TempFileTest {

    @Test
    void writesAndReadsTempFile(ExtensionContext ctx) throws Exception {
        var path = TempFileExtension.get(ctx);
        java.nio.file.Files.writeString(path, "hello");
        assertThat(java.nio.file.Files.readString(path)).isEqualTo("hello");
        // File is automatically deleted after this test by the CloseableResource
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: Storing `CloseableResource` cleanup in the `Store` avoids `@AfterEach` boilerplate but makes the cleanup logic invisible to readers of the test class — it lives inside the extension. Always document the lifecycle contract in the extension's Javadoc. JUnit 6 allows any `AutoCloseable` as a stored value (not just the marker interface); this simplifies extension code but creates an implicit coupling between the store key and the lifecycle that must be understood when debugging stale resources. [official]

**Pattern 269: Testcontainers `Network` with aliases for multi-service integration tests** [community]
When two containers need to communicate with each other (e.g., an application container querying a database container), bind them to a shared Testcontainers `Network` and assign DNS aliases. This avoids hard-coded IPs and makes inter-container hostnames predictable and readable.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.testcontainers.containers.GenericContainer;
import org.testcontainers.containers.PostgreSQLContainer;
import org.testcontainers.containers.Network;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Container;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Testcontainers;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@Testcontainers
class FullStackIntegrationTest {

    static final Network NETWORK = Network.newNetwork();

    @Container
    static PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres = new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine")
        .withNetwork(NETWORK)
        .withNetworkAliases("db");

    @Container
    static GenericContainer<?> app = new GenericContainer<>("myapp:latest")
        .withNetwork(NETWORK)
        .withEnv("DB_URL", "jdbc:postgresql://db:5432/test")
        .withEnv("DB_USER", postgres.getUsername())
        .withEnv("DB_PASS", postgres.getPassword())
        .dependsOn(postgres)
        .withExposedPorts(8080);

    @Test
    void appHealthEndpointResponds() {
        String host = app.getHost();
        int port = app.getMappedPort(8080);
        // Issue a health check to the mapped external port
        var response = java.net.http.HttpClient.newHttpClient().sendAsync(
            java.net.http.HttpRequest.newBuilder()
                .uri(java.net.URI.create("http://" + host + ":" + port + "/actuator/health"))
                .GET().build(),
            java.net.http.HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString()
        ).join();
        assertThat(response.statusCode()).isEqualTo(200);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: Testcontainers networks are not automatically cleaned up if the JVM crashes mid-test — orphaned Docker networks accumulate and can exhaust the Docker network limit. Add `Runtime.getRuntime().addShutdownHook(new Thread(NETWORK::close))` or declare the `Network` as a `@RegisterExtension`-managed resource for automatic cleanup. [community]

**Pattern 270: Spring Boot `@AutoConfigureObservability` + `TestObservationRegistry` for span and metric assertions** [official]
Spring Boot's `@AutoConfigureObservability` wires a `TestObservationRegistry` into the test application context. After exercising production code, you can assert that specific named observations (spans/metrics) were recorded, verifying observability without a live Zipkin or Prometheus backend.
```java
import io.micrometer.observation.tck.TestObservationRegistry;
import io.micrometer.observation.tck.TestObservationRegistryAssert;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.AfterEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.actuate.observability.AutoConfigureObservability;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;

@SpringBootTest
@AutoConfigureObservability
class OrderServiceObservabilityTest {

    @Autowired
    OrderService orderService;

    @Autowired
    TestObservationRegistry registry;

    @AfterEach
    void clearRegistry() {
        registry.clear();
    }

    @Test
    void placeOrderEmitsOrderPlacedObservation() {
        orderService.placeOrder("ORD-77", "ITEM-3", 2);

        TestObservationRegistryAssert.assertThat(registry)
            .hasObservationWithNameEqualTo("order.placed")
            .that()
            .hasLowCardinalityKeyValue("status", "success")
            .hasHighCardinalityKeyValue("orderId", "ORD-77");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `TestObservationRegistry` captures all observations globally within the test context — if parallel tests share the same `ApplicationContext` (and therefore the same registry), observations from one test leak into another's assertions. Always call `registry.clear()` in `@AfterEach`, and if context reuse is a concern, annotate tests that assert observations with `@DirtiesContext` or isolate them in a separate class. [official]

### Community Gotchas — Cycle 56

**Gotcha G1: `MockedConstruction` captures only `new` calls on the same thread as the `try` block — objects constructed on virtual threads or via `CompletableFuture.supplyAsync` are NOT intercepted, and production code silently gets real instances instead of mocks — WHY: Mockito stores the mock-construction interceptor in a `ThreadLocal` keyed to the calling thread. Virtual threads and `ForkJoinPool` worker threads do not inherit the carrier thread's `ThreadLocal` state (they start with empty locals), so any `new T()` call dispatched off the original thread finds no interceptor and constructs the real class. This causes the test to verify against real objects without any assertion failure at setup time, producing false-positive "passes." Fix: refactor production code to accept a factory interface injected via constructor and mock the factory instead, which is interceptable regardless of thread; or, if the construction must be tested, run the dispatch synchronously in the test (e.g., by configuring `Executor.current()` to be the direct executor) to keep all `new` calls on the test thread.**

**Gotcha G2: `@DataJpaTest` without `@Sql(executionPhase = AFTER_TEST_METHOD)` cleanup leaves rows in the in-memory database when `@Transactional` rollback is disabled — subsequent tests in the same class see stale rows and fail with duplicate-key or wrong-count assertions — WHY: `@DataJpaTest` wraps each test in a transaction that is rolled back by default. When a test calls `saveAndFlush` and is itself `@Transactional`, the rollback cleans up automatically. But when a test is annotated `@Transactional(propagation = NOT_SUPPORTED)` to test non-transactional behavior, the transaction is committed to the embedded database and rows persist. The next test's `findAll()` now returns rows from the previous test's data. Fix: add `@Sql(scripts = "classpath:cleanup.sql", executionPhase = Sql.ExecutionPhase.AFTER_TEST_METHOD)` to any `@DataJpaTest` method that disables transaction rollback, or use `@BeforeEach` to call `repository.deleteAll()` explicitly before each test.**

**Gotcha G3: `Awaitility.await().untilAsserted(ThrowingRunnable)` swallows `AssertionError` during polling and only surfaces the LAST assertion failure at timeout — if the assertion error message changes between polls (e.g., because state partially updated), the final error message may be misleading about what actually failed — WHY: Awaitility's polling loop catches `AssertionError` and `Exception` on every poll, treating each as a transient failure and retrying. Only when the timeout expires does it re-throw the most recent caught `AssertionError`. If the system under test partially mutates state between polls, the assertion that fires last (at timeout) may reflect a different failure condition than the one that was failing for the first 9 seconds. Fix: add `conditionEvaluationListener` logging (via `Awaitility.setDefaultConditionEvaluationListener`) to capture every poll's assertion message, so the full history is visible in test output when debugging flaky async tests.**

**Gotcha G4: `@DefaultLocale` in JUnit 6 does NOT affect static `Locale` caches initialized by third-party libraries at class load time — libraries that call `Locale.getDefault()` during class initialization store the result in a `private static final Locale` field, making them immune to `@DefaultLocale` — WHY: `@DefaultLocale` calls `Locale.setDefault()` on the JVM in the `beforeEach` lifecycle phase, after all test class static initializers have already run. A library that calls `Locale.getDefault()` inside `static { ... }` or a `static final` field initializer captures the JVM default before any JUnit lifecycle method runs. Subsequent calls to `Locale.setDefault()` by `@DefaultLocale` update the JVM global but cannot retroactively update the cached value in the library's static field. Fix: for libraries with eagerly-cached locales, either restart the JVM with `-Duser.language=de -Duser.country=DE` system properties, or isolate locale-sensitive tests in a separate JVM fork using Surefire's `forkCount=1` with `reuseForks=false`.**

**Gotcha G5: `@SpringBootTest` with `@ServiceConnection` Testcontainers does NOT automatically share the same container instance across test classes — each class that declares its own `@Container static` field gets a fresh container despite identical configuration, multiplying Docker startup costs — WHY: Testcontainers' container sharing via `withReuse(true)` is opt-in and controlled by a label hash of the container's image and environment. When multiple test classes each declare an identical `static PostgreSQLContainer<?>` field without `withReuse(true)`, JUnit's `@Testcontainers` extension manages each independently and starts a new Docker container for each class. Spring's `@ServiceConnection` wires the dynamic port into the application context, but context caching requires the port to be identical across classes — it cannot share a context between classes whose containers have different ports. Fix: declare the container in a shared abstract base class or a JUnit 5 extension registered globally, and enable `withReuse(true)` with `.testcontainers.reuse.enable=true` in `~/.testcontainers.properties` to allow Docker container reuse across test-class boundaries.**
