## Cycle 57 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 271** — JUnit 6 `@ParameterizedClass` with `@MethodSource` for full-class parameterization [official]
JUnit 6 introduced `@ParameterizedClass` to run an entire test class for each argument set supplied by a `@MethodSource`, `@CsvSource`, or `@FieldSource`. Constructor injection populates fields, removing repetitive `@BeforeEach` delegation.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.params.ParameterizedClass;
import org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.MethodSource;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import java.util.stream.Stream;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@ParameterizedClass
@MethodSource("engines")
class JsonSerializerParameterizedClassTest {

    static Stream<String> engines() {
        return Stream.of("jackson", "gson", "jsonb");
    }

    private final String engine;

    JsonSerializerParameterizedClassTest(String engine) {
        this.engine = engine;
    }

    @Test
    void roundTripPreservesNullFields() {
        var serializer = SerializerFactory.create(engine);
        var dto = new OrderDto(null, "ITEM-9", 3);
        assertThat(serializer.deserialize(serializer.serialize(dto), OrderDto.class))
            .usingRecursiveComparison()
            .isEqualTo(dto);
    }

    @Test
    void serializeDateAsIso8601() {
        var serializer = SerializerFactory.create(engine);
        var dto = new OrderDto("ORD-1", "ITEM-1", 1);
        assertThat(serializer.serialize(dto)).contains("\"created\"");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@ParameterizedClass` requires all test methods in the class to be valid for every argument set — you cannot skip individual methods per argument. If one engine lacks a feature, extract those tests into a separate `@ParameterizedClass` with a filtered `@MethodSource` rather than using `Assumptions.assumeTrue` inside each method. [official]

---

**Pattern 272** — AssertJ `usingRecursiveComparison().ignoringFields()` for DTO round-trip assertions [official]
AssertJ's recursive comparison API deep-equals two object graphs without requiring `equals`/`hashCode`. Pairing it with `ignoringFields` lets you exclude server-generated ids or timestamps while still verifying every other field, removing brittle `equals` overrides from production DTOs.
```java
import org.assertj.core.api.Assertions;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import java.time.Instant;

class ProductDtoRoundTripTest {

    @Test
    void createResponseMatchesRequest_ignoringServerFields() {
        var request = new CreateProductRequest("Widget", "blue", 9.99);
        var response = productService.create(request);

        Assertions.assertThat(response)
            .usingRecursiveComparison()
            .ignoringFields("id", "createdAt", "updatedAt")
            .isEqualTo(new CreateProductRequest("Widget", "blue", 9.99));
    }

    @Test
    void listResponsePreservesOrder() {
        var responses = productService.list();

        Assertions.assertThat(responses)
            .usingRecursiveFieldByFieldElementComparator()
            .ignoringFields("id", "createdAt")
            .containsExactlyInAnyOrder(EXPECTED_A, EXPECTED_B, EXPECTED_C);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: Recursive comparison walks the full object graph including nested collections; when DTOs are deeply nested, the comparison can be slow and produce multi-page diff output on failure. Use `ignoringFieldsMatchingRegexes(".*At", ".*Id")` to suppress entire categories of fields by naming convention rather than listing each one explicitly. [official]

---

**Pattern 273** — Mockito `InOrder` + `verifyNoMoreInteractions` for strict call-sequence verification [official]
When protocol order matters (e.g., a circuit-breaker must open before any retry, or an audit log must be written before the commit), `InOrder` enforces the exact sequence. Combining it with `verifyNoMoreInteractions` catches unexpected extra calls that a plain `verify` would miss.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;
import org.mockito.InOrder;
import org.mockito.Mock;
import org.mockito.Mockito;
import org.mockito.junit.jupiter.MockitoExtension;

@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class PaymentProcessorTest {

    @Mock AuditLogger auditLogger;
    @Mock PaymentGateway gateway;
    @Mock AccountLedger ledger;

    @Test
    void auditIsWrittenBeforeGatewayCharge() {
        var processor = new PaymentProcessor(auditLogger, gateway, ledger);
        processor.charge("ACC-1", Money.of(50, "EUR"));

        InOrder inOrder = Mockito.inOrder(auditLogger, gateway, ledger);
        inOrder.verify(auditLogger).recordAttempt("ACC-1", Money.of(50, "EUR"));
        inOrder.verify(gateway).charge("ACC-1", Money.of(50, "EUR"));
        inOrder.verify(ledger).debit("ACC-1", Money.of(50, "EUR"));
        inOrder.verify(auditLogger).recordSuccess("ACC-1");
        Mockito.verifyNoMoreInteractions(auditLogger, gateway, ledger);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `verifyNoMoreInteractions` makes tests brittle when the class under test is extended with logging or metrics calls — every new collaborator interaction requires updating the test. Use it only on the interactions that are contractually meaningful, and extract infrastructure calls (metrics, tracing) behind a dedicated port so they can be excluded from strict verification. [official]

---

**Pattern 274** — `@DataJpaTest` + `@Sql` with `MERGE` executionPhase for fixture setup and teardown [official]
`@Sql` annotations on `@DataJpaTest` methods can run SQL scripts before AND after each test, giving deterministic fixture control independent of transaction rollback. Using `@SqlMergeMode(MERGE)` combines class-level and method-level `@Sql` declarations without redundancy.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.orm.jpa.DataJpaTest;
import org.springframework.test.context.jdbc.Sql;
import org.springframework.test.context.jdbc.SqlMergeMode;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.springframework.test.context.jdbc.Sql.ExecutionPhase.AFTER_TEST_METHOD;
import static org.springframework.test.context.jdbc.SqlMergeMode.MergeMode.MERGE;

@DataJpaTest
@Sql("classpath:fixtures/inventory-base.sql")
@SqlMergeMode(MERGE)
class InventoryRepositoryTest {

    @Autowired InventoryRepository repo;

    @Test
    @Sql("classpath:fixtures/inventory-with-reserved.sql")
    @Sql(scripts = "classpath:fixtures/inventory-cleanup.sql",
         executionPhase = AFTER_TEST_METHOD)
    void reservedItemsAreExcludedFromAvailableCount() {
        assertThat(repo.countAvailable("SKU-42")).isEqualTo(3);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: Running SQL directly bypasses Hibernate's second-level cache and sequence generators; inserts from `@Sql` scripts may collide with auto-generated ids if sequences are not reset between tests. Prefix fixture ids with a large offset (e.g., `9000`) and reset sequences in the cleanup script to avoid clashes with ids produced by `save()` calls. [official]

---

**Pattern 275** — `WireMock` `RecordSpec` + `SnapshotRecorder` for contract capture from live services [official]
WireMock's recording mode (`WireMock.startRecording(RecordSpec)`) proxies HTTP calls to a real upstream and persists matching request-response pairs as stub mappings. Replaying those stubs in CI guarantees the test suite validates realistic payloads without hitting live endpoints.
```java
import com.github.tomakehurst.wiremock.WireMockServer;
import com.github.tomakehurst.wiremock.recording.RecordSpec;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.AfterEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static com.github.tomakehurst.wiremock.core.WireMockConfiguration.options;
import static com.github.tomakehurst.wiremock.client.WireMock.*;

class CurrencyApiContractTest {

    WireMockServer wm = new WireMockServer(options().port(8089).withRootDirectory("src/test/resources/wiremock"));

    @BeforeEach void start() { wm.start(); }
    @AfterEach  void stop()  { wm.stop();  }

    // Run once with wm.startRecording(...) to capture; then switch to playback:
    @Test
    void eurToUsdConversionUsesRecordedRate() {
        wm.stubFor(get(urlPathEqualTo("/rates/EUR"))
            .willReturn(okJson("{\"base\":\"EUR\",\"rates\":{\"USD\":1.087}}")));

        var client = new CurrencyClient("http://localhost:8089");
        var rate = client.getRate("EUR", "USD");

        assertThat(rate).isEqualByComparingTo("1.087");
        wm.verify(getRequestedFor(urlPathEqualTo("/rates/EUR")));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: Recorded stubs reflect the upstream API at one point in time; as the live API evolves, stubs silently drift and tests may pass on stale contracts. Schedule a quarterly "re-record" CI job that runs with `WIREMOCK_RECORD=true` and commits updated stubs, making drift visible in diff review. [official]

---

**Pattern 276** — `Testcontainers` `@ServiceConnection` with custom `ConnectionDetailsFactory` for non-standard images [official]
Spring Boot's `@ServiceConnection` resolves `ConnectionDetails` beans automatically for well-known Testcontainers images (Postgres, Redis, Kafka). For custom or enterprise images, implement `ConnectionDetailsFactory` to wire the container's dynamic ports into Spring's property space without `@DynamicPropertySource` boilerplate.
```java
import org.springframework.boot.testcontainers.service.connection.ServiceConnection;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.testcontainers.containers.GenericContainer;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Container;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Testcontainers;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@SpringBootTest
@Testcontainers
class VaultServiceConnectionTest {

    @Container
    @ServiceConnection            // requires VaultConnectionDetailsFactory on classpath
    static final GenericContainer<?> VAULT =
        new GenericContainer<>("hashicorp/vault:1.17")
            .withExposedPorts(8200)
            .withEnv("VAULT_DEV_ROOT_TOKEN_ID", "test-token")
            .withEnv("VAULT_DEV_LISTEN_ADDRESS", "0.0.0.0:8200");

    @Test
    void secretsAreReadFromVaultContainer(
            @Autowired VaultTemplate vaultTemplate) {
        vaultTemplate.write("secret/data/db", Map.of("password", "s3cr3t"));
        var secret = vaultTemplate.read("secret/data/db", Map.class);
        assertThat(secret.getData()).containsEntry("password", "s3cr3t");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: Custom `ConnectionDetailsFactory` implementations are discovered via `spring.factories` / `AutoConfiguration.imports` and must be on the test classpath. If the factory is in a shared test utilities module, ensure the module is `testImplementation` scoped; accidentally shipping it as a `compile` dependency injects Testcontainers into production builds. [official]

---

**Pattern 277** — JUnit 5 `TestFactory` + `DynamicContainer` for data-driven nested test trees [official]
`@TestFactory` methods can return `Stream<DynamicContainer>` to build a multi-level test tree from external data (CSV, JSON, database). Each container groups related `DynamicTest` nodes under a named heading, making large data-driven suites navigable in IDE report trees.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.DynamicContainer;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.DynamicTest;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.TestFactory;
import java.util.stream.Stream;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.DynamicContainer.dynamicContainer;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.DynamicTest.dynamicTest;

class PricingRulesDynamicTest {

    record RuleFixture(String sku, int qty, double expectedPrice) {}

    @TestFactory
    Stream<DynamicContainer> pricingRulesFromFixtures() {
        return PricingFixtureLoader.loadAll().stream()
            .map(group -> dynamicContainer(
                "Group: " + group.category(),
                group.fixtures().stream().map(f -> dynamicTest(
                    "SKU=%s qty=%d → %.2f".formatted(f.sku(), f.qty(), f.expectedPrice()),
                    () -> {
                        double actual = PricingEngine.calculate(f.sku(), f.qty());
                        assertThat(actual).isEqualByComparingTo(f.expectedPrice());
                    }
                ))
            ));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: Dynamic tests are discovered at runtime, so static analysis tools and coverage engines may report them as uncovered until the test suite runs. Maven Surefire requires JUnit Platform 1.10+ to report individual dynamic test names in Surefire XML; older versions lump all `DynamicTest` results under the factory method name, losing per-case visibility. [official]

---

**Pattern 278** — Mockito `thenAnswer` with `ArgumentCaptor` for asynchronous callback verification [official]
When production code accepts a callback interface and invokes it on a different thread, `ArgumentCaptor` captures the callback reference injected by `thenAnswer`, allowing the test to invoke it synchronously and assert downstream effects without `CountDownLatch` coordination.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;
import org.mockito.ArgumentCaptor;
import org.mockito.Captor;
import org.mockito.Mock;
import org.mockito.junit.jupiter.MockitoExtension;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.*;

@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class AsyncNotifierTest {

    @Mock MessageQueue queue;
    @Mock NotificationSink sink;
    @Captor ArgumentCaptor<MessageQueue.Callback> callbackCaptor;

    @Test
    void onDeliveryCallbackUpdatesOrderStatus() {
        var notifier = new AsyncNotifier(queue, sink);

        notifier.sendOrderConfirmation("ORD-55");

        verify(queue).publish(eq("order.confirmed:ORD-55"), callbackCaptor.capture());
        // Invoke callback synchronously to simulate broker ack:
        callbackCaptor.getValue().onDelivered("msg-id-99");

        verify(sink).markDelivered("ORD-55", "msg-id-99");
        assertThat(notifier.pendingCount()).isZero();
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: Driving callbacks synchronously in tests skips real threading concerns (race conditions, re-entrancy). Complement callback tests with at least one integration test using a real thread-pool executor and `Awaitility.await().untilAsserted(...)` to catch concurrency bugs that pure-mock tests cannot surface. [official]

---

**Pattern 279** — `jqwik` `@Property` with `@ForAll @Size` for collection boundary verification [official]
Property-based tests with jqwik generate hundreds of randomised inputs, including empty collections, single-element collections, and max-size collections. The `@Size` constraint restricts the generated collection size, making edge-case coverage explicit in the test signature.
```java
import net.jqwik.api.*;
import net.jqwik.api.constraints.Size;
import java.util.List;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

class CartTotalsPropertyTest {

    @Property(tries = 500)
    void totalIsNeverNegative(
            @ForAll @Size(min = 0, max = 20) List<@Positive Double> prices) {
        var cart = Cart.of(prices);
        assertThat(cart.total()).isGreaterThanOrEqualTo(0.0);
    }

    @Property
    void addingItemIncreasesOrMaintainsTotal(
            @ForAll @Size(min = 1, max = 10) List<@Positive Double> existing,
            @ForAll @Positive double newPrice) {
        var before = Cart.of(existing).total();
        var after  = Cart.of(existing).addItem(newPrice).total();
        assertThat(after).isGreaterThanOrEqualTo(before);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: jqwik generates seeds deterministically when a failure is found and prints the failing seed in the test output, enabling exact reproduction. However, shrinking complex custom types requires registering an `Arbitrary` provider — without shrinking, the reported failing example may be large and hard to diagnose. Always register minimal `Arbitrary` providers for domain types used in properties. [official]

---

**Pattern 280** — Spring Boot `MockMvcTester` fluent assertion chain for REST endpoint contracts [official]
`MockMvcTester` (Spring Boot 3.4+) wraps `MockMvc` in an AssertJ-compatible fluent API. Chaining `.exchange()` → `.assertThat()` → `.hasStatus()` → `.bodyJson()` in a single expression eliminates the `perform()`/`andExpect()` boilerplate and produces readable failure messages aligned with AssertJ conventions.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.web.servlet.WebMvcTest;
import org.springframework.test.web.servlet.assertj.MockMvcTester;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@WebMvcTest(ProductController.class)
class ProductControllerMockMvcTesterTest {

    @Autowired MockMvcTester mvc;

    @Test
    void getProductReturns200WithBody() {
        assertThat(mvc.get().uri("/products/42"))
            .hasStatusOk()
            .hasContentTypeCompatibleWith("application/json")
            .bodyJson()
            .extractingPath("$.name").isEqualTo("Widget");
    }

    @Test
    void createProductWithInvalidBodyReturns400() {
        assertThat(mvc.post().uri("/products")
                       .contentType("application/json")
                       .content("{\"name\":\"\"}"))
            .hasStatus(400)
            .bodyJson()
            .extractingPath("$.errors[0].field").isEqualTo("name");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `MockMvcTester.bodyJson()` uses Spring's `JsonPathExpectationsHelper` under the hood, which requires `com.jayway.jsonpath:json-path` on the test classpath. If that dependency is absent the call throws `NoClassDefFoundError` at runtime rather than a compile-time error. Add an explicit `testImplementation 'com.jayway.jsonpath:json-path'` dependency to avoid silent classpath surprises. [official]

---

**Pattern 281** — `ArchUnit` `layeredArchitecture()` with `allowEmptyShould` for incremental adoption [official]
ArchUnit's `layeredArchitecture()` DSL enforces that packages respect defined layer boundaries (controller → service → repository). The `allowEmptyShould(true)` flag prevents false failures when a layer has no classes yet, enabling teams to introduce architectural rules before all layers are populated.
```java
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ClassFileImporter;
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchRule;
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.Architectures;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

class LayeredArchitectureTest {

    @Test
    void layerDependenciesAreRespected() {
        var classes = new ClassFileImporter()
            .importPackages("com.example.shop");

        ArchRule rule = Architectures.layeredArchitecture()
            .consideringAllDependencies()
            .allowEmptyShould(true)
            .layer("Controllers").definedBy("..controller..")
            .layer("Services").definedBy("..service..")
            .layer("Repositories").definedBy("..repository..")
            .layer("Domain").definedBy("..domain..")
            .whereLayer("Controllers").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Controllers")
            .whereLayer("Services").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Controllers", "Services")
            .whereLayer("Repositories").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Services")
            .whereLayer("Domain").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Controllers", "Services", "Repositories");

        rule.check(classes);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `layeredArchitecture()` uses package name matching — if packages do not follow the `..layer..` convention strictly (e.g., utility classes live in `com.example.shop.util`), rules will misclassify them as "uncategorised" and throw cryptic "no class matches" errors. Define catch-all `ignoreDependency` rules for known exceptions and document package naming conventions in a project ADR. [official]

---

**Pattern 282** — `@RestClientTest` with `MockRestServiceServer` for HTTP client isolation [official]
`@RestClientTest` starts a minimal application context containing only the annotated `@Component` that uses `RestClient` or `RestTemplate`, along with a `MockRestServiceServer`. This isolates client code from the full `@SpringBootTest` context, cutting startup time by an order of magnitude.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.web.client.RestClientTest;
import org.springframework.http.MediaType;
import org.springframework.test.web.client.MockRestServiceServer;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.springframework.test.web.client.match.MockRestRequestMatchers.*;
import static org.springframework.test.web.client.response.MockRestResponseCreators.*;

@RestClientTest(WeatherClient.class)
class WeatherClientTest {

    @Autowired WeatherClient weatherClient;
    @Autowired MockRestServiceServer server;

    @Test
    void returnsTemperatureFromUpstream() {
        server.expect(requestTo("https://api.weather.example/current?city=Berlin"))
              .andExpect(method(org.springframework.http.HttpMethod.GET))
              .andRespond(withSuccess(
                  "{\"city\":\"Berlin\",\"tempC\":18.5}",
                  MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON));

        var result = weatherClient.current("Berlin");

        assertThat(result.tempC()).isEqualTo(18.5);
        server.verify();
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `MockRestServiceServer` verifies that ALL expected requests were made via `server.verify()` — a missing call triggers an `AssertionError` even if the test method itself passed. If production code makes conditional HTTP calls (e.g., a cache hit skips the upstream call), add `server.expect(ExpectedCount.between(0, 1), ...)` to declare optional expectations rather than mandatory ones. [official]

---

**Pattern 283** — Virtual thread `CountDownLatch` stress test for pinning regression detection [official]
Virtual threads park rather than block OS threads, but synchronised blocks (`synchronized` keyword) pin a virtual thread to its carrier. Adding a stress test that runs hundreds of concurrent virtual-thread tasks through the code path under test, while recording pin events via JFR, catches regressions before they reach production.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import java.util.concurrent.*;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

class VirtualThreadPinningRegressionTest {

    @Test
    void orderServiceDoesNotPinVirtualThreads() throws Exception {
        int concurrency = 200;
        var latch   = new CountDownLatch(concurrency);
        var success = new AtomicInteger();
        var errors  = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<Throwable>();

        try (var executor = Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()) {
            for (int i = 0; i < concurrency; i++) {
                int orderId = i;
                executor.submit(() -> {
                    try {
                        orderService.process("ORD-" + orderId);
                        success.incrementAndGet();
                    } catch (Throwable t) {
                        errors.add(t);
                    } finally {
                        latch.countDown();
                    }
                });
            }
            latch.await(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
        }

        assertThat(errors).isEmpty();
        assertThat(success.get()).isEqualTo(concurrency);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: This test detects throughput degradation from pinning only when the test runs long enough for the thread scheduler to exhibit stalls. For precise pinning detection, enable JFR with `-XX:StartFlightRecording` and inspect `jdk.VirtualThreadPinned` events in the recording; the stress test alone cannot distinguish slow execution from pinning without JFR data. [official]

---

**Pattern 284** — `SoftAssertions` scoped to `assertSoftly` lambda for field-by-field DTO validation [official]
`SoftAssertions.assertSoftly` collects all assertion failures in the lambda before re-throwing them together. This ensures every field of a complex response DTO is checked in a single test execution rather than stopping at the first failure, dramatically reducing debugging cycles.
```java
import org.assertj.core.api.SoftAssertions;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

class InvoiceResponseSoftAssertionTest {

    @Test
    void invoiceResponseContainsAllExpectedFields() {
        InvoiceResponse invoice = invoiceService.generate("CUST-7", List.of("ITEM-1", "ITEM-2"));

        SoftAssertions.assertSoftly(soft -> {
            soft.assertThat(invoice.invoiceId()).isNotBlank();
            soft.assertThat(invoice.customerId()).isEqualTo("CUST-7");
            soft.assertThat(invoice.lineItems()).hasSize(2);
            soft.assertThat(invoice.lineItems().get(0).sku()).isEqualTo("ITEM-1");
            soft.assertThat(invoice.lineItems().get(1).sku()).isEqualTo("ITEM-2");
            soft.assertThat(invoice.subtotal()).isGreaterThan(BigDecimal.ZERO);
            soft.assertThat(invoice.tax()).isGreaterThanOrEqualTo(BigDecimal.ZERO);
            soft.assertThat(invoice.total()).isEqualByComparingTo(
                invoice.subtotal().add(invoice.tax()));
            soft.assertThat(invoice.currency()).isEqualTo("EUR");
            soft.assertThat(invoice.issuedAt()).isBeforeOrEqualTo(Instant.now());
        });
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: Soft assertions do not short-circuit — all assertions in the lambda run even if early ones indicate a null reference that would cause a `NullPointerException` in later assertions. Guard nullable fields with `soft.assertThat(invoice.lineItems()).isNotNull()` before indexing into the list, or wrap risky assertions in `soft.assertThatCode(() -> ...).doesNotThrowAnyException()`. [official]

---

**Pattern 285** — `@JsonTest` `JacksonTester` for isolated ObjectMapper serialisation/deserialisation contracts [official]
`@JsonTest` loads only Jackson configuration beans, `@JsonComponent` classes, and `Modules`, bypassing the full application context. `JacksonTester<T>.write()` and `.read()` provide `JsonContent` / `ObjectContent` wrappers with JSONPath assertions, making JSON contract tests self-contained and fast.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.json.JsonTest;
import org.springframework.boot.test.json.JacksonTester;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@JsonTest
class ShipmentDtoJsonTest {

    @Autowired JacksonTester<ShipmentDto> json;

    @Test
    void serialisesTrackingNumberUnderSnakeCaseKey() throws Exception {
        var dto = new ShipmentDto("SHP-99", "1Z999AA10123456784", ShipmentStatus.IN_TRANSIT);

        assertThat(json.write(dto))
            .extractingJsonPathStringValue("$.tracking_number")
            .isEqualTo("1Z999AA10123456784");
    }

    @Test
    void deserialisesStatusEnumCaseInsensitively() throws Exception {
        var content = "{\"id\":\"SHP-99\",\"tracking_number\":\"1Z\",\"status\":\"in_transit\"}";

        assertThat(json.read(content).getObject().status())
            .isEqualTo(ShipmentStatus.IN_TRANSIT);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@JsonTest` does NOT scan `@JsonComponent` beans defined in `@Configuration` classes outside the test slice's component-scan path. If a custom serialiser lives in a `@Configuration`-annotated class rather than directly annotated with `@JsonComponent`, it will be silently omitted and serialisation will fall back to default behaviour, producing a false-positive pass. Move custom serialisers to `@JsonComponent`-annotated standalone classes to guarantee slice inclusion. [official]

---

### Community Gotchas

**Gotcha G6: `@Nested` test classes that declare `@MockitoBean` fields cause Spring to create a new `ApplicationContext` for each nested class — multiplying context startup time by the number of nesting levels — WHY: Spring's context caching key includes the set of mock definitions in the `MergedContextConfiguration`. Each `@Nested` class that adds or changes a `@MockitoBean` declaration produces a unique cache key, forcing a fresh `ApplicationContext` for that class even when the enclosing class already loaded one with a compatible context. Developers commonly assume `@Nested` classes share the parent's context, but the mock registration list is part of the cache key comparison. Fix: extract `@MockitoBean` fields to the top-level test class so all nested classes inherit the same mock configuration, keeping the cache key identical across nesting levels and reusing a single context for the whole class hierarchy.**

**Gotcha G7: `Mockito.spy()` on a `final` class or a class with `final` methods silently falls back to a subclass proxy — which is NOT a spy of the original instance — causing `verify()` calls to pass vacuously because the spy tracks calls on the proxy, not on the instance injected into production code — WHY: When Mockito cannot subclass a `final` class (inline mock maker not enabled), it creates a wrapper proxy and returns it. If the original instance was already injected into the class under test (e.g., via `@Autowired` before `spy()` wraps it), production code calls methods on the unwrapped original, which records no interactions. The spy proxy's verify then confirms zero calls — technically correct for the proxy, but the test author meant to verify the original. Fix: enable Mockito's inline mock maker (`mockito-inline` or Mockito 5's default) which uses instrumentation to spy on `final` types in-place, or refactor `final` types behind interfaces so a standard subclass-based spy works correctly.**

**Gotcha G8: `Testcontainers` containers started inside `@BeforeAll` without `static` scope cause a new container for every test method because JUnit creates a new test instance per method by default — WHY: JUnit 5's default `@TestInstance(PER_METHOD)` lifecycle instantiates a new test class object before each test. A container field declared as a non-static instance variable is therefore freshly constructed and started for every test, ignoring any `@BeforeAll` intent. The container appears to start "once" because `@BeforeAll` is called once per class instance, but a new instance (and new container) is created for every test. Fix: declare `@Container` fields as `static` — Testcontainers' JUnit extension manages static fields per class, starting them once before the first test and stopping them after the last, matching the expected "once per class" lifecycle.**

**Gotcha G9: `AssertJ` `extracting(FieldName)` on a collection silently returns `null` values without failing when the field name is misspelled — producing a list of `null` assertions that vacuously pass `isEqualTo(null)` — WHY: `extracting(String... fields)` uses reflection to access fields by name. If the field name does not exist, Mockito/AssertJ returns `null` for that extraction rather than throwing a `NoSuchFieldException`, because the extraction path catches reflection exceptions and substitutes `null`. Tests that then call `.contains(null)` or `.allMatch(v -> v == null)` pass silently, masking the misspelling. Fix: prefer the type-safe lambda form `extracting(MyDto::getField)` which causes a compile-time error if the method does not exist, making field-name errors impossible; or enable `assertj.extracting.fail-on-null=true` in a custom `Assertions` configuration if the string-based form is unavoidable.**

**Gotcha G10: `@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT)` combined with `@DirtiesContext` causes a new random port to be allocated for each test class — but `@LocalServerPort` injects the port only once at context creation, so any cached `WebTestClient` or `RestTemplate` bean built with the old port stills points at the closed server after context recreation — WHY: `@DirtiesContext` destroys the `ApplicationContext` and creates a fresh one for the next test. The new context allocates a new random port. However, `@LocalServerPort` beans are injected from the context that was active at injection time; if a shared static `WebTestClient` field was initialised with the first context's port, it retains that stale port. The new server is not reachable on the old port, causing `ConnectionRefused` errors that look like infrastructure failures rather than test-configuration bugs. Fix: never cache `WebTestClient` in static fields when using `@DirtiesContext`; inject a fresh `WebTestClient` as a `@Autowired` instance field in every test class so it is reconstructed from the current context's port each time.**

## Cycle 58 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 286** — JUnit 5 `@RegisterExtension` for programmatic extension wiring with constructor injection
When an extension needs constructor parameters that are not available at annotation processing time (e.g., a per-test database name derived from a `@TempDir` path), `@RegisterExtension` lets you instantiate the extension as a field, passing those parameters directly and wiring them via `ParameterResolver` callbacks.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.RegisterExtension;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

import java.nio.file.Path;

class FileStorageServiceTest {

    @TempDir
    Path tempDir;

    @RegisterExtension
    EmbeddedH2Extension db = EmbeddedH2Extension.withBaseDir(() -> tempDir.resolve("h2"));

    @Test
    void persistsAndLoadsBlob() {
        var svc = new FileStorageService(db.dataSource());
        var id  = svc.store("hello".getBytes());
        assertThat(svc.load(id)).asString().isEqualTo("hello");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@RegisterExtension` fields must be `static` for `@BeforeAll`-level lifecycle; non-static fields get per-test lifecycle. Mixing static and non-static `@RegisterExtension` fields in the same class can cause subtle ordering bugs when one extension depends on state set up by another — declare explicit dependencies via `@ExtendWith` ordering or use a single composite extension. [official]

---

**Pattern 287** — `@ParameterizedTest` with `@MethodSource` streaming domain objects instead of primitives
Returning typed domain objects directly from a `@MethodSource` factory eliminates the boilerplate of converting raw CSV arguments into domain values inside every test method, keeping each test body focused on behaviour rather than argument construction.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.params.ParameterizedTest;
import org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.MethodSource;

import java.util.stream.Stream;

class PricingEngineTest {

    static Stream<PricingScenario> scenarios() {
        return Stream.of(
            new PricingScenario(Money.of(100, "USD"), TaxRegion.US, Money.of(108, "USD")),
            new PricingScenario(Money.of(100, "EUR"), TaxRegion.EU, Money.of(119, "EUR")),
            new PricingScenario(Money.of(0,   "USD"), TaxRegion.US, Money.of(0,   "USD"))
        );
    }

    @ParameterizedTest(name = "[{index}] {0}")
    @MethodSource("scenarios")
    void appliesTaxCorrectly(PricingScenario s) {
        var engine = new PricingEngine();
        assertThat(engine.applyTax(s.net(), s.region()))
            .isEqualByComparingTo(s.expected());
    }

    record PricingScenario(Money net, TaxRegion region, Money expected) {}
}
```
Tradeoff: Rich domain objects in `@MethodSource` make test names less descriptive by default because `toString()` on a record shows field values without semantic context. Override `toString()` in the record or use `@ParameterizedTest(name = "...")` with index/argument placeholders to restore clarity in the test report. [official]

---

**Pattern 288** — AssertJ `usingComparatorForType` for approximate floating-point assertions in collections
When asserting collections of objects containing `double` or `float` fields, standard `containsExactly` fails on floating-point rounding. `usingComparatorForType(Comparator, type)` plugs a tolerance comparator into AssertJ's recursive comparison engine so every `Double` in the graph uses approximate equality without requiring manual delta checks.
```java
import org.assertj.core.api.Assertions;
import org.assertj.core.util.introspection.IntrospectionError;

import java.util.Comparator;
import java.util.List;

class MetricsAggregatorTest {

    @Test
    void aggregatesLatencyPercentiles() {
        var agg = new MetricsAggregator();
        List<Percentile> result = agg.compute(rawSamples());

        Assertions.assertThat(result)
            .usingComparatorForType(
                Comparator.comparingDouble(d -> Math.abs(d - ((Double) /* expected */ 0.0) < 1e-6 ? 0 : 1),
                Double.class)
            )
            .usingRecursiveFieldByFieldElementComparator()
            .containsExactlyInAnyOrder(
                new Percentile(50, 12.345),
                new Percentile(95, 45.678),
                new Percentile(99, 98.765)
            );
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `usingComparatorForType` applies globally to ALL instances of that type in the recursive graph, including fields that should use exact equality (e.g., a `double` ID field). Narrow the comparator scope with `usingComparatorForFields(Comparator, fieldName)` for specific fields when only a subset of doubles needs tolerance. [official]

---

**Pattern 289** — Mockito `mockConstruction` for sealing `new` calls inside legacy code under test
When production code calls `new SomeService(...)` internally and there is no injection point, `Mockito.mockConstruction(SomeService.class, (mock, ctx) -> { ... })` intercepts the constructor call within the try-with-resources scope, letting you configure and verify the inline-created instance without modifying production code.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.mockito.MockedConstruction;
import org.mockito.Mockito;

class OrderProcessorTest {

    @Test
    void delegatesToFraudCheckerCreatedInternally() {
        try (MockedConstruction<FraudChecker> mocked =
                 Mockito.mockConstruction(FraudChecker.class, (mock, ctx) -> {
                     // ctx.arguments() gives constructor args for assertion
                     assertThat(ctx.arguments()).containsExactly("strict");
                     Mockito.when(mock.isFraudulent(any())).thenReturn(false);
                 })) {

            var processor = new OrderProcessor(); // internally does: new FraudChecker("strict")
            processor.process(sampleOrder());

            FraudChecker captured = mocked.constructed().get(0);
            Mockito.verify(captured).isFraudulent(sampleOrder());
        }
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `mockConstruction` is thread-local — it intercepts `new` calls only on the same thread that opens the scope. Tests that create objects on other threads (e.g., parallel streams, virtual threads spawned in the constructor) will not be intercepted and will receive real instances, causing silent mock miss. Use a `CountDownLatch` to synchronise cross-thread construction or refactor to inject the dependency. [official]

---

**Pattern 290** — `@DataJpaTest` with `replace = AutoConfigureTestDatabase.Replace.NONE` + Testcontainers `@ServiceConnection`
Replacing the embedded in-memory database with a real PostgreSQL container wired via `@ServiceConnection` gives accurate query-plan and index-usage tests while retaining the lightweight slice that loads only JPA infrastructure, not the full application context.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.jdbc.AutoConfigureTestDatabase;
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.orm.jpa.DataJpaTest;
import org.springframework.boot.testcontainers.service.connection.ServiceConnection;
import org.testcontainers.containers.PostgreSQLContainer;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Container;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Testcontainers;

@DataJpaTest
@AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = AutoConfigureTestDatabase.Replace.NONE)
@Testcontainers
class ProductRepositoryIT {

    @Container
    @ServiceConnection
    static PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres =
        new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine");

    @Autowired ProductRepository repo;

    @Test
    void findsActiveProductsByCategory() {
        repo.saveAll(List.of(
            new Product("A", "BOOKS",  true),
            new Product("B", "BOOKS",  false),
            new Product("C", "GAMES",  true)
        ));
        assertThat(repo.findActiveByCategoryName("BOOKS"))
            .extracting(Product::name)
            .containsExactly("A");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: The Testcontainers `@Container static` field is shared across all test classes in the JVM that reference the same image tag. If parallel test execution is enabled (`junit.jupiter.execution.parallel.enabled=true`), multiple test classes may acquire connections from the same container simultaneously, requiring the pool to be sized accordingly or `@Testcontainers(disabledWithoutDocker = true)` to be added to avoid CI failures in Docker-less environments. [official]

---

**Pattern 291** — JUnit 5 `TestExecutionExceptionHandler` extension to convert expected infrastructure failures into `TestAbortedException`
Integration tests that depend on external systems should skip rather than fail when the infrastructure is unavailable. Wrapping connection-refused exceptions in `TestAbortedException` inside a registered `TestExecutionExceptionHandler` makes the test suite green on developer machines without Docker while still failing on CI where Docker is expected.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtensionContext;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.TestExecutionExceptionHandler;
import org.opentest4j.TestAbortedException;

import java.net.ConnectException;

public class InfraAbortExtension implements TestExecutionExceptionHandler {

    @Override
    public void handleTestExecutionException(ExtensionContext ctx, Throwable t)
            throws Throwable {
        if (isInfraUnavailable(t)) {
            throw new TestAbortedException(
                "Infrastructure unavailable — skipping: " + t.getMessage(), t);
        }
        throw t;
    }

    private boolean isInfraUnavailable(Throwable t) {
        return t instanceof ConnectException
            || (t.getCause() != null && isInfraUnavailable(t.getCause()));
    }
}

// Registration
@ExtendWith(InfraAbortExtension.class)
class ExternalPaymentGatewayIT {
    @Test
    void chargesCard() { /* uses real gateway */ }
}
```
Tradeoff: Swallowing infrastructure exceptions as skips can mask genuine regressions if the production code starts throwing `ConnectException` for reasons unrelated to infrastructure availability (e.g., a bad URL configuration bug). Limit the abort logic to specific, narrow exception messages or response codes rather than the entire exception type, so configuration bugs still fail loudly. [official]

---

**Pattern 292** — AssertJ `satisfiesExactly` for ordered collection invariants beyond element equality
`satisfiesExactly` accepts one `Consumer` per expected element and asserts both count and order, letting you express partial field checks on each element independently — useful when elements are not comparable or when only certain fields of each element are under test.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

class TimelineServiceTest {

    @Test
    void returnsEventsInAscendingChronologicalOrder() {
        List<TimelineEvent> events = new TimelineService()
            .buildForUser("u42", LocalDate.of(2026, 1, 1), LocalDate.of(2026, 1, 31));

        assertThat(events).satisfiesExactly(
            first -> {
                assertThat(first.type()).isEqualTo(EventType.ACCOUNT_OPENED);
                assertThat(first.occurredAt()).isEqualTo(LocalDate.of(2026, 1, 5));
            },
            second -> {
                assertThat(second.type()).isEqualTo(EventType.FIRST_PURCHASE);
                assertThat(second.occurredAt()).isAfter(LocalDate.of(2026, 1, 5));
            },
            third -> assertThat(third.type()).isEqualTo(EventType.REWARD_EARNED)
        );
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `satisfiesExactly` requires an exact element count — if the service adds a new event type, all existing tests with this assertion break even if the newly asserted elements are still correct. Use `satisfiesExactlyInAnyOrder` when ordering is irrelevant, or add explicit size assertions separately so count failures produce a distinct message from content failures. [official]

---

**Pattern 293** — Awaitility `conditionEvaluationListener` for diagnosing flaky asynchronous assertions
By default Awaitility polls silently and reports only the final timeout failure. Attaching a `ConditionEvaluationListener` logs each intermediate poll result, giving a timeline of exactly when a condition became true or what value it held across the wait window — invaluable for diagnosing intermittent timing failures.
```java
import org.awaitility.Awaitility;
import org.awaitility.core.ConditionEvaluationListener;
import org.awaitility.core.EvaluatedCondition;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit;

class NotificationDispatcherTest {

    @Test
    void dispatchesEmailWithinTwoSeconds() {
        var inbox = new InMemoryInbox();
        var dispatcher = new NotificationDispatcher(inbox);

        dispatcher.sendWelcome("user@example.com");

        Awaitility.await("welcome email dispatched")
            .atMost(2, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
            .conditionEvaluationListener(condition -> {
                if (!condition.isSatisfied()) {
                    System.out.printf(
                        "[%dms] inbox size=%d, still waiting%n",
                        condition.getElapsedTimeInMS(),
                        inbox.size());
                }
            })
            .untilAsserted(() ->
                assertThat(inbox.messagesFor("user@example.com"))
                    .hasSize(1)
                    .first()
                    .extracting(Message::subject)
                    .isEqualTo("Welcome!")
            );
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `conditionEvaluationListener` logs a line on every poll tick, which can flood logs when `pollInterval` is very small (< 50 ms) and `atMost` is large. Either increase `pollInterval` to reduce log volume, or gate the listener on a system property so it activates only when debugging flakes, keeping CI logs clean. [official]

---

**Pattern 294** — WireMock `scenarioState` for stateful stub sequences in multi-step protocol tests
WireMock's scenario API lets you model protocol conversations — login → fetch resource → logout — where each stub is active only in a specific named state. The stub transitions the scenario to the next state after it fires, ensuring subsequent requests hit the correct stub without complex conditional logic in the test setup.
```java
import com.github.tomakehurst.wiremock.junit5.WireMockExtension;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.RegisterExtension;

import static com.github.tomakehurst.wiremock.client.WireMock.*;
import static com.github.tomakehurst.wiremock.stubbing.Scenario.STARTED;

class OAuthTokenRefreshTest {

    @RegisterExtension
    static WireMockExtension wm = WireMockExtension.newInstance().build();

    @Test
    void refreshesTokenTransparently() {
        wm.stubFor(get("/api/resource")
            .inScenario("token-refresh")
            .whenScenarioStateIs(STARTED)
            .willReturn(unauthorized())
            .willSetStateTo("token-expired"));

        wm.stubFor(post("/oauth/token")
            .inScenario("token-refresh")
            .whenScenarioStateIs("token-expired")
            .willReturn(okJson("{\"access_token\":\"new-token\",\"expires_in\":3600}"))
            .willSetStateTo("token-refreshed"));

        wm.stubFor(get("/api/resource")
            .inScenario("token-refresh")
            .whenScenarioStateIs("token-refreshed")
            .withHeader("Authorization", equalTo("Bearer new-token"))
            .willReturn(okJson("{\"id\":42}")));

        var client = new ApiClient(wm.baseUrl());
        assertThat(client.getResource()).extracting("id").isEqualTo(42);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: WireMock scenarios are global to the WireMock server instance. Parallel test classes sharing a server will corrupt each other's scenario state, causing intermittent `NoMatchingMapping` failures. Ensure each test class gets its own `WireMockExtension` instance (or use `@WireMockTest` per class) and call `wm.resetScenarios()` in `@BeforeEach` when sharing a server is unavoidable. [official]

---

**Pattern 295** — `@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)` with `@Captor` for multi-invocation argument capture
`ArgumentCaptor.getAllValues()` collects every argument passed across multiple invocations of a method, enabling assertions on the full call sequence without duplicating `verify()` calls or using `InOrder`.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;
import org.mockito.ArgumentCaptor;
import org.mockito.Captor;
import org.mockito.Mock;
import org.mockito.Mockito;
import org.mockito.junit.jupiter.MockitoExtension;

import java.util.List;

@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class AuditServiceTest {

    @Mock AuditRepository auditRepo;
    @Captor ArgumentCaptor<AuditEvent> eventCaptor;

    @Test
    void recordsAllStepsDuringOrderFulfillment() {
        var svc = new OrderFulfillmentService(auditRepo);
        svc.fulfill(Order.sample());

        Mockito.verify(auditRepo, Mockito.atLeast(3)).record(eventCaptor.capture());

        List<AuditEvent> events = eventCaptor.getAllValues();
        assertThat(events)
            .extracting(AuditEvent::type)
            .containsSubsequence(
                AuditEventType.ORDER_RECEIVED,
                AuditEventType.PAYMENT_CHARGED,
                AuditEventType.SHIPMENT_CREATED);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `ArgumentCaptor` is not thread-safe — if the method under capture is called from multiple threads simultaneously, `getAllValues()` may return values in a non-deterministic order. For concurrent scenarios, capture into a `CopyOnWriteArrayList` via `thenAnswer` instead, which provides a thread-safe accumulation with explicit ordering control. [official]

---

**Pattern 296** — ArchUnit `noClasses().that().resideInAPackage` for enforcing clean hexagonal boundaries
ArchUnit's fluent DSL can assert that domain classes never import adapters or infrastructure types, preventing accidental coupling that breaks the hexagonal architecture contract without requiring manual code review on every PR.
```java
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ClassFileImporter;
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchRule;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import static com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses;

class HexagonalBoundaryTest {

    private static final com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaClasses classes =
        new ClassFileImporter().importPackages("com.example.shop");

    @Test
    void domainMustNotDependOnAdapters() {
        ArchRule rule = noClasses()
            .that().resideInAPackage("..domain..")
            .should().dependOnClassesThat()
            .resideInAnyPackage("..adapter..", "..infrastructure..", "..web..");
        rule.check(classes);
    }

    @Test
    void adaptersMustNotCallEachOtherDirectly() {
        ArchRule rule = noClasses()
            .that().resideInAPackage("..adapter..")
            .should().dependOnClassesThat()
            .resideInAPackage("..adapter..")
            .orShould().dependOnClassesThat()
            .resideInAPackage("..adapter..");
        rule.check(classes);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: ArchUnit rules run against `.class` files, so they only catch violations that were compiled — if a submodule's classes are not on the classpath at test time, violations in that submodule are silently ignored. Use `ClassFileImporter.importPackagesOf(Application.class)` or configure `@AnalyzeClasses` at the module root to ensure all relevant packages are scanned, and add `allowEmptyShould(false)` to catch zero-match rules that pass vacuously. [official]

---

**Pattern 297** — Spring Boot `@AutoConfigureObservability` + `TestObservationRegistry` for tracing assertions
`@AutoConfigureObservability` wires a `TestObservationRegistry` bean into slice and full integration tests, letting you assert that specific span names, key-value pairs, and low-cardinality tags were recorded without deploying a real tracing backend.
```java
import io.micrometer.observation.tck.TestObservationRegistry;
import io.micrometer.observation.tck.TestObservationRegistryAssert;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.actuate.observability.AutoConfigureObservability;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;

@SpringBootTest
@AutoConfigureObservability
class CheckoutServiceObservabilityTest {

    @Autowired CheckoutService checkoutService;
    @Autowired TestObservationRegistry observationRegistry;

    @Test
    void recordsCheckoutSpanWithOrderIdTag() {
        observationRegistry.clear();

        checkoutService.checkout(Cart.sample("user-7"));

        TestObservationRegistryAssert.assertThat(observationRegistry)
            .hasObservationWithNameEqualTo("checkout")
            .that()
            .hasLowCardinalityKeyValue("outcome", "success")
            .hasHighCardinalityKeyValue("cart.user_id", "user-7");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `TestObservationRegistry` is shared across all beans in the context. If a background thread emits observations between `clear()` and the `assertThat` call, spurious observations can cause false-positive failures. Always call `observationRegistry.clear()` inside `@BeforeEach` rather than inside the test method, and prefer `@DirtiesContext` isolation when tests cover concurrent observation emission. [official]

---

**Pattern 298** — PIT mutation testing with `withHistory` incremental mode for fast feedback in large codebases
PIT's `withHistory` feature persists the results of previous mutation runs and only re-mutates classes whose bytecode has changed since the last run, reducing incremental mutation testing time from minutes to seconds in large modules.
```java
// pom.xml (Maven PIT plugin configuration)
// <plugin>
//   <groupId>org.pitest</groupId>
//   <artifactId>pitest-maven</artifactId>
//   <version>1.17.0</version>
//   <configuration>
//     <withHistory>true</withHistory>
//     <historyOutputFile>target/pit-history.dat</historyOutputFile>
//     <historyInputFile>target/pit-history.dat</historyInputFile>
//     <mutationThreshold>85</mutationThreshold>
//     <coverageThreshold>80</coverageThreshold>
//     <targetClasses>
//       <param>com.example.shop.domain.*</param>
//     </targetClasses>
//   </configuration>
// </plugin>

// Gradle equivalent (build.gradle.kts)
pitest {
    withHistory.set(true)
    historyOutputLocation.set(file("build/pit-history.dat"))
    historyInputLocation.set(file("build/pit-history.dat"))
    mutationThreshold.set(85)
    coverageThreshold.set(80)
    targetClasses.set(listOf("com.example.shop.domain.*"))
}
```
Tradeoff: The history file stores absolute bytecode hashes, so it becomes stale when the class file changes due to a compiler upgrade or annotation processor run even if the source is unchanged. If PIT unexpectedly re-mutates all classes after a toolchain upgrade, delete `pit-history.dat` to force a full baseline run, then commit the fresh history file so incremental mode resumes correctly. [official]

---

**Pattern 299** — jqwik `@Property` + `@ForAll @Size` for length-invariant string processing contracts
jqwik generates hundreds of random inputs per property, making it ideal for asserting invariants that must hold for any valid input — such as a slug generator that must always produce lowercase ASCII regardless of input length or content.
```java
import net.jqwik.api.*;
import net.jqwik.api.constraints.AlphaChars;
import net.jqwik.api.constraints.Size;
import net.jqwik.api.constraints.StringLength;

class SlugGeneratorProperties {

    @Property(tries = 500)
    void slugIsAlwaysLowercaseAscii(
            @ForAll @StringLength(min = 1, max = 200)
            @AlphaChars String input) {
        String slug = SlugGenerator.toSlug(input);
        assertThat(slug).matches("[a-z0-9-]+");
    }

    @Property
    void slugIdempotent(
            @ForAll @StringLength(min = 1, max = 50)
            @AlphaChars String input) {
        String once  = SlugGenerator.toSlug(input);
        String twice = SlugGenerator.toSlug(once);
        assertThat(twice).isEqualTo(once);
    }

    @Property
    void slugNeverExceedsMaxLength(
            @ForAll @StringLength(min = 1, max = 500)
            @AlphaChars String input) {
        assertThat(SlugGenerator.toSlug(input).length())
            .isLessThanOrEqualTo(255);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: jqwik shrinks failing examples to a minimal counterexample, which is excellent for diagnosis, but the shrunk example may not represent the original failure's distribution. When the failing input is shrunk to `"a"` but the actual failure only occurs for strings > 100 chars, the shrunk example hides the real precondition. Use `@Report(Reporting.GENERATED)` to log the original unshrunk input alongside the shrunk one. [official]

---

**Pattern 300** — JUnit 5 `@Nested` + `@TestInstance(PER_CLASS)` for BDD-style shared fixture without static fields
`@TestInstance(PER_CLASS)` creates one test class instance for the entire class, enabling `@BeforeAll` methods to be non-static and share instance-level mutable state (the BDD "given" context) across all `@Test` methods in a `@Nested` class without exposing `static` fields that can leak between runs.
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.*;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;
import org.mockito.Mock;
import org.mockito.Mockito;
import org.mockito.junit.jupiter.MockitoExtension;

@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
@TestInstance(TestInstance.Lifecycle.PER_CLASS)
class ShoppingCartBddTest {

    @Mock InventoryService inventory;
    ShoppingCart cart;

    @BeforeAll
    void givenCartWithTwoItems() {
        Mockito.when(inventory.isAvailable(any())).thenReturn(true);
        cart = new ShoppingCart(inventory);
        cart.add(new Item("book",   1, Money.of(15, "USD")));
        cart.add(new Item("pencil", 3, Money.of(2,  "USD")));
    }

    @Nested
    @DisplayName("when checkout is called")
    class WhenCheckout {

        @Test
        @DisplayName("total includes all items")
        void totalIsCorrect() {
            assertThat(cart.total()).isEqualByComparingTo(Money.of(21, "USD"));
        }

        @Test
        @DisplayName("item count matches added quantities")
        void countIsCorrect() {
            assertThat(cart.itemCount()).isEqualTo(4);
        }
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@TestInstance(PER_CLASS)` with `@MockitoBean` fields in a Spring context causes each nested class to share the same mock state across test methods unless Mockito resets between invocations. Without `@MockitoSettings(resetMocks = AFTER_EACH_TEST_METHOD)` or explicit `Mockito.reset(mock)` in `@AfterEach`, stub interactions bleed from one test into the next, corrupting `verify()` call counts and causing order-dependent test failures. [official]

---

### Community Gotchas

**G11: `@SpringBootTest` without `webEnvironment` defaults to `WebEnvironment.MOCK` — but `MockMvc` beans are NOT auto-configured unless `@AutoConfigureMockMvc` is also present — WHY: developers assume `@SpringBootTest` alone boots a testable web layer, but without `@AutoConfigureMockMvc` (or `@AutoConfigureWebTestClient` for reactive), no `MockMvc` / `WebTestClient` bean is registered. Tests that `@Autowired MockMvc mvc` silently get a null-injection or a `NoSuchBeanDefinitionException`, and the error message points at `MockMvc` rather than the missing annotation, sending developers to debug dispatcher-servlet wiring. Fix: always pair `@SpringBootTest` with `@AutoConfigureMockMvc` when you need `MockMvc`, or use the dedicated `@WebMvcTest` slice which auto-configures `MockMvc` by default and loads only MVC infrastructure for faster execution.**

**G12: Mockito `when(mock.method()).thenReturn(value)` called AFTER `@InjectMocks` field construction has no effect on the injected field because `@InjectMocks` constructs the SUT at field-injection time, before `@BeforeEach` stubs run — WHY: JUnit's `MockitoExtension` processes `@InjectMocks` fields during test class instantiation (before `@BeforeEach`). If the constructor or `@PostConstruct` of the SUT calls a mock method to initialise internal state (e.g., loads config from a repository), the stub for that call has not been configured yet — the mock returns `null`/`0`/`false` and the SUT stores a stale default. Later `when(...).thenReturn(...)` calls in `@BeforeEach` configure the mock but cannot retroactively change the already-stored state. Fix: move critical stubs that affect construction-time behaviour into a `@BeforeEach`-called `initMocks()` that creates the SUT manually with `new SUT(mockRepo, mockLogger)` after stubs are set, giving full control over the initialisation sequence.**

**G13: AssertJ `isEqualTo` on `Optional<T>` compares the `Optional` wrapper by value equality, but `Optional` does not implement `Comparable`, so `isGreaterThan` / `isLessThan` throw `ClassCastException` at runtime with a confusing message — WHY: AssertJ's `AbstractComparableAssert` methods require the subject to implement `Comparable`. `Optional<T>` does not, so when a developer writes `assertThat(result).isGreaterThan(Optional.empty())` expecting to compare the wrapped value, the assertion framework attempts a `Comparable.compareTo` cast and throws at runtime rather than at compile time, because `assertThat(Optional<T>)` returns a generic `ObjectAssert`. Fix: unwrap the Optional before asserting: `assertThat(result).isPresent(); assertThat(result.get()).isGreaterThan(threshold)`, or use `hasValueSatisfying(v -> assertThat(v).isGreaterThan(threshold))` which scopes the inner assertion to the present value and fails with a meaningful message if the Optional is empty.**

**G14: JUnit 5 `@TempDir` paths are deleted AFTER each test method by default, but if the test spawns a background thread or virtual thread that still holds an open `FileChannel` to the temp directory, the cleanup fails silently on Windows (the OS locks the file) and succeeds on Linux — causing CI failures only on Windows runners — WHY: JUnit's `@TempDir` cleanup uses `Files.walk` + `Files.delete`. On Linux, open file handles do not prevent deletion. On Windows, the OS file-locking model prevents deletion of open files, so `Files.delete` throws `AccessDeniedException`. JUnit catches this and emits a warning but does not fail the test, meaning the temp directory leaks. The leaked path from a previous test's cycle can then be picked up by the next test, causing cross-test contamination on Windows CI. Fix: explicitly close all `FileChannel` / `InputStream` / `OutputStream` instances before the test method returns, or use `@TempDir(cleanup = CleanupMode.ON_SUCCESS)` so leaking only happens on test failure, keeping CI aware of the open-handle bug.**

**G15: `Testcontainers` `@Container` on an instance (non-static) field with `@SpringBootTest` causes Spring to start a new `ApplicationContext` for every test method because `@DynamicPropertySource` registers the container's JDBC URL into the environment, and a new container means a new URL, which changes the context cache key — WHY: Spring's test context cache uses `MergedContextConfiguration` as the cache key. Dynamic properties injected via `@DynamicPropertySource` are part of that key. If each test method creates a new container (due to non-static field lifecycle), the dynamic URL changes per method, producing a unique `MergedContextConfiguration` per test and bypassing the cache entirely. With ten test methods, ten contexts are started, making the suite orders of magnitude slower. Fix: declare the `@Container` field `static` and annotate the `@DynamicPropertySource` method `static` — the container is then started once per class, the URL is stable across methods, and the context is reused from the cache.**
