**Pattern 342** — Mockito `@Captor` with `ArgumentCaptor<List<String>>` and AssertJ for bulk argument inspection
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;
import org.mockito.ArgumentCaptor;
import org.mockito.Captor;
import org.mockito.Mock;
import org.mockito.junit.jupiter.MockitoExtension;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.*;

@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class BatchEmailServiceTest {

    @Mock EmailClient emailClient;
    @Captor ArgumentCaptor<List<String>> recipientCaptor;

    @Test
    void sendsEmailToAllActiveUsers() {
        var service = new BatchEmailService(emailClient, userRepository);
        service.notifyActiveUsers("System maintenance at midnight");

        verify(emailClient).sendBulk(recipientCaptor.capture(), anyString());

        List<String> captured = new ArrayList<>(recipientCaptor.getValue());
        assertThat(captured)
            .hasSize(3)
            .containsExactlyInAnyOrder("alice@example.com", "bob@example.com", "carol@example.com")
            .doesNotContain("inactive@example.com");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@Captor` on a `List<String>` field avoids the raw-type warning of `ArgumentCaptor.forClass(List.class)` because Mockito's annotation processor infers the generic type; however the captured `List` is the exact same instance passed to the mock, so if the SUT mutates the list after the call (e.g., `list.clear()`), `captor.getValue()` returns the mutated (empty) list. Always copy the captured value with `new ArrayList<>(captor.getValue())` before asserting if the SUT may modify the list post-call. [community]

**Pattern 343** — AssertJ `usingRecursiveComparison().withEqualsForType()` for type-specific comparison overrides in deep object graph assertions
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.time.Instant;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

class OrderMapperTest {

    @Test
    void mapsEntityToDtoWithPrecisionAndTimeTolerance() {
        OrderEntity entity = OrderEntity.builder()
            .id(1L).total(new BigDecimal("99.990")).createdAt(Instant.now()).build();

        OrderDto dto = mapper.toDto(entity);

        assertThat(dto)
            .usingRecursiveComparison()
            .withEqualsForType(
                (a, b) -> a.compareTo(b) == 0,
                BigDecimal.class)
            .withEqualsForType(
                (a, b) -> Math.abs(a.toEpochMilli() - b.toEpochMilli()) < 1000,
                Instant.class)
            .ignoringFields("auditMetadata")
            .isEqualTo(expectedDto());
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `withEqualsForType()` injects a custom `BiPredicate` into the recursive comparator for a specific type, so `BigDecimal("99.990")` equals `BigDecimal("99.99")` via `compareTo` without affecting any other type's equality; the risk is that registering a comparator that is too permissive (e.g., ignoring scale entirely for financial values) can mask precision regressions that should fail the test — scope each custom comparator as narrowly as possible and document why the default `equals` is insufficient for that type. [official]

**Pattern 344** — JUnit 5 `@RegisterExtension` with a custom `ParameterResolver` for injecting domain test fixtures
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.*;
import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.time.LocalDate;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

class TestFixtureExtension implements ParameterResolver {
    @Override
    public boolean supportsParameter(ParameterContext p, ExtensionContext e) {
        return p.getParameter().getType() == TestFixtures.class;
    }
    @Override
    public Object resolveParameter(ParameterContext p, ExtensionContext e) {
        return new TestFixtures(/* load from classpath JSON */);
    }
}

class ProductPricingTest {

    @RegisterExtension
    static final TestFixtureExtension fixtures = new TestFixtureExtension();

    @Test
    void appliesSeasonalDiscount(TestFixtures f) {
        var product = f.product("seasonal-item");
        var pricer  = new SeasonalPricer(LocalDate.of(2026, 12, 24));
        assertThat(pricer.price(product))
            .isLessThan(product.basePrice())
            .isGreaterThan(BigDecimal.ZERO);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@RegisterExtension` on a `static final` field means the extension is shared across all test instances in the class (the default `PER_METHOD` lifecycle), which is correct for stateless fixture loaders; if the extension maintains mutable state (e.g., a counter or accumulator), declare it as an instance field without `static` to get a fresh instance per test method, at the cost of per-method initialisation overhead. [official]

**Pattern 345** — Testcontainers `DockerComposeContainer` with `withExposedService()` for spinning up multi-service compose stacks in integration tests
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.testcontainers.containers.DockerComposeContainer;
import org.testcontainers.containers.wait.strategy.Wait;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Container;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Testcontainers;
import java.io.File;
import java.net.URI;
import java.net.http.*;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@Testcontainers
class FullStackIT {

    @Container
    static final DockerComposeContainer<?> COMPOSE =
        new DockerComposeContainer<>(new File("src/test/resources/docker-compose-it.yml"))
            .withExposedService("postgres_1", 5432,
                Wait.forListeningPort())
            .withExposedService("redis_1", 6379,
                Wait.forListeningPort())
            .withExposedService("app_1", 8080,
                Wait.forHttp("/actuator/health").forStatusCode(200));

    @Test
    void fullStackHealthEndpointIsReachable() throws Exception {
        String host = COMPOSE.getServiceHost("app_1", 8080);
        int    port = COMPOSE.getServicePort("app_1", 8080);

        var response = HttpClient.newHttpClient().send(
            HttpRequest.newBuilder(URI.create(
                "http://" + host + ":" + port + "/actuator/health"))
                .build(),
            HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString());

        assertThat(response.statusCode()).isEqualTo(200);
        assertThat(response.body()).contains("\"status\":\"UP\"");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `DockerComposeContainer` reuses an existing `docker-compose` binary on the host and preserves full compose semantics (networks, volumes, depends_on), making it the most faithful replica of production topology; however it does not reliably support Docker Compose V2 plugin syntax (`docker compose` without hyphen) on all platforms — if the CI host has only the V2 plugin, Testcontainers falls back to a compatibility mode that silently omits healthcheck-based wait strategies, causing flaky startup races. Verify `docker-compose --version` is available in CI and pin a compose binary version in the runner image. [community]

### Community Gotchas

**G26** — JUnit 5 `@BeforeAll` in a `@Nested` class requires `@TestInstance(Lifecycle.PER_CLASS)` or it throws at discovery time
Why this matters: `@Nested` test classes are always non-static inner classes by design, so they have an associated outer instance. JUnit 5 requires `@BeforeAll` and `@AfterAll` methods to be `static` in the default `PER_METHOD` lifecycle. When developers add `@BeforeAll` to a `@Nested` class without `@TestInstance(Lifecycle.PER_CLASS)`, JUnit throws `JUnitException: @BeforeAll method 'setUp' must be static unless the test class is annotated with @TestInstance(Lifecycle.PER_CLASS)` — because this error fires during test discovery, not execution, IDEs often surface it as a generic "test suite failure" rather than pointing to the offending annotation.
Fix: Annotate the `@Nested` class with `@TestInstance(TestInstance.Lifecycle.PER_CLASS)` to allow instance-level `@BeforeAll`, or move the shared setup into the outer class's `@BeforeAll` if the state is truly class-scoped. When using `PER_CLASS` on a nested class, remember that test instance fields are shared across methods and must be reset in `@BeforeEach`. [official]

**G27** — Mockito `when(mock.voidMethod()).thenReturn(null)` compiles silently but throws `MissingMethodInvocationException` at runtime
Why this matters: `when()` expects a non-void method call in its argument expression. When a developer writes `when(mock.voidMethod()).thenReturn(null)` instead of `doNothing().when(mock).voidMethod()`, the compiler does not flag it because `when()` accepts `T` and a `void` call is a valid Java expression. At runtime, Mockito detects the mismatch during framework state validation and throws `MissingMethodInvocationException: when() requires an argument which has to be a method call on a mock` — this message does not mention "void" and leaves developers searching for a missing mock that is actually present.
Fix: Use the `doNothing().when(mock).voidMethod()` form for all void stubs, and `doThrow()` / `doAnswer()` for void methods that must throw or invoke callbacks. Enable `MockitoHints` or read the full exception message — the third bullet of the Mockito error text typically lists "stubbing a void method" as a cause. A team lint rule that flags `when(...)` calls where the inner expression's return type is `void` catches this at review time. [official]

**G28** — AssertJ `containsExactly()` on a `Set` asserts insertion order, which is non-deterministic for `HashSet`
Why this matters: `containsExactly()` asserts that the iterable contains exactly the given elements in exactly that order with no others. When the collection under test is a `HashSet`, iteration order depends on the JVM hash seed, which changes between JVM invocations and across JDK versions. A test that passes locally with `containsExactly("A", "B", "C")` may fail in CI with elements in a different order, producing an intermittent failure that is extremely hard to reproduce and often dismissed as flakiness.
Fix: Use `containsExactlyInAnyOrder()` for any `Set`, `Queue`, or other unordered collection. Reserve `containsExactly()` strictly for `List`, arrays, or other ordered sequence types. If ordering genuinely matters for a set-backed result, assert on the sorted view: `assertThat(result.stream().sorted().collect(Collectors.toList())).containsExactly(...)`. [community]

**G29** — Testcontainers `@Container` on an instance field re-creates the container for every test method, multiplying startup cost across the suite
Why this matters: When `@Container` annotates an instance field (not `static`), the Testcontainers JUnit 5 extension treats it as a per-test-method resource and starts and stops the container before and after every `@Test` method. In a class with 20 tests, a PostgreSQL container that takes 3 seconds to start adds 60 seconds to the suite. Developers who copy-paste container declarations from single-test examples into multi-test classes silently pay this penalty without any warning from the framework.
Fix: Declare shared containers as `static final` fields annotated with `@Container`. The Testcontainers extension starts a `static @Container` once per test class and stops it after the last test in the class runs. For true per-test isolation, prefer database transaction rollback (`@Transactional` on the test class with `ROLLBACK` semantics) rather than restarting the container. [official]

**G30** — JUnit 5 `assertThrows()` swallows AssertJ `AssertionError` failures thrown from inside the lambda, hiding the root-cause message
Why this matters: `assertThrows(MyException.class, () -> sut.call())` returns the thrown exception if and only if the lambda throws exactly `MyException` or a subtype. If the lambda contains an AssertJ assertion that fails (e.g., a developer adds a state-check assertion inside an `assertThrows` block), JUnit catches the `AssertionError` thrown by AssertJ — because `AssertionError` is not `MyException` — and reports `assertThrows` as failed due to an unexpected exception type, completely obscuring the original assertion failure message and making the root cause invisible.
Fix: Never put assertions inside an `assertThrows` lambda; extract pre-exception setup assertions to before the `assertThrows` call. For asserting both the exception and post-exception state, use `assertThatThrownBy()` (which supports fluent chaining on the thrown exception) followed by separate assertions outside the lambda for any state checks. If you need to capture state changes that happen before the throw, use a local `AtomicReference` populated inside the lambda and assert on it after `assertThrows` returns. [community]

## Cycle 62 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 346** — JUnit 5 `@TestFactory` dynamic test generation from external data source
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.DynamicTest;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.TestFactory;

import java.util.stream.Stream;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.data.Offset.offset;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.DynamicTest.dynamicTest;

class PricingEngineTest {

    private final PricingEngine engine = new PricingEngine();

    record Scenario(String name, double basePrice, int qty, double expectedTotal) {}

    @TestFactory
    Stream<DynamicTest> pricingScenarios() {
        return Stream.of(
            new Scenario("bulk discount",       100.0, 10,  950.0),
            new Scenario("no discount",         100.0,  1,  100.0),
            new Scenario("max tier discount",   100.0, 50, 4000.0),
            new Scenario("zero quantity",       100.0,  0,    0.0)
        ).map(s -> dynamicTest(s.name(), () -> {
            double result = engine.calculate(s.basePrice(), s.qty());
            assertThat(result)
                .as("total for scenario '%s'", s.name())
                .isEqualTo(s.expectedTotal(), offset(0.01));
        }));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@TestFactory` generates `DynamicTest` nodes that are discovered lazily at runtime, which means IDE test runners display each dynamic test by its display-name string rather than a stable method name — test history and re-run-last-failed features in IntelliJ and Maven Surefire cannot address individual dynamic tests by a stable identifier, so a single failing scenario forces a full re-run of all generated tests in some CI setups. [official]

**Pattern 347** — Mockito `MockedStatic` for scoped stubbing of `static` utility methods
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.mockito.MockedStatic;
import org.mockito.Mockito;

import java.time.Clock;
import java.time.Instant;
import java.time.ZoneOffset;
import java.util.UUID;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

class OrderIdGeneratorTest {

    @Test
    void generatesOrderIdWithCurrentTimestampAndUUID() {
        Instant fixedInstant = Instant.parse("2024-06-01T12:00:00Z");
        UUID fixedUuid = UUID.fromString("00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001");

        try (MockedStatic<UUID> uuidMock = Mockito.mockStatic(UUID.class)) {
            uuidMock.when(UUID::randomUUID).thenReturn(fixedUuid);

            OrderIdGenerator gen = new OrderIdGenerator(
                Clock.fixed(fixedInstant, ZoneOffset.UTC));
            String id = gen.next();

            assertThat(id).isEqualTo("2024060100000000000000000000000000001");
        }
        // static mock is fully removed after try-with-resources
        assertThat(UUID.randomUUID()).isNotEqualTo(fixedUuid);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `MockedStatic` installs a `ThreadLocal`-scoped interception table via the Mockito inline byte-buddy agent; if the try-with-resources block is not closed (e.g., due to an exception escaping before `close()`), the static mock leaks into subsequent tests on the same thread, causing inexplicable failures that vanish when test order changes — always use try-with-resources, never assign `MockedStatic` to a field without a corresponding `@AfterEach` close. [official]

**Pattern 348** — AssertJ `satisfiesExactlyInAnyOrder` for unordered element-level predicate matching
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import java.util.List;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

class NotificationDispatcherTest {

    @Test
    void dispatchedNotificationsHaveCorrectTypesAndRecipients() {
        NotificationDispatcher dispatcher = new NotificationDispatcher();
        List<Notification> sent = dispatcher.dispatch(
            new OrderEvent("ORD-1", "alice@example.com", OrderStatus.SHIPPED));

        assertThat(sent)
            .hasSize(2)
            .satisfiesExactlyInAnyOrder(
                n -> {
                    assertThat(n.type()).isEqualTo(NotificationType.EMAIL);
                    assertThat(n.recipient()).isEqualTo("alice@example.com");
                },
                n -> {
                    assertThat(n.type()).isEqualTo(NotificationType.PUSH);
                    assertThat(n.recipient()).isEqualTo("alice@example.com");
                }
            );
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `satisfiesExactlyInAnyOrder` evaluates every consumer against every element permutation until all consumers are satisfied, making its time complexity O(n!) in the number of consumers; for collections beyond 6–8 elements, use `allSatisfy()` + `anySatisfy()` combinations or extract and sort before asserting, because the factorial explosion will noticeably slow test execution at 10+ unordered elements. [official]

**Pattern 349** — Awaitility `await().untilAsserted()` for testing asynchronous domain events
```java
import org.awaitility.Awaitility;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;

import java.time.Duration;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@SpringBootTest
class OrderProcessingIntegrationTest {

    @Autowired
    private OrderService orderService;

    @Autowired
    private ShipmentRepository shipmentRepository;

    @Test
    void shipmentIsCreatedAsynchronouslyAfterOrderPlaced() {
        String orderId = orderService.place(new PlaceOrderCommand("SKU-42", 2));

        Awaitility.await("shipment creation")
            .atMost(Duration.ofSeconds(5))
            .pollInterval(Duration.ofMillis(200))
            .untilAsserted(() ->
                assertThat(shipmentRepository.findByOrderId(orderId))
                    .isPresent()
                    .hasValueSatisfying(s ->
                        assertThat(s.status()).isEqualTo(ShipmentStatus.PENDING))
            );
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `untilAsserted()` re-throws the last `AssertionError` as the timeout cause, preserving the full AssertJ failure message in CI logs; however the `pollInterval` interacts with `atMost` by checking the condition only at poll boundaries, so a very long `pollInterval` relative to a short `atMost` may miss a transient state window that was present and gone between polls — set `pollInterval` to at most 10% of `atMost` for fine-grained async verification. [official]

**Pattern 350** — ArchUnit `@AnalyzeClasses` layered-architecture rule enforcement
```java
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption;
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.AnalyzeClasses;
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest;
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchRule;

import static com.tngtech.archunit.library.Architectures.layeredArchitecture;

@AnalyzeClasses(
    packages = "com.example.shop",
    importOptions = ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests.class)
class LayerArchitectureTest {

    @ArchTest
    static final ArchRule layersAreRespected =
        layeredArchitecture()
            .consideringAllDependencies()
            .layer("API")         .definedBy("com.example.shop.api..")
            .layer("Application") .definedBy("com.example.shop.application..")
            .layer("Domain")      .definedBy("com.example.shop.domain..")
            .layer("Infra")       .definedBy("com.example.shop.infrastructure..")
            .whereLayer("API")         .mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()
            .whereLayer("Application") .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("API")
            .whereLayer("Domain")      .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("API", "Application")
            .whereLayer("Infra")       .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Application");
}
```
Tradeoff: ArchUnit's `layeredArchitecture()` performs bytecode-level class import at test startup, which means it scans and parses every `.class` file in the target packages — on a module with 2,000+ classes this import can add 3–8 seconds to the test JVM warmup; use `@AnalyzeClasses(importOptions = ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests.class)` to exclude test classes and consider splitting architecture tests into a dedicated Maven/Gradle module so they run in parallel rather than gating the unit test phase. [official]

**Pattern 351** — WireMock `@WireMockTest` with request-body JSON path matching
```java
import com.github.tomakehurst.wiremock.junit5.WireMockTest;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import java.net.URI;
import java.net.http.*;

import static com.github.tomakehurst.wiremock.client.WireMock.*;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@WireMockTest(httpPort = 8089)
class PaymentGatewayClientTest {

    @Test
    void chargesCorrectAmountAndCurrency() throws Exception {
        stubFor(post(urlEqualTo("/v1/charges"))
            .withRequestBody(matchingJsonPath("$.amount", equalTo("5000")))
            .withRequestBody(matchingJsonPath("$.currency", equalTo("USD")))
            .willReturn(okJson("{\"id\":\"ch_test_001\",\"status\":\"succeeded\"}")));

        PaymentGatewayClient client =
            new PaymentGatewayClient("http://localhost:8089");
        ChargeResponse response = client.charge(new ChargeRequest(5000, "USD"));

        assertThat(response.status()).isEqualTo("succeeded");
        verify(postRequestedFor(urlEqualTo("/v1/charges"))
            .withRequestBody(matchingJsonPath("$.amount")));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@WireMockTest` starts a per-test WireMock server on a fixed port, meaning parallel test execution with `@Execution(CONCURRENT)` causes port-binding conflicts unless you use `httpPort = 0` (random port) and inject the dynamic port via `WireMockRuntimeInfo`; fixed ports are safe only in strictly sequential test suites and mask parallelism bugs in the code under test. [official]

**Pattern 352** — Spring Boot `@WebMvcTest` with `MockMvc` and `SecurityMockMvcConfigurer`
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.web.servlet.WebMvcTest;
import org.springframework.boot.test.mock.mockito.MockBean;
import org.springframework.security.test.web.servlet.request.SecurityMockMvcRequestPostProcessors;
import org.springframework.test.web.servlet.MockMvc;

import static org.mockito.BDDMockito.given;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.request.MockMvcRequestBuilders.get;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.*;

@WebMvcTest(ProductController.class)
class ProductControllerTest {

    @Autowired
    private MockMvc mvc;

    @MockBean
    private ProductService productService;

    @Test
    void returnsProductJsonForAuthenticatedUser() throws Exception {
        given(productService.findById("P-1"))
            .willReturn(new Product("P-1", "Widget", 9.99));

        mvc.perform(get("/api/products/P-1")
                .with(SecurityMockMvcRequestPostProcessors.user("alice").roles("USER")))
            .andExpect(status().isOk())
            .andExpect(jsonPath("$.name").value("Widget"))
            .andExpect(jsonPath("$.price").value(9.99));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@WebMvcTest` loads only the web layer slice (controllers, filters, `@ControllerAdvice`) and does not start a full `ApplicationContext`, cutting startup time from 8–15 seconds to under 2 seconds for most applications; however the security auto-configuration is partially included, so omitting `SecurityMockMvcRequestPostProcessors` on endpoints protected by Spring Security causes 401/403 responses that look like controller bugs rather than test-setup gaps. [official]

**Pattern 353** — JUnit 5 `@TempDir` with pre-populated fixture files for file-processing tests
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.List;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

class CsvImporterTest {

    @Test
    void importsAllRowsFromValidCsv(@TempDir Path tempDir) throws IOException {
        Path csv = tempDir.resolve("products.csv");
        Files.writeString(csv,
            "id,name,price\n" +
            "1,Widget,9.99\n" +
            "2,Gadget,24.99\n");

        CsvImporter importer = new CsvImporter();
        List<Product> products = importer.importFrom(csv);

        assertThat(products)
            .hasSize(2)
            .extracting(Product::name)
            .containsExactly("Widget", "Gadget");
    }

    @Test
    void returnsEmptyListForHeaderOnlyCsv(@TempDir Path tempDir) throws IOException {
        Path csv = tempDir.resolve("empty.csv");
        Files.writeString(csv, "id,name,price\n");

        assertThat(new CsvImporter().importFrom(csv)).isEmpty();
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@TempDir` creates an OS temp directory that JUnit 5 cleans up after each test method (or after the test class when the field is `static`), so there is no manual teardown overhead; however on Windows, cleanup silently fails if a `FileInputStream` or `BufferedReader` opened on a temp file is not closed before the test ends — the JUnit cleanup swallows the `IOException` and logs a warning without failing the test, leaving orphaned temp directories that accumulate in `%TEMP%` across CI runs. [official]

**Pattern 354** — Mockito `ArgumentMatcher` custom predicate for complex domain-object matching
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;
import org.mockito.Mock;
import org.mockito.junit.jupiter.MockitoExtension;

import static org.mockito.ArgumentMatchers.argThat;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.verify;

@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class AuditLogServiceTest {

    @Mock
    private AuditRepository repository;

    @Test
    void recordsAuditEntryWithCorrectPrincipalAndAction() {
        AuditLogService service = new AuditLogService(repository);
        service.record("alice", AuditAction.DELETE, "resource/42");

        verify(repository).save(argThat(entry ->
            entry.principal().equals("alice")
            && entry.action() == AuditAction.DELETE
            && entry.resourceId().equals("resource/42")
            && entry.occurredAt() != null
        ));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `argThat(lambda)` with a multi-predicate lambda provides precise verification without requiring an `equals()` override on the domain object, but when verification fails, Mockito prints `argThat(lambda)` as the matcher description with no indication of which predicate failed — use a named `ArgumentMatcher` class that overrides `toString()` returning a human-readable description, or break the single `argThat` into multiple `verify` calls with `@Captor` + individual AssertJ assertions for richer failure messages. [official]

**Pattern 355** — Testcontainers `GenericContainer` with `withCopyFileToContainer` for seeded test data
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.testcontainers.containers.GenericContainer;
import org.testcontainers.containers.wait.strategy.Wait;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Container;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Testcontainers;
import org.testcontainers.utility.MountableFile;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@Testcontainers
class RedisSessionStoreIT {

    @Container
    static final GenericContainer<?> REDIS =
        new GenericContainer<>("redis:7.2-alpine")
            .withExposedPorts(6379)
            .withCopyFileToContainer(
                MountableFile.forClasspathResource("redis/seed.rdb"),
                "/data/dump.rdb")
            .withCommand("redis-server", "--appendonly", "no",
                         "--dbfilename", "dump.rdb")
            .waitingFor(Wait.forLogMessage(
                ".*Ready to accept connections.*", 1));

    @Test
    void findsPreSeededSessionInRedis() {
        RedisSessionStore store = new RedisSessionStore(
            REDIS.getHost(), REDIS.getMappedPort(6379));

        assertThat(store.get("seed-session-001"))
            .isPresent()
            .hasValueSatisfying(s ->
                assertThat(s.userId()).isEqualTo("user-42"));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `withCopyFileToContainer` copies files from the classpath into the container filesystem before the entry-point runs, ensuring seed data is present without a separate init-container or volume mount; however when the source path is a classpath resource inside a JAR (e.g., in a fat-jar CI build), Testcontainers must extract it to a temp file before transfer — this extraction path is not logged, and if the classpath resource is missing the error message is `MountableFile: resource not found` with no indication of which JAR was searched, making classpath packaging mistakes hard to diagnose. [official]

**Pattern 356** — AssertJ `usingRecursiveComparison().ignoringFields()` for partial DTO assertion
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

class CustomerMapperTest {

    @Test
    void mapsCommandToDtoIgnoringServerGeneratedFields() {
        CreateCustomerCommand cmd = new CreateCustomerCommand(
            "Bob", "bob@example.com", "555-0100");

        CustomerDto actual = new CustomerMapper().toDto(cmd);

        CustomerDto expected = CustomerDto.builder()
            .name("Bob")
            .email("bob@example.com")
            .phone("555-0100")
            .build();

        assertThat(actual)
            .usingRecursiveComparison()
            .ignoringFields("id", "createdAt", "version")
            .isEqualTo(expected);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `ignoringFields()` accepts field-name strings that are matched by exact name recursively across the object graph, so renaming a field in the production code silently causes the `ignoringFields` exclusion to stop applying — the test starts asserting on the previously-ignored field without any compile-time or startup-time warning, potentially re-introducing false positives hidden behind the renaming. [official]

**Pattern 357** — JUnit 5 `@ParameterizedTest` with `@CsvFileSource` for data-driven edge-case tables
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.params.ParameterizedTest;
import org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.CsvFileSource;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.within;

class TaxCalculatorTest {

    private final TaxCalculator calc = new TaxCalculator();

    @ParameterizedTest(name = "income={0}, state={1}, expectedTax={2}")
    @CsvFileSource(
        resources = "/tax-scenarios.csv",
        numLinesToSkip = 1,
        delimiter = ',',
        nullValues = "NULL")
    void calculatesStateTaxCorrectly(
            double income, String state, double expectedTax) {
        assertThat(calc.computeStateTax(income, state))
            .as("state tax for income=%.2f, state=%s", income, state)
            .isEqualTo(expectedTax, within(0.005));
    }
}
// tax-scenarios.csv (in src/test/resources):
// income,state,expectedTax
// 50000,CA,2315.00
// 50000,TX,0.00
// 100000,NY,5853.00
// 0,CA,0.00
```
Tradeoff: `@CsvFileSource` externalises test data into a CSV file that can be edited by non-developers and diffed independently of Java source, lowering the friction for adding new edge cases; however the CSV is parsed once during test discovery and any type-conversion failure (e.g., a non-numeric value in a `double` column) throws a `ParameterResolutionException` that aborts the entire parameterized test class rather than failing just the offending row, making the root cause harder to locate in large files. [official]

**Pattern 358** — Spring Boot `@DataJpaTest` with `TestEntityManager` for repository slice testing
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.orm.jpa.DataJpaTest;
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.orm.jpa.TestEntityManager;

import java.util.Optional;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@DataJpaTest
class ProductRepositoryTest {

    @Autowired
    private TestEntityManager em;

    @Autowired
    private ProductRepository repository;

    @Test
    void findsBySku_whenProductExists() {
        em.persistAndFlush(new Product(null, "SKU-99", "Sprocket", 3.50));

        Optional<Product> found = repository.findBySku("SKU-99");

        assertThat(found)
            .isPresent()
            .hasValueSatisfying(p -> {
                assertThat(p.name()).isEqualTo("Sprocket");
                assertThat(p.price()).isEqualByComparingTo("3.50");
            });
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@DataJpaTest` rolls back each test method's transaction automatically (via `@Transactional` applied at class level), so entities persisted with `TestEntityManager` are never committed to the in-memory H2 or Testcontainers database — this means native SQL assertions via `JdbcTemplate` run within the same transaction will see the uncommitted rows, but out-of-transaction reads (e.g., a second connection from a `DataSource`) will not, causing confusion when testing second-level caching or optimistic-lock conflict scenarios. [official]

**Pattern 359** — Mockito `BDDMockito.given/then` style with `willAnswer` for stateful stub sequences
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;
import org.mockito.InjectMocks;
import org.mockito.Mock;
import org.mockito.junit.jupiter.MockitoExtension;

import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.mockito.BDDMockito.*;

@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class RetryPolicyServiceTest {

    @Mock  private ExternalApi api;
    @InjectMocks private RetryPolicyService service;

    @Test
    void retriesOnTransientFailureThenSucceeds() {
        AtomicInteger calls = new AtomicInteger(0);

        given(api.fetchData("key-1")).willAnswer(inv -> {
            if (calls.incrementAndGet() < 3) {
                throw new TransientApiException("service unavailable");
            }
            return new DataPayload("result");
        });

        DataPayload result = service.fetchWithRetry("key-1");

        assertThat(result.value()).isEqualTo("result");
        then(api).should(times(3)).fetchData("key-1");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `willAnswer` with an `AtomicInteger` counter creates a stateful stub that mirrors real transient-failure behaviour without spawning threads, but the stub state is attached to the mock instance rather than the test method — if Mockito reuses the same mock instance across test methods (e.g., with `@TestInstance(PER_CLASS)` and no `MockitoAnnotations.openMocks(this)` reset), the counter carries over from a previous test and the third-call success threshold triggers on the wrong invocation count, causing timing-sensitive failures that disappear when tests run in isolation. [official]

**Pattern 360** — ArchUnit `noClasses().that()` naming-convention and dependency enforcement
```java
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.AnalyzeClasses;
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest;
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchRule;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption;

import static com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses;
import static com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.classes;

@AnalyzeClasses(packages = "com.example.shop",
    importOptions = ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests.class)
class NamingConventionTest {

    @ArchTest
    static final ArchRule serviceClassesShouldNotDependOnControllers =
        noClasses().that().resideInAPackage("..service..")
            .should().dependOnClassesThat()
            .resideInAPackage("..api.controller..");

    @ArchTest
    static final ArchRule repositoryInterfacesMustEndWithRepository =
        classes().that().resideInAPackage("..infrastructure.persistence..")
            .and().areInterfaces()
            .should().haveSimpleNameEndingWith("Repository");

    @ArchTest
    static final ArchRule noRawJdbcInApplicationLayer =
        noClasses().that().resideInAPackage("..application..")
            .should().accessClassesThat()
            .areAssignableTo(java.sql.Connection.class);
}
```
Tradeoff: Combining multiple `@ArchTest` fields in one class shares a single class-import scan (controlled by `@AnalyzeClasses`), amortising the expensive bytecode-import cost across all rules; however ArchUnit evaluates all `@ArchTest` fields eagerly and independently — a violation in one rule does not abort others, so multiple architectural violations surface in one test run, which is desirable for comprehensive reporting but can produce verbose CI output when a large refactor temporarily breaks many rules simultaneously. [official]

### Community Gotchas

**G31** — Mockito `@InjectMocks` silently skips injection when no matching constructor or setter exists, leaving fields `null`
Why this matters: Mockito's `@InjectMocks` attempts constructor injection first, then setter injection, then field injection — in that priority order. If the class under test has a constructor with parameters that do not match any available `@Mock` or `@Spy` by type (e.g., a `String` configuration parameter alongside a mocked collaborator), Mockito silently falls back to the next strategy. If setter injection also fails, field injection is attempted via reflection. When all three strategies fail partially, Mockito does not throw — it quietly leaves unmatched fields at their default values (`null` for objects). Tests then fail with `NullPointerException` deep inside the SUT with no indication that the mock was never injected, and since the NPE stack trace points at production code, developers spend time investigating the wrong layer.
Fix: Prefer explicit constructor injection in tests — create the SUT with `new ServiceUnderTest(mockA, mockB)` instead of relying on `@InjectMocks`, which makes injection failures compile-time visible. If `@InjectMocks` is used, add an `assertThat(sut).isNotNull()` and verify key field values in `@BeforeEach`. Enable `MockitoSession` strict stubbing (`@MockitoSettings(strictness = Strictness.STRICT_STUBS)`) which surfaces unused stubs but does not directly detect injection misses — combine with a constructor-based SUT for the strongest guarantee. [official]

**G32** — Spring Boot `@MockBean` causes full `ApplicationContext` reload on every test class, destroying context caching
Why this matters: Spring Boot's test context caching mechanism caches the `ApplicationContext` by its configuration key, which includes the set of `@MockBean` and `@SpyBean` definitions in the test class. Every unique combination of `@MockBean` types forces a new context to be created. In a large test suite where 30 test classes each declare a slightly different set of `@MockBean` fields, Spring creates 30 separate application contexts instead of reusing one — in a Spring Boot application with a 6-second startup time, this adds 3 minutes to the total test suite runtime. This is one of the most common causes of inexplicably slow Spring Boot integration test suites and is invisible in per-class timing reports because each individual context creation appears as normal startup latency.
Fix: Consolidate `@MockBean` declarations into a shared base test class or a `@TestConfiguration` class that is consistent across all test classes; Spring will reuse the same context for all subclasses with the same effective configuration. Alternatively, use Mockito's `@Mock` with `@Autowired` `@SpyBean` narrowly — avoid `@MockBean` for pure unit concerns handled by `@WebMvcTest` slices. Measure context cache hit ratio by enabling `spring.test.context.cache.maxSize` logging to confirm sharing is occurring. [official]

**G33** — Awaitility `await().until(callable)` with a `Callable<Boolean>` swallows `AssertionError` and retries instead of failing fast
Why this matters: `await().until(callable)` polls the `Callable<Boolean>` and considers the condition satisfied only when it returns `true`. If an `AssertionError` is thrown inside the callable (e.g., from an AssertJ assertion), Awaitility's default exception handling catches it and treats it as a transient condition failure — retrying until the timeout expires rather than propagating the error immediately. This means a test with a logical assertion error (wrong field value, wrong type) waits the full `atMost` duration before reporting failure, turning an instant failure into a 10-second timeout. Developers mistake this for a timing problem and increase the timeout, compounding the issue.
Fix: Use `untilAsserted(ThrowingRunnable)` instead of `until(Callable<Boolean>)` for any condition that contains assertions — `untilAsserted` is specifically designed to propagate `AssertionError` on timeout with the last failure message. For `until(callable)`, never embed assertions; use pure boolean conditions: `until(() -> repository.findById(id).isPresent())`. If both assertion content and retry semantics are needed, use `untilAsserted` with a full AssertJ assertion block. [official]

**G34** — JUnit 5 `@ExtendWith` on a base class is not inherited by `@Nested` inner classes in the expected order
Why this matters: JUnit 5's extension model merges extensions from outer and inner classes during test discovery, meaning a `@Nested` class inherits `@ExtendWith` annotations declared on its enclosing class. However, extensions registered on a base class via inheritance (`class MyTest extends BaseTest`) are inherited by `@Nested` classes only if those `@Nested` classes are declared in `MyTest` itself. When a developer uses a mixin pattern — inheriting from multiple base classes or using `@ExtendWith` on both a base class and an interface — they encounter subtle extension lifecycle issues where `@BeforeEach` from the extension fires out of order relative to `@Nested` `@BeforeEach` methods, causing test fixture state to be set up before outer-class mocks are initialised.
Fix: Declare all `@ExtendWith` annotations on the top-level test class or register extensions programmatically with `@RegisterExtension` at the exact field scope where their lifecycle is needed. For shared infrastructure (e.g., Mockito + Spring), keep a single concrete base class with all extensions declared, and use `@Nested` only for logical grouping without adding extensions on the nested class itself. Review JUnit 5's documented extension composition order: extensions on outer classes execute their before-callbacks before extensions on inner classes, and after-callbacks in reverse. [official]

**G35** — AssertJ `isEqualTo()` on `BigDecimal` uses `equals()` semantics and fails on scale mismatch
Why this matters: `BigDecimal("2.0")` and `BigDecimal("2.00")` are unequal under `BigDecimal.equals()` because `equals` compares both value and scale, while `compareTo` considers them mathematically equivalent. AssertJ's `isEqualTo()` delegates to the object's `equals()` method by default, so `assertThat(new BigDecimal("2.0")).isEqualTo(new BigDecimal("2.00"))` fails with `expected: 2.00 but was: 2.0` — a counterintuitive failure when the test intent is purely numeric equivalence. This is especially common in repository tests where a mapped `BigDecimal` column loses trailing zeros in round-trip serialisation through JDBC or JSON deserialisation.
Fix: Use `assertThat(actual).isEqualByComparingTo(new BigDecimal("2.00"))` for numeric-only `BigDecimal` comparisons, which delegates to `compareTo()` and ignores scale differences. For object graphs containing `BigDecimal` fields, use `usingRecursiveComparison().withComparatorForType(Comparator.naturalOrder(), BigDecimal.class)` to apply `compareTo` semantics recursively. Document this policy in a shared `AbstractDomainAssert` base class so all custom assertions inherit the correct comparator automatically. [community]

### Patterns

**Pattern 361** — JUnit 5 `@RepeatedTest` with `RepetitionInfo` for flakiness detection
```java
@RepeatedTest(value = 10, name = "{displayName} — run {currentRepetition}/{totalRepetitions}")
void rateLimiterShouldNeverExceedThreshold(RepetitionInfo info) {
    RateLimiter limiter = RateLimiter.create(5.0); // 5 permits/sec
    Instant start = Instant.now();
    int acquired = 0;
    while (Duration.between(start, Instant.now()).toMillis() < 200) {
        if (limiter.tryAcquire()) acquired++;
    }
    assertThat(acquired)
        .as("repetition %d: permits acquired in 200 ms", info.getCurrentRepetition())
        .isLessThanOrEqualTo(2); // at most 1 permit per 200ms window
    if (info.getCurrentRepetition() == info.getTotalRepetitions()) {
        // last repetition: log aggregate pass count via system property for CI
        System.setProperty("rate.limiter.passed.reps",
            String.valueOf(info.getTotalRepetitions()));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@RepeatedTest` surfaces timing-dependent flakiness early in local runs, but each repetition counts as a separate test in CI reports, inflating pass/fail counts and making dashboards noisy; gate repeated tests behind a `@Tag("flakiness")` profile and exclude them from the default Surefire execution so they only run on a dedicated flakiness-detection job. [official]

**Pattern 362** — Mockito `ArgumentCaptor` with multi-invocation capture and ordered assertion
```java
@Test
void auditServiceShouldRecordThreeEventsDuringCheckout() {
    ArgumentCaptor<AuditEvent> captor = ArgumentCaptor.forClass(AuditEvent.class);

    checkoutFacade.checkout(buildCart());

    // capture all invocations in declaration order
    verify(auditService, times(3)).record(captor.capture());
    List<AuditEvent> events = captor.getAllValues();

    assertThat(events)
        .extracting(AuditEvent::type)
        .containsExactly(
            AuditEventType.CART_VALIDATED,
            AuditEventType.PAYMENT_CHARGED,
            AuditEventType.ORDER_CONFIRMED
        );
    assertThat(events.get(1).metadata())
        .containsEntry("amount", "49.99")
        .containsEntry("currency", "USD");
}
```
Tradeoff: `getAllValues()` returns a live-captured list in Mockito invocation order, which is deterministic only when the code under test calls the mock on a single thread; for concurrent code paths where audit events arrive from multiple threads, invocation order is non-deterministic and `containsExactlyInAnyOrder` must replace `containsExactly`, sacrificing ordering guarantees but preserving safety. [official]

**Pattern 363** — AssertJ `SoftAssertions` with `assertSoftly` lambda to avoid missing failures
```java
@Test
void userProfileResponseShouldContainAllRequiredFields() {
    UserProfileResponse response = profileService.getProfile(USER_ID);

    SoftAssertions.assertSoftly(softly -> {
        softly.assertThat(response.username())
              .as("username")
              .isNotBlank()
              .hasSizeLessThanOrEqualTo(50);
        softly.assertThat(response.email())
              .as("email")
              .matches("^[^@]+@[^@]+\\.[^@]+$");
        softly.assertThat(response.roles())
              .as("roles")
              .isNotEmpty()
              .doesNotContainNull();
        softly.assertThat(response.createdAt())
              .as("createdAt")
              .isBeforeOrEqualTo(Instant.now())
              .isAfter(Instant.EPOCH);
        softly.assertThat(response.avatarUrl())
              .as("avatarUrl")
              .startsWith("https://");
    });
}
```
Tradeoff: `assertSoftly` collects all failures and reports them together, eliminating the "fix one failure, discover the next" cycle in large DTO validation tests; the trade-off is that later assertions in the lambda execute even when earlier ones have failed, so if a later assertion depends on the first having passed (e.g., accessing a field of a potentially null object), it will throw a `NullPointerException` that obscures the original assertion failure — guard dependent assertions with explicit null checks before entering the soft scope. [official]

**Pattern 364** — Testcontainers `Network` for multi-container integration with service aliases
```java
@Testcontainers
class PaymentGatewayIntegrationTest {

    static Network network = Network.newNetwork();

    @Container
    static GenericContainer<?> redis = new GenericContainer<>("redis:7-alpine")
        .withNetwork(network)
        .withNetworkAliases("cache");

    @Container
    static PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres = new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine")
        .withNetwork(network)
        .withNetworkAliases("db");

    @Container
    static GenericContainer<?> gateway = new GenericContainer<>("payment-gateway:latest")
        .withNetwork(network)
        .withEnv("REDIS_URL", "redis://cache:6379")
        .withEnv("DB_URL", "jdbc:postgresql://db:5432/payments")
        .withExposedPorts(8080)
        .waitingFor(Wait.forHttp("/actuator/health").forPort(8080));

    @Test
    void chargeShouldPersistAndCacheResult() {
        String baseUrl = "http://localhost:" + gateway.getMappedPort(8080);
        // ... RestAssured or WebClient call
        assertThat(chargeRepository.findById(CHARGE_ID)).isPresent();
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: Shared `Network` with DNS aliases precisely mirrors production container networking and eliminates hardcoded host-port wiring between containers, but `Network.newNetwork()` is not automatically closed by the `@Container` lifecycle — declare it as a static field annotated with `@Container` on a `Closeable` wrapper, or call `network.close()` in an `@AfterAll`, otherwise Docker networks accumulate silently during CI and eventually exhaust the `br-*` bridge namespace limit on the host. [official]

**Pattern 365** — WireMock `@WireMockTest` stateful scenario for multi-step workflow stubbing
```java
@WireMockTest
class OrderFulfillmentScenarioTest {

    @Test
    void orderShouldTransitionThroughPendingToShipped(WireMockRuntimeInfo wm) {
        // Step 1: first call returns PENDING
        stubFor(get(urlEqualTo("/orders/42"))
            .inScenario("order-lifecycle")
            .whenScenarioStateIs(STARTED)
            .willReturn(okJson("{\"status\":\"PENDING\"}"))
            .willSetStateTo("ALLOCATED"));

        // Step 2: second call returns ALLOCATED
        stubFor(get(urlEqualTo("/orders/42"))
            .inScenario("order-lifecycle")
            .whenScenarioStateIs("ALLOCATED")
            .willReturn(okJson("{\"status\":\"ALLOCATED\"}"))
            .willSetStateTo("SHIPPED"));

        // Step 3: third call returns SHIPPED
        stubFor(get(urlEqualTo("/orders/42"))
            .inScenario("order-lifecycle")
            .whenScenarioStateIs("SHIPPED")
            .willReturn(okJson("{\"status\":\"SHIPPED\"}")));

        OrderPoller poller = new OrderPoller(wm.getHttpBaseUrl());
        assertThat(poller.pollUntilShipped("42", Duration.ofSeconds(5)))
            .isEqualTo(OrderStatus.SHIPPED);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: WireMock scenarios produce deterministic state-machine stubs without needing a running external service, making them ideal for testing polling or retry logic; however scenario state is global within the WireMock server instance — if two tests in the same class share the same scenario name but different intended starting states, they will interfere with each other, so always use unique scenario names per test method or call `resetAllScenarios()` in `@BeforeEach`. [official]

**Pattern 366** — ArchUnit `FreezingArchRule` to track and manage existing violations incrementally
```java
@AnalyzeClasses(packages = "com.example", importOptions = ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests.class)
class ArchitectureFreezingTest {

    @ArchTest
    static final ArchRule noDirectDatabaseAccessFromServiceLayer =
        FreezingArchRule.freeze(
            noClasses()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..service..")
                .should().accessClassesThat()
                .resideInAPackage("..infrastructure.db..")
        ).persistIn(FreezingArchRule.persistIn("build/archunit-freeze-store"))
         .associateViolationLinesVia(FreezingArchRule.ViolationLineAssociation.IGNORE_CLASSNAME)
         .allowStoredViolations(10); // allow up to 10 pre-existing violations until cleaned up

    @ArchTest
    static final ArchRule noUtilityClassesInDomainLayer =
        FreezingArchRule.freeze(
            noClasses()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..domain..")
                .and().haveSimpleNameEndingWith("Util")
                .should().exist()
        ).persistIn(FreezingArchRule.persistIn("build/archunit-freeze-store"));
}
```
Tradeoff: `FreezingArchRule` allows gradual architecture cleanup by treating pre-existing violations as known technical debt rather than immediate failures, preventing a rule from blocking all merges when introduced on a legacy codebase; the trade-off is that the freeze store (stored JSON file) must be committed to source control and kept in sync with the codebase — if classes are renamed or moved without updating the freeze store, violations are silently removed from the known-bad list even if the underlying architectural problem remains, creating false confidence. [official]

**Pattern 367** — Spring Boot `@SpringBootTest` with `RANDOM_PORT` and `TestRestTemplate` for full-stack slice
```java
@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = SpringBootTest.WebEnvironment.RANDOM_PORT)
@ActiveProfiles("test")
class ProductCatalogEndToEndTest {

    @LocalServerPort
    int port;

    @Autowired
    TestRestTemplate restTemplate;

    @Autowired
    ProductRepository productRepository;

    @BeforeEach
    void seedDatabase() {
        productRepository.deleteAll();
        productRepository.save(new Product("SKU-001", "Widget", new BigDecimal("9.99")));
    }

    @Test
    void listProductsShouldReturnSeededItem() {
        ResponseEntity<List<ProductDto>> response = restTemplate.exchange(
            "/api/v1/products",
            HttpMethod.GET,
            null,
            new ParameterizedTypeReference<>() {}
        );
        assertThat(response.getStatusCode()).isEqualTo(HttpStatus.OK);
        assertThat(response.getBody())
            .hasSize(1)
            .first()
            .extracting(ProductDto::sku, ProductDto::price)
            .containsExactly("SKU-001", new BigDecimal("9.99"));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `RANDOM_PORT` with `TestRestTemplate` exercises the full HTTP stack including filters, exception handlers, and serialisation, catching wiring bugs that `@WebMvcTest` mocked slices miss; the cost is that `@SpringBootTest` loads the entire application context (including all beans and datasource connections), making each test class 3–8x slower than a `@WebMvcTest` slice, so reserve full-stack tests for critical path workflows and use slices for controller-layer unit tests. [official]

**Pattern 368** — Awaitility `pollInterval` with `ConditionFactory` and `failFast` for eventual-consistency assertions
```java
@Test
void inventoryProjectionShouldReflectEventWithin5Seconds() {
    // Arrange: publish a domain event to the Kafka topic
    kafkaTemplate.send("inventory-events",
        new InventoryReducedEvent(PRODUCT_ID, 3));

    // Assert: projection catches up asynchronously
    await()
        .pollDelay(Duration.ofMillis(100))     // initial delay before first poll
        .pollInterval(Duration.ofMillis(250))   // check every 250ms
        .atMost(Duration.ofSeconds(5))
        .failFast("Kafka consumer thread died",  // abort if consumer crashes
            () -> !kafkaConsumerHealthChecker.isAlive())
        .untilAsserted(() ->
            assertThat(inventoryProjectionRepository.findByProductId(PRODUCT_ID))
                .isPresent()
                .get()
                .extracting(InventoryProjection::quantityAvailable)
                .isEqualTo(97)   // 100 initial − 3 reduced
        );
}
```
Tradeoff: Combining `pollDelay`, `pollInterval`, and `failFast` produces a precise, self-documenting async assertion that neither busy-waits nor silently misses consumer crashes; the trade-off is that `failFast` uses a `Callable<Boolean>` that is polled on each check interval, so any exception thrown inside the `failFast` supplier itself (e.g., a `NullPointerException` in the health checker) is treated as `false` rather than aborting the await, requiring defensive null-safe implementation of the health predicate. [official]

**Pattern 369** — JUnit 5 `@MethodSource` with a `Stream<Arguments>` factory for complex parameterised test data
```java
static Stream<Arguments> discountScenarios() {
    return Stream.of(
        Arguments.of("NEW_USER",    OrderTier.STANDARD, new BigDecimal("100.00"), new BigDecimal("10.00")),
        Arguments.of("NEW_USER",    OrderTier.PREMIUM,  new BigDecimal("100.00"), new BigDecimal("15.00")),
        Arguments.of("RETURNING",   OrderTier.STANDARD, new BigDecimal("200.00"), new BigDecimal("20.00")),
        Arguments.of("RETURNING",   OrderTier.PREMIUM,  new BigDecimal("200.00"), new BigDecimal("40.00")),
        Arguments.of("VIP",         OrderTier.STANDARD, new BigDecimal("500.00"), new BigDecimal("100.00")),
        Arguments.of("VIP",         OrderTier.PREMIUM,  new BigDecimal("500.00"), new BigDecimal("150.00"))
    );
}

@ParameterizedTest(name = "[{index}] {0} + {1}: {2} → discount {3}")
@MethodSource("discountScenarios")
void discountCalculatorShouldApplyCorrectDiscount(
        String customerType, OrderTier tier,
        BigDecimal subtotal, BigDecimal expectedDiscount) {
    BigDecimal actual = discountCalculator.calculate(customerType, tier, subtotal);
    assertThat(actual)
        .as("discount for %s/%s on %s", customerType, tier, subtotal)
        .isEqualByComparingTo(expectedDiscount);
}
```
Tradeoff: `@MethodSource` with typed `Arguments` provides full IDE autocompletion and refactoring support unlike `@CsvSource` string literals, and the factory method can be extracted to a shared test-data utility class for reuse across multiple test classes; however the factory method must be `static` (unless `@TestInstance(Lifecycle.PER_CLASS)` is used), which prevents accessing instance-level `@Mock` or `@Autowired` fields from within the argument factory, requiring test data to be self-contained value objects rather than pre-built mock-dependent fixtures. [official]

**Pattern 370** — Mockito `MockedConstruction` to intercept `new` expressions in legacy code
```java
@Test
void legacyOrderProcessorShouldUseNewHttpClientForEachRequest() {
    try (MockedConstruction<HttpClient> mockedClient =
            mockConstruction(HttpClient.class, (mock, ctx) -> {
                // configure the mock at construction time — ctx.arguments() gives constructor args
                assertThat(ctx.arguments()).containsExactly("https://payments.example.com");
                when(mock.post(anyString(), anyString()))
                    .thenReturn(new HttpResponse(200, "{\"charged\":true}"));
            })) {

        LegacyOrderProcessor processor = new LegacyOrderProcessor();
        OrderResult result = processor.process(buildOrder());

        assertThat(result.isSuccessful()).isTrue();
        // verify exactly one HttpClient was constructed per process call
        assertThat(mockedClient.constructed()).hasSize(1);
        verify(mockedClient.constructed().get(0)).post(
            eq("https://payments.example.com/charge"), anyString());
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `MockedConstruction` enables testing legacy code that instantiates collaborators with `new` internally without requiring any production-code refactoring (unlike `PowerMock`), and Mockito 4.x implements it without bytecode manipulation by replacing the constructor in a thread-local scope; the critical limitation is that the mock scope is thread-local — code that dispatches `new HttpClient()` on a different thread (e.g., via `CompletableFuture.supplyAsync`) will not intercept the construction and will attempt to create a real instance, so `MockedConstruction` is only safe for single-threaded legacy code paths. [official]

**Pattern 371** — Spring Boot `@WebMvcTest` with `@WithMockUser` for role-based controller tests
```java
@WebMvcTest(OrderController.class)
@Import(TestSecurityConfig.class)
class OrderControllerSecurityTest {

    @Autowired MockMvc mvc;

    @MockBean OrderService orderService;

    @Test
    @WithMockUser(roles = "CUSTOMER")
    void customerShouldBeAbleToViewOwnOrder() throws Exception {
        given(orderService.findByIdAndOwner(eq(42L), eq("user")))
            .willReturn(Optional.of(buildOrder(42L)));

        mvc.perform(get("/api/orders/42").accept(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON))
           .andExpect(status().isOk())
           .andExpect(jsonPath("$.id").value(42))
           .andExpect(jsonPath("$.status").value("PENDING"));
    }

    @Test
    @WithMockUser(roles = "GUEST")
    void guestShouldReceive403WhenAccessingOrders() throws Exception {
        mvc.perform(get("/api/orders/42").accept(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON))
           .andExpect(status().isForbidden());
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@WebMvcTest` loads only the web layer (controllers, filters, `WebMvcConfigurer`, security config) and keeps the startup time under 1 second for most controllers; the limitation is that `@WebMvcTest` does not load `@Service` or `@Repository` beans, requiring every collaborator to be declared as `@MockBean`, which means business logic bugs are invisible at this layer — use `@WebMvcTest` exclusively for HTTP binding, request mapping, security rules, and response serialisation verification, and test business logic in isolation from the web layer entirely. [official]

**Pattern 372** — AssertJ `usingRecursiveComparison` with custom `Comparator` for domain value types
```java
@Test
void orderDtoShouldMatchDomainObjectStructurally() {
    Order domain = Order.builder()
        .id(OrderId.of(UUID.fromString("a1b2c3d4-0000-0000-0000-000000000001")))
        .total(Money.of(new BigDecimal("99.99"), Currency.getInstance("USD")))
        .placedAt(Instant.parse("2026-05-01T10:00:00Z"))
        .build();

    OrderDto dto = orderMapper.toDto(domain);

    assertThat(dto)
        .usingRecursiveComparison()
        .withComparatorForType(
            Comparator.comparing(BigDecimal::stripTrailingZeros),
            BigDecimal.class
        )
        .ignoringFields("auditMetadata", "etag")
        .isEqualTo(new OrderDto(
            "a1b2c3d4-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
            new BigDecimal("99.99"),
            "USD",
            Instant.parse("2026-05-01T10:00:00Z")
        ));
}
```
Tradeoff: `usingRecursiveComparison` eliminates the need for bespoke `equals`/`hashCode` on DTOs and supports ignoring irrelevant fields and applying type-specific comparators in a single fluent expression; the pitfall is that recursive comparison traverses the entire object graph including inherited fields from framework superclasses (e.g., JPA proxy fields or Hibernate internals), which can produce misleading "fields differ" errors on objects that are logically equal — use `ignoringFieldsMatchingRegexes` to exclude framework-managed fields or call `withEqualsForType` to short-circuit comparison at known value-type boundaries. [official]

**Pattern 373** — Testcontainers `@DynamicPropertySource` with `PostgreSQLContainer` for Spring context wiring
```java
@SpringBootTest
@Testcontainers
class OrderRepositoryIntegrationTest {

    @Container
    static PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres =
        new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine")
            .withDatabaseName("orders_test")
            .withUsername("test")
            .withPassword("test")
            .withReuse(true);

    @DynamicPropertySource
    static void registerDataSourceProperties(DynamicPropertyRegistry registry) {
        registry.add("spring.datasource.url",      postgres::getJdbcUrl);
        registry.add("spring.datasource.username", postgres::getUsername);
        registry.add("spring.datasource.password", postgres::getPassword);
        registry.add("spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto", () -> "validate");
        registry.add("spring.flyway.enabled", () -> "true");
    }

    @Autowired OrderRepository orderRepository;
    @Autowired Flyway flyway;

    @BeforeEach
    void resetSchema() { flyway.clean(); flyway.migrate(); }

    @Test
    void shouldPersistAndRetrieveOrderWithLineItems() {
        Order saved = orderRepository.save(buildCompleteOrder());
        Order found = orderRepository.findById(saved.getId()).orElseThrow();
        assertThat(found.getLineItems()).hasSize(2);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@DynamicPropertySource` overrides Spring `Environment` properties before the context is loaded, making the container's dynamically assigned JDBC URL available to `DataSource` auto-configuration without any XML or `application-test.properties` changes; using `withReuse(true)` drastically reduces per-test-suite startup overhead by keeping the container alive across JVM restarts, but the reused container accumulates state between test runs unless the test explicitly resets the schema, making `@BeforeEach` schema reset mandatory to prevent data leaking between local re-runs. [official]

**Pattern 374** — WireMock snapshot contract testing against a live external API response
```java
@WireMockTest
class ExchangeRateClientContractTest {

    @Test
    void exchangeRateClientShouldHandleLiveApiResponse(WireMockRuntimeInfo wm)
            throws IOException {
        // Load pre-recorded response snapshot from test resources
        String snapshot = Files.readString(
            Path.of("src/test/resources/wiremock/exchange-rates-eur-usd.json"));

        stubFor(get(urlPathEqualTo("/latest"))
            .withQueryParam("base", equalTo("EUR"))
            .withQueryParam("symbols", equalTo("USD"))
            .willReturn(okJson(snapshot)
                .withHeader("X-Rate-Limit-Remaining", "450")));

        ExchangeRateClient client =
            new ExchangeRateClient(wm.getHttpBaseUrl());
        ExchangeRate rate = client.getRate(Currency.EUR, Currency.USD);

        assertThat(rate.value())
            .as("EUR/USD rate from snapshot")
            .isBetween(new BigDecimal("1.05"), new BigDecimal("1.15"));
        assertThat(rate.timestamp()).isAfter(Instant.parse("2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"));

        verify(getRequestedFor(urlPathEqualTo("/latest"))
            .withQueryParam("base", equalTo("EUR")));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: Storing WireMock response snapshots in `src/test/resources` decouples tests from live API availability and enables deterministic CI execution without network access; the trade-off is snapshot staleness — if the external API changes its response schema, the snapshot silently continues to pass while the production code fails against the live API, requiring a deliberate re-recording process gated behind a separate `@Tag("contract-refresh")` test profile run on a scheduled basis against the real endpoint. [official]

**Pattern 375** — ArchUnit `slices().beFreeOfCycles()` for bounded-context cycle detection
```java
@AnalyzeClasses(
    packages = "com.example.billing",
    importOptions = {
        ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests.class,
        ImportOption.DoNotIncludeJars.class
    }
)
class NoCyclicDependenciesTest {

    @ArchTest
    static final ArchRule noCyclesInApplicationLayer =
        slices().matching("com.example.billing.(*)..")
            .should().beFreeOfCycles();

    @ArchTest
    static final ArchRule domainMustNotDependOnInfrastructure =
        noClasses()
            .that().resideInAPackage("..billing.domain..")
            .should().dependOnClassesThat()
            .resideInAnyPackage(
                "..billing.infrastructure..",
                "..billing.adapter..",
                "..billing.api.."
            );

    @ArchTest
    static final ArchRule commandHandlersMustNotCallCommandHandlers =
        noClasses()
            .that().haveSimpleNameEndingWith("CommandHandler")
            .should().dependOnClassesThat()
            .haveSimpleNameEndingWith("CommandHandler");
}
```
Tradeoff: `slices().matching(...).should().beFreeOfCycles()` detects package-level dependency cycles that JVM compilation does not prevent and that cause hidden coupling debt in large modules; the performance cost is significant for packages containing 500+ classes — confine `@AnalyzeClasses` to the specific bounded context package rather than the entire application root, and cache the imported classes in a static field to amortise the cost across all `@ArchTest` rules in the same class. [official]

---

### Community Gotchas

**G36** — Testcontainers `withReuse(true)` combined with `@DynamicPropertySource` causes Spring context cache misses
Why this matters: Spring Boot's test context cache key includes the exact `@DynamicPropertySource` values registered at context creation time, including the JDBC URL with its dynamically assigned host port. When a reused container is detected on a subsequent run, it may bind to the same port (Docker reuse guarantees this when the hash matches), but if any other environmental factor changes (e.g., a different `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto` property or an extra `@MockBean`), Spring creates a new context anyway. Meanwhile, in environments with strict Docker socket restrictions (DinD CI pipelines with `--privileged` disabled), the Ryuk reaper cannot connect and containers are abandoned rather than reused, so `withReuse(true)` produces the opposite effect — a growing pool of orphaned containers — without any warning in the test output.
Fix: Combine `withReuse(true)` only with an explicit `TC_REUSE_ENABLE=true` environment variable set in the CI pipeline configuration, and add a `.waitingFor(Wait.forListeningPort())` health check so Testcontainers detects a reused container is ready without re-running the startup probe from scratch. For environments where reuse is unreliable, remove it and instead use `@TestClassOrder(ClassOrderer.ClassName.class)` to run integration tests sequentially, enabling Spring context reuse via consistent `@MockBean` sets across test classes. [official]

**G37** — WireMock stub priority ordering causes unexpected `404` when multiple stubs match the same URL pattern
Why this matters: WireMock evaluates stubs in order of descending `priority` (lower number = higher priority, default is `5`). When two stubs match the same URL — one as a broad catch-all (`get(anyUrl())`) and one as a specific path matcher (`get(urlEqualTo("/api/orders/42"))`) — WireMock uses the last-registered stub if both have the same priority, not the most specific one. This is the opposite of most routing frameworks (Spring MVC, JAX-RS) where specificity determines precedence. Test authors accustomed to Spring's specificity rules accidentally register a wildcard stub first in `@BeforeEach` and a specific stub second, expecting specificity-based routing, but WireMock picks the first registered stub (for equal priorities), returning the wildcard response and making the specific stub unreachable.
Fix: Always assign explicit `.withPriority(1)` to specific stubs and `.withPriority(10)` (or higher number) to catch-all or fallback stubs, making priority explicit and independent of registration order. Alternatively, avoid mixing wildcard and specific stubs for the same HTTP method in a single test — create separate test classes for fallback behavior vs. happy-path behavior. [official]

**G38** — JUnit 5 `@TempDir` shared across `@Nested` classes and `@BeforeAll` results in premature directory deletion
Why this matters: JUnit 5 cleans up `@TempDir` directories after the test or test class in which they are declared, depending on whether the annotated field is `static` or instance-scoped. When a `static @TempDir` is declared in an outer test class and `@Nested` inner classes also reference that directory in their `@BeforeAll` setup, the outer `@TempDir` is deleted after the outer class's teardown. Custom JUnit 5 extensions that hook into `afterAll` for the outer class may run before nested classes complete if not ordered explicitly, causing file-not-found failures deep inside nested test setup rather than in the outer class where the deletion occurs.
Fix: Declare `@TempDir` at the level where it is actually used — if only a single `@Nested` class needs the directory, declare it as `static` within that nested class, not the outer class. When multiple nested classes must share a directory, use a `@RegisterExtension` instance of a custom `TemporaryDirectoryExtension` that implements `BeforeAllCallback` and `AfterAllCallback` at the `ExtensionContext.Store` level with the enclosing class as the namespace key, ensuring cleanup happens after all nested classes complete. [official]

**G39** — AssertJ `extracting(String fieldName)` uses reflection and bypasses `private` accessor methods, returning raw field values that differ from getter output
Why this matters: `assertThat(list).extracting("price")` accesses the `price` field directly via reflection, bypassing any getter logic (e.g., a `getPrice()` that applies rounding, currency conversion, or lazy initialisation). If the domain model's `getPrice()` returns a derived or transformed value — such as stripping trailing zeros from a `BigDecimal` or converting a stored cents integer to a `BigDecimal` — then `extracting("price")` returns the raw stored field (e.g., `Long 999`) while the test author expected the getter's output (e.g., `BigDecimal("9.99")`). The assertion fails with a confusing type mismatch rather than a meaningful domain-logic failure, and the test message gives no indication that getter bypassing is the cause.
Fix: Prefer `extracting(Product::getPrice)` (method reference form) over `extracting("price")` (string form) for all non-trivial domain objects — method references use the actual getter, honour access modifiers, are refactor-safe (renamed fields break the lambda at compile time, not at runtime), and return the semantically correct value. Reserve string-based `extracting` only for simple data transfer objects or records with no getter logic. [official]

**G40** — Mockito `@Spy` on a real object double-counts self-call invocations, producing misleading `verify` results
Why this matters: When Mockito creates a `@Spy` wrapping a real object, every call to the spy is intercepted. If the method under spy calls another method on the same spy instance (`this.methodB()` called from `this.methodA()`), Mockito sees two intercepted invocations: one for `methodA` and one for the self-call to `methodB`. `verify(spy, times(1)).methodB()` passes even when the test author intended to verify an external call to `methodB` (i.e., called from outside the class), because the internal self-invocation is indistinguishable from an external call in Mockito's invocation recorder. In production code that uses template-method patterns (a concrete method calling abstract hooks on `this`), spy verification produces misleading pass results when the actual external call path is never exercised.
Fix: Design the system under test to delegate to injected collaborators rather than calling `this.methodB()` internally — this eliminates the ambiguity entirely and allows plain `@Mock` verification with unambiguous invocation counts. When self-delegation cannot be avoided (e.g., legacy template-method patterns), use `@Spy` only to stub the specific hook method (`doReturn(value).when(spy).methodB()`) and verify business outcomes through public-method return values rather than verifying the number of internal self-calls. [official]
