### Patterns

**Pattern 376** — JUnit 5 `@TestTemplate` with `TestTemplateInvocationContextProvider` for multi-environment execution
```java
@ExtendWith(MultiEnvExtension.class)
class OrderServiceTemplateTest {

    @TestTemplate
    void order_placed_successfully(String env, OrderService service) {
        Order order = service.place(new OrderRequest("SKU-42", 3));
        assertThat(order.getStatus()).isEqualTo(OrderStatus.CONFIRMED);
        assertThat(order.getEnvironment()).isEqualTo(env);
    }
}

class MultiEnvExtension implements TestTemplateInvocationContextProvider {

    private static final List<String> ENVS = List.of("staging", "canary", "production");

    @Override
    public boolean supportsTestTemplate(ExtensionContext ctx) { return true; }

    @Override
    public Stream<TestTemplateInvocationContext> provideTestTemplateInvocationContexts(
            ExtensionContext ctx) {
        return ENVS.stream().map(env -> new TestTemplateInvocationContext() {
            @Override
            public String getDisplayName(int index) { return "[" + env + "]"; }

            @Override
            public List<Extension> getAdditionalExtensions() {
                return List.of(new ParameterResolver() {
                    @Override
                    public boolean supportsParameter(ParameterContext p, ExtensionContext e) {
                        return p.getParameter().getType() == String.class
                            || p.getParameter().getType() == OrderService.class;
                    }
                    @Override
                    public Object resolveParameter(ParameterContext p, ExtensionContext e) {
                        if (p.getParameter().getType() == String.class) return env;
                        return OrderServiceFactory.forEnv(env);
                    }
                });
            }
        });
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@TestTemplate` with a custom `TestTemplateInvocationContextProvider` avoids duplicating `@ParameterizedTest` test classes per environment and injects fully initialised service objects rather than primitive values, but the extension wiring is significantly more verbose than `@ParameterizedTest` with `@EnumSource`; prefer `@TestTemplate` only when the invocation context requires injecting typed collaborators that cannot be expressed as `Arguments` instances. [official]

**Pattern 377** — Mockito `InOrder` chained verification with `verifyNoMoreInteractions` for strict protocol compliance
```java
@Test
void payment_gateway_protocol_is_strictly_ordered() {
    PaymentGateway gateway = mock(PaymentGateway.class);
    PaymentProcessor processor = new PaymentProcessor(gateway);

    when(gateway.authorise(any())).thenReturn(AuthResult.APPROVED);
    when(gateway.capture(anyString())).thenReturn(CaptureResult.SUCCESS);

    processor.charge(new PaymentRequest("tok_visa", Money.of(99_99, "GBP")));

    InOrder order = inOrder(gateway);
    order.verify(gateway).authorise(
        argThat(req -> req.getToken().equals("tok_visa")
            && req.getAmount().equals(Money.of(99_99, "GBP")))
    );
    order.verify(gateway).capture(argThat(id -> id.startsWith("auth_")));
    order.verify(gateway).notify(any(CaptureResult.class));
    order.verifyNoMoreInteractions();
}
```
Tradeoff: `InOrder.verifyNoMoreInteractions()` enforces that no calls occur outside the verified sequence and catches regressions where a refactor reorders or inserts gateway calls; however, it over-constrains tests when the SUT calls stateless query methods (e.g., `gateway.isHealthy()`) as side effects — use `ignoreStubs()` from `Mockito.ignoreStubs(gateway)` to exclude pure stub interactions from the `verifyNoMoreInteractions` check. [official]

**Pattern 378** — AssertJ `satisfies` with multiple `ThrowingConsumer` assertions for rich domain-object inspection
```java
@Test
void shipment_enriched_with_all_required_fields() {
    Shipment shipment = ShipmentBuilder.from(order)
        .withCarrier(Carrier.DHL)
        .withTrackingCode("1Z999AA10123456784")
        .build();

    assertThat(shipment)
        .satisfies(
            s -> assertThat(s.getTrackingCode())
                    .startsWith("1Z")
                    .hasSize(18),
            s -> assertThat(s.getCarrier())
                    .isEqualTo(Carrier.DHL),
            s -> assertThat(s.getEstimatedDelivery())
                    .isAfter(LocalDate.now())
                    .isBefore(LocalDate.now().plusDays(7)),
            s -> assertThat(s.getWeight())
                    .isPositive()
                    .isLessThanOrEqualTo(BigDecimal.valueOf(30)),
            s -> assertThat(s.getLabel())
                    .isNotNull()
                    .extracting(Label::getFormat)
                    .isEqualTo(LabelFormat.PDF)
        );
}
```
Tradeoff: `satisfies(ThrowingConsumer...)` runs all consumer assertions before reporting failures, giving a complete picture of a malformed domain object in one test run — unlike chained `assertThat` calls that stop at the first failure; the downside is that deeply nested `satisfies` blocks become hard to read once more than five consumers are needed, at which point a custom `AbstractAssert` subclass for the domain type is the cleaner alternative. [official]

**Pattern 379** — Testcontainers `DockerComposeContainer` with `WaitingFor` per service for realistic integration bootstrapping
```java
@Testcontainers
@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT)
class FullStackIntegrationTest {

    @Container
    static final DockerComposeContainer<?> compose =
        new DockerComposeContainer<>(new File("src/test/resources/docker-compose-it.yml"))
            .withExposedService("postgres_1", 5432,
                Wait.forLogMessage(".*database system is ready to accept connections.*\\n", 1)
                    .withStartupTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(60)))
            .withExposedService("redis_1", 6379,
                Wait.forListeningPort().withStartupTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(30)))
            .withExposedService("kafka_1", 9092,
                Wait.forLogMessage(".*Kafka Server started.*\\n", 1)
                    .withStartupTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(90)))
            .withLocalCompose(true)
            .withOptions("--compatibility");

    @DynamicPropertySource
    static void registerPorts(DynamicPropertyRegistry registry) {
        registry.add("spring.datasource.url", () ->
            "jdbc:postgresql://%s:%d/testdb".formatted(
                compose.getServiceHost("postgres_1", 5432),
                compose.getServicePort("postgres_1", 5432)));
        registry.add("spring.data.redis.host",
            () -> compose.getServiceHost("redis_1", 6379));
        registry.add("spring.kafka.bootstrap-servers", () ->
            "%s:%d".formatted(
                compose.getServiceHost("kafka_1", 9092),
                compose.getServicePort("kafka_1", 9092)));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: Per-service `WaitingFor` strategies using log-message matchers ensure each service is truly ready before the Spring context starts, eliminating race-condition failures in CI; however, log-message patterns are Kafka/Postgres version-specific and silently break on image upgrades — complement log matchers with a `Wait.forLogMessage(...).orElse(Wait.forListeningPort())` fallback or pin Docker image digests in the compose file. [official]

**Pattern 380** — WireMock response templating with Handlebars helpers for dynamic request-correlated stubs
```java
@WireMockTest
class ProductApiClientTest {

    @Test
    void fetch_product_echoes_requested_id_in_response(WireMockRuntimeInfo wm) {
        WireMock wireMock = wm.getWireMock();
        wireMock.register(
            get(urlPathMatching("/products/[0-9]+"))
                .willReturn(aResponse()
                    .withHeader("Content-Type", "application/json")
                    .withBodyFile("product-template.json")
                    .withTransformers("response-template"))
        );
        // product-template.json:
        // { "id": {{request.pathSegments.[1]}},
        //   "name": "Product-{{request.pathSegments.[1]}}",
        //   "requestedAt": "{{now format='yyyy-MM-dd'}}" }

        ProductApiClient client = new ProductApiClient("http://localhost:" + wm.getHttpPort());
        Product p = client.fetchById(42L);

        assertThat(p.getId()).isEqualTo(42L);
        assertThat(p.getName()).isEqualTo("Product-42");
        assertThat(p.getRequestedAt()).isEqualTo(LocalDate.now());
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: Handlebars response templating lets a single stub handle any ID without registering N individual stubs, making tests concise and the stub library maintainable; the tradeoff is that template errors (mismatched Handlebars syntax) fail silently at stub registration time and produce `200` responses with empty or malformed JSON bodies rather than explicit errors, so always assert on the deserialized response fields rather than raw body strings to catch template regressions. [official]

**Pattern 381** — ArchUnit `methods().that().areAnnotatedWith` naming convention enforcement across service layer
```java
@AnalyzeClasses(packages = "com.example.order", importOptions = ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests.class)
class ServiceNamingConventionTest {

    @ArchTest
    static final ArchRule transactional_methods_must_follow_naming_convention =
        methods()
            .that().areAnnotatedWith(Transactional.class)
            .and().areDeclaredInClassesThat()
                .resideInAPackage("..service..")
            .should().haveNameMatching(
                "(execute|handle|process|save|update|delete|create)[A-Z].*")
            .because("transactional service methods must use verb-prefixed names "
                + "to distinguish write operations from queries at a glance");

    @ArchTest
    static final ArchRule query_methods_must_not_be_transactional =
        methods()
            .that().haveNameMatching("(find|get|list|search|fetch)[A-Z].*")
            .and().areDeclaredInClassesThat()
                .resideInAPackage("..service..")
            .should().notBeAnnotatedWith(Transactional.class)
            .orShould().beAnnotatedWith(
                describe("@Transactional(readOnly=true)",
                    a -> a.type().equals(Transactional.class)));
}
```
Tradeoff: Enforcing naming conventions via ArchUnit catches accidental transactional queries (which hold database connections longer than necessary) at CI time rather than in production profiling; the regex-based `haveNameMatching` rule requires updating the pattern list whenever a new approved verb prefix is adopted — maintain the list in a shared constants class and reference it from the rule to avoid drift. [official]

**Pattern 382** — Spring Boot `@DataJpaTest` with `TestEntityManager` and explicit `flush`/`clear` for persistence validation
```java
@DataJpaTest
@AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = Replace.NONE)
@Testcontainers
class InventoryRepositoryTest {

    @Container
    static PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres =
        new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine");

    @DynamicPropertySource
    static void overrideProps(DynamicPropertyRegistry registry) {
        registry.add("spring.datasource.url", postgres::getJdbcUrl);
        registry.add("spring.datasource.username", postgres::getUsername);
        registry.add("spring.datasource.password", postgres::getPassword);
    }

    @Autowired TestEntityManager em;
    @Autowired InventoryRepository repo;

    @Test
    void find_low_stock_items_returns_only_below_threshold() {
        em.persistAndFlush(new InventoryItem("SKU-1", 100));
        em.persistAndFlush(new InventoryItem("SKU-2", 4));
        em.persistAndFlush(new InventoryItem("SKU-3", 0));
        em.clear(); // evict L1 cache so repo hits the database

        List<InventoryItem> low = repo.findLowStock(5);

        assertThat(low)
            .extracting(InventoryItem::getSku)
            .containsExactlyInAnyOrder("SKU-2", "SKU-3");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: Calling `em.clear()` after `persistAndFlush()` forces repository queries to hit the actual database rather than the first-level JPA cache, catching column mapping errors, missing `@Index` definitions, and JPQL translation bugs that Hibernate's identity map would otherwise mask; the downside is that `em.clear()` invalidates all managed entities in the session, so any entity references held in local variables become detached and throw `LazyInitializationException` if accessed after the clear. [official]

**Pattern 383** — Awaitility `conditionEvaluationListener` with structured logging for asynchronous Kafka consumer assertions
```java
@Test
void order_event_consumed_and_projection_updated() {
    List<String> pollLog = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>();

    await()
        .atMost(Duration.ofSeconds(20))
        .pollInterval(fibonacci())
        .conditionEvaluationListener(condition ->
            pollLog.add("[%dms] attempts=%d result=%s: %s".formatted(
                condition.getElapsedTimeInMS(),
                condition.getPollCount(),
                condition.isConditionSatisfied() ? "PASS" : "fail",
                condition.getDescription())))
        .failFast("Dead-letter-queue received message — consumer is broken",
            () -> dlqMonitor.messageCount() > 0)
        .untilAsserted(() -> {
            OrderProjection projection = projectionStore.findByOrderId("ORD-001");
            assertThat(projection).isNotNull();
            assertThat(projection.getStatus()).isEqualTo(ProjectionStatus.SHIPPED);
            assertThat(projection.getLastUpdated()).isAfterOrEqualTo(testStart);
        });

    if (!pollLog.isEmpty()) {
        log.debug("Poll history:\n{}", String.join("\n", pollLog));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `conditionEvaluationListener` with `fibonacci()` polling reduces unnecessary CPU and network calls during early polling while accumulating enough diagnostic history to pinpoint the exact poll number at which the condition first satisfied or failed; the Fibonacci strategy introduces growing inter-poll delays that can cause a 20-second `atMost` budget to exhaust before reaching 20 polls if initial intervals are too small — set an explicit `pollDelay(Duration.ofMillis(100))` to prevent the first Fibonacci step from starting at 1 ms. [official]

**Pattern 384** — JUnit 5 `@ParameterizedTest` with `@CsvFileSource` and custom `ArgumentConverter` for typed domain inputs
```java
@ParameterizedTest(name = "[{index}] {0} → expect status={2}")
@CsvFileSource(resources = "/test-data/pricing-scenarios.csv", numLinesToSkip = 1)
void pricing_engine_applies_correct_discount(
        @ConvertWith(MoneyConverter.class) Money listPrice,
        @ConvertWith(CustomerTierConverter.class) CustomerTier tier,
        @ConvertWith(MoneyConverter.class) Money expectedNet,
        String description) {

    Money actualNet = pricingEngine.calculateNet(listPrice, tier);

    assertThat(actualNet)
        .as(description)
        .usingComparator(Money.CURRENCY_AWARE_COMPARATOR)
        .isEqualTo(expectedNet);
}

// pricing-scenarios.csv:
// listPrice,tier,expectedNet,description
// GBP 100.00,GOLD,GBP 80.00,Gold tier 20% discount
// GBP 100.00,SILVER,GBP 90.00,Silver tier 10% discount
// USD 50.00,BRONZE,USD 50.00,Bronze tier no discount
```
Tradeoff: `@CsvFileSource` with `ArgumentConverter` implementations separates test data from test logic and allows non-engineers to maintain pricing scenarios in a CSV without editing Java source; the tradeoff is that converter errors (malformed CSV values that fail type conversion) surface as `ParameterResolutionException` at test launch rather than assertion failures, so add an `@BeforeAll`-level smoke test that parses the CSV with the same converters and fails with a human-readable error listing all rows that do not parse cleanly. [official]

**Pattern 385** — Mockito `MockedStatic` with `try-with-resources` for thread-safe static method mocking in parallel tests
```java
@Test
void order_id_generation_uses_deterministic_uuid_in_isolation() {
    UUID fixedId = UUID.fromString("00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001");

    try (MockedStatic<UUID> uuidMock = mockStatic(UUID.class)) {
        uuidMock.when(UUID::randomUUID).thenReturn(fixedId);

        Order order = new OrderFactory().createDraftOrder(customerId);

        assertThat(order.getId()).isEqualTo(fixedId);
        assertThat(order.getStatus()).isEqualTo(OrderStatus.DRAFT);
        uuidMock.verify(UUID::randomUUID, times(1));
    }
    // Static mock is automatically closed and restored here
}
```
Tradeoff: `MockedStatic` scoped to a `try` block restores the original static implementation when the block exits, making static mocking safe in test classes that run methods in parallel (`@Execution(CONCURRENT)`); however, `MockedStatic` uses a `ThreadLocal`-backed classloader hook that is tied to the thread that opened the mock — if the production code dispatches work to a different thread pool inside the `try` block, those threads see the original (un-mocked) static and the test assertion for the generated UUID will fail intermittently with no obvious cause. [official]

**Pattern 386** — Spring Boot `@RestClientTest` with `MockRestServiceServer` for `RestTemplate`-based HTTP client isolation
```java
@RestClientTest(ExchangeRateClient.class)
class ExchangeRateClientTest {

    @Autowired ExchangeRateClient client;
    @Autowired MockRestServiceServer server;
    @Autowired ObjectMapper objectMapper;

    @Test
    void fetch_rate_returns_parsed_exchange_rate() throws Exception {
        ExchangeRateResponse stubResponse = new ExchangeRateResponse(
            "EUR", Map.of("GBP", 0.857, "USD", 1.082));

        server.expect(once(),
                requestTo("https://api.rates.io/v1/latest?base=EUR"))
            .andExpect(method(HttpMethod.GET))
            .andExpect(header("X-Api-Key", "test-key"))
            .andRespond(withSuccess(
                objectMapper.writeValueAsString(stubResponse),
                MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON));

        ExchangeRate rate = client.fetchRate(Currency.EUR, Currency.GBP);

        assertThat(rate.getValue())
            .isCloseTo(0.857, within(0.001));
        server.verify();
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@RestClientTest` loads only the HTTP client bean and its auto-configuration (Jackson, `RestTemplate`), making the test start in under 500 ms compared to a full `@SpringBootTest`; the slice does not load `@Service` or `@Repository` beans, so any `@Autowired` dependency on the client's collaborators must be manually declared with `@MockBean` — forgetting this causes a `NoSuchBeanDefinitionException` that is reported as an application context failure rather than a missing-mock error. [official]

**Pattern 387** — AssertJ `usingRecursiveComparison().ignoringFields()` for partial domain-object equality without Lombok `@EqualsAndHashCode`
```java
@Test
void order_confirmation_matches_request_ignoring_server_assigned_fields() {
    OrderRequest request = new OrderRequest(
        "CUST-001", List.of(new LineItem("SKU-A", 2), new LineItem("SKU-B", 1)),
        ShippingMethod.EXPRESS);

    OrderConfirmation confirmation = orderService.place(request);

    assertThat(confirmation)
        .usingRecursiveComparison()
        .ignoringFields(
            "orderId",          // server-generated UUID
            "placedAt",         // server timestamp
            "estimatedDelivery" // computed field
        )
        .ignoringCollectionOrder()
        .withComparatorForType(BigDecimal::compareTo, BigDecimal.class)
        .isEqualTo(new OrderConfirmation(
            null,
            "CUST-001",
            List.of(new LineItem("SKU-A", 2), new LineItem("SKU-B", 1)),
            ShippingMethod.EXPRESS,
            null,
            null));
}
```
Tradeoff: `usingRecursiveComparison().ignoringFields(...)` avoids the maintenance burden of implementing `equals`/`hashCode` on domain objects solely for test purposes, and `withComparatorForType(BigDecimal::compareTo, ...)` prevents false failures from `BigDecimal` scale differences (`1.0` vs `1.00`); the risk is that `ignoringFields` uses field names as strings, so renamed fields silently widen the comparison scope — annotate ignored fields with a custom marker annotation and add a compile-time ArchUnit rule asserting that all fields with that annotation appear in the `ignoringFields` call. [official]

**Pattern 388** — Testcontainers `GenericContainer` with `withCopyFileToContainer` for pre-seeded test fixtures

@Testcontainers
class ElasticsearchRepositoryTest {

            .withEnv("discovery.type", "single-node")

[official]

**Pattern 389** — JUnit 5 `@RegisterExtension` with `BeforeEachCallback`/`AfterEachCallback` for reusable audit-trail capture
```java
class AuditTrailExtension implements BeforeEachCallback, AfterEachCallback, ParameterResolver {

    private final List<AuditEvent> captured = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>();
    private AuditEventCaptor captor;

    @Override
    public void beforeEach(ExtensionContext ctx) {
        captor = AuditEventCaptor.install(captured::add);
    }

    @Override
    public void afterEach(ExtensionContext ctx) {
        captor.uninstall();
        captured.clear();
    }

    @Override
    public boolean supportsParameter(ParameterContext p, ExtensionContext e) {
        return p.getParameter().getType() == AuditCapture.class;
    }

    @Override
    public Object resolveParameter(ParameterContext p, ExtensionContext e) {
        return new AuditCapture(List.copyOf(captured));
    }
}

class OrderServiceAuditTest {

    @RegisterExtension
    AuditTrailExtension auditTrail = new AuditTrailExtension();

    @Test
    void placing_order_emits_created_and_reserved_events(AuditCapture audit) {
        orderService.place(new OrderRequest("CUST-1", items));
        assertThat(audit.events())
            .extracting(AuditEvent::getType)
            .containsExactly(AuditEventType.ORDER_CREATED, AuditEventType.INVENTORY_RESERVED);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@RegisterExtension` as an instance field creates one extension instance per test method, giving each test an isolated `captured` list with no cross-test pollution; if the extension is declared `static`, it is shared across all methods in the class and `CopyOnWriteArrayList` prevents concurrent modification failures in parallel execution, but accumulated events from earlier tests can leak into later ones unless `afterEach` clears the list — always match the extension lifecycle to the list lifecycle. [official]

**Pattern 390** — WireMock fault simulation with `withFault(Fault.RANDOM_DATA_THEN_CLOSE)` for resilience and retry testing
```java
@WireMockTest
class PaymentGatewayResilienceTest {

    @Test
    void payment_client_retries_on_malformed_response_and_succeeds(WireMockRuntimeInfo wm) {
        WireMock wireMock = wm.getWireMock();

        // First two requests return garbage + abrupt close
        wireMock.register(post(urlEqualTo("/v1/charges"))
            .inScenario("retry-scenario")
            .whenScenarioStateIs(STARTED)
            .willSetStateTo("first-retry")
            .willReturn(aResponse().withFault(Fault.RANDOM_DATA_THEN_CLOSE)));

        wireMock.register(post(urlEqualTo("/v1/charges"))
            .inScenario("retry-scenario")
            .whenScenarioStateIs("first-retry")
            .willSetStateTo("success")
            .willReturn(aResponse().withFault(Fault.RANDOM_DATA_THEN_CLOSE)));

        wireMock.register(post(urlEqualTo("/v1/charges"))
            .inScenario("retry-scenario")
            .whenScenarioStateIs("success")
            .willReturn(okJson("{\"id\":\"ch_001\",\"status\":\"succeeded\"}")));

        ChargeResult result = resilientGatewayClient.charge(
            new ChargeRequest("tok_visa", 9999L, "GBP"));

        assertThat(result.getStatus()).isEqualTo("succeeded");
        wireMock.verifyThat(3, postRequestedFor(urlEqualTo("/v1/charges")));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `Fault.RANDOM_DATA_THEN_CLOSE` is more realistic than `withStatus(503)` for testing retry logic because it exercises the TCP-level error path in the HTTP client (connection reset / malformed response parsing), not just HTTP status code routing; the fault closes the underlying socket, which may cause `SocketException` to surface on a background thread inside the HTTP client's connection pool — configure the resilience library's retry predicate to catch `IOException` and not just `HttpServerErrorException` or the retry will not trigger. [official]

### Community Gotchas

**G41** — JUnit 5 `@ParameterizedTest` with `@MethodSource` fails when the factory method has the same name as the test method in a superclass
Why this matters: JUnit 5 resolves `@MethodSource` factory methods by name, searching the current test class and then its superclass hierarchy. When a base class defines a parameterized test named `testScenario()` and a factory method named `testScenario()` (a common convention), a subclass that overrides `testScenario()` will inadvertently also shadow the factory method if it declares a method of the same name with a different signature. JUnit resolves the factory by simple name matching and picks the subclass method first; since the subclass method's return type is not `Stream<Arguments>`, JUnit throws a `PreconditionViolationException` with a message about the return type rather than indicating that the factory was resolved to the wrong method — the root cause is invisible from the error message alone.
Fix: Always qualify `@MethodSource` with the fully-qualified class name when the factory method lives in a superclass: `@MethodSource("com.example.BaseTest#testScenario")`. Alternatively, adopt the convention of naming factory methods with a `provideX` prefix (e.g., `provideTestScenario`) to prevent accidental name collisions between test methods and their data sources. [official]

**G42** — AssertJ `containsExactlyInAnyOrder` passes when a list contains duplicate elements that mask a missing element
Why this matters: `assertThat(list).containsExactlyInAnyOrder("A", "B", "C")` verifies that the list contains exactly the specified elements regardless of order. However, if the actual list is `["A", "A", "C"]` and the expected set is `["A", "B", "C"]`, AssertJ's matching algorithm pairs the first expected `"A"` with the first actual `"A"`, the expected `"B"` with the second actual `"A"` (both are unmatched after the first pairing), and the expected `"C"` with the actual `"C"`. This produces a spurious failure correctly. The dangerous case is when the expected list itself contains a duplicate: `containsExactlyInAnyOrder("A", "A", "C")` will pass against `["A", "B", "C"]` in some older AssertJ versions (pre-3.21) because the extra `"A"` in the expected list matches the `"B"` slot via a greedy matching algorithm, hiding the fact that `"B"` was expected but never asserted.
Fix: Upgrade to AssertJ 3.21 or later, which uses a correct bipartite-matching algorithm. For lists where ordering matters partially, use `containsSubsequence` for ordered subsets combined with `hasSize` to catch count discrepancies, rather than relying on `containsExactlyInAnyOrder` alone for correctness-critical assertions. [official]

**G43** — Spring Boot `@MockBean` on a `@Primary` bean does not replace the primary candidate and causes ambiguous autowiring failures
Why this matters: When a Spring context contains two beans of the same type — one annotated `@Primary` in production code and one registered as `@MockBean` in a test — Spring's `MockitoPostProcessor` replaces the mock's corresponding real bean by type, not by `@Primary` qualifier. If the real `@Primary` bean is in a `@Configuration` that is part of the test slice (e.g., because it matches a component-scan pattern), Spring registers both the original primary bean and the mock, resulting in `NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException` at context startup rather than silently selecting the mock. This is especially common with `@DataJpaTest` slices that auto-configure a `@Primary DataSource` alongside a test `@MockBean DataSource` for connection-pool behaviour testing.
Fix: Add `@Qualifier` to both the `@MockBean` declaration and the injection site, or use `@MockBean(name = "primaryDataSource")` to target the specific bean by name. For `@Primary` beans that should always be replaced by the mock in tests, move the `@Primary` annotation to a separate `@TestConfiguration` class that provides a `@MockBean`-compatible substitute and exclude the production `@Primary` configuration class using `@SpringBootTest(excludeAutoConfiguration = ...)`. [official]

**G44** — Awaitility `untilAsserted` swallows `AssertionError` from AssertJ `SoftAssertions` when soft-assertion failures are not rethrown
Why this matters: Awaitility's `untilAsserted` catches `AssertionError` thrown by the supplied lambda and retries until the condition is satisfied or the timeout expires. AssertJ's `SoftAssertions.assertSoftly` collects assertion failures internally and throws a single `SoftAssertionError` (a subtype of `AssertionError`) only at the end of the lambda body. When both are combined — `await().untilAsserted(() -> SoftAssertions.assertSoftly(soft -> { ... }))` — Awaitility catches the `SoftAssertionError` from each poll attempt, treats it as a retryable failure, and continues polling until timeout. This is correct behaviour in isolation, but if the soft-assertion lambda catches its own internal errors (via a try/catch for logging) and does not rethrow them, Awaitility sees no `AssertionError` and concludes the condition is satisfied even when assertions failed, causing a false pass.
Fix: Never use try/catch inside an `untilAsserted` lambda that would suppress `AssertionError` subtypes. When using `SoftAssertions` inside `untilAsserted`, prefer a plain `AssertionError`-throwing form (`assertThat(...)` directly) for the conditions that Awaitility should retry, and reserve soft assertions for the final post-await assertion block that runs outside the polling loop. [official]

**G45** — Testcontainers `PostgreSQLContainer` `withInitScript` runs DDL before Flyway migrations, causing duplicate table errors
Why this matters: `PostgreSQLContainer.withInitScript("schema.sql")` executes the provided SQL script during container startup using a JDBC connection, before the Spring application context is created. When the application also uses Flyway (`spring.flyway.enabled=true`), Flyway executes its migration scripts (including the same schema definitions) when the Spring context starts. The result is that `CREATE TABLE` statements in the init script are executed twice — once by Testcontainers and once by Flyway's V1 migration — producing `ERROR: relation "orders" already exists` and a context startup failure. This is particularly confusing because the error appears in Flyway's migration log rather than in the Testcontainers startup log, making the init-script origin non-obvious.
Fix: Use `withInitScript` exclusively for test-data seeding (`INSERT` statements only), not for DDL. Let Flyway own all schema creation, and if the test requires a specific schema state that Flyway migrations alone cannot produce (e.g., legacy column data for migration testing), create a dedicated Flyway migration script in `src/test/resources/db/migration` with a version number that precedes the scripts under test, and activate it only in tests via `spring.flyway.locations=classpath:db/migration,classpath:db/test-migration`. [official]

### Patterns

**Pattern 391** — Spring Boot `MockMvcTester` AssertJ-native Controller Assertions
```java
@WebMvcTest(OrderController.class)
class OrderControllerTest {

    @Autowired
    private MockMvcTester mvc;

    @MockitoBean
    private OrderService orderService;

    @Test
    void getOrder_returnsOrderDto_whenFound() {
        OrderDto dto = new OrderDto("ORD-001", "SHIPPED", BigDecimal.valueOf(49.99));
        given(orderService.findById("ORD-001")).willReturn(dto);

        assertThat(mvc.get().uri("/orders/ORD-001"))
            .hasStatusOk()
            .hasContentTypeCompatibleWith(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
            .bodyJson()
            .extractingPath("$.status").asString()
            .isEqualTo("SHIPPED");
    }

    @Test
    void getOrder_returns404_whenNotFound() {
        given(orderService.findById("MISSING")).willThrow(new OrderNotFoundException("MISSING"));

        assertThat(mvc.get().uri("/orders/MISSING"))
            .hasStatus(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND)
            .bodyJson()
            .extractingPath("$.code").asString()
            .isEqualTo("ORDER_NOT_FOUND");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `MockMvcTester` (introduced in Spring Boot 3.4) removes the need for `andExpect(status().isOk())` + `andReturn().getResponse()` boilerplate by integrating directly with AssertJ's fluent chain; however, `MockMvcTester` requires Spring Boot 3.4+ and AssertJ 3.26+, so projects on older Spring Boot versions must continue using `MockMvc` with `andExpect`, and the two APIs cannot be mixed — migrating partially within a module produces confusing test failures when `MockMvcTester` and `MockMvc` both try to autowire from the same `AutoConfigureMockMvc`-provided infrastructure bean. [official]

**Pattern 392** — `@MockitoBean` / `@MockitoSpyBean` as Replacement for `@MockBean` / `@SpyBean`
```java
@SpringBootTest
class PaymentServiceIntegrationTest {

    // Spring Boot 3.4+: use @MockitoBean instead of @MockBean
    @MockitoBean
    private PaymentGatewayClient gatewayClient;

    // Spring Boot 3.4+: use @MockitoSpyBean instead of @SpyBean
    @MockitoSpyBean
    private AuditLogger auditLogger;

    @Autowired
    private PaymentService paymentService;

    @Test
    void processPayment_delegatesToGatewayAndAudits() {
        PaymentRequest req = new PaymentRequest("tok_visa", 5000L, "USD");
        given(gatewayClient.charge(req))
            .willReturn(new ChargeResult("ch_001", "succeeded"));

        PaymentResult result = paymentService.process(req);

        assertThat(result.getStatus()).isEqualTo("succeeded");
        // Spy captures real call + allows verification
        then(auditLogger).should().log(eq("PAYMENT_PROCESSED"), argThat(
            ctx -> "ch_001".equals(ctx.getChargeId())
        ));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@MockitoBean` and `@MockitoSpyBean` (Spring Boot 3.4) replace the deprecated `@MockBean`/`@SpyBean` and avoid the `spring-boot-test` dependency on the internal `MockitoPostProcessor`; they use Mockito's own `MockitoSession` lifecycle rather than Spring's `ResetMocksTestExecutionListener`, which means mock state is reset between tests at the Mockito layer rather than the Spring layer — this is faster but means that a test that forgets `@DirtiesContext` can see cross-test mock state leakage if a `@MockitoSpyBean` interaction from a previous test influences `ApplicationContext` bean state (e.g., a spy on a `@Cacheable` service that was called in test N may deliver the cached result in test N+1 before the spy resets). [official]

**Pattern 393** — JUnit 5 `@TempDir` with `CleanupMode.NEVER` for Post-Failure Artifact Inspection
```java
@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class ReportGeneratorTest {

    @TempDir(cleanup = CleanupMode.NEVER)
    private Path reportDir;   // directory survives the test run for manual inspection

    private ReportGenerator generator = new ReportGenerator();

    @Test
    void generatePdfReport_createsValidPdfFile() throws Exception {
        ReportRequest req = ReportRequest.builder()
            .title("Q1 Summary")
            .dataSource(List.of(new Row("Jan", 1200), new Row("Feb", 980)))
            .outputDir(reportDir)
            .build();

        Path generated = generator.generate(req);

        assertThat(generated)
            .exists()
            .hasExtension("pdf")
            .satisfies(p -> assertThat(Files.size(p)).isGreaterThan(1024L));

        // If the test fails, reportDir is retained at its printed path:
        System.out.println("Report artifacts at: " + reportDir.toAbsolutePath());
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `CleanupMode.NEVER` (JUnit 5.9+) retains temp directories unconditionally — including on test success — so CI runners accumulate orphaned directories across builds; use `CleanupMode.ON_SUCCESS` to retain directories only on failure, which keeps CI clean while still preserving diagnostic artifacts exactly when they are needed; `CleanupMode.ON_SUCCESS` requires JUnit 5.10+ and the distinction is not obvious from the enum name (it deletes on success, retains on failure), leading developers to accidentally configure `NEVER` where `ON_SUCCESS` was intended. [official]

**Pattern 394** — Mockito `ArgumentCaptor` Multi-Invocation Capture with `@Captor`
```java
@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class OrderEventPublisherTest {

    @Mock
    private EventBus eventBus;

    @Captor
    private ArgumentCaptor<OrderEvent> eventCaptor;

    @InjectMocks
    private OrderEventPublisher publisher;

    @Test
    void publishLifecycleEvents_emitsCreatedThenShippedInOrder() {
        Order order = new Order("ORD-42", OrderStatus.PENDING);

        publisher.publishLifecycle(order, List.of(
            OrderStatus.CONFIRMED, OrderStatus.SHIPPED));

        verify(eventBus, times(3)).publish(eventCaptor.capture()); // PENDING → CONFIRMED → SHIPPED

        List<OrderEvent> events = eventCaptor.getAllValues();
        assertThat(events).extracting(OrderEvent::getStatus)
            .containsExactly(
                OrderStatus.PENDING,
                OrderStatus.CONFIRMED,
                OrderStatus.SHIPPED);
        assertThat(events).allMatch(e -> "ORD-42".equals(e.getOrderId()));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `ArgumentCaptor.getAllValues()` returns a live list that accumulates across all matching `verify()` calls on the same captor — if the same `@Captor` field is reused across multiple `@Test` methods without `MockitoExtension` resetting it (which the extension does automatically via `MockitoSession`), stale values from a previous test bleed into the next; when sharing a captor in a `@BeforeEach`-initialized helper class that is not a proper Mockito extension, you must call `captor = ArgumentCaptor.forClass(OrderEvent.class)` inside `@BeforeEach` rather than reusing the field-level instance to avoid cross-test capture accumulation. [official]

**Pattern 395** — AssertJ `usingComparatorForType` in Recursive Comparison for Custom Equality
```java
class InvoiceComparisonTest {

    @Test
    void compareInvoices_toleratesMonetaryRounding_andIgnoresAuditFields() {
        Invoice actual = invoiceService.generate(order);
        Invoice expected = Invoice.builder()
            .orderId("ORD-100")
            .subtotal(new BigDecimal("99.99"))
            .tax(new BigDecimal("10.00"))
            .total(new BigDecimal("109.99"))
            .lineItems(List.of(
                new LineItem("SKU-A", 2, new BigDecimal("49.995"))))
            .build();

        assertThat(actual)
            .usingRecursiveComparison()
            .ignoringFields("createdAt", "updatedAt", "invoiceId") // audit fields
            .usingComparatorForType(
                (a, b) -> a.subtract(b).abs().compareTo(new BigDecimal("0.01")) <= 0 ? 0 : a.compareTo(b),
                BigDecimal.class)                                  // ±0.01 monetary tolerance
            .isEqualTo(expected);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `usingComparatorForType` applies the custom comparator to every field of the given type throughout the entire object graph, including nested collections — this is convenient for `BigDecimal` rounding tolerance but dangerous for `String` fields where accidental near-equality (e.g., case-insensitive comparator) would mask genuine mismatches; prefer `usingComparatorForFields` to scope the custom comparator to specific field paths rather than all fields of a type, reserving `usingComparatorForType` only for truly type-wide semantic equality like monetary tolerance or timestamp approximation. [official]

**Pattern 396** — JUnit 5 `@EnabledIfEnvironmentVariable` + `@DisabledIfSystemProperty` Conditional Execution
```java
// Run only when INTEGRATION_TESTS=true env var is set (e.g., CI pipeline stage)
@Target({ElementType.TYPE, ElementType.METHOD})
@Retention(RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME)
@EnabledIfEnvironmentVariable(named = "INTEGRATION_TESTS", matches = "true")
public @interface IntegrationTest {}

@IntegrationTest
@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = SpringBootTest.WebEnvironment.RANDOM_PORT)
class ExternalPaymentGatewayIT {

    @LocalServerPort
    private int port;

    @Autowired
    private TestRestTemplate restTemplate;

    @Test
    @DisabledIfSystemProperty(named = "skip.payment.tests", matches = "true")
    void chargeEndpoint_returnsSucceeded_againstSandbox() {
        ChargeRequest req = new ChargeRequest("tok_visa_sandbox", 1000L, "USD");

        ResponseEntity<ChargeResult> resp = restTemplate.postForEntity(
            "http://localhost:" + port + "/charges", req, ChargeResult.class);

        assertThat(resp.getStatusCode()).isEqualTo(HttpStatus.OK);
        assertThat(resp.getBody()).isNotNull()
            .extracting(ChargeResult::getStatus)
            .isEqualTo("succeeded");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@EnabledIfEnvironmentVariable` and `@DisabledIfSystemProperty` skip tests at the JUnit launcher level (the test is reported as `SKIPPED`, not as a failure), which means CI pipelines that check for zero skipped tests will flag these as unexpected skips; use a JUnit tag (`@Tag("integration")`) with Gradle `test { useJUnitPlatform { includeTags "integration" } }` filter instead for CI-controlled inclusion, reserving `@EnabledIfEnvironmentVariable` for developer-machine gating where env variable presence is a natural signal (e.g., a secret API key being set). [official]

**Pattern 397** — Testcontainers `Network.newNetwork()` for Multi-Container Integration with Explicit Aliases
```java
@Testcontainers
class OrderPipelineIntegrationTest {

    static final Network PIPELINE_NETWORK = Network.newNetwork();

    @Container
    static final PostgreSQLContainer<?> POSTGRES = new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine")
        .withNetwork(PIPELINE_NETWORK)
        .withNetworkAliases("postgres");

    @Container
    static final GenericContainer<?> ORDER_PROCESSOR = new GenericContainer<>("myapp/order-processor:latest")
        .withNetwork(PIPELINE_NETWORK)
        .withEnv("DB_URL", "jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/test") // resolves via alias
        .withEnv("DB_USER", POSTGRES.getUsername())
        .withEnv("DB_PASS", POSTGRES.getPassword())
        .waitingFor(Wait.forHttp("/actuator/health").forPort(8080))
        .dependsOn(POSTGRES);

    @Test
    void processOrder_persistsToDatabase() throws Exception {
        try (Connection conn = DriverManager.getConnection(
                POSTGRES.getJdbcUrl(), POSTGRES.getUsername(), POSTGRES.getPassword())) {
            // seed
            conn.createStatement().execute(
                "INSERT INTO orders VALUES ('ORD-1','PENDING',100)");
        }

        // trigger processing via the sidecar container's HTTP API
        HttpResponse<String> resp = HttpClient.newHttpClient().send(
            HttpRequest.newBuilder()
                .uri(URI.create("http://localhost:" + ORDER_PROCESSOR.getMappedPort(8080) + "/process/ORD-1"))
                .POST(BodyPublishers.noBody()).build(),
            BodyHandlers.ofString());

        assertThat(resp.statusCode()).isEqualTo(200);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `Network.newNetwork()` creates an isolated Docker bridge network scoped to the test class, preventing port conflicts with parallel test classes; however, the network object is a `@Container`-independent resource and is NOT automatically closed by `@Testcontainers` — it must be closed in a `@AfterAll` or declared as a `static final` field on a `@Container`-annotated holder class that implements `Closeable`, otherwise each test-class run leaks a Docker network, exhausting the Docker daemon's default limit of 30 custom bridge networks after repeated test runs in CI without Docker pruning. [official]

**Pattern 398** — Spring Boot `@JsonTest` + `JacksonTester` Bidirectional JSON Contract Testing
```java
@JsonTest
class OrderDtoJsonTest {

    @Autowired
    private JacksonTester<OrderDto> json;

    @Test
    void serialise_producesContractCompliantJson() throws IOException {
        OrderDto dto = new OrderDto(
            "ORD-007",
            OrderStatus.SHIPPED,
            BigDecimal.valueOf(149.99),
            Instant.parse("2025-11-01T09:00:00Z"));

        JsonContent<OrderDto> content = json.write(dto);

        assertThat(content).extractingJsonPathStringValue("$.orderId").isEqualTo("ORD-007");
        assertThat(content).extractingJsonPathStringValue("$.status").isEqualTo("SHIPPED");
        assertThat(content).extractingJsonPathNumberValue("$.totalAmount").isEqualTo(149.99);
        // ISO-8601 format enforced by @JsonFormat on the field
        assertThat(content).extractingJsonPathStringValue("$.createdAt")
            .startsWith("2025-11-01T09:00:00");
        assertThat(content).doesNotHaveJsonPath("$.internalAuditId"); // excluded from API
    }

    @Test
    void deserialise_parsesContractCompliantJson() throws IOException {
        String contractJson = """
            {"orderId":"ORD-007","status":"SHIPPED",
             "totalAmount":149.99,"createdAt":"2025-11-01T09:00:00Z"}
            """;

        OrderDto dto = json.parseObject(contractJson);

        assertThat(dto.getOrderId()).isEqualTo("ORD-007");
        assertThat(dto.getStatus()).isEqualTo(OrderStatus.SHIPPED);
        assertThat(dto.getTotalAmount()).isEqualByComparingTo("149.99");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@JsonTest` loads only Jackson auto-configuration (no `@Service` or `@Repository` beans), making it extremely fast — but it does NOT load `@JsonComponent` beans from sub-packages unless they are on the component-scan path, meaning a custom serialiser registered via `@JsonComponent` in a `com.example.serializers` sub-package will silently be absent, causing the serialisation test to pass with the default `toString()` representation while the production context uses the custom serialiser; always confirm that `@JsonComponent` classes reside in the same package tree as the `@SpringBootApplication` entry point or explicitly `@Import` them in the test class. [official]

**Pattern 399** — JUnit 5 `TestWatcher` Extension for Capturing Post-Failure Diagnostics
```java
public class DiagnosticsCapturingExtension
    implements TestWatcher, AfterEachCallback {

    private static final Path DIAGNOSTICS_DIR =
        Path.of(System.getProperty("diagnostics.dir", "build/test-diagnostics"));

    @Override
    public void testFailed(ExtensionContext ctx, Throwable cause) {
        try {
            Files.createDirectories(DIAGNOSTICS_DIR);
            String safeName = ctx.getDisplayName()
                .replaceAll("[^a-zA-Z0-9_\\-]", "_");
            Path report = DIAGNOSTICS_DIR.resolve(safeName + "-failure.txt");
            Files.writeString(report,
                "Test: " + ctx.getDisplayName() + "\n" +
                "Class: " + ctx.getRequiredTestClass().getName() + "\n" +
                "Cause: " + cause.getMessage() + "\n" +
                stackTraceOf(cause));
        } catch (IOException e) {
            // non-fatal: do not mask the original test failure
        }
    }

    private String stackTraceOf(Throwable t) {
        StringWriter sw = new StringWriter();
        t.printStackTrace(new PrintWriter(sw));
        return sw.toString();
    }

    @Override
    public void afterEach(ExtensionContext ctx) { /* no-op */ }
}

// Usage:
@ExtendWith(DiagnosticsCapturingExtension.class)
class CheckoutFlowTest { /* ... */ }
```
Tradeoff: `TestWatcher.testFailed` is invoked after all `@AfterEach` methods complete, meaning any cleanup performed by `@AfterEach` (e.g., closing a browser or rolling back a database transaction) has already occurred before the watcher runs — diagnostic artifacts that depend on live state (e.g., browser screenshot, current database rows) cannot be captured in a `TestWatcher` and must instead be collected inside `@AfterEach` or an `AfterEachCallback` extension that executes in `ExtensionContext` before other `@AfterEach` methods by using `@Order` on the extension registration. [official]

---

**Pattern 400** — Mockito `RETURNS_DEEP_STUBS` for Fluent Builder / Query Chain Mocking
```java
@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class QueryBuilderServiceTest {

    // Deep stubs allow chaining: criteria.where().and().orderBy().limit()
    @Mock(answer = Answers.RETURNS_DEEP_STUBS)
    private CriteriaBuilder cb;

    @Mock(answer = Answers.RETURNS_DEEP_STUBS)
    private EntityManager em;

    @InjectMocks
    private ProductSearchService searchService;

    @Test
    void search_appliesPriceRangeAndCategoryFilter() {
        // Deep stub: em.getCriteriaBuilder().createQuery() returns a CriteriaQuery mock
        // without configuring each intermediate call
        CriteriaQuery<Product> cq = mock(CriteriaQuery.class);
        given(em.getCriteriaBuilder().createQuery(Product.class)).willReturn(cq);
        given(cq.from(Product.class)).willReturn(mock(Root.class));

        TypedQuery<Product> typedQuery = mock(TypedQuery.class);
        given(em.createQuery(cq)).willReturn(typedQuery);
        given(typedQuery.getResultList()).willReturn(List.of(
            new Product("SKU-1", "Widget", BigDecimal.valueOf(9.99), "TOOLS")));

        List<Product> results = searchService.findByPriceAndCategory(
            BigDecimal.ZERO, BigDecimal.TEN, "TOOLS");

        assertThat(results).hasSize(1)
            .first().extracting(Product::getSku).isEqualTo("SKU-1");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `RETURNS_DEEP_STUBS` creates an implicit mock for every intermediate method call in a chain, making test setup concise for fluent APIs; however, deep stubs create unmocked inner mocks that Mockito does not report in `verifyNoMoreInteractions` checks, so unexpected method calls on intermediate chain objects are silently ignored rather than causing test failures — use `RETURNS_DEEP_STUBS` only when the intermediate objects are pure query/builder objects with no side-effect methods, and prefer explicit mocks for service objects that perform I/O to preserve the test's ability to detect accidental invocations. [official]

**Pattern 401** — AssertJ `filteredOn` + `extracting` Chained Iterable Assertions
```java
class InvoiceLineItemAssertionTest {

    @Test
    void invoice_containsCorrectDiscountedLineItems() {
        List<LineItem> items = invoiceService.computeLineItems(cart);

        // Assert count and values of discounted items only
        assertThat(items)
            .filteredOn(LineItem::isDiscounted)
            .hasSize(2)
            .extracting(LineItem::getSku, LineItem::getDiscountPercent)
            .containsExactlyInAnyOrder(
                tuple("SKU-A", 10),
                tuple("SKU-B", 15));

        // Assert no zero-quantity items survived
        assertThat(items)
            .filteredOn("quantity", not(0))
            .hasSameSizeAs(items); // all items should have quantity > 0

        // Assert total across premium items
        assertThat(items)
            .filteredOn(item -> item.getCategory() == Category.PREMIUM)
            .extracting(LineItem::getUnitPrice)
            .allMatch(price -> price.compareTo(BigDecimal.valueOf(50)) > 0);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `filteredOn(Predicate)` returns a new `AbstractListAssert` scoped to the filtered subset, enabling highly readable assertions; however, it creates an intermediate list via `StreamSupport.stream().filter().collect(toList())` on every call — for collections of tens of thousands of elements this is fast, but for entity graphs loaded eagerly from a database in a `@DataJpaTest`, the filtering triggers additional lazy-loading proxy initializations outside the Hibernate session (if the session is already closed), causing `LazyInitializationException`; always load test data inside the assertion lambda scope when the JPA session is active, or use `@Transactional` on the test method to keep the session open during assertion. [official]

**Pattern 402** — Spring Boot `@WebMvcTest` Structured Error Response Assertion with `MockMvcTester`
```java
@WebMvcTest(ProductController.class)
class ProductControllerErrorHandlingTest {

    @Autowired
    private MockMvcTester mvc;

    @MockitoBean
    private ProductService productService;

    @Test
    void createProduct_returns400WithValidationErrors_whenNameBlank() {
        String invalidJson = """
            {"name": "", "price": -1.00, "category": null}
            """;

        assertThat(mvc.post().uri("/products")
                .contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
                .content(invalidJson))
            .hasStatus(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST)
            .bodyJson()
            .satisfies(body -> {
                assertThat(body.extractingPath("$.errors").asList())
                    .hasSizeGreaterThanOrEqualTo(2);
                assertThat(body.extractingPath("$.errors[*].field").asList())
                    .contains("name", "price");
            });
    }

    @Test
    void getProduct_returns404_withRfcProblemDetail_whenNotFound() {
        given(productService.findById(999L))
            .willThrow(new ProductNotFoundException(999L));

        assertThat(mvc.get().uri("/products/999"))
            .hasStatus(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND)
            .bodyJson()
            .extractingPath("$.type").asString()
            .contains("product-not-found");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `MockMvcTester.bodyJson().extractingPath()` uses JsonPath under the hood and returns typed `AbstractStringAssert`, `AbstractIntegerAssert`, etc., based on the `asString()` / `asNumber()` cast — if the path resolves to a JSON array but the test calls `.asString()`, AssertJ throws `ClassCastException` with an unhelpful message about `net.minidev.json.JSONArray` rather than the JsonPath expression, making the assertion failure difficult to debug; always verify the JSON structure in a browser or with `System.out.println(response.getBody())` when writing a new `extractingPath` assertion, and prefer `.asList()` over `.asString()` for array nodes. [official]

**Pattern 403** — JUnit 5 `@MethodSource` Cross-Class Named Factory Method
```java
// Shared test data factory in a separate class
public class ShippingTestData {

    public static Stream<Arguments> validAddressVariants() {
        return Stream.of(
            Arguments.of("US", "90210", "Beverly Hills", true),
            Arguments.of("CA", "M5H 2N2", "Toronto",    true),
            Arguments.of("GB", "SW1A 1AA", "London",    true),
            Arguments.of("DE", "10115",   "Berlin",     true)
        );
    }

    public static Stream<Arguments> invalidAddressVariants() {
        return Stream.of(
            Arguments.of("US", "ABCDE",  "Nowhere",  false),
            Arguments.of("XX", "00000",  "Nowhere",  false)
        );
    }
}

// Consumer test class
class AddressValidatorTest {

    private final AddressValidator validator = new AddressValidator();

    @ParameterizedTest(name = "[{index}] country={0} postal={1}")
    @MethodSource("com.example.testdata.ShippingTestData#validAddressVariants")
    void validate_returnsTrue_forValidAddresses(
            String country, String postal, String city, boolean expected) {
        assertThat(validator.validate(new Address(country, postal, city)))
            .isEqualTo(expected);
    }

    @ParameterizedTest(name = "[{index}] country={0} postal={1}")
    @MethodSource("com.example.testdata.ShippingTestData#invalidAddressVariants")
    void validate_returnsFalse_forInvalidAddresses(
            String country, String postal, String city, boolean expected) {
        assertThat(validator.validate(new Address(country, postal, city)))
            .isEqualTo(expected);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: Cross-class `@MethodSource` with fully-qualified method references decouples test data from test logic and enables sharing across multiple test classes, but the factory class is resolved via reflection at test instantiation time — if the factory class is inside `src/test/java` but not on the test classpath of a specific Gradle sub-project that only adds the current module's test classes (via `testImplementation(project(":other-module").sourceSets.test.output)`), JUnit throws `PreconditionViolationException: Could not find factory method` at runtime rather than a compile error, making the missing classpath dependency invisible until CI runs the specific test class. [official]

**Pattern 404** — Testcontainers `withReuse(true)` for Local Development Speed
```java
// Container definition in a shared base class
public abstract class PostgresIntegrationBase {

    static final PostgreSQLContainer<?> POSTGRES;

    static {
        POSTGRES = new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine")
            .withDatabaseName("testdb")
            .withUsername("test")
            .withPassword("test")
            .withReuse(true);         // reuse running container between test runs
        POSTGRES.start();
    }

    @DynamicPropertySource
    static void configureProperties(DynamicPropertyRegistry registry) {
        registry.add("spring.datasource.url",     POSTGRES::getJdbcUrl);
        registry.add("spring.datasource.username", POSTGRES::getUsername);
        registry.add("spring.datasource.password", POSTGRES::getPassword);
    }
}

// Subclass simply extends:
@DataJpaTest
@AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = NONE)
class OrderRepositoryTest extends PostgresIntegrationBase {

    @Autowired
    private OrderRepository orderRepo;

    @Test
    @Transactional
    void save_andFindById_roundTrips() {
        Order saved = orderRepo.save(new Order(null, "ORD-X", OrderStatus.PENDING));
        assertThat(orderRepo.findById(saved.getId()))
            .isPresent()
            .get().extracting(Order::getReference).isEqualTo("ORD-X");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `withReuse(true)` requires `testcontainers.reuse.enable=true` in `~/.testcontainers.properties` on each developer machine — it is a per-developer opt-in, not a project-wide setting — so tests that rely on `withReuse(true)` for correctness (e.g., assuming a container is pre-warmed with seed data from a previous run) will fail on a fresh CI agent where the property is absent; use `withReuse(true)` strictly as a speed optimisation and ensure each test class seeds its own data in `@BeforeAll` (with an idempotent `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`) so tests are correct both with and without an already-running container. [official]

**Pattern 405** — Awaitility `await().during()` Negative Assertion (Condition Must Never Become True)
```java
class CircuitBreakerStabilityTest {

    private final CircuitBreaker breaker = CircuitBreaker.create("payment",
        CircuitBreakerConfig.custom()
            .slidingWindowSize(5)
            .failureRateThreshold(60)
            .build());

    @Test
    void circuitBreaker_remainsClosed_whenFailureRateBelowThreshold() {
        // Simulate 2/5 failures (40% — below 60% threshold)
        for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
            final int attempt = i;
            breaker.executeRunnable(() -> {
                if (attempt % 3 == 0) throw new RuntimeException("simulated failure");
            });
        }

        // Assert that the breaker NEVER opens during a 2-second observation window
        await()
            .during(Duration.ofSeconds(2))
            .atMost(Duration.ofSeconds(3))
            .pollInterval(Duration.ofMillis(100))
            .failFast("Circuit breaker opened unexpectedly",
                () -> breaker.getState() == CircuitBreaker.State.OPEN)
            .untilAsserted(() ->
                assertThat(breaker.getState()).isEqualTo(CircuitBreaker.State.CLOSED));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `await().during(D).atMost(D + epsilon)` combined with `untilAsserted` polls the condition for the full `during` duration and passes only if the assertion holds on every poll — this is the intended pattern for "never-true" assertions; however, `during()` without `atMost()` greater than `during()` causes Awaitility to throw `ConditionTimeoutException` on the very first poll because the total allowed time equals the required stable time with zero margin, making the test always fail regardless of the system's actual behavior — always set `atMost` to at least `during + 1 poll interval` to give Awaitility room to evaluate the full observation window. [official]

### Community Gotchas

**G46** — `@MockitoSpyBean` Does Not Reset Call History Between Tests
Why this matters: Unlike `@MockitoBean`, which provides a fresh mock for each test method (Mockito resets interactions via `MockitoSession.finishMocking()`), `@MockitoSpyBean` wraps a real Spring bean with a spy. The Spring context is cached between tests for performance, and the spy wrapper is applied once at context creation time. Mockito's `MockitoSession` resets stub configurations between tests, but it does NOT clear the invocation history recorded by the spy — `then(spyBean).should().someMethod()` verification counts accumulated calls from ALL previous test methods in the same context cache, not just the current test. This causes flaky verification failures that depend on test execution order. [official]
Fix: Explicitly reset the spy's interaction history in `@BeforeEach` using `Mockito.clearInvocations(spyBean)`, or use `@DirtiesContext(methodMode = BEFORE_METHOD)` to force a fresh context (at the cost of context startup time). For `@MockitoSpyBean` on high-frequency beans like `ApplicationEventPublisher`, prefer `@MockitoBean` with a custom `@TestConfiguration` that delegates to the real bean for most methods via `willCallRealMethod()` rather than using a spy, to avoid the accumulated-interaction problem entirely. [official]

**G47** — JUnit 5 `@TempDir` Declared as `static` Field Shares One Directory Across All Test Methods
Why this matters: JUnit 5 creates a new temporary directory for each `@TempDir` injection point. When `@TempDir` is declared on an instance field (non-static), each test method receives a fresh directory. When declared as a `static` field, JUnit creates one shared directory for the entire test class lifecycle — all test methods write into the same directory, and files created by one test method are visible to subsequent test methods. If two tests write a file with the same name (e.g., `output.csv`), the second test silently overwrites the first test's artifact, and any `@AfterAll` cleanup that counts files or inspects directory contents sees the merged state, producing false assertions about file isolation. [official]
Fix: Declare `@TempDir` on instance fields (not `static`) when each test method must be isolated. Use a `static @TempDir` only when tests intentionally build on each other's file system output (a rare pattern, usually a sign of poor test design). If a shared base directory is required for test-class-level setup, create a subdirectory per test method using `Files.createTempDirectory(sharedTempDir, testInfo.getDisplayName())` injected via `TestInfo`. [official]

**G48** — Testcontainers `withReuse(true)` Leaves Containers Running When Ryuk Is Disabled
Why this matters: Testcontainers' Ryuk side-car container is the process that terminates containers after the JVM exits — it subscribes to container labels and sends `docker rm -f` when the test JVM shuts down. When `withReuse(true)` is set, containers are intentionally not registered with Ryuk for termination (so they survive for the next test run). However, if Ryuk is disabled via `TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED=true` (common in some CI environments that prohibit privileged containers), ALL containers — including those without `withReuse(true)` — survive JVM exit. Combining `withReuse(true)` and disabled Ryuk means containers accumulate across CI pipeline runs indefinitely, eventually exhausting Docker's per-host container limit and causing `docker: error response from daemon: conflict` errors in unrelated pipelines. [official]
Fix: Never set `TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED=true` in production CI; instead, run Ryuk as a non-privileged sidecar by setting `TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_PRIVILEGED=false`. When Ryuk truly cannot run, implement a `@AfterAll static void stopContainer()` that calls `container.stop()` explicitly, and document that `withReuse(true)` must not be used in that environment. [official]

**G49** — AssertJ `usingRecursiveComparison().withStrictTypeChecking()` Fails on `ArrayList` vs `LinkedList`
Why this matters: By default, AssertJ's recursive comparison is type-flexible: it compares fields structurally regardless of the concrete collection implementation. When `withStrictTypeChecking()` is enabled (often added to prevent false positives where a `HashMap` is compared to a `TreeMap`), AssertJ requires that corresponding fields have exactly the same declared type. A service that returns `List<Item>` backed by `Collections.unmodifiableList(new ArrayList<>(...))` will fail comparison against an expected `List<Item>` backed by `new LinkedList<>()` — even when both lists contain identical elements in the same order — because `java.util.Collections$UnmodifiableRandomAccessList` != `java.util.LinkedList`. This causes spurious test failures when the implementation changes from `ArrayList` to an unmodifiable wrapper without changing observable behavior. [official]
Fix: Use `withStrictTypeChecking()` only when concrete implementation types are semantically significant (e.g., comparing `TreeMap` vs `HashMap` where iteration order matters). For general domain-object comparison, omit `withStrictTypeChecking()` and instead use `usingRecursiveComparison().ignoringCollectionOrder()` (when order is irrelevant) or the default structural comparison. When you need to assert the concrete type separately, chain a distinct `assertThat(result).isInstanceOf(ArrayList.class)` rather than baking the type requirement into the recursive comparison. [official]

**G50** — Spring `@WebMvcTest` Does Not Activate `@ControllerAdvice` from Outside the Slice Package
Why this matters: `@WebMvcTest` loads only `@Controller`, `@ControllerAdvice`, `Filter`, `WebMvcConfigurer`, and `HandlerInterceptor` beans that are part of the auto-scanned slice. When a `@ControllerAdvice` class (e.g., `GlobalExceptionHandler`) resides in a different sub-package than the controller under test — for example, the controller is in `com.example.orders.web` and the advice is in `com.example.shared.web` — the advice class may not be scanned by the slice's component scan, which is bounded to the controller's package tree. The test then exercises the controller without the advice, causing exception-response assertions (e.g., asserting a 400 with a structured error body) to return 500 or a default error response instead, producing misleading test failures that do not reproduce in production. [official]
Fix: Explicitly import the `@ControllerAdvice` class using `@Import(GlobalExceptionHandler.class)` on the test class, or use a shared `@Configuration` class annotated with `@ControllerAdvice` and place it under the `@SpringBootApplication` root package so all slices can scan it. Alternatively, annotate the advice with `@Order(Ordered.HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE)` — while this does not affect scan discovery, it ensures consistent advice ordering once the advice is imported, avoiding non-deterministic exception-handler resolution when multiple advice classes are in scope. [official]
