## Cycle 67 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 421** — JUnit 5 `@Execution(CONCURRENT)` with `@ResourceLock` for shared state isolation in parallel test suites
```java
@TestMethodOrder(MethodOrderer.Random.class)
@Execution(ExecutionMode.CONCURRENT)
class ParallelInventoryServiceTest {

    // Tests that read the shared counter may run concurrently with each other
    @Test
    @ResourceLock(value = "inventoryCounter", mode = ResourceAccessMode.READ)
    void queryAvailableStock_returnsNonNegativeCount() {
        long available = inventoryService.countAvailable("SKU-001");
        assertThat(available).isGreaterThanOrEqualTo(0L);
    }

    // Tests that mutate the counter must acquire an exclusive write lock
    @Test
    @ResourceLock(value = "inventoryCounter", mode = ResourceAccessMode.READ_WRITE)
    void reserveStock_decrementsByRequestedQuantity() {
        long before = inventoryService.countAvailable("SKU-001");
        inventoryService.reserve("SKU-001", 3);
        assertThat(inventoryService.countAvailable("SKU-001")).isEqualTo(before - 3);
    }

    // Tests that are inherently non-thread-safe opt back to serial execution
    @Test
    @Execution(ExecutionMode.SAME_THREAD)
    void bulkRestock_requiresSerialExecution() {
        inventoryService.bulkRestock(Map.of("SKU-001", 100, "SKU-002", 50));
        assertThat(inventoryService.countAvailable("SKU-001")).isGreaterThanOrEqualTo(100L);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `READ` vs `READ_WRITE` lock granularity controls parallelism precisely — using `READ_WRITE` on every method degrades throughput to serial execution as effectively as disabling `CONCURRENT` entirely, but using `READ` on a mutating test allows data races that surface only intermittently in CI; `@Execution(SAME_THREAD)` on a single outlier test preserves parallelism for the rest of the class without requiring the entire class to revert to `SAME_THREAD`, but the outlier's isolation is invisible to callers who grep for `@Execution` and find only the class-level `CONCURRENT` annotation. [official]

**Pattern 422** — Mockito `ArgumentCaptor` with `getAllValues()` for multi-invocation event capture and ordered assertion
```java
@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class OrderLifecyclePublisherTest {

    @Mock
    private DomainEventBus eventBus;

    @InjectMocks
    private OrderLifecycleService service;

    @Test
    void fulfillOrder_publishesThreeEventsInSequence() {
        ArgumentCaptor<DomainEvent> captor = ArgumentCaptor.forClass(DomainEvent.class);

        service.fulfill(new FulfillRequest("ORD-001", "WH-EAST", "CARRIER-DHL"));

        verify(eventBus, times(3)).publish(captor.capture());
        List<DomainEvent> published = captor.getAllValues();

        assertThat(published).hasSize(3);
        assertThat(published.get(0)).isInstanceOf(OrderPickedEvent.class);
        assertThat(published.get(1)).isInstanceOf(OrderPackedEvent.class);
        assertThat(published.get(2))
            .isInstanceOf(OrderShippedEvent.class)
            .satisfies(e -> assertThat(((OrderShippedEvent) e).getCarrier())
                .isEqualTo("CARRIER-DHL"));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `getAllValues()` captures all invocations in call order, enabling sequence assertions that a single `ArgumentCaptor.getValue()` call cannot provide; the caveat is that `verify(eventBus, times(3)).publish(captor.capture())` fails with a `WantedButNotInvoked` or `TooManyActualInvocations` exception if the count is wrong before the captor is even accessed — so the count check is coupled to the captor in a single line, which is useful for diagnostics but makes it impossible to independently assert on "at least these events were published" without also constraining the total count. [official]

**Pattern 423** — Spring Boot `@WebMvcTest` with `MockMvcResultMatchers.jsonPath` and `@JsonTest` for JSON contract validation
```java
@WebMvcTest(ProductController.class)
class ProductControllerJsonTest {

    @Autowired
    private MockMvc mockMvc;

    @MockBean
    private ProductService productService;

    @Test
    void getProduct_serialisesAllFieldsCorrectly() throws Exception {
        Product product = Product.builder()
            .id("PROD-001")
            .name("Ergonomic Chair")
            .price(new BigDecimal("299.99"))
            .available(true)
            .tags(List.of("furniture", "office"))
            .build();
        given(productService.findById("PROD-001")).willReturn(Optional.of(product));

        mockMvc.perform(get("/api/products/PROD-001")
                .accept(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON))
            .andExpect(status().isOk())
            .andExpect(jsonPath("$.id").value("PROD-001"))
            .andExpect(jsonPath("$.name").value("Ergonomic Chair"))
            .andExpect(jsonPath("$.price").value(299.99))
            .andExpect(jsonPath("$.available").value(true))
            .andExpect(jsonPath("$.tags").isArray())
            .andExpect(jsonPath("$.tags", hasSize(2)))
            .andExpect(jsonPath("$.tags[0]").value("furniture"))
            .andExpect(content().contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `jsonPath` assertions verify the exact JSON wire format (field names, types, array shapes) that `@ResponseBody` serializes, catching `@JsonProperty` renaming regressions that typed `isEqualTo(product)` assertions miss entirely; the downside is that `jsonPath("$.price").value(299.99)` compares against a `Double`, so if the controller serializes `BigDecimal` with trailing zeros (`299.990`), the floating-point comparison passes vacuously — for financial APIs, assert with `jsonPath("$.price", is("299.99"))` using a string matcher after configuring `ObjectMapper` with `WRITE_BIGDECIMAL_AS_PLAIN`. [official]

**Pattern 424** — Testcontainers `@ServiceConnection` with Spring Boot 3.1+ for zero-config container property binding
```java
@SpringBootTest
@Testcontainers
class OrderRepositoryServiceConnectionIT {

    // @ServiceConnection reads the container type and automatically sets
    // spring.datasource.url, spring.datasource.username, spring.datasource.password
    // — no @DynamicPropertySource method required
    @Container
    @ServiceConnection
    static final PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres =
        new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine");

    @Container
    @ServiceConnection
    static final RedisContainer redis = new RedisContainer("redis:7-alpine");

    @Autowired
    private OrderRepository orderRepository;

    @Test
    void saveAndFind_roundTripsOrderThroughDatabase() {
        Order saved = orderRepository.save(
            new Order("customer-7", "SKU-X", BigDecimal.valueOf(49.95)));

        Order found = orderRepository.findById(saved.getId()).orElseThrow();

        assertThat(found.getCustomerId()).isEqualTo("customer-7");
        assertThat(found.getTotalAmount()).isEqualByComparingTo(BigDecimal.valueOf(49.95));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@ServiceConnection` eliminates the `@DynamicPropertySource` boilerplate by relying on a `ConnectionDetailsFactory` SPI that maps container types to Spring property prefixes, removing three lines of property registration per container and making the test class match its intent without ceremony; the limitation is that `@ServiceConnection` only works for container types that have a registered `ConnectionDetailsFactory` in `spring-boot-testcontainers` — custom or third-party containers (e.g., a proprietary message broker) require a fallback `@DynamicPropertySource` block, and mixing both approaches in a single test class creates two property-injection paths that are easy to confuse when debugging connection failures. [official]

**Pattern 425** — AssertJ `satisfiesExactlyInAnyOrder` for unordered element-by-element assertion with per-element conditions
```java
@Test
void processPaymentBatch_returnsOneResultPerInput_withCorrectStatuses() {
    List<PaymentRequest> requests = List.of(
        new PaymentRequest("REQ-1", "card_valid", 1000L),
        new PaymentRequest("REQ-2", "card_declined", 500L),
        new PaymentRequest("REQ-3", "card_valid", 2000L)
    );

    List<PaymentResult> results = paymentBatchProcessor.process(requests);

    // Order of results is non-deterministic (async processing),
    // but we can assert one Consumer per element regardless of order
    assertThat(results)
        .satisfiesExactlyInAnyOrder(
            r -> {
                assertThat(r.getRequestId()).isEqualTo("REQ-1");
                assertThat(r.getStatus()).isEqualTo(PaymentStatus.SUCCESS);
            },
            r -> {
                assertThat(r.getRequestId()).isEqualTo("REQ-2");
                assertThat(r.getStatus()).isEqualTo(PaymentStatus.DECLINED);
                assertThat(r.getDeclineCode()).isEqualTo("insufficient_funds");
            },
            r -> {
                assertThat(r.getRequestId()).isEqualTo("REQ-3");
                assertThat(r.getStatus()).isEqualTo(PaymentStatus.SUCCESS);
            }
        );
}
```
Tradeoff: `satisfiesExactlyInAnyOrder` performs bipartite matching between consumers and elements, so each consumer is applied to exactly one element and every element must be covered — this is stronger than `allSatisfy` (which applies all consumers to all elements) and stronger than `containsExactlyInAnyOrder` (which only checks identity); the computational cost is `O(n!)` in the worst case for the matching algorithm when all consumers are equally applicable to all elements, but AssertJ uses a greedy short-circuit approach that is `O(n^2)` for typical cases — for batches larger than 50 elements, extract matching by ID first and assert sequentially to avoid the polynomial matching overhead. [official]

**Pattern 426** — JUnit 5 `@RegisterExtension` with `ParameterResolver` for injecting typed test fixtures
```java
// Extension that creates a unique transactional boundary per test and
// injects the connection as a typed parameter
class TransactionScopeExtension
    implements BeforeEachCallback, AfterEachCallback, ParameterResolver {

    @Override
    public boolean supportsParameter(ParameterContext paramCtx,
                                     ExtensionContext extCtx) {
        return paramCtx.getParameter().getType() == TestTransaction.class;
    }

    @Override
    public Object resolveParameter(ParameterContext paramCtx,
                                   ExtensionContext extCtx) {
        TestTransaction txn = TestTransaction.begin();
        extCtx.getStore(Namespace.create(getClass(), extCtx.getUniqueId()))
              .put("txn", txn);
        return txn;
    }

    @Override
    public void afterEach(ExtensionContext context) {
        TestTransaction txn = context
            .getStore(Namespace.create(getClass(), context.getUniqueId()))
            .remove("txn", TestTransaction.class);
        if (txn != null) txn.rollback();
    }
}

class OrderPersistenceTest {

    @RegisterExtension
    TransactionScopeExtension txnScope = new TransactionScopeExtension();

    @Test
    void save_withTransaction_isVisibleInsideSameTxn(TestTransaction txn) {
        txn.execute(() -> orderRepository.save(new Order("ORD-TEST", "c1")));
        assertThat(txn.query("SELECT id FROM orders WHERE id = 'ORD-TEST'"))
            .hasSize(1);
        // rollback happens in afterEach — DB is clean for next test
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@RegisterExtension` with `ParameterResolver` injects the fixture as a method parameter rather than a field, which makes the dependency explicit in the method signature and enables different tests in the same class to use different fixture configurations by overloading the extension; the tradeoff is that method-parameter injection via `ParameterResolver` is invoked after `BeforeEachCallback`, meaning the resolved parameter value is available only within the test method body and cannot be referenced from within `@BeforeEach` setup methods — fixture initialization that must happen before `@BeforeEach` code must use `BeforeEachCallback.beforeEach()` on the extension instead. [official]

**Pattern 427** — WireMock scenario-based stateful stub sequencing for retry and idempotency testing
```java
@RegisterExtension
static WireMockExtension wm = WireMockExtension.newInstance()
    .options(wireMockConfig().dynamicPort())
    .build();

@Test
void submitOrder_retriesOnServerError_andSucceedsOnThirdAttempt() {
    wm.stubFor(post(urlEqualTo("/api/orders"))
        .inScenario("order-submit")
        .whenScenarioStateIs(STARTED)
        .willSetStateTo("first-retry")
        .willReturn(serverError()));

    wm.stubFor(post(urlEqualTo("/api/orders"))
        .inScenario("order-submit")
        .whenScenarioStateIs("first-retry")
        .willSetStateTo("second-retry")
        .willReturn(serverError()));

    wm.stubFor(post(urlEqualTo("/api/orders"))
        .inScenario("order-submit")
        .whenScenarioStateIs("second-retry")
        .willSetStateTo("succeeded")
        .willReturn(okJson("{\"orderId\":\"ORD-999\",\"status\":\"ACCEPTED\"}")));

    OrderResult result = orderClient.submit(new OrderRequest("customer-1", "SKU-A", 2));

    assertThat(result.getOrderId()).isEqualTo("ORD-999");
    assertThat(result.getStatus()).isEqualTo("ACCEPTED");
    wm.verify(3, postRequestedFor(urlEqualTo("/api/orders")));
}
```
Tradeoff: WireMock scenario state transitions model exactly the server-side state that triggers retry behavior, enabling deterministic regression tests for exponential-backoff and idempotency logic; the maintenance overhead is that scenario names are untyped strings and the state machine is spread across multiple `stubFor` calls with no compile-time validation — a typo in a state name (e.g., `"second-rety"` vs `"second-retry"`) causes the stub sequence to short-circuit silently, with WireMock returning its fallback `404` response rather than advancing the scenario, and `wm.verify(3, ...)` then fails with a count error that misleads the developer into thinking the retry count is wrong rather than the state machine is broken. [official]

**Pattern 428** — Spring Boot `@DataJpaTest` with `AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = NONE)` and Testcontainers for dialect-accurate tests
```java
@DataJpaTest
@AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = AutoConfigureTestDatabase.Replace.NONE)
@Testcontainers
class ProductRepositoryDialectTest {

    @Container
    @ServiceConnection
    static final PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres =
        new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine");

    @Autowired
    private ProductRepository productRepository;

    @Test
    void findByNameContainingIgnoreCase_usesPostgresIlikeOperator() {
        productRepository.saveAll(List.of(
            new Product("Ergonomic Chair", new BigDecimal("299.99")),
            new Product("Standing Desk", new BigDecimal("499.99")),
            new Product("ergonomic mouse", new BigDecimal("79.99"))
        ));

        List<Product> matches = productRepository
            .findByNameContainingIgnoreCase("ergonomic");

        assertThat(matches)
            .hasSize(2)
            .extracting(Product::getName)
            .containsExactlyInAnyOrder("Ergonomic Chair", "ergonomic mouse");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `replace = NONE` preserves the configured `DataSource` so `@ServiceConnection` can inject the real Postgres URL, enabling tests to exercise Postgres-specific behavior like `ILIKE`, `JSONB` operators, and sequence behavior that H2's compatibility mode does not faithfully replicate; the cost is that `@DataJpaTest` no longer applies its default in-memory H2 replacement, so every `@DataJpaTest` class that uses `replace = NONE` requires a running container, increasing per-class startup time from ~0.3s (H2) to ~3s (Postgres) — gate `replace = NONE` tests with a Maven profile or JUnit `@Tag("integration")` to allow fast H2-backed unit runs during development and Postgres-backed runs in CI. [official]

**Pattern 429** — AssertJ `usingRecursiveComparison().ignoringFields()` for domain object partial equality in update scenarios
```java
@Test
void updateProduct_preservesUnchangedFieldsAndUpdatesOnlySpecified() {
    Product existing = productRepository.findById("PROD-001").orElseThrow();

    UpdateProductRequest request = new UpdateProductRequest("PROD-001",
        "Updated Chair Name", null, null); // only name change

    Product updated = productService.update(request);

    assertThat(updated)
        .usingRecursiveComparison()
        .ignoringFields("name", "updatedAt", "version")
        .isEqualTo(existing);  // all other fields must be identical to existing

    assertThat(updated.getName()).isEqualTo("Updated Chair Name");
    assertThat(updated.getUpdatedAt()).isAfter(existing.getUpdatedAt());
}
```
Tradeoff: `ignoringFields("name", "updatedAt", "version")` allows a precise assertion that "everything except the explicitly changed fields stayed the same," which catches accidental field-clearing bugs that a field-by-field `isEqualTo` on every unchanged field would detect only if all those fields are explicitly asserted; the risk is that field names are untyped strings — if the `Product` class renames `updatedAt` to `lastModifiedAt`, the assertion silently starts including the old field name in the comparison (treating it as a structural field that both objects have as `null`) and failing on a false positive, rather than the test failing with a compile error or an informative `"field not found"` warning. [official]

**Pattern 430** — ArchUnit `noClasses().that().areAnnotatedWith()` to forbid deprecated API usage across modules
```java
@AnalyzeClasses(packages = "com.example", importOptions = ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests.class)
class DeprecatedApiEnforcementTest {

    @ArchTest
    static final ArchRule no_production_class_may_use_deprecated_http_client =
        noClasses()
            .should().callMethodWhere(
                JavaCall.Predicates.target(
                    HasName.Predicates.name("execute")
                    .and(JavaMember.Predicates.declaredIn(
                        JavaClass.Predicates.assignableTo(
                            org.apache.http.client.HttpClient.class))))
            )
            .because("Use Spring's RestClient or WebClient instead of deprecated Apache HttpClient");

    @ArchTest
    static final ArchRule no_class_may_extend_deprecated_base_service =
        noClasses()
            .that().resideInAPackage("com.example..")
            .should().beAssignableTo(LegacyBaseService.class)
            .because("LegacyBaseService is deprecated; extend AbstractService instead");

    @ArchTest
    static final ArchRule repository_classes_must_reside_in_repository_package =
        classes()
            .that().areAnnotatedWith(Repository.class)
            .should().resideInAPackage("com.example..repository..")
            .because("Repository classes must be in the repository package for discoverability");
}
```
Tradeoff: ArchUnit rules enforced via `@ArchTest` run during the test phase and fail the build at the same time as unit tests, providing immediate feedback to developers before code reaches CI review stages; the limitation is that ArchUnit analyzes bytecode-level class files and cannot catch reflection-based usages of deprecated APIs (`Class.forName("org.apache.http.client.DefaultHttpClient")`) — reflection-driven adapter patterns that bridge to deprecated APIs will pass ArchUnit checks while still violating the migration intent, requiring additional runtime detection (e.g., deprecation warnings in logs) to surface. [official]

**Pattern 431** — Mockito `doAnswer` with `InvocationOnMock` for stateful stub side-effect simulation
```java
@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class ShoppingCartServiceTest {

    @Mock
    private CartRepository cartRepository;

    @InjectMocks
    private ShoppingCartService cartService;

    @Test
    void addItem_updatesCartAndReturnsNewTotal() {
        // Simulate a repository that accumulates saved states in-memory
        Map<String, Cart> store = new HashMap<>();
        doAnswer(invocation -> {
            Cart cart = invocation.getArgument(0, Cart.class);
            store.put(cart.getId(), cart);
            return cart;
        }).when(cartRepository).save(any(Cart.class));

        doAnswer(invocation -> {
            String id = invocation.getArgument(0, String.class);
            return Optional.ofNullable(store.get(id));
        }).when(cartRepository).findById(anyString());

        cartService.addItem("CART-001", new CartItem("SKU-A", 2, new BigDecimal("15.00")));
        cartService.addItem("CART-001", new CartItem("SKU-B", 1, new BigDecimal("40.00")));

        Cart cart = cartService.getCart("CART-001");
        assertThat(cart.getTotal()).isEqualByComparingTo(new BigDecimal("70.00"));
        assertThat(cart.getItems()).hasSize(2);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `doAnswer` with a `HashMap` accumulator simulates a stateful repository without a real database, enabling multi-step interaction tests that verify state changes across calls; the tradeoff is that this approach creates a partial fake embedded inside the test, which duplicates logic that should live in a proper `FakeCartRepository` class — when the same pattern is needed in three or more tests, extract it to a reusable in-memory fake to avoid subtle inconsistencies between how different test methods implement the `doAnswer` logic (e.g., one test forgetting to handle `null` `id` the same way as another). [official]

**Pattern 432** — JUnit 5 `@TestFactory` with `DynamicTest.stream()` for data-driven test generation from external sources
```java
@TestFactory
Stream<DynamicTest> validateCurrencyConversion_forAllSupportedPairs() throws IOException {
    // Load test cases from a CSV resource bundled with test resources
    List<CurrencyConversionCase> testCases = CurrencyTestDataLoader
        .loadFromCsv("currency-conversion-cases.csv");

    return DynamicTest.stream(
        testCases.iterator(),
        tc -> String.format("%s->%s @ rate %.4f", tc.from(), tc.to(), tc.rate()),
        tc -> {
            BigDecimal result = converter.convert(tc.amount(), tc.from(), tc.to(), tc.rate());
            assertThat(result)
                .usingComparator(BigDecimal::compareTo)
                .isEqualTo(tc.expectedResult());
        }
    );
}
```
Tradeoff: `@TestFactory` with `DynamicTest.stream()` generates individual named test entries for each data row, so CI reports show exactly which currency pair failed rather than failing the entire parameterized test method; the limitation is that `@TestFactory` methods cannot be combined with `@BeforeEach`/`@AfterEach` callbacks in the same lifecycle scope — the `DynamicTest` lambdas run outside the normal JUnit lifecycle, so extensions that rely on `BeforeEachCallback` (e.g., transaction-scoped extensions or `@MockitoExtension`'s stub reset) are NOT invoked around each dynamic test execution, requiring the test factory to manage any per-case setup and teardown explicitly within the lambda. [official]

**Pattern 433** — Spring Boot `WebTestClient` with `@SpringBootTest(RANDOM_PORT)` for reactive endpoint E2E testing
```java
@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = SpringBootTest.WebEnvironment.RANDOM_PORT)
class OrderFluxControllerIT {

    @Autowired
    private WebTestClient webTestClient;

    @Test
    void streamOrders_returnsFluxOfOrderEvents() {
        webTestClient.get()
            .uri("/api/orders/stream?customerId=c-001")
            .accept(MediaType.TEXT_EVENT_STREAM)
            .exchange()
            .expectStatus().isOk()
            .expectHeader().contentTypeCompatibleWith(MediaType.TEXT_EVENT_STREAM)
            .returnResult(OrderEvent.class)
            .getResponseBody()
            .take(3)
            .as(StepVerifier::create)
            .expectNextMatches(e -> e.getCustomerId().equals("c-001"))
            .expectNextMatches(e -> e.getType() == EventType.ORDER_CREATED)
            .expectNextCount(1)
            .verifyComplete();
    }

    @Test
    void createOrder_returnsMonoWithLocationHeader() {
        webTestClient.post()
            .uri("/api/orders")
            .contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
            .bodyValue(new OrderRequest("c-001", "SKU-X", 2))
            .exchange()
            .expectStatus().isCreated()
            .expectHeader().valueMatches("Location", "/api/orders/[A-Z0-9-]+")
            .expectBody(OrderResponse.class)
            .value(resp -> assertThat(resp.getOrderId()).isNotBlank());
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `WebTestClient` integrated with `StepVerifier` via `returnResult(...).getResponseBody()` allows Reactor's `StepVerifier` semantics (backpressure, timeout, `take(n)`) to be applied to streaming responses, catching issues that `expectBodyList()` alone cannot surface because it buffers the full response; the cost is that `StepVerifier.verify()` blocks the test thread until the stream completes or the implicit timeout expires — for long-lived SSE streams, always set `webTestClient = webTestClient.mutate().responseTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(10)).build()` in `@BeforeEach` to prevent an accidental infinite stream from hanging the test runner. [official]

**Pattern 434** — Awaitility `failFast` condition for early termination when a compensating error event fires
```java
@Test
void processPayment_onFraudDetection_publishesFailureEventAndHalts() {
    String paymentId = UUID.randomUUID().toString();
    AtomicReference<String> failedPaymentId = new AtomicReference<>();

    // Register an event listener that signals fast-fail
    applicationContext.addApplicationListener((PaymentFailedEvent event) ->
        failedPaymentId.set(event.getPaymentId()));

    paymentService.processAsync(new PaymentRequest(paymentId, "flagged-card", 9999L));

    await()
        .failFast("Payment processing hung — failure event never fired",
            () -> fraudAuditLog.contains(paymentId))
        .atMost(Duration.ofSeconds(5))
        .pollInterval(Duration.ofMillis(100))
        .untilAsserted(() -> {
            assertThat(failedPaymentId.get()).isEqualTo(paymentId);
            assertThat(paymentRepository.findById(paymentId))
                .isPresent()
                .get()
                .satisfies(p -> assertThat(p.getStatus()).isEqualTo("FRAUD_REJECTED"));
        });
}
```
Tradeoff: `failFast` exits the polling loop immediately when the condition specified in its lambda becomes `true`, converting a 5-second timeout-wait into an instant failure when an error state is detected — this makes test failures readable ("payment failed before assertion condition was met") rather than cryptic ("condition not met within 5 seconds"); the risk is that the `failFast` condition must be stricter than the `untilAsserted` condition, otherwise it can trigger before the assertion condition has a chance to satisfy, making the test flaky — if fraud detection and the expected failure event fire simultaneously, a race between `failFast` and `untilAsserted` can cause the test to fail on a technically passing scenario. [official]

**Pattern 435** — ArchUnit `layeredArchitecture()` with strict mode for multi-module bounded context isolation
```java
@AnalyzeClasses(packages = "com.example.ecommerce",
    importOptions = ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests.class)
class BoundedContextIsolationTest {

    @ArchTest
    static final ArchRule ecommerce_contexts_must_not_cross_boundaries =
        layeredArchitecture()
            .consideringAllDependencies()
            .layer("OrderContext").definedBy("com.example.ecommerce.order..")
            .layer("InventoryContext").definedBy("com.example.ecommerce.inventory..")
            .layer("PaymentContext").definedBy("com.example.ecommerce.payment..")
            .layer("SharedKernel").definedBy("com.example.ecommerce.shared..")
            .whereLayer("OrderContext").mayOnlyAccessLayers("SharedKernel")
            .whereLayer("InventoryContext").mayOnlyAccessLayers("SharedKernel")
            .whereLayer("PaymentContext").mayOnlyAccessLayers("SharedKernel")
            .whereLayer("SharedKernel").mayNotAccessAnyLayer()
            .withOptionalLayers(false);  // strict — all declared layers must exist

    @ArchTest
    static final ArchRule shared_kernel_must_not_contain_framework_specific_types =
        noClasses()
            .that().resideInAPackage("com.example.ecommerce.shared..")
            .should().dependOnClassesThat()
            .resideInAnyPackage(
                "org.springframework.data.jpa..",
                "jakarta.persistence..")
            .because("SharedKernel must not leak JPA/Spring annotations into the domain");
}
```
Tradeoff: `consideringAllDependencies()` makes the layer rule strict — any class that is not assigned to a declared layer causes a violation rather than being silently ignored, preventing packages added during refactoring from bypassing the architecture rules; `withOptionalLayers(false)` additionally fails the test if a declared layer has no matching classes (protecting against a layer being renamed in source but not updated in the ArchUnit rule), and together these two options prevent the silent decay of architecture tests that begins when classes slip into unmonitored packages. [official]

### Community Gotchas

**G56** — JUnit 5 `@ExtendWith` ordering causes extensions to see stale context store state when two extensions use the same namespace key
Why this matters: JUnit 5 runs `BeforeEachCallback` extensions in declaration order and `AfterEachCallback` extensions in reverse (LIFO) order. When two extensions both store objects under the same `ExtensionContext.Namespace` — which happens when extensions share a common base class that uses `Namespace.create(AbstractBaseExtension.class)` as the key — the second extension's `beforeEach` silently overwrites the first extension's stored value under the same namespace. The first extension's `afterEach` (running last in reverse order) then retrieves the second extension's value and operates on the wrong object. The failure mode is silent resource leaks (wrong connection closed) or incorrect teardown rather than an obvious test error, making the root cause invisible from the failure message alone.
Fix: Use `Namespace.create(getClass(), extensionContext.getUniqueId())` as the namespace for all extension-stored state, where `getClass()` refers to the concrete extension class rather than any superclass. This guarantees per-extension, per-test-method uniqueness of the store key and prevents cross-extension contamination even when extensions share inheritance hierarchies. [official]

**G57** — Spring `@Transactional` test method causes `@TransactionalEventListener(AFTER_COMMIT)` to never fire, producing false-green tests
Why this matters: When a test method is annotated with `@Transactional`, Spring's test infrastructure wraps the entire method in a transaction that is rolled back after the test completes, meaning the `AFTER_COMMIT` phase of the transaction never occurs within the test's execution scope. Any `@TransactionalEventListener(phase = TransactionPhase.AFTER_COMMIT)` listener will not fire because no actual commit happens — the event is queued but the commit trigger that would dispatch it is suppressed. This produces tests that pass (the event queue contains the event) while production behavior fails (the listener that sends emails, updates audit logs, or invalidates caches never runs). The bug is particularly hard to spot because `@TransactionalEventListener(BEFORE_COMMIT)` does fire in the same scenario, making phase-specific tests appear to work until a different phase is tested.
Fix: For tests that must verify `AFTER_COMMIT` listeners, remove `@Transactional` from the test method and instead explicitly commit using `TestTransaction.flagForCommit(); TestTransaction.end();` before the assertion, then clean up with a separate `@AfterEach` transactional delete. Alternatively, annotate only the setup and assertion phases with `@Transactional` using `@Sql` scripts and leave the event-publishing action outside any managed transaction boundary. [official]

**G58** — AssertJ `isEqualByComparingTo` on `Comparable` types uses `compareTo` semantics, which passes for `Optional.empty()` vs `Optional.of(0)` if `Optional` is not `Comparable`
Why this matters: `isEqualByComparingTo` is appropriate for `Comparable` types like `BigDecimal` but is sometimes mistakenly used on types that do not implement `Comparable`, causing AssertJ to fall back to `equals()` without warning. Conversely, for domain value objects that implement `Comparable` but where `compareTo` returns `0` for objects that `equals` considers different (e.g., a `Money` class where `Money("10 USD").compareTo(Money("10 EUR")) == 0` due to a bug), `isEqualByComparingTo` will pass while `isEqualTo` would correctly fail. This manifests as currency-agnostic financial assertions that pass regardless of currency code, producing false confidence that multi-currency correctness is tested when it is not.
Fix: Reserve `isEqualByComparingTo` exclusively for `BigDecimal`, `BigInteger`, and other types where `compareTo` and `equals` are documented as equivalent (excluding scale). For domain value objects, use `isEqualTo` which delegates to `equals()`, and ensure the domain `equals()` implementation covers all identity-determining fields. For custom `Comparable` types, write an explicit test that `assertThat(moneyUSD).isNotEqualTo(moneyEUR)` to verify that `equals()` is correctly implemented independently of `compareTo`. [official]

**G59** — Testcontainers container `withReuse(true)` leaves state from previous test runs, causing cross-run contamination when the container is not cleaned between CI jobs
Why this matters: `withReuse(true)` on a Testcontainers container instructs the Testcontainers daemon to reuse an already-running container with the same configuration hash across test runs, rather than starting a new container. This works correctly in local development where a developer runs tests iteratively, but in ephemeral CI environments (e.g., a Kubernetes pod per build) the container from a previous build's pod is never available — `withReuse(true)` silently falls back to starting a new container, so the behavior appears correct. However, in CI setups with persistent Docker daemons (e.g., GitLab runners with `docker:dind` in privileged mode reused across pipelines), a container from a failed test run that left data in an invalid state is reused, causing subsequent pipelines to inherit the corrupted state and fail with non-deterministic errors that are nearly impossible to reproduce locally.
Fix: Enable `withReuse(true)` only in developer-controlled environments by gating it behind a system property or environment variable: `.withReuse(Boolean.parseBoolean(System.getenv("TC_REUSE")))`. In CI, leave `TC_REUSE` unset or set to `false` to always start fresh containers. Alternatively, ensure every test class that uses a reused container has a `@BeforeAll` cleanup step (e.g., `TRUNCATE TABLE ... RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE`) that resets state to a known baseline before the test suite runs. [official]

**G60** — Mockito `when(mock.method()).thenReturn(value)` on a `void`-returning method throws `MissingMethodInvocationException` and the correct form is `doReturn`/`doNothing`
Why this matters: `when(mock.method()).thenReturn(value)` is Mockito's BDD-style stubbing chain that works by calling the method on the mock first (to record the invocation) and then configuring the return value. For `void`-returning methods, there is no return value to chain — calling `when(mock.voidMethod())` throws `MissingMethodInvocationException` because the compiler evaluates `mock.voidMethod()` before `when()` is called, and the `void` return is not a value that can be passed to `when()`. Developers who see the error message "MissingMethodInvocationException: when() requires an argument" often misinterpret it as a Mockito configuration problem rather than recognizing that the API is simply incompatible with `void` returns.
Fix: For `void`-returning methods, always use the `doReturn`/`doNothing`/`doThrow`/`doAnswer` API: `doNothing().when(mock).voidMethod()` or `doThrow(new RuntimeException()).when(mock).voidMethod(arg)`. For methods that return a value but are called on a spy (where calling the real method during stub setup is undesirable), also prefer `doReturn(value).when(spy).method()` over `when(spy.method()).thenReturn(value)` because the former avoids invoking the real method during setup. [official]

**Pattern 436** — JUnit 5 `@ParameterizedTest` with `@CsvSource` for Inline Boundary-Value Testing
```java
@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class AgeValidatorTest {

    @InjectMocks
    private AgeValidator validator;

    @ParameterizedTest(name = "age={0} → valid={1} ({2})")
    @CsvSource({
        "0,   true,  minimum boundary",
        "17,  true,  under 18 permitted",
        "18,  true,  exactly 18",
        "65,  true,  normal adult",
        "120, true,  maximum permitted",
        "121, false, above maximum",
        "-1,  false, negative age",
        "0,   true,  zero boundary"
    })
    void validate_returnsExpectedResult(int age, boolean expectedValid, String scenario) {
        ValidationResult result = validator.validate(age);
        assertThat(result.isValid())
            .as("scenario: %s", scenario)
            .isEqualTo(expectedValid);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@CsvSource` with inline CSV rows is the fastest way to express boundary-value and equivalence partition test cases because the data lives adjacent to the test method, making the relationship between inputs and outcomes immediately visible in code review — but `@CsvSource` parses all values as `String` before JUnit's implicit conversion to the declared parameter type, meaning `null` values must be expressed as the string `"null"` (the implicit null character) rather than leaving the field empty, and `BigDecimal` or `LocalDate` parameters require either `@ConvertWith` annotations or a registered `TypedArgumentConverter`; for complex types, prefer `@MethodSource` or `@ArgumentsSource` with a custom provider class. [official]

**Pattern 437** — Spring Boot `@WebFluxTest` with `WebTestClient` for Reactive Controller Testing
```java
@WebFluxTest(controllers = ProductCatalogHandler.class)
class ProductCatalogHandlerTest {

    @Autowired
    private WebTestClient webClient;

    @MockitoBean
    private ProductRepository productRepository;

    @Test
    void getProductStream_emitsProductsAsServerSentEvents() {
        given(productRepository.findAllAsFlux())
            .willReturn(Flux.interval(Duration.ofMillis(10))
                .take(3)
                .map(i -> new Product("P" + i, "Product " + i, BigDecimal.valueOf(i * 10))));

        webClient.get()
            .uri("/products/stream")
            .accept(MediaType.TEXT_EVENT_STREAM)
            .exchange()
            .expectStatus().isOk()
            .expectHeader().contentTypeCompatibleWith(MediaType.TEXT_EVENT_STREAM)
            .expectBodyList(Product.class)
            .hasSize(3)
            .value(products ->
                assertThat(products)
                    .extracting(Product::getId)
                    .containsExactly("P0", "P1", "P2"));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@WebFluxTest` loads only the WebFlux infrastructure — router functions, handler beans, and `WebExceptionHandler` components — making reactive controller tests faster than `@SpringBootTest`; but `@WebFluxTest` does NOT load `@Service`, `@Repository`, or `@Component` beans, so any bean the handler depends on must be explicitly mocked via `@MockitoBean`, and `WebTestClient` blocks until the entire response body (or the `expectBodyList` buffer size) is received — for infinite streams, always use `.take(N)` or `StepVerifier.create(flux).expectNextCount(N).verifyComplete()` in a separate reactive test to avoid the test hanging indefinitely waiting for the stream to complete. [official]

**Pattern 438** — AssertJ `AbstractStringAssert.satisfies` for Multi-Condition String Validation
```java
@Test
void generateOrderReference_producesCorrectlyFormattedReference() {
    String reference = orderReferenceGenerator.generate(
        "ACME_CORP", OrderType.PRIORITY, LocalDate.of(2026, 5, 14));

    assertThat(reference)
        .as("order reference for ACME_CORP priority order on 2026-05-14")
        .satisfies(
            ref -> assertThat(ref).startsWith("ORD-"),
            ref -> assertThat(ref).endsWith("-PRIORITY"),
            ref -> assertThat(ref).containsPattern("\\d{8}"),  // yyyyMMdd date segment
            ref -> assertThat(ref).hasSize(24),
            ref -> assertThat(ref).isUpperCase()
        );
}
```
Tradeoff: `satisfies(ThrowingConsumer<? super T>...)` in AssertJ 3.22+ accepts varargs of consumers, making it possible to express multiple independent conditions on the same value in a single fluent chain that reads as a specification — unlike `allOf(Condition...)` which requires pre-built `Condition` objects, `satisfies` accepts any lambda including ones that use the full AssertJ assertion API internally; however, `satisfies` runs each consumer independently and reports all failures at once (behaving like soft assertions for the supplied consumers), but unlike `SoftAssertions.assertSoftly`, it does NOT propagate assertion failures from within nested `satisfies` blocks across different assertion chains — keep each consumer focused on a single aspect to ensure clear failure messages. [official]

**Pattern 439** — Testcontainers `@ServiceConnection` with Spring Boot 3.1+ for Zero-Config Property Binding
```java
@SpringBootTest
@Testcontainers
class OrderRepositoryIntegrationTest {

    // @ServiceConnection eliminates the need for @DynamicPropertySource —
    // Spring Boot auto-detects the container type and binds datasource properties
    @Container
    @ServiceConnection
    static PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres =
        new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine")
            .withInitScript("sql/schema.sql");

    @Container
    @ServiceConnection
    static RedisContainer redis = new RedisContainer("redis:7-alpine");

    @Autowired
    private OrderRepository orderRepository;

    @Autowired
    private OrderCacheService cacheService;

    @Test
    void save_and_cache_RoundTrip() {
        Order order = new Order("ORD-001", "CUST-42", OrderStatus.PENDING);
        orderRepository.save(order);
        cacheService.cache(order);

        Order fromDb = orderRepository.findById("ORD-001").orElseThrow();
        Order fromCache = cacheService.get("ORD-001").orElseThrow();

        assertThat(fromDb).usingRecursiveComparison().isEqualTo(order);
        assertThat(fromCache).usingRecursiveComparison().isEqualTo(order);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@ServiceConnection` auto-detects well-known container types (PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, RabbitMQ, MongoDB, and others via `ContainerConnectionDetailsFactory`) and registers `ConnectionDetails` beans that Spring Boot's auto-configuration uses instead of `application.properties` values — eliminating the boilerplate `@DynamicPropertySource` method entirely; however, the auto-detection relies on the container class's type matching a registered `ContainerConnectionDetailsFactory`, so custom or less common containers (e.g., a `GenericContainer` running a proprietary service) will not be detected and still require `@DynamicPropertySource`; check which containers are supported by inspecting the `spring-boot-testcontainers` module's `META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.service.connection.ContainerConnectionDetailsFactory` file. [official]

**Pattern 440** — JUnit 5 `@TestMethodOrder(MethodOrderer.OrderAnnotation.class)` for Ordered Integration Tests
```java
@TestMethodOrder(MethodOrderer.OrderAnnotation.class)
@SpringBootTest
@Transactional
class CheckoutFlowOrderedTest {

    @Autowired
    private CartService cartService;

    @Autowired
    private CheckoutService checkoutService;

    @Autowired
    private OrderRepository orderRepository;

    @Test
    @Order(1)
    @DisplayName("Step 1: Add items to cart")
    void addItemsToCart() {
        cartService.addItem("SESSION-001", new CartItem("SKU-42", 2, BigDecimal.valueOf(19.99)));
        assertThat(cartService.getCart("SESSION-001").getItems()).hasSize(1);
    }

    @Test
    @Order(2)
    @DisplayName("Step 2: Apply discount coupon")
    void applyDiscountCoupon() {
        cartService.applyCoupon("SESSION-001", "SAVE10");
        assertThat(cartService.getCart("SESSION-001").getDiscountRate())
            .isEqualByComparingTo(BigDecimal.valueOf(0.10));
    }

    @Test
    @Order(3)
    @DisplayName("Step 3: Complete checkout creates order")
    void completeCheckout() {
        Order order = checkoutService.checkout("SESSION-001", PaymentMethod.CARD);
        assertThat(order.getStatus()).isEqualTo(OrderStatus.CONFIRMED);
        assertThat(orderRepository.findById(order.getId())).isPresent();
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@TestMethodOrder(MethodOrderer.OrderAnnotation.class)` with `@Order` is the correct approach for intentionally ordered scenarios like workflow step testing — it is explicit and documented rather than relying on alphabetical or class-file ordering; however, ordered tests are inherently stateful across methods, which means the `@Transactional` rollback at the method level (each test's transaction is rolled back independently) means state from `@Order(1)` is NOT visible to `@Order(2)` unless the test class uses `@TestInstance(PER_CLASS)` with a single class-level transaction managed via `TestTransaction.end()` / `TestTransaction.start()` between steps; for true stateful ordered integration tests, manage the transaction lifecycle explicitly or use `@Rollback(false)` with `@AfterAll` cleanup. [official]

**Pattern 441** — Mockito `MockedStatic` for Testing Code That Calls Static Utility Methods
```java
@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class UuidGeneratorServiceTest {

    @Test
    void createOrder_usesProvidedUUIDForOrderId() {
        UUID fixedUuid = UUID.fromString("00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000042");

        try (MockedStatic<UUID> uuidMock = mockStatic(UUID.class)) {
            uuidMock.when(UUID::randomUUID).thenReturn(fixedUuid);

            OrderService service = new OrderService(new InMemoryOrderRepository());
            Order order = service.createOrder("CUST-1", List.of("SKU-A"));

            assertThat(order.getId()).isEqualTo(fixedUuid.toString());
            uuidMock.verify(UUID::randomUUID, times(1));
        }
        // After the try-with-resources block, UUID.randomUUID() is restored
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `MockedStatic` intercepts static method invocations on the specified class for the duration of the `try` block and is automatically closed via `AutoCloseable` — this is Mockito's recommended approach for static mocking that avoids PowerMock's classpath manipulation; however, `MockedStatic` is thread-local per Mockito's design, meaning a `MockedStatic<UUID>` opened on thread A does NOT intercept `UUID.randomUUID()` calls made by code running on a different thread (e.g., a `CompletableFuture` with a custom executor or a virtual thread), so tests that exercise multi-threaded code paths that call the static method will see the real implementation even inside the `try` block; for thread-spanning cases, prefer dependency injection of a `Supplier<UUID>` over direct `UUID.randomUUID()` invocations to make the dependency fully mockable. [official]

**Pattern 442** — Spring Boot `@DataMongoTest` with Testcontainers `MongoDBContainer` for Repository Testing
```java
@DataMongoTest
@Testcontainers
@AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = AutoConfigureTestDatabase.Replace.NONE)
class ProductDocumentRepositoryTest {

    @Container
    @ServiceConnection
    static MongoDBContainer mongodb = new MongoDBContainer("mongo:7.0");

    @Autowired
    private ProductDocumentRepository repository;

    @Test
    void save_and_findByCategory_roundTrip() {
        ProductDocument product = new ProductDocument(
            null, "Widget Pro", "TOOLS", BigDecimal.valueOf(49.99),
            Map.of("weight", "250g", "warranty", "2 years"));

        ProductDocument saved = repository.save(product);

        assertThat(saved.getId()).isNotNull();
        assertThat(saved.getId()).matches("^[a-f0-9]{24}$");  // MongoDB ObjectId format

        List<ProductDocument> byCategory = repository.findByCategory("TOOLS");
        assertThat(byCategory)
            .hasSize(1)
            .first()
            .satisfies(p -> {
                assertThat(p.getName()).isEqualTo("Widget Pro");
                assertThat(p.getAttributes()).containsEntry("warranty", "2 years");
            });
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@DataMongoTest` loads only the MongoDB-related auto-configuration (Spring Data MongoDB repositories, `MongoTemplate`, `MongoMappingContext`) and excludes the full `@SpringBootApplication` context — making MongoDB repository tests fast; but `@DataMongoTest` without `@AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = NONE)` will attempt to use an embedded MongoDB instance (via `de.flapdoodle.embed.mongo`) if it is on the classpath, silently ignoring the Testcontainers `MongoDBContainer`; always add `replace = NONE` and `@ServiceConnection` (or `@DynamicPropertySource`) to force the test to use the Testcontainers container's connection string rather than the embedded fallback. [official]

**Pattern 443** — AssertJ `AbstractIterableAssert.allMatch` vs `allSatisfy` for Predicate vs Full-Assertion Conditions
```java
@Test
void processInvoices_marksAllOverdueInvoicesAsEscalated() {
    List<Invoice> invoices = List.of(
        new Invoice("INV-001", LocalDate.now().minusDays(45), InvoiceStatus.OVERDUE),
        new Invoice("INV-002", LocalDate.now().minusDays(31), InvoiceStatus.OVERDUE),
        new Invoice("INV-003", LocalDate.now().minusDays(60), InvoiceStatus.OVERDUE)
    );
    invoiceService.escalateOverdue(invoices);

    // allMatch for simple predicate — failure message shows only "predicate failed"
    assertThat(invoices).allMatch(i -> i.getStatus() == InvoiceStatus.ESCALATED,
        "all overdue invoices should be escalated");

    // allSatisfy for AssertJ assertions — failure message shows which field and value
    assertThat(invoices)
        .allSatisfy(invoice -> {
            assertThat(invoice.getStatus())
                .as("status of invoice %s", invoice.getId())
                .isEqualTo(InvoiceStatus.ESCALATED);
            assertThat(invoice.getEscalationDate())
                .as("escalation date of invoice %s", invoice.getId())
                .isNotNull()
                .isBeforeOrEqualTo(LocalDate.now());
        });
}
```
Tradeoff: `allMatch(Predicate)` produces a brief failure message like "expected all elements to satisfy given predicate but this element did not: Invoice{id='INV-002', status=OVERDUE}" with no information about which condition failed or what the actual value was — it is appropriate only when the predicate is self-documenting (e.g., `i -> i.isActive()`); use `allSatisfy(ThrowingConsumer)` for multi-field checks because the inner `assertThat` statements produce specific field-level failure messages that identify exactly which field on which element was wrong, at the cost of slightly more verbose assertion code. [official]

**Pattern 444** — Testcontainers `Network.newNetwork()` with Named Aliases for Container-to-Container Communication
```java
@Testcontainers
@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = SpringBootTest.WebEnvironment.RANDOM_PORT)
class MessageBrokerIntegrationTest {

    static Network network = Network.newNetwork();

    @Container
    static RabbitMQContainer rabbitmq = new RabbitMQContainer("rabbitmq:3.13-management")
        .withNetwork(network)
        .withNetworkAliases("rabbitmq");  // reachable as "rabbitmq" inside the network

    @Container
    static GenericContainer<?> messageConsumer =
        new GenericContainer<>("company/message-consumer:latest")
            .withNetwork(network)
            .withEnv("RABBITMQ_HOST", "rabbitmq")  // uses network alias
            .withEnv("RABBITMQ_PORT", "5672")
            .waitingFor(Wait.forLogMessage(".*Consumer started.*", 1));

    @DynamicPropertySource
    static void registerProperties(DynamicPropertyRegistry registry) {
        registry.add("spring.rabbitmq.host", rabbitmq::getHost);
        registry.add("spring.rabbitmq.port", rabbitmq::getAmqpPort);
    }

    @Autowired
    private MessagePublisher publisher;

    @Test
    void publishMessage_isConsumedByMessageConsumerContainer() throws Exception {
        publisher.publish("test-queue", new TestMessage("hello", "world"));

        await().atMost(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
            .untilAsserted(() ->
                assertThat(messageConsumer.getLogs())
                    .contains("Received message: hello"));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `Network.newNetwork()` creates a Docker bridge network scoped to the test class, enabling container-to-container communication via network aliases without exposing ports on the host — but `Network` must be declared as a `static` field and is closed after the last `@Container static` field's lifecycle ends (managed by Testcontainers' JUnit 5 extension), so if `Network.newNetwork()` is called in a `@BeforeAll` method instead of at the static field level, the network may be created after the containers have already started (or closed before they stop), causing `ContainerStartException: No such network` errors; always declare the `Network` as a `static final` field to ensure it is created before any container references it. [official]

**Pattern 445** — JUnit 5 `@ExtendWith` with Custom `InvocationInterceptor` for Test Execution Timing
```java
public class TestTimingExtension implements InvocationInterceptor {

    private static final Logger log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(TestTimingExtension.class);
    private static final long SLOW_TEST_THRESHOLD_MS = 500;

    @Override
    public void interceptTestMethod(
            Invocation<Void> invocation,
            ReflectiveInvocationContext<Method> invocationContext,
            ExtensionContext extensionContext) throws Throwable {

        long start = System.currentTimeMillis();
        try {
            invocation.proceed();
        } finally {
            long elapsed = System.currentTimeMillis() - start;
            String testName = extensionContext.getDisplayName();
            if (elapsed > SLOW_TEST_THRESHOLD_MS) {
                log.warn("SLOW TEST [{} ms]: {}", elapsed, testName);
            }
            extensionContext.getStore(Namespace.create(TestTimingExtension.class))
                .put(testName + ".elapsed", elapsed);
        }
    }
}

// Usage:
@ExtendWith(TestTimingExtension.class)
class PaymentIntegrationTest { /* ... */ }
```
Tradeoff: `InvocationInterceptor.interceptTestMethod` wraps the test method invocation and provides precise wall-clock timing — including `@BeforeEach` setup time is NOT included because `interceptTestMethod` wraps only the `@Test` method body, not the full lifecycle; to time the full lifecycle including setup and teardown, implement `BeforeTestExecutionCallback` and `AfterTestExecutionCallback` in the same extension class and compute the delta between the two callbacks, storing the start timestamp in the extension store's `BEFORE_TEST_EXECUTION` key as recommended by the JUnit 5 documentation for this exact use case. [official]

**Pattern 446** — Mockito `BDDMockito.given().willAnswer()` with `AdditionalAnswers.returnsFirstArg()` for Pass-Through Stubs
```java
@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class OrderEnricherTest {

    @Mock
    private OrderRepository orderRepository;

    @Mock
    private TaxCalculator taxCalculator;

    @InjectMocks
    private OrderEnricher enricher;

    @Test
    void enrich_appendsTaxAndSavesEnrichedOrder() {
        Order input = new Order("ORD-001", BigDecimal.valueOf(100), null);
        given(taxCalculator.calculate(any(Order.class))).willReturn(BigDecimal.valueOf(20));

        // The repository save should return the order it was given (pass-through)
        given(orderRepository.save(any(Order.class)))
            .willAnswer(AdditionalAnswers.returnsFirstArg());

        Order result = enricher.enrich(input);

        assertThat(result.getTotal()).isEqualByComparingTo(BigDecimal.valueOf(120));
        assertThat(result.getTax()).isEqualByComparingTo(BigDecimal.valueOf(20));

        ArgumentCaptor<Order> savedOrder = ArgumentCaptor.forClass(Order.class);
        verify(orderRepository).save(savedOrder.capture());
        assertThat(savedOrder.getValue().getTotal())
            .isEqualByComparingTo(BigDecimal.valueOf(120));
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `AdditionalAnswers.returnsFirstArg()` (and its siblings `returnsSecondArg()`, `returnsArgAt(N)`) provides a concise pass-through stub for repository `save` methods that return the persisted entity — avoiding the need to configure `willReturn(specificInstance)` when the actual returned instance is whatever was passed in, which mirrors real JPA repository behavior; however, `returnsFirstArg()` returns the same object reference that was passed to the method, so if the production code modifies the object after the save call (e.g., sets the audit timestamp), the returned reference reflects those mutations — use `ArgumentCaptor` after the call to verify the exact state of the object at save time, rather than asserting on the returned reference after possible post-save mutations. [official]

**Pattern 447** — Spring Boot `@JsonTest` with `JacksonTester` for Bi-Directional Serialization Contract Testing
```java
@JsonTest
class PaymentRequestJsonTest {

    @Autowired
    private JacksonTester<PaymentRequest> json;

    @Test
    void serialize_producesExpectedJsonStructure() throws Exception {
        PaymentRequest request = new PaymentRequest(
            "PAY-001",
            new Money(BigDecimal.valueOf(99.99), Currency.getInstance("USD")),
            PaymentMethod.CARD,
            Instant.parse("2026-05-14T10:00:00Z")
        );

        assertThat(json.write(request))
            .hasJsonPath("$.paymentId")
            .extractingJsonPathStringValue("$.paymentId").isEqualTo("PAY-001")
            .and()
            .hasJsonPath("$.amount.value").extractingJsonPathNumberValue("$.amount.value")
                .isEqualByComparingTo(BigDecimal.valueOf(99.99))
            .hasJsonPath("$.amount.currency").extractingJsonPathStringValue("$.amount.currency")
                .isEqualTo("USD")
            .hasJsonPath("$.timestamp").extractingJsonPathStringValue("$.timestamp")
                .isEqualTo("2026-05-14T10:00:00Z");
    }

    @Test
    void deserialize_parsesJsonIntoCorrectObject() throws Exception {
        String jsonContent = """
            {
              "paymentId": "PAY-001",
              "amount": { "value": 99.99, "currency": "USD" },
              "method": "CARD",
              "timestamp": "2026-05-14T10:00:00Z"
            }
            """;

        assertThat(json.parse(jsonContent))
            .satisfies(req -> {
                assertThat(req.getPaymentId()).isEqualTo("PAY-001");
                assertThat(req.getAmount().getCurrency())
                    .isEqualTo(Currency.getInstance("USD"));
            });
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@JsonTest` loads only Jackson auto-configuration — `ObjectMapper`, `JsonComponent` beans, `Module` beans, and `DateTimeModule` — making it the fastest way to verify serialization contracts without starting a full application context; but `@JsonTest` does NOT load `@Service`, `@Component`, or `@Repository` beans, so any `JsonSerializer`/`JsonDeserializer` that depends on a Spring-managed bean (e.g., a custom deserializer that calls a repository to resolve a foreign key) must be declared as a `@JsonComponent` and mocked via `@MockitoBean` inside the `@JsonTest` class, or moved to a `@ControllerAdvice` tested via `@WebMvcTest` instead. [official]

**Pattern 448** — ArchUnit `SlicesRuleDefinition` for Cycle-Free Package Dependency Enforcement
```java
@AnalyzeClasses(packages = "com.example.shop",
    importOptions = ImportOption.Predefined.DO_NOT_INCLUDE_TESTS)
class CycleFreeArchitectureTest {

    @ArchTest
    static final ArchRule no_cycles_within_domain_slices =
        SlicesRuleDefinition.slices()
            .matching("com.example.shop.(*)..")
            .should().beFreeOfCycles();

    @ArchTest
    static final ArchRule no_cycles_within_infrastructure_adapters =
        SlicesRuleDefinition.slices()
            .matching("com.example.shop.infrastructure.(*)..")
            .should().beFreeOfCycles();

    @ArchTest
    static final ArchRule domain_slices_do_not_depend_on_infrastructure =
        SlicesRuleDefinition.slices()
            .matching("com.example.shop.domain.(*)..")
            .should().notDependOnEachOther()
            .ignoreDependency(SharedKernel.class, Object.class);
}
```
Tradeoff: `SlicesRuleDefinition.slices().matching("com.example.shop.(*)..")` derives slice names from the first captured group (`(*)`) in the matching pattern — in this case the second path segment — and detects circular dependencies between those slices; the rule reports the full cycle path in the failure message (e.g., "Slice order → Slice payment → Slice order"), making the exact dependency cycle identifiable without manual graph traversal; however, `beFreeOfCycles()` considers all transitive dependencies (including third-party libraries that both slices depend on) as intra-cycle edges unless excluded with `ignoreDependency(...)`, so the first run of this rule on a pre-existing codebase often surfaces false-positive cycles through shared library classes; use `SlicesRuleDefinition.slices().matching(...).namingSlices(...)` with explicit exclusion patterns to scope the cycle check to first-party code only. [official]

**Pattern 449** — Awaitility `untilCallTo` for Polling a Method Reference Directly
```java
@SpringBootTest
class CacheWarmupServiceTest {

    @Autowired
    private CacheWarmupService warmupService;

    @Autowired
    private CacheHealthIndicator cacheHealth;

    @Test
    void warmup_populatesCacheWithinTimeout() {
        warmupService.triggerAsync();

        await()
            .pollInterval(Duration.ofMillis(100))
            .atMost(Duration.ofSeconds(5))
            .failFast("cache warmup failed",
                () -> cacheHealth.getStatus() == CacheStatus.ERROR)
            .untilCallTo(() -> cacheHealth.getLoadedEntryCount())
            .matches(count -> count >= 100);

        CacheMetrics metrics = cacheHealth.getMetrics();
        assertThat(metrics.getLoadedEntryCount())
            .as("entries loaded after warmup")
            .isGreaterThanOrEqualTo(100);
        assertThat(metrics.getWarmupDurationMs())
            .as("warmup completed within SLA")
            .isLessThan(4_000L);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `untilCallTo(Callable<T>).matches(Predicate<T>)` separates the data retrieval from the condition check — `Callable` returns the current value and `Predicate` evaluates it — which makes the intent clearer than `until(() -> cacheHealth.getLoadedEntryCount() >= 100)` (where both retrieval and condition are mixed in one lambda) and produces better failure messages because Awaitility can show the last polled value ("last evaluated value: 87") rather than just "condition was not met"; the `failFast` overload that accepts a description string and a `Callable<Boolean>` causes immediate failure if the callable returns `true`, short-circuiting the retry loop and producing a clearer error message when the system under test enters a known error state rather than waiting for the full timeout. [official]

---

**Pattern 450** — Spring Boot `@SpringBootTest` with `ApplicationContextRunner` for Conditional Auto-Configuration Testing
```java
class CacheAutoConfigurationTest {

    private final ApplicationContextRunner contextRunner =
        new ApplicationContextRunner()
            .withConfiguration(AutoConfigurations.of(CacheAutoConfiguration.class));

    @Test
    void cacheIsDisabledByDefault() {
        contextRunner.run(context -> {
            assertThat(context).doesNotHaveBean(CacheManager.class);
        });
    }

    @Test
    void cacheIsEnabledWhenPropertySet() {
        contextRunner
            .withPropertyValues("app.cache.enabled=true")
            .run(context -> {
                assertThat(context).hasSingleBean(CacheManager.class);
                CacheManager cacheManager = context.getBean(CacheManager.class);
                assertThat(cacheManager).isInstanceOf(RedisCacheManager.class);
            });
    }

    @Test
    void cacheUsesCustomTtlWhenConfigured() {
        contextRunner
            .withPropertyValues("app.cache.enabled=true", "app.cache.ttl-seconds=300")
            .run(context -> {
                CacheProperties props = context.getBean(CacheProperties.class);
                assertThat(props.getTtlSeconds()).isEqualTo(300);
            });
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `ApplicationContextRunner` starts a lightweight application context that loads only the specified auto-configurations — it does NOT scan any packages or load `@SpringBootApplication` — making it ideal for testing `@ConditionalOnProperty`, `@ConditionalOnBean`, and `@ConditionalOnMissingBean` conditions without the overhead of a full `@SpringBootTest`; but `ApplicationContextRunner` does NOT register the Spring Security filter chain, embedded server, or Spring MVC infrastructure, so it cannot test web-layer conditions (`@ConditionalOnWebApplication`) accurately — use `WebApplicationContextRunner` or `ReactiveWebApplicationContextRunner` for web-environment-dependent conditional tests to ensure the correct `WebApplicationType` is active during condition evaluation. [official]

### Community Gotchas

**G61** — JUnit 5 `@TestFactory` Returning a `Stream` Closes the Stream After Test Discovery, Breaking Reuse
Why this matters: When a `@TestFactory` method returns a `Stream<DynamicTest>`, JUnit 5 consumes the stream exactly once during test execution and closes it via `Stream.close()` after all dynamic tests have run. If the stream is backed by a resource that requires explicit lifecycle management (e.g., a JDBC `ResultSet` wrapped in a `Stream` via `StreamSupport.stream(spliterator, false)`, or a file `Files.lines(path)` stream), the stream is closed by JUnit after the last dynamic test completes — not after each test. However, if the stream source throws a `SQLException` or `IOException` during lazy evaluation (e.g., when the database cursor is advanced between test executions), the subsequent dynamic tests fail with a resource-closed exception rather than a meaningful test assertion failure.
Fix: Materialize the data source into an eagerly-evaluated collection (e.g., `List<DynamicTest>`) inside the `@TestFactory` method before returning, ensuring all resource-dependent data is loaded before JUnit begins executing the dynamic tests. For large data sets that cannot be materialized, wrap the stream in a try-with-resources block and convert to a `List` of pre-computed `DynamicTest` objects, closing the resource immediately after generating all test instances. [official]

**G62** — Spring Boot `@MockitoBean` on a Field That Is Also Used by `@Autowired` in the Same Test Class Injects Different Instances
Why this matters: `@MockitoBean` replaces the bean in the `ApplicationContext` with a Mockito mock, and `@Autowired` in the same test class injects a reference to the bean from the same `ApplicationContext`. For most scenarios, both annotations refer to the same mock instance. However, when `@MockitoBean` is declared on a field of type `Interface` while `@Autowired` injects a `ConcreteClass`, Spring may inject a proxy-wrapped instance via `@Autowired` that is not the same object reference as the raw mock injected via `@MockitoBean`. Calling `Mockito.verify(mockitoBean.field)` will fail with "the argument passed to verify() is not a mock" if the `@Autowired` field and the `@MockitoBean` field are the same interface but the `@Autowired` injection resolves to a proxy.
Fix: Declare both `@MockitoBean` and `@Autowired` on fields of the same type (use the interface for both, or the concrete class for both). When `@Transactional` is on the mocked bean, Spring wraps it in a CGLIB proxy — always declare `@MockitoBean` on the interface type to ensure the mock is the target of the proxy, and use `AopTestUtils.getTargetObject(autowiredBean)` to unwrap the proxy when passing to `verify()` if needed. [official]

**G63** — AssertJ `containsExactly` Fails With `ClassCastException` When the List Contains Proxied Spring Beans
Why this matters: `assertThat(actualList).containsExactly(expected1, expected2)` calls `expected1.equals(actual)` via AssertJ's element comparison, which works correctly when the list contains plain Java objects. However, when the actual list is populated with Spring bean proxies (e.g., because `ApplicationContext.getBeansOfType()` returns proxy-wrapped instances), and `expected1` is a plain unproxied instance, the `equals` call may throw a `ClassCastException` because the CGLIB proxy's auto-generated `equals` method attempts to cast the argument to the proxied type using an incompatible class hierarchy. This is particularly common when asserting on results from `@Autowired List<SomeInterface>` injection points.
Fix: Unwrap proxies before assertion using `AopTestUtils.getTargetObject(bean)` for CGLIB proxies, or use `assertThat(actualList).usingRecursiveComparison().isEqualTo(expectedList)` which compares fields recursively without calling `equals()` on the proxy objects, avoiding the CGLIB cast entirely. Alternatively, avoid asserting on bean proxy instances by instead asserting on the data they produce (e.g., call the method and assert the return value) rather than on the beans themselves. [official]

**G64** — Testcontainers `withFileSystemBind` Silently Creates an Empty Directory Instead of Failing When the Source Path Does Not Exist
Why this matters: `container.withFileSystemBind("/host/path/that/does/not/exist", "/container/path", BindMode.READ_WRITE)` will NOT throw an exception when the source path does not exist on the host. Docker's bind-mount semantics automatically create an empty directory at the source path if it does not exist (on Linux; behavior varies on Windows/macOS with Docker Desktop). The container starts successfully, but the expected file content (e.g., configuration files, SSL certificates, seed data) is not present inside the container, causing the application running in the container to start without the expected configuration — sometimes silently falling back to defaults. The test then passes because the container reports healthy, but the tested behavior is incorrect because the application is using wrong configuration.
Fix: Validate that the source path exists before registering the file system bind: `Path sourcePath = Path.of("/host/path/..."); assertThat(sourcePath).exists().isReadable();` — place this check in the `@BeforeAll` static setup before the container starts. Alternatively, use `withCopyFileToContainer(MountableFile.forHostPath(path), "/container/path")` which throws `IllegalArgumentException` immediately if the source file does not exist, giving a clear failure at container startup time rather than a confusing runtime mismatch. [official]

**G65** — Mockito `spy(realObject)` Does Not Intercept `this`-Reference Calls Made Inside the Spied Object's Methods
Why this matters: `OrderService spy = Mockito.spy(new OrderService(repo)); doReturn(discount).when(spy).calculateDiscount(any());` creates a Mockito spy that intercepts calls to `calculateDiscount` made from test code directly on the `spy` reference. However, if `OrderService.processOrder()` internally calls `this.calculateDiscount(...)` (a `this`-reference call), the spy does NOT intercept that call — it routes to the real `calculateDiscount` implementation directly via the object's virtual dispatch table, bypassing the Mockito proxy entirely. The test then fails or produces incorrect results because the stubbed discount was never applied despite the `doReturn` being configured.
Fix: Mockito spies use subclass proxying (CGLIB), and `this`-reference calls bypass the proxy layer by definition. To intercept internal calls, refactor `OrderService` to call `calculateDiscount` through a separate `DiscountStrategy` dependency that can be directly mocked — this is also better design because it separates concerns. If refactoring is not possible, use `doCallRealMethod()` on all non-stubbed methods and mock only the top-level method being tested, or restructure the test to inject the spy into a wrapper service that calls the method externally through the spy reference. [official]

### Patterns

**Pattern 451** — JUnit 5 `@TempDir` with `CleanupMode.ON_SUCCESS` for Failure-Preserving File Artifact Tests
```java
@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class ReportExporterTest {

    @TempDir(cleanup = CleanupMode.ON_SUCCESS)
    Path reportDir;

    @InjectMocks
    private ReportExporter exporter;

    @Test
    void exportPdfReport_writesValidPdfFile() throws IOException {
        ReportRequest request = ReportRequest.builder()
            .title("Q1 2026 Sales Summary")
            .periodStart(LocalDate.of(2026, 1, 1))
            .periodEnd(LocalDate.of(2026, 3, 31))
            .outputDir(reportDir)
            .build();

        Path outputFile = exporter.export(request);

        assertThat(outputFile)
            .exists()
            .isRegularFile()
            .hasExtension("pdf");
        assertThat(outputFile.toFile().length())
            .as("PDF must be non-empty")
            .isGreaterThan(0L);
        // Verify PDF header bytes ("%PDF-")
        byte[] header = Files.readAllBytes(outputFile);
        assertThat(new String(header, 0, 5, StandardCharsets.US_ASCII))
            .isEqualTo("%PDF-");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@TempDir(cleanup = CleanupMode.ON_SUCCESS)` leaves the temporary directory intact when the test fails, making the generated file artifacts available for post-failure inspection — this is essential when debugging output-format bugs because the actual file (PDF, CSV, XML) can be opened directly rather than reconstructed from log output; the directory is only deleted when the test passes, preventing accumulation of artifacts from successful runs. The risk is that repeated test failures across CI runs can accumulate large artifact directories if the temp location maps to a shared filesystem; always combine `ON_SUCCESS` with a CI artifact collection step (`artifacts: paths: [/tmp/junit-*]`) to capture and expire them automatically rather than relying on OS-level temp cleanup. [official]

---

**Pattern 452** — `jqwik` Property-Based Test with `@ForAll @StringLength` for Invariant Verification
```java
import net.jqwik.api.*;
import net.jqwik.api.constraints.*;

class SlugGeneratorProperties {

    private final SlugGenerator generator = new SlugGenerator();

    @Property(tries = 500)
    void generated_slug_is_always_lowercase(@ForAll @AlphaChars @StringLength(min = 1, max = 100) String input) {
        String slug = generator.generate(input);
        assertThat(slug).isEqualTo(slug.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT));
    }

    @Property(tries = 500)
    void generated_slug_contains_only_alphanumeric_and_hyphens(
            @ForAll @StringLength(min = 1, max = 200) String input) {
        String slug = generator.generate(input);
        assertThat(slug).matches("[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*");
    }

    @Property(tries = 500)
    void slug_generation_is_idempotent(
            @ForAll @StringLength(min = 1, max = 100) String input) {
        String firstSlug  = generator.generate(input);
        String secondSlug = generator.generate(firstSlug);
        assertThat(secondSlug)
            .as("re-slugifying a slug must be idempotent")
            .isEqualTo(firstSlug);
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@Property` with jqwik generates 500 random inputs per test run (configurable via `tries`), exercising boundary conditions that no manually written example set would cover — consecutive Unicode characters, empty strings after trim, all-whitespace inputs, strings containing only special characters — and reports the minimal failing example via shrinking; jqwik's shrinking narrows a 200-character failing input to the smallest string that still triggers the bug (often 1-3 characters), making root-cause identification immediate. The limitation is that jqwik's default string generation uses the full Unicode BMP including control characters and right-to-left marks; use `@AlphaChars`, `@NumericChars`, or `@Chars` constraints to restrict the alphabet when the system under test is documented to accept only a specific character set, otherwise generated inputs may trigger failure modes that are intentionally out of scope. [community]

**Pattern 453** — Spring Boot `@AutoConfigureObservability` with `TestObservationRegistry` for Span and Metric Assertions
```java
@WebMvcTest(controllers = OrderController.class)
@AutoConfigureObservability
class OrderControllerObservabilityTest {

    @Autowired
    private MockMvc mockMvc;

    @Autowired
    private TestObservationRegistry observationRegistry;

    @MockitoBean
    private OrderService orderService;

    @BeforeEach
    void resetObservations() {
        observationRegistry.clear();
    }

    @Test
    void createOrder_recordsSpanWithOrderIdTag() throws Exception {
        given(orderService.create(any())).willReturn(new Order("ORD-001", OrderStatus.PENDING));

        mockMvc.perform(post("/orders")
                .contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
                .content("{\"customerId\":\"C001\",\"amount\":49.99}"))
            .andExpect(status().isCreated());

        TestObservationRegistryAssert.assertThat(observationRegistry)
            .hasObservationWithNameEqualTo("order.create")
            .that()
            .hasLowCardinalityKeyValue("status", "PENDING")
            .hasHighCardinalityKeyValue("order.id", "ORD-001");
    }
}
```
Tradeoff: `@AutoConfigureObservability` loads the Micrometer Observation API and `TestObservationRegistry` into the test context, replacing the production `ObservationRegistry` with a test-scoped one that records all observations made during the request — this allows asserting on span names, low-cardinality tags (dimensions), and high-cardinality tags (trace attributes) without running an actual tracing backend; `observationRegistry.clear()` in `@BeforeEach` is required because the registry accumulates observations across tests in the same context, and stale observations from previous tests can cause false positives or false negatives when counting spans. The limitation is that `@WebMvcTest` loads a thin slice that excludes `@Scheduled` beans and async processing, so observations recorded outside the HTTP request boundary (e.g., from a scheduled job that triggers during the test) are not captured unless `@SpringBootTest` is used instead. [official]
